docs.title: Fleet
docs.text:
Fleet is a lazy expression accumulator with an immutable builder API that specializes in creating CDISC SDTM/ADaM datasets using the well-known Polars library.

  • Polars-fast

    Lazy, multi-threaded pipelines: hundreds of derivations collapse into one optimized query plan. Zero Pandas.

    Namespace pipeline

  • Reads like the spec

    One verb per intent — assign, date, baseline, flag — so the code is the specification a reviewer reads.

    Verb cheat sheet

  • Dual workflow

    Chain verbs inline or drive the same pipeline from define.yaml — and round-trip between the two.

    How define.yaml works

  • Submission-ready

    Define-XML 2.1 generation, CDISC CORE validation, trial-design conformance audits with P21 rule IDs.

    Validation strategy

  • AI-native by consequence

    A sharp workflow is what makes assistants reliable. MCP server, define.yaml language server and llms.txt expose it — so they write and verify.

    IDE & AI tooling

  • Six core dependencies

    polars, pydantic, pyyaml, httpx, jsonschema, lxml. Everything else is an opt-in extra.

    Installation

docs.title: What is Fleet?
docs.text:
Fleet adds chainable verb pipelines directly onto every Polars DataFrame so you can build standards-compliant CDISC datasets with minimal boilerplate:

import fleet
import polars as pl
from codelists import SEX  # generated by: fleet add-ct --domains DM --output codelists.py

# SDTM DM domain from raw data — `assign` is the one assignment verb.
# Raw collected values ("Male"/"Female") remap to CT submission values.
dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")
    .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=SEX, ct_map={"Male": "M", "Female": "F"})
    .to_frame()
)

# ADaM BDS dataset (ADVS) from SDTM — one unbroken chain
advs = (
    vs_sdtm.adam.source("USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVAL")
    .study_day("ADY", date_col="ADT", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria='pl.col("VISITNUM") == 1', by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

Most verbs accumulate into a single Polars with_columns pass; window verbs (baseline, cross-domain joins) checkpoint internally without breaking the chain.

docs.title: Namespace Extensions
docs.text:
Importing fleet registers chainable namespaces on every Polars DataFrame (and LazyFrame):

Namespace Target dataset Description df.sdtm SDTM domains domain mapping, CT via assign(ct=), datetime normalisation, TDD (call .verbs()) df.adam ADaM BDS study day, baseline, change, flags, BSA, MAP, QTc, LOCF, summary records (call .verbs())

ADaM sub-structures and therapeutic-area extensions are nested under df.adam:

Property Target dataset Description df.adam.adsl ADSL patient-level verbs: treatment dates, duration, population flags, age conversion, periods df.adam.occds OCCDS (ADAE, ADCM…) occurrence verbs: treatment-emergent flag, ASEQ, onset/recovery df.adam.onco Oncology RECIST response, BOR, filter_pd df.adam.ophtha Ophthalmology ETDRS/LogMAR, study eye df.adam.peds Pediatrics Age derivations, prematurity df.adam.vaccine Vaccine Fever, seroconversion, ADIS AVAL df.adam.metabolic Metabolic Waist ratios, body fat % df.adam.neuro Neuroscience Centiloid, MMSE, CDR-SoB df.adam.tte ADTTE Event/censor sources, TTE params, AVAL/AVALU, KM inputs

These mirror the admiral TA packages.

docs.title: Architecture at a Glance
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    CFG["study_config.yaml"] --> SPEC["define.yaml<br/>(metadata spec)"]
    RAW["Raw data<br/>CSV · XPT · Parquet"] --> SDTM

    subgraph FLEET["Fleet pipelines"]
        direction TB
        SDTM["df.sdtm<br/>SDTM domains"]
        ADAM["df.adam · df.adam.adsl<br/>ADaM datasets"]
        TLG["df.tlg<br/>Tables · Listings · Graphs"]
        SDTM --> ADAM
        ADAM --> TLG
    end

    SPEC --> FLEET
    FLEET --> VAL["CORE validation<br/>fleet validate"]
    SPEC --> XML["Define-XML 2.1<br/>fleet define-xml"]
    TLG --> OUT["HTML · RTF · PDF · PPTX"]

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to Fleet are documented here.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Toxicity grades equal admiral (ADR-0014, alpha audit package D). The 8 bundled criteria files are generated from the admiral 1.4.1 metadata by scripts/regen_grading_criteria.R and keep the admiral text of each term; a frozen admiral grid of 34,146 rows is the CI test.
  • A null BNRIND takes the ULN criteria: ALT 900 with ULN 40 is grade 4, not 0.
  • The unit matches without case: potassium 7.5 in mmol/L is grade 4, not null.
  • Each row is graded with the entry of its own DAIDS subgroup and unit: DAIDS Hemoglobin, Low 60 g/L is grade 4 for adults and neonates. A term with criteria for several units needs unit_var=. Every row keeps its place.
  • CTCAE v5 and v6 INR take the worse of the absolute and the baseline cut-offs (INR 3.0 is grade 3, also with no BASE), as admiral. v4 Hemoglobin increased no longer raises; Fibrinogen, Creatinine clearance and Alkaline phosphatase follow admiral.
  • atoxgr(signif_dig=) defaults to 15, as admiral.
  • A custom criteria file needs schema_version: 2 (ordered case_when arms); a file in the old format stops with a message.
  • One reader for --DTC text (ADR-0011, alpha audit package A). Every date verb reads --DTC through fleet.core.dtc:
  • study_day, duration in days and visit_map use the date portion of a timed value (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4.4): 2021-03-20T10:30 against 2021-03-15T08:00 is day 6, not null. A pl.Datetime gives its date.
  • duration adds one day before dividing for weeks, months and years (85 days is 2.79 months, not 3.76), gives the raw difference for hours by default, and adds nothing to a negative span (-1, not 0), as admiral compute_duration. tte.aval has the same sign rule.
  • baseline_flag takes the last record strictly before the reference: a record on the reference date counts only when both times show it is earlier. Date-only records on that date are no longer baseline.
  • epoch_assign(se=) reads timed and date-only values, treats a blank SEENDTC as open and skips a partial one with a warning. On a transition date the time decides; with no time, new same_day= decides ("by_class" default: --DTC earlier element, --STDTC later), with a warning for the SDRG.
  • .sdtm.date() never guesses: a slash date or a two-digit year raises until format= names the layout; a value that is not ISO 8601 becomes null with one warning (count and values), instead of being copied into --DTC; 2021-03-15 10:30 becomes 2021-03-15T10:30. With time=, a blank time keeps the date, a partial date takes hyphens (2021-03--T08:30) and a time with no date gives -----T08:30.
  • .adam.date() to a *DTM keeps the collected hour and minute (T10:30 is 10:30:00, flag S), keeps a fraction, and drops an offset with a warning. min_date and max_date move only an imputed date whose possible range holds the bound; a complete date never moves, and a *DTM target refuses them.
  • first_date and last_date compare dates and give pl.Date (pl.Datetime for *DTM); a partial value is left out with a warning, and new impute= imputes it and writes the *DTF flag.
  • select(spec=) leaves every SDTM column and every *DTC as text; ADaM *DT and *DTM are read from text with no invented time, and a value that is not complete becomes null with a warning. DatasetChecker expects text for *DTC.
  • Every CORE finding blocks until the study accepts it (ADR-0017, alpha audit package H, part 1):
  • fleet validate, .validate() and the MCP tool no longer read an invented Severity key: every CORE finding blocks. A DM without COUNTRY now gives Status: FAIL and exit 1, not PASS. New validation.accepted in study_config.yaml lists rule, dataset and reason for a finding the study explains, as in the SDRG; an accepted finding gives Status: FINDINGS (n) and shows its reason.
  • New status NOT ASSESSED when the engine executed no rule (exit 0). Study-level findings get their own STUDY block in a sweep and are information only in a single-dataset run. The last line of fleet validate counts each status and the findings.
  • An engine crash, a missing or unreadable report, or a timeout gives COULD NOT RUN (exit 2; ValidationSetupError on the verb) instead of FAIL with ENGINE-001, ERROR-001 or TIMEOUT-001. The return code is read before the report. On timeout Fleet stops the engine and all its workers. New --timeout on fleet validate and validation.timeout in the study config (default 300 s).
  • Fleet no longer passes -rr to CORE. New fleet.validation.engine.TESTED_ENGINE_VERSIONS (0.15.0 and 1.0.0); the report header and fleet doctor name an untested CORE version. fleet install-engine still installs v0.15 by default; --version v1.0.0 installs CORE 1.0. CORE 1.0 has no ADaM rules yet: its "No rules were selected" stop reads as NOT ASSESSED. New weekly workflow core-canary.yml runs Fleet on the newest CORE release.
  • assign(ct=, ct_map=) checks the mapped values by default: raw Unknown outside the map warns with SEX, C66731 and the value, and the value stays (as SAS PUT with no OTHER=). Null and blank values are never findings; validate_values=False or ct: {validate: false} in a spec switch the check off. Generated codelist classes list every term in _terms, so a term that starts with a digit (10^9/L) or shares an attribute name is no longer reported.
  • BLQ comes from the SDTM text, and confirmed response uses every by column (ADR-0015, alpha audit package E):
  • blq_flag, blqfn, blq_impute and avalcat share one BLQ rule: a number below the LLOQ, or no number and a BLQ text in PCSTRESC (<0.1, BLQ, BQL, BLOQ, LLOQ; new blq_text=). A record with PCSTRESC BLQ and a null PCSTRESN is now BLQFL Y and imputed; before it was skipped with no message. ALQ, >1000 and a missed sample are not BLQ. New text_col="PCSTRESC" (a frame without it stops; text_col=None for numeric results only) and numeric_below_lloq=True (False lets only the text decide, as admiral).
  • avalcat gives a record with no number that is not BLQ its PCSTRESC text (>1000), or null for a missed sample, not BLQ.
  • confirmed_response_flag checks the confirmation within every by= column, not only the first: by=["STUDYID", "USUBJID"] no longer flags a subject with one PR. A null by value is a group.
  • SAS files follow SAS rules (ADR-0010, alpha audit package F):
  • XPT and SAS7BDAT read and write with the io extra alone, through the Polars route of pyreadstat; pandas and pyarrow are no longer needed. The io extra requires pyreadstat>=1.3.3.
  • save_xpt writes SAS transport version 5 with the member named as the file (FDA TCG 3.1.1). A pl.Date is stored as SAS days with DATE9 (2024-01-15 is 23390), not DATETIME seconds. NaN and infinity become SAS missing. A name over 8 characters, a label over 40 or a value over 200 bytes stops the write instead of being cut. A value that is not ASCII is written as UTF-8 with a warning. New label= and column_labels= arguments; fleet run --format xpt, fleet tdd build --format xpt and DatasetChecker.write_xpt write the define and IG labels.
  • A blank character value in an XPT or SAS7BDAT file reads as null, the SAS missing value. A variable with no value keeps its SAS type, and TIME formats read as pl.Time.
  • Every verb join on user keys matches a missing key to a missing key, as SAS MERGE BY does: derive_param keeps the group with a missing ATPT, and merge, pick, first_date, count_events and flag(criteria="exists") no longer lose such records. worst_case never keeps a null over a value.
  • A CSV column with a leading zero (SITEID 001) reads as text with a warning, types are inferred from every row, and fleet run reads define type text variables as text, so LBORRES 1.10 stays 1.10.
  • fleet compare types CSV sides across both files: SITEID 001 against 1 differs, AVAL 1.10 against 1.1 is equal, and --text keeps a column text. New blank_is_missing / --blank-is-missing reads "" as missing on both sides; the default stays exact.
  • load_raw_data(..., encoding=) reaches the SAS reader, and --encoding is on fleet compare and fleet validate, so a file from a WLATIN1 SAS session can be read. A keyword the reader does not take raises.
  • The bootstrap pins two CT packages and invents no text (ADR-0019, alpha audit package H, part 3):
  • study_config.yaml gets ct.adam_package (ADaM CT). fleet init cfg and fleet new with ADaM datasets pin adamct-2023-06-30, the latest ADaM package on or before the default SDTM package; with another --package, new --adam-package is required.
  • fleet init ct takes each codelist from the first pinned package that holds it, so DTYPE (C81224) comes from ADaM CT. Before, ADaM-only codelists were dropped with no message. A codelist that no pinned package holds stops the command with its ID, and no file is written; a 401 or a network error stops it too.
  • fleet init ct writes the terms and decodes into the codelists: entries of the define.yaml files, so fleet define-xml gives a valid CodeList. A codelist with no terms is named with the fix.
  • A codelists.py from both pins has the marker __ct_packages__; load_codelists returns a tuple of packages. Two SDTM CT dates still fail fleet check.
  • The ADaM define.yaml gets adam_ct_version, and its Define-XML lists SDTM CT and ADaM CT. ct_version now has the publishing set SDTM (SEND for SENDIG) in every define.
  • The scaffold keeps study.description and study.originator empty when none is given; one message names the empty fields, with no traceback. New --description on fleet init cfg and fleet new. IG template names (TRxxSDT, ANLzzFL) are skipped by the schema name rule.
  • The README python blocks run as written in an empty folder, with inline data, and a test runs them. The schema says that a raw input path: is relative to the study root.
  • Define-XML gaps are named, and --strict refuses (ADR-0018, alpha audit package H):
  • fleet define-xml emits a <MethodDef> per Derived variable by default. A Derived variable with no method text, a text, integer or float item with no length: and a float item with no significant_digits: are listed in one warning, as DM.SAFFL: no method text (add a comment: or a derivation: block). Before, the MethodOID was left out with no message.
  • New --strict (DefineSpecGenerator(spec, strict=True)) refuses: SpecError, exit code 1, no file.
  • New spec key significant_digits: on a variable and on a value-level entry, emitted as SignificantDigits. The schema refuses it on a type other than float, and refuses length: on date and datetime. A schema error is a SpecSchemaError that names the path.
  • fleet check runs the real generator in strict mode. Before, it ran DefineValidator, which read a retired dialect.
  • DefineXMLGenerator, DefineValidator, StudyContext.define_schema() and define_xml_2_1_schema.json are removed; use DefineSpecGenerator(spec).generate(out) and fleet check.
  • The CDISC pilot specs carry length:, significant_digits:, method text for the inline derivations and origin: Predecessor for the ADSL copies; four variables the pipeline does not make are removed from the ADaM spec.
  • TLG numbers count only what the spec states (ADR-0016, alpha audit package G):
  • adsl_filter now selects the subjects of n as well as N: an ADAE record of a subject with SAFFL N is not counted (before, a percentage could pass 100). A subject in ADSL but outside the filter is left out with an INFO note on the fleet logger; a subject not in ADSL is left out with a warning. An adsl_filter with no adsl stops. The deaths table and lb.t_abnormal follow the same rule.
  • On a table with continuous statistics, n is the count of non-missing values in the cell, as PROC MEANS N: a null value never counts, and two records of one subject count twice. Q1 and Q3 follow SAS QNTLDEF=5 (1, 2, 3, 4 gives 1.5 and 3.5).
  • worst_case stops when a value is not in the order: AEREL POSSIBLY RELATED with the default relationship_order ['N', 'Y'] raises and names the field to set, instead of losing to N. A null or blank value still ranks lowest; ties keep the record order. sdtm.ae_aerel says that its default map is Fleet's, not CDISC terminology.
  • lb.t_shift and lb.t_abnormal take the post-baseline rule from the spec prefilter, default ONTRTFL = 'Y' and not the ABLFL record. Data without these columns stops with a proposal (prefilter='pl.col("ADY") > 1') instead of counting screening records. An explicit prefilter: null survives to_yaml().
  • eg.t_qtcat gives one block per parameter and visit, with an n row; the percentage base is that n (new percent_base="adsl" selects the big N). A null or blank AVALCAT1 is not counted; two records of one subject in one block stop the table. Visits follow AVISITN and categories AVALCAT1N when present.
  • VSSummarySpec rows default to PARAMCD and AVISIT (AVISIT is required), so vst01 no longer pools every visit.
  • ADSL and OCCDS verbs follow the admiral rules they name (ADR-0012, alpha audit package B):
  • treatment_emergent follows admiral derive_var_trtemfl: an AE with no start date is Y unless it ended before TRTSDT, an AE that ended before TRTSDT is null, and a start after TRTEDT is Y only within end_window days. New required keyword end_date= (pass None when there is none) and new end_window= (required with trtedt=). Dates are read with the --DTC reader of ADR-0011.
  • pick with a top-level order keeps the extreme value over all events, as admiral derive_vars_extreme_event: order=["LSTALVDT"], mode="last" gives the latest date, not the first listed event's date. A tie goes to the first listed event; with no top-level order the first listed event with a record still wins. The result no longer depends on the sort engine's order.
  • recode types the output from the map: {"MILD": 1, "MODERATE": 2, "SEVERE": 3} gives an integer ASEVN, not text. A map that mixes text and numbers raises DerivationError.
  • The SAFFL recipes in the README, GUIDE, quickstart, installation, define-yaml and both pilot examples keep placebo subjects (EXDOSE = 0 with PLACEBO in EXTRT, the admiral template rule) and give N to non-members, as ADaMIG 1.3 requires. Both pilot examples now have SAFFL = Y for 5 of 5.
  • One flagged record per group, and units stated for QTc (ADR-0013, alpha audit package C):
  • baseline_flag takes only a record with a result: not null or blank in --STRESC (else --ORRES, or new result_col=), and --STAT not NOT DONE. A NOT DONE record on the last date no longer takes the flag. With no result column the verb stops.
  • baseline_flag flags one record on a tie: the last by new order_by= (default --SEQ), then input order, as SAS LAST., with a warning when order_by= is not given. Before, every record on the last date got the flag.
  • flag(criteria="last", where=) no longer loses the flag when a record that fails where ties on order_by; ABLFL, BASE and CHG come back. A tie among candidates goes to the last input record (first: the first). flag_all=True takes the extreme over the records that pass where.
  • qtc reads RR in ms by default, as admiral compute_qtc: QT 400 and RR 800 give QTcF 430.89, not 43.09. New rr_unit= (ms, msec, s, sec). The verb stops when a value cannot be in its unit.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• TLG summary specs are the engine contract (ADR-0005) — one seam, fleet.tlg.summarize_spec(df, spec, groupby=, adsl=), reads every engine argument from the spec; sixteen df.tlg.<domain>.t_* methods are now one call on it, and the seven composite tables (AE severity, grade and relationship, deaths, lab shift and abnormal, demographics) share prepare_frame before their own logic. Public method signatures are unchanged.
  • two template rules leave method bodies and become spec fields, visible in YAML and settable inline: uncoded (an Uncoded(columns, label) model, GDSR default "No Coding Available" on the AE, CM and MH tables; null switches it off) and prefilter (an expression string in the same form as dataset_filter, applied after it; default per template; null switches it off). Builder verbs .uncoded() and .prefilter() map onto them.
  • every column a prefilter names is a required column: lb.t_chg and eg.t_chg on a dataset without ABLFL, and ex.t_summary on a dataset without PARCAT1, now raise SchemaError instead of counting baseline or per-interval records silently. check() reports the missing column.
  • the dataset filter on lb.t_shift now bites before the worst-case reduction, as it already did on the AE tables.
  • the AE and VS spec classes moved from fleet.tlg._specs to their domain modules; fleet.tlg.AESummarySpec and friends are unchanged. prepare_frame, summarize_ard and Uncoded are new public names on fleet.tlg.

docs.title: [0.2.0a1] — pre-alpha
docs.text: First pre-alpha on PyPI. It replaces 0.1.0, which is yanked. Install with pip install --pre fleet-cdisc.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• verbs() reports where each verb comes from — a third column, origin, holds the path you type to reach the namespace that defines the verb (sdtm, adam, adam.onco) or core for the verbs every namespace shares. A therapeutic-area namespace inherits about 41 verbs; df.adam.onco.verbs().filter(pl.col("origin") == "adam.onco") lists the few it adds. Every row stays, so existing readers of the frame are unchanged (#160)
  • Admission bar for clinical verbs — ADR-0009 writes down when a verb that encodes a clinical rule earns its place: deleting it must let a programmer get a wrong answer, not only type more, and its docstring must cite the rule under References. The rule applies to new verbs only; the eight existing verbs that fail it are named in the ADR and kept. The 20 therapeutic-area verbs that pass now carry their references. Glossary terms: verb, chain verb, clinical verb, admission bar (#160)

  • mmse_category cut-offs are arguments — normal_threshold, mild_threshold and moderate_threshold default to the Tombaugh and McIntyre (1992) bands (24 to 30 normal, 19 to 23 mild, 10 to 18 moderate, 9 and below severe) instead of the unsourced 27, 18 and 10. A SAP with other bands passes its own cut-offs (#160)

  • Dataset comparison — a PROC COMPARE analogue in pure Polars (no new dependency), reachable three ways over one engine:

  • fleet.compare(base, candidate, keys=...) pairs observations on keys and variables by name, and returns a ComparisonReport with the data set, variables, observation and values summaries, the long value listing, named flags (values_differ, base_only_observations, …) and is_equal
  • .compare(base, keys=..., on_fail="warn") on every namespace (sdtm, adam, adsl, occds, …) — the chain is the candidate, the report stays on last_comparison, and on_fail speaks the same vocabulary as .validate()
  • fleet compare BASE CANDIDATE --keys K1,K2 [--all] — exit 0 equal, 1 different, 2 the comparison could not run
  • machine-readable outputs: report.to_json() / save_json(path) render one JSON document whose keys mirror the report and are additive-only within a major version; save_listing(path) writes the complete value listing as parquet; fleet compare --format json prints the document and nothing else, --out differences.parquet writes the listing
  • tolerances and trailing whitespace: abs_tol / rel_tol widen equality on the numeric variables (a pair differs when the absolute difference exceeds max(abs_tol, rel_tol × |base|), anchored on the base as in SAS), ignore_trailing_whitespace makes a legacy SAS dataset's padded character values equal Fleet's stripped ones; exact stays the default, nulls and NaN keep their rule, and the rule in effect shows on the text settings line, the HTML header and the JSON settings block. Same three options on every surface: fleet.compare(...), .compare(...) and fleet compare --abs-tol --rel-tol --ignore-trailing-whitespace
  • HTML report for a reviewer without Python: report.to_html() / save_html_report(path) render one self-contained page — raised flags as chips, then only the mismatched observations with the base and candidate values side by side, one collapsible block per differing variable, sectioned per group once the listing's group column is populated; fleet compare --report compare.html writes it
  • duplicate-key override and BY groups: allow_duplicates pairs duplicate keys by their position within each key group instead of refusing to run — counting them per side, raising duplicate_keys and warning above every report — and by prepends the BY variables to the keys, labels every difference with its group, reports the observation and values summaries per group in text, JSON and HTML, and flags the groups found on one side only while the verdict stays global. On every surface: fleet.compare(...), .compare(...) and fleet compare --by TRT01P --allow-duplicates
  • variable pairs and restriction: pairs={"WEIGHT": "WT"} compares two variables named differently on each side, on top of the automatic name matching, and names them after the base throughout the report; variables=["WEIGHT", "AVISIT"] narrows the comparison to the variables that matter, ignoring the rest on both sides so a work-in-progress candidate raises no missing-variable flag. On every surface: fleet.compare(...), .compare(...) and fleet compare --pairs WEIGHT=WT --variables WEIGHT,AVISIT
  • a compare that checks no values keeps the two-value verdict (ADR-0004): sides that share only their keys follow the observations, two empty sides are EQUAL, and the report warns in both cases; fleet compare now prints the report and exits 1 for one-sided variables instead of exiting 2, and a variables= list of keys only is refused

  • summary statistics: report.statistics gives, per differing numeric variable, the n, mean, std, min and max of the base, the candidate, their difference and its percent, over the matched observations where both sides are finite. A null, NaN or infinite value on either side is left out, so no measure is NaN and the text report, the HTML page and the JSON document show the same numbers (#112)

  • CDISC Library API integration — native client (CDISCClient) for downloading Controlled Terminology directly from the authoritative CDISC Library REST API

  • CDISCClient.get_packages() — list available CT versions (SDTM, ADaM)
  • CDISCClient.get_codelist() — download a single codelist by NCI concept ID with version pinning
  • Credentials via .env file or CDISC_API_KEY environment variable
  • CT Code Generator — CodelistGenerator converts CDISC Library JSON into typed Python constants with IDE auto-completion
  • CodelistGenerator.from_sdtm_ig() — derive codelists from the SDTM IG (source of truth), scoped to requested domains
  • CodelistGenerator.from_concept_ids() — download codelists from an explicit set of NCI concept IDs
  • Generated classes include _concept_id attribute, submission value constants, human-readable aliases (e.g. SEX = C66731), and __all__ for clean imports
  • Optional include_docs flag to inject CDISC definitions into code comments
  • fleet CLI bootstrapping pipeline and standalone commands:
  • fleet init cfg — create study_config.yaml with study metadata, IG versions, domains, and directory structure
  • fleet init define — generate define.yaml pre-populated with standard variables from the CDISC Library IG (SDTM + ADaM)
  • fleet init ct — generate codelists.py from codelist references in the define.yaml files
  • fleet init-ct — standalone bootstrap of codelists.py from the SDTM IG for given domains
  • fleet add-ct — incrementally add domains to an existing codelists.py (preserves existing codelists)
  • fleet define-xml — generate Define-XML 2.1 from a define.yaml specification (with optional HTML preview)
  • Custom Validation Rules — sponsor-specific CDISC rule authoring and validation workflow:
  • fleet add-rule — scaffold a schema-valid rule YAML skeleton (auto-increments ID, uniqueness check across directory)
  • fleet check-rule — validate a rule file (YAML syntax + structure + JSON Schema); exits 1 on error for CI gates
  • custom_rules= parameter on .validate(), ValidationService.validate_sdtm(), and .validate_adam() — load a directory of rules via the engine's -lr flag
  • validation.custom_rules in study_config.yaml — team-wide default rules directory
  • fleet init cfg scaffolds the custom_rules/ directory and field automatically

  • Header comments in generated rule files include CDISC operator reference link and rule type guide

  • CT assignment now accepts codelist classes (today: assign(ct=...)) — pass a generated class (e.g. SEX) instead of a raw NCI string; ct_map is optional when raw data already matches CDISC submission values

  • Spec-driven CT checks use the study's codelists.py — inside a study, from_spec resolves a ct_codelist: ID to the class of that ID in the generated codelists.py, so algorithm: assign_ct gives the same "values not in codelist" warning as .assign(..., ct=<class>); before, the spec copied values unvalidated unless a CT file was loaded (#131)

  • stale detection: codelists.py gets a __ct_package__ marker; a file from another package than ct.package, mixing packages, missing a referenced codelist, or missing warns once in from_spec, fails fleet check and shows in fleet doctor; fleet add-ct --package refuses another package

  • Admiral-parity expansion — new core computations and record-generating verbs:

  • utils.py: bsa() (Body Surface Area, 4 methods), mean_arterial_pressure(), qtc() (Fridericia/Bazett), age_in_years() (unit-aware), extreme_flag() (min/max per group)
  • df.adam: .bsa(), .map(), .qtc() — namespace wrappers for the new computations
  • df.adam: .derive_summary_records() — aggregate by group and append summary rows (mean, sum, min, max, median, count)
  • df.adam: .derive_locf_records() — forward-fill (LOCF) within patient groups
  • df.adam: .derive_param() — pivot source parameters, compute a new AVAL, and append as new records (e.g. BMI from HEIGHT+WEIGHT)
  • df.adam.adsl: .age_years() — unit-aware age conversion (YEARS, MONTHS, WEEKS, DAYS)
  • df.adam.adsl: .derive_period() — create standard Subperiod/Phase variables (APxxSDT, APxxEDT, TRTxxP)
  • Spec-driven support: bsa, map, qtc are available as algorithm values in define.yaml
  • StudyContext.init() — scaffolds a new study workspace (folder tree, study_config.yaml) with full IG/CT/domain configuration; raises StudyConfigError if already initialised
  • DefineScaffolder — queries CDISC Library IG to generate define.yaml pre-populated with standard variables, types, labels, mandatory flags, and codelist references
  • Evolved StudyConfig model with SDTMConfig, ADAMConfig, CTConfig sub-models for IG versions, domains, and CT package
  • MkDocs documentation site with Material theme
  • mike versioned deployment to GitHub Pages
  • Pre-executed example notebook: ADSL pipeline (CDISCPILOT01)
  • llms.txt for LLM-friendly documentation

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Polars stays below 2.0: the requirement is now polars>=1.41,<2. Polars 2.0 runs lazy queries on the streaming engine by default, which does not keep the row order of joins, and it removes the cast from a string to a date. Fleet moves to Polars 2.0 after its tests pass on it.
  • Python 3.12 to 3.14, httpx below 1.0: the requirements are now requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15" and httpx>=0.27,<1. On Python 3.15, Polars 1.x Series methods return None, so import fleet now stops there with an ImportError that gives a working command. httpx 1.0 pre-releases change the Client constructor, and a --pre install picked them up, so fleet install-engine and the CDISC Library commands stopped with a TypeError.
  • Spec parameter facts are checked against the verb signature (ADR-0007, #179 phase 1) — the parity test now compares every Param of a spec algorithm with inspect.signature() of its verb: the spec may be stricter than the verb, never looser. The ten spec-only defaults are gone, so a define.yaml must state aval, low and high for nrind, the three dates for on_treatment, term_var for atoxgr, on for merge and lookup, and agg for group_by; ct_codelist is required on assign_ct and hardcode_ct, as the define.yaml concept doc already stated. A missing key is a load-time error

  • One validation HTML page: fleet validate --report and ValidationResult.save_html_report() write the same page (fleet.validation.models.write_html_report()): a status row per dataset, then one row per finding. Every cell is HTML-escaped, so a < in a data value or a custom rule message no longer breaks the page or injects markup; rows_affected=0 is shown (#119)

  • API simplification: therapeutic-area namespaces (onco, ophtha, peds, vaccine, metabolic, neuro) and ADaM sub-structures (adsl, occds) are now accessed via df.adam.<name> instead of df.<name> — reduces registered namespaces from 10 to 2 (df.sdtm and df.adam)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Define-XML FormalExpression names the method the run records: the verb the algorithm dispatches to, by the class that defines it on the define's own namespace, as VariableNode.method does (the fleet lsp hover names the defining class too). ADaM defines named SDTMNamespace and rendered calls that do not exist, such as study_day('ADY', end=..., start=...); ADY now reads fleet.core._verb_mixin.SharedVerbsMixin.duration('ADY', end='ASTDT', start='TRTSDT') (#93)

docs.title: Fleet Validation Strategy
docs.text: Package: fleet-cdisc (import name: fleet)  |  Specification version: 1.0  |  Date: 2026-03-30

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: Fleet is a Python library that generates CDISC SDTM and ADaM datasets for clinical statistical programming. It is built entirely on Polars through a namespace extension API, and is designed to run inside a sponsor's existing validated Python infrastructure. This document defines Fleet's validation strategy using the risk-based framework established by the R Validation Hub and the software-agnostic regulatory context articulated by the FDA. The strategy is structured around four complementary pillars: standards traceability through the CDISC Library API, cross-language benchmark parity against {admiral}, regulatory-grade validation via the official CDISC Rules Engine (CORE), and automated unit testing with static analysis.

docs.title: 2.1 FDA Position on Statistical Software
docs.text:
The FDA's 2015 Statistical Software Clarifying Statement[^1] explicitly states that the agency does not require nor endorse any specific software for analyzing data from clinical investigations. Sponsors are responsible for ensuring that any software used produces accurate results and for maintaining adequate documentation of that accuracy. This places the validation obligation on the sponsor's qualified infrastructure — of which Fleet is one component — rather than on the software vendor alone.

Implication for Fleet

Fleet does not need to be independently validated by a regulatory body. Sponsors qualify Fleet by demonstrating it produces accurate, traceable, and reproducible CDISC-compliant outputs within their own validated environment.

docs.title: 2.2 R Validation Hub Framework
docs.text:
The R Validation Hub white paper[^2] — co-authored by representatives from AstraZeneca, GSK, Roche/Genentech, Amgen, and other sponsors — establishes a risk-based approach for assessing package accuracy within validated infrastructure. Although written for R, the framework is language-agnostic and is increasingly applied to Python packages used in regulatory submissions. The framework classifies packages into three risk tiers based on:

Risk Factor Description Intended use How directly the package generates submission-ready outputs Consequence of inaccuracy Patient safety risk and regulatory impact if results are wrong Testability Availability of unit tests, cross-validation tools, and independent benchmarks

Fleet addresses all three dimensions, as documented in the qualification summary in §5.

docs.title: Pillar 1 — CDISC Library Traceability
docs.text:
Fleet's fleet init define and fleet init ct CLI commands query the CDISC Library REST API[^3] directly to bootstrap study specifications and controlled terminology. Variable metadata (labels, types, core designations, permitted terms) is sourced from the authoritative CDISC machine-readable IG model — not hard-coded. The resulting define.yaml and codelists.py are committed artefacts that provide full lineage from source variable to CDISC standard.

# Step 1: Pull domain variable metadata from the CDISC Library IG for SDTM 3.4
uv run fleet init define

# Step 2: Generate codelists.py from NCI concept IDs in define.yaml
uv run fleet init ct

This produces codelist classes — for example SEX (C66731), RACE (C74457) — that are used in pipeline code by class name, never raw string ID:

from examples.cdiscpilot01.sdtm.codelists import SEX, RACE

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=SEX)
    .assign("RACE", source="race", ct=RACE)
    .to_frame()
)

Traceability chain: CDISC Library API → define.yaml → codelists.py → pipeline code → output dataset

Each link is a versioned, reviewable artefact stored alongside the study specification.

docs.title: Pillar 2 — Cross-Language Benchmark: {admiral} Parity
docs.text:
{admiral}[^4] is the Roche/Atorus R package for ADaM derivations; it is the de-facto gold standard in R-based clinical programming and is documented in multiple regulatory submissions. Fleet's test suite contains tests/unit/test_admiral_parity.py — 400+ lines of tests that benchmark Fleet's Python outputs against documented {admiral} algorithm specifications.

Coverage as of v0.1.0:

Test class Algorithms verified TestBSA Dubois-DuBois, Mosteller, Haycock, Gehan-George (4 methods) TestMeanArterialPressure Standard MAP formula TestQTc Bazett, Fridericia (2 methods) TestAgeInYears Day-accurate age in years, months, weeks TestDeriveSummaryRecords Mean aggregation by parameter group (BDS record generation) TestDeriveLOCFRecords Last-observation-carried-forward imputation TestDeriveParam BMI derivation from height/weight TestADSLAgeYears Age derivations on ADSL frame TestADSLDerivePeriod Exposure period flags TestANL01FLAdmiralParity restrict_derivation + derive_var_extreme_flag (last-valid-row ANL01FL pattern)

No R runtime is required. The parity tests work in two ways:

  • Formula transcription — mathematical formulas (BSA, QTc, MAP, age conversion) are transcribed directly from {admiral}'s published R source code. The tests then assert that Fleet's Polars implementation produces numerically identical results for the same inputs, using analytically-derived expected values computed in pure Python from the same formula.
  • Behavioural specification — for higher-level patterns such as ANL01FL flagging, the expected output rows and flag values are transcribed verbatim from {admiral}'s documented examples (the test comments quote the equivalent R code). Fleet's Python implementation is then verified to reproduce that exact output.

This approach means the validation does not depend on an R installation, a specific R version, or rpy2. The published {admiral} specification is the invariant; Fleet's implementation is validated against it.

# Example: ANL01FL last-valid-row parity test
# tests/unit/test_admiral_parity.py — TestANL01FLAdmiralParity
#
# Equivalent admiral R pattern (quoted in test docstring):
#   restrict_derivation(advs, derivation = derive_var_extreme_flag,
#     args = params(by_vars = exprs(USUBJID, PARAMCD),
#                   order = exprs(ADT), new_var = ANL01FL, mode = "last"),
#     filter = !is.na(AVAL))

result = bds_frame.adam.flag(
    "ANL01FL",
    criteria="last",
    order_by="ADT",
    by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
    where='~pl.col("AVAL").is_null()',
).to_frame()
# Only the last non-null-AVAL record per group receives "Y"; all others are null
assert result["ANL01FL"].to_list() == [None, "Y", None, "Y", None, "Y"]

docs.title: Pillar 3 — Official CDISC Rules Engine (CORE)
docs.text: Fleet integrates the official CDISC Rules Engine (CORE)[^5] — the open-source validation binary published by CDISC and used by FDA as the reference conformance checker for SDTM and SEND submissions. (ADaM standard/version selection is supported by the engine, but CDISC has not yet published an executable ADaMIG rule set — ADaM validation today runs custom rules; see Validation with CORE.) Fleet manages the engine lifecycle through its own CLI and wraps it via a Python API.

docs.title: Installation and health check
docs.text:
# Download the managed engine binary for the current platform
# (CORE 0.15.0, the version Fleet is tested with)
uv run fleet install-engine

# Verify engine and supporting dependencies
uv run fleet doctor

fleet doctor outputs a structured status report covering: engine binary presence, engine version, pyreadstat availability for XPT serialisation, and environment variable overrides.

docs.title: Python validation API
docs.text:
from fleet import ValidationService

svc = ValidationService()

# Validate an SDTM domain against SDTMIG 3.4
dm_result = svc.validate_sdtm(dm, domain="DM", version="3.4")
dm_result.print_report()  # console: pass/warn/fail by rule
dm_result.save_html_report("outputs/dm_validation.html")  # archivable HTML

# Validate an ADaM dataset against ADaMIG 1.3
adsl_result = svc.validate_adam(adsl, dataset="ADSL", version="1.3")
assert adsl_result.is_valid

The ValidationResult object exposes .is_valid (bool), .print_report(report_type="summary") (or "full" for expanded details including INFO-level engine noise), and .save_html_report(path) — an HTML page with the dataset status and one table row per error, warning and info finding, suitable for archiving as a validation deliverable. Every cell is HTML-escaped, because messages carry data values and the text of custom rules. fleet validate --report writes the same page for a sweep.

docs.title: Engine discovery order
docs.text:
Fleet resolves the engine path at runtime via a four-tier chain (first match wins):

  1. validation.engine_path in study_config.yaml (committable to VCS for team reuse)
  2. FLEET_RULES_ENGINE environment variable (.env at project root)
  3. Managed install under ~/.fleet/cdisc-rules-engine/core/
  4. Legacy ../cdisc-rules-engine/core.py (development fallback)

The study config comes first, so a stale environment variable on one machine cannot replace the engine the team pinned. An explicit rules_engine_path= on .validate() beats all four.

docs.title: Pillar 4 — Automated Test Suite and Static Analysis
docs.text:
Fleet maintains a comprehensive automated test suite executed on every change:

uv run pytest                  # unit + integration tests
uv run ruff check              # style and lint (PEP 8, import ordering, type hints)
uv run ruff format --check     # formatting consistency

In addition, all five example scripts in examples/ are treated as integration smoke tests and must execute without error after every feature change:

uv run python examples/full_pipeline_example.py
uv run python examples/cdiscpilot01_inline.py
uv run python examples/cdiscpilot01_spec_driven.py
uv run python examples/adnca_example.py
uv run python examples/tdd_example.py

These scripts exercise the complete derivation pipeline end-to-end — from raw CSV ingestion through SDTM and ADaM derivation to final export — against the CDISCPILOT01 reference study.

docs.title: Pillar 5 — Local Rule Snapshot (fleet init rules)
docs.text:
Fleet's fleet init rules command caches the exact CDISC conformance rules for the IG versions declared in the study's define.yaml files. Rules are fetched from the CDISC Library API, grouped by domain, and written as human-readable YAML into metadata/sdtm/rules/ and metadata/adam/rules/.

# After fleet init define has created define.yaml files:
uv run fleet init rules

Each YAML file records the rule's CORE ID, description, check logic, scope, severity, and regulatory citations. When committed to VCS, these files provide:

  • Version lock: The exact rule definitions in effect when the study was validated, immune to upstream CDISC updates.
  • Audit trail: Reviewers (including regulators) can inspect which rules were applied without re-querying the CDISC Library.
  • Diff visibility: Any change in the rule set between study milestones is visible in version control history.

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
When the standard CDISC CORE rule set does not cover a study-specific requirement, sponsors can author custom rules in the same YAML schema used by the engine.

Fleet provides first-class support for custom rules through:

  • validation.custom_rules in study_config.yaml — sets a team-wide default directory
  • fleet add-rule — scaffolds a schema-valid YAML skeleton with a # TODO Check: block
  • fleet check-rule — validates a rule file (YAML syntax, structure, full JSON Schema)
  • custom_rules= parameter on .validate() — loads rules per-pipeline
# Scaffold a new rule (auto-increments ID)
uv run fleet add-rule --domain AE --description "AESEV required when AESER = Y"

# Validate the rule file before running against datasets
uv run fleet check-rule metadata/custom_rules/FLEET-AE-001.yaml

# Use in pipeline
# .validate("AE", custom_rules="metadata/custom_rules")

Use a company prefix (e.g. ACME-AE-001) to avoid collisions with CORE-XXXXXX.

docs.title: 4. Risk Assessment
docs.text:
Applying the R Validation Hub risk-based framework to Fleet:

Dimension Fleet's profile Risk Intended use Generates submission-ready SDTM/ADaM datasets included in regulatory packages High intended-use criticality Consequence of inaccuracy Incorrect derivations could affect safety/efficacy conclusions; however, CORE validation provides an independent runtime check before submission Mitigated by Pillar 3 Testability 400+ admiral parity tests; CDISC Library traceability; CORE conformance checking; smoke test examples; ruff static analysis High testability → lowers residual risk Open source provenance Public GitHub repository; MIT license; full source inspectable by sponsor QA Transparent Dependency surface Polars ≥ 1.0, Pydantic ≥ 2.0, PyYAML, httpx, lxml; all actively maintained, no high-CVE dependencies (check at installation) Low-medium

Overall risk classification: Medium (high criticality, but substantially mitigated by the four pillars above). This places Fleet in the same tier as {admiral}, tern, and other commonly qualified open-source clinical packages.

docs.title: 5. Qualification Summary
docs.text: Validation activity Primary artefact Scope Status Standards metadata sourcing fleet init define → define.yaml SDTM IG + ADaM IG variable metadata from CDISC Library Automated at study setup Controlled terminology generation fleet init ct → codelists.py NCI concept IDs for all study domains Automated at study setup Conformance rule snapshot fleet init rules → metadata/*/rules/*.yaml All CDISC CORE rules for IG version, version-locked Automated at study setup Custom rule scaffolding fleet add-rule → metadata/custom_rules/ Sponsor SOP / TCG gap rules, schema-validated On demand Custom rule schema check fleet check-rule <file> YAML syntax + structure + JSON Schema validation On demand / CI gate Cross-language algorithm benchmark tests/unit/test_admiral_parity.py BSA, MAP, QTc, LOCF, BMI, ANL01FL, age/period Runs in CI on every commit SDTM conformance ValidationService.validate_sdtm() All SDTM domains, SDTMIG 3.4 Run at study delivery ADaM conformance ValidationService.validate_adam() ADSL, BDS, OCCDS datasets, ADaMIG 1.3 Run at study delivery Unit and integration tests pytest (400+ tests across 20 test modules) Namespace verbs, CT validation, Define-XML, TDD workflows Runs in CI on every commit Static analysis ruff check + ruff format Full source tree Runs in CI on every commit End-to-end smoke tests examples/*.py (5 scripts, CDISCPILOT01 study) Full SDTM + ADaM pipelines Runs in CI on every commit Validation HTML report ValidationResult.save_html_report() Per-domain, per-delivery, archivable Generated at study delivery

docs.title: 6. References
docs.text:
[^1]: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2015). Statistical Software Clarifying Statement. Office of Translational Sciences, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. Available from: https://www.fda.gov/media/161196/download

[^2]: R Validation Hub (2020). A Risk-based Approach for Assessing R Package Accuracy within a Validated Infrastructure. pharmaR Working Group. Available from: https://www.pharmar.org/white-paper/

[^3]: CDISC (2024). CDISC Library API. Available from: https://library.cdisc.org/api

[^4]: Atorus Research & Roche (2021–present). {admiral}: ADaM in R Asset Library. CRAN. Available from: https://cran.r-project.org/package=admiral

[^5]: CDISC (2022–present). CDISC Rules Engine (CORE). Open-source reference implementation for CDISC conformance checking. Available from: https://github.com/cdisc-org/cdisc-rules-engine

docs.title: Why Fleet?
docs.text:
Fleet is designed to bridge the gap between modern, high-performance data engineering and the specialized business logic of clinical statistical programming (SDTM and ADaM).

While traditional tools (like SAS or SQL) or general-purpose Python libraries (like Pandas or plain Polars) are capable of building clinical datasets, they often require writing hundreds of lines of boilerplate code to handle common CDISC requirements: merging controlled terminology, calculating study days, deriving baselines, and maintaining traceability.

Fleet solves this by extending Polars with chainable, domain-specific verbs.

The organising principle is workflow quality: one obvious path from raw data to submission artefact. Everything below — including how well Fleet works with AI coding assistants — falls out of that.

docs.title: 1. Simplicity: Intent-Driven Syntax
docs.text:
With Fleet, your code reads like a specification. Instead of writing complex join logic and conditional expressions, you use verbs that exactly match CDISC concepts.

Without Fleet (Manual Polars):

import polars as pl

# Deriving a baseline value requires multiple steps and intermediate variables
# 1. Filter to baseline records
baseline_df = adbd.filter(pl.col("ABLFL") == "Y").select(["USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVAL"])
baseline_df = baseline_df.rename({"AVAL": "BASE"})

# 2. Join back to the main dataset
adbd = adbd.join(baseline_df, on=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"], how="left")

# 3. Calculate change from baseline
adbd = adbd.with_columns((pl.col("AVAL") - pl.col("BASE")).alias("CHG"))

With Fleet:

import fleet

# Intent is immediately clear in a single chain
adbd = (
    adbd.adam.baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 2. Power: High Performance Lazy Evaluation
docs.text:
Fleet doesn't just wrap Polars; it deeply integrates with its lazy evaluation engine. When you chain Fleet verbs (e.g., .assign(), .study_day()), most accumulate business logic into a single optimized set of Polars expressions rather than computing immediately.

When you call .to_frame(), Polars executes the pipeline in one pass, leveraging multithreading and query optimization. A few window/cross-domain verbs (baseline, pinned study_day) checkpoint internally — but they re-wrap the collected frame and keep the chain going, so flag → baseline → chg stays a single pipeline. The namespaces are also registered on pl.LazyFrame, so pl.scan_parquet(...).sdtm keeps the whole pipeline lazy with predicate pushdown.

  • No intermediate DataFrames: Saves memory.
  • Blazing fast: Processes millions of records in milliseconds.
  • Zero overhead: Fleet verbs compile down to native Polars pl.Expr objects.

docs.title: 3. Clarity: Specification-Driven Development
docs.text:
Fleet natively understands the define.yaml specification. You can define your metadata, controlled terminology, and derivation rules in a single, human-readable file.

Fleet can read this YAML to automatically apply derivations, validate data, and generate CDISC-compliant define.xml exports, ensuring your documentation and your code are never out of sync. A spec entry and an inline call are the same step written two ways — algorithm: chg with aval: AVAL and base: BASE is .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE") — so you can be fully code-driven, fully spec-driven, or a hybrid, and move a step between the two without re-deriving it.

docs.title: 4. Flexibility: Built for Extension
docs.text:
Fleet comes with built-in namespaces for core SDTM (df.sdtm), ADaM BDS (df.adam), ADSL (df.adam.adsl), OCCDS (df.adam.occds), and specialized therapeutic areas (Oncology, Ophthalmology, Vaccines, etc.). Fleet also includes verbs for Body Surface Area (bsa), Mean Arterial Pressure (map), corrected QT (qtc), LOCF imputation, summary record derivation, and parameter-level record generation.

If you have proprietary study requirements, Fleet is designed to be easily extended with custom verbs using standard Polars expressions via the .derivation() method, or by subclassing the namespaces to add your own company-specific logic.

docs.title: 5. Predictability: AI-Native by Consequence
docs.text:
Workflow quality is a promise to human reviewers first. For the same reasons, it is why Fleet works well with AI coding agents.

Coding assistants fail in the same places human newcomers fail. Point one at a codebase with a weak, ambiguous workflow — three ways to derive a baseline, macro names that don't say what they compute, errors that surface three steps later — and it produces plausible code with the wrong derivation. Point the same model at a codebase where the workflow is unambiguous and the search space collapses: the structure itself guides the agent toward the expected outcome, which is what actually raises the probability of a correct first pass.

So Fleet is AI-native by consequence, not by bolt-on. Every property below started as a workflow decision:

  • Standardised Foundation: Built entirely on Python and Polars, two of the most widely represented tools in LLM training data — chosen because they are the ones your team already reads, not to please a model.
  • Unified Package: No need to juggle 10 different sub-packages. One import (import fleet) means there is one place to look, for a person and for an agent.
  • Clear Intent-Driven API: Because derivations are simple verbs (.study_day(), .baseline()), there is usually exactly one right way to express a step. That is what removes the guesswork — and with it, the hallucinations.
  • Tight Feedback Loops: The define.yaml structure is validated through bundled JSON schemas, and CDISC core data validations output structured error arrays. Fast, specific, machine-readable failures let a programmer or an agent course-correct immediately instead of compounding a wrong assumption.
  • Readable Specs: The declarative, YAML-based approach reflects clinical data specification standards, so the artefact a reviewer signs off on and the artefact a model reads are the same file.
  • Built-in llms.txt: Fleet ships structured context (llms.txt, JSON schemas, an MCP server, a define.yaml language server) so the workflow is legible to tooling, not just to people.

docs.title: 6. Native CDISC Library Integration
docs.text:
Fleet is the first open-source clinical toolkit with built-in CDISC Library API support. Instead of manually downloading PDF terminology files or maintaining hand-curated codelist dictionaries, Fleet connects directly to the authoritative source.

# Full bootstrapping pipeline: config → define.yaml → codelists.py
fleet init cfg --study-id STUDY01 --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS
fleet init define
fleet init ct

# Or standalone: bootstrap codelists directly from the SDTM IG
fleet add-ct --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --output codelists.py
  • Source of truth is the CDISC Library IG — Fleet queries the Implementation Guide model to discover every variable and codelist for your domains. No manual curation, no guessing concept IDs.
  • IDE auto-completion for CT values — the generated codelists.py gives you typed constants (SEX.M, RACE.WHITE) with full definitions as code comments. Your IDE autocompletes both the codelist name and every permitted submission value.
  • Incremental domain expansion — start with DM and AE, then fleet add-ct --domains LB,CM later. Existing codelists are preserved; only new ones are added.
  • Version-pinned reproducibility — pin your CT package version (e.g. --package sdtmct-2025-09-26) so every team member and CI run generates identical constants.
from codelists import SEX, RACE

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=SEX)
    .assign("RACE", source="race", ct=RACE)
    .to_frame()
)

No NCI codes to memorise. No CSV lookups at runtime. Just import the codelist and use it — the _concept_id is carried through for Define-XML generation and P21 validation automatically.

docs.title: Protocol adapters consume a narrow introspection surface, not the registries
docs.text:
The language server reached directly into fleet.core.spec_registry, fleet.core.algorithm_resolver, fleet.define_xml.schema_builder and fleet._version — four private-ish import paths with no contract. Once the VS Code client ships from its own repository on its own cadence, those imports become an accidental public API that no test guards and no version promise covers.

So fleet.introspect is the single contract: algorithms, get_algorithm, suggest_algorithm, algorithm_doc, define_schema, returning purpose-built frozen dataclasses (AlgorithmInfo, ParamInfo, AlgorithmDoc) rather than SpecAlgorithm itself, whose dispatch callable, overwrite_guard and define_template are execution internals that must stay free to change.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Additive-only within a major version, tracked by fleet.__version__ alone — no separate surface version. Names, return fields and algorithms may be added; nothing is removed or renamed except on a major. A client therefore declares a minimum Fleet version and never a maximum.
  • The LSP handshake carries the same promise. initialize announces serverInfo of {"name": "fleet-lsp", "version": fleet.__version__}, and a shipped client reads it to enforce that minimum, so it is part of the surface rather than an incidental argument to LanguageServer(...). Pinned by a test alongside the import sweep.
  • The DTOs duplicate part of the registry's shape. That duplication is the price of letting spec_registry be refactored without breaking a shipped extension.
  • An AST sweep in tests/unit/test_introspect.py fails when lsp_server.py imports anything from fleet outside the surface, using the grandfathered-allowlist pattern already established by tests/unit/test_api_conventions.py.
  • mcp_server.py got a weaker boundary, deliberately (#68). It ships inside Fleet and versions with it, so it needs no frozen DTOs and no additive-only promise — nothing external imports it. What it does need is the right dependency direction: it may use Fleet's public packages (fleet, fleet.tlg, fleet.validation, …) and may not import fleet.cli or any private name. tests/unit/test_mcp_boundary.py enforces exactly that.

docs.title: The comparison engine is Fleet's own, written in pure Polars
docs.text: Fleet needs a PROC COMPARE equivalent: pair two datasets on keys, report common and missing variables and observations, list every differing value with tolerances, and give a pass or fail. Polars itself only offers DataFrame.equals and the unit-test assert in polars.testing, and upstream issue pola-rs/polars#14373 has been accepted but unimplemented since February 2024. We decided to write the engine ourselves as Polars expressions in a dedicated comparison package, with the CLI verb, the top-level fleet.compare function and the namespace verb as thin callers over it, and to take no new runtime dependency.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• datacompy (Capital One) accepts Polars input but hard-requires pandas and numpy, runs its numeric comparison through np.isclose, and pins polars below the current release. Adopting it would put pandas back into Fleet's core dependency set and tie our polars upgrades to theirs.
  • diffly (QuantCo) is pure Polars and actively maintained, but it requires a primary key, has no BY groups, no variable pairing and no pass/fail code in the SAS sense, and brings rich with it. The SAS-shaped layer we need is most of the work, so wrapping it saves little and leaves a small third-party package on the QC-critical path that Fleet's qualification strategy would then have to cover.
  • Contributing upstream to Polars is the right long-term home, but two and a half years of open API debate rule it out of Fleet's critical path.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The comparison engine is qualified as Fleet code, with its own SAS-parity fixtures, rather than as an inherited dependency.
  • Fleet keeps its promise of a pure-Polars core: pandas and numpy stay confined to the optional io extra. Amended by ADR-0010: the io extra now reads and writes SAS files through the Polars route of pyreadstat, with no pandas.
  • If Polars ships a native compare later, fleet.compare can delegate to it behind the same three surfaces without changing the comparison report.

docs.title: One run setup for every validation surface
docs.text: The verb .validate(), fleet validate, the MCP tool fleet_validate and the fleet check gate each resolved the standard, the IG version, the custom rules and the engine in their own way, so one study gave different rules on different surfaces. We decided that one module in fleet.validation builds a run setup, a fixed record of every input of a validation with the source of each, and that every surface validates from it and resolves nothing itself.

docs.title: Decisions a reader would not expect
docs.text:
• The study config beats FLEET_RULES_ENGINE inside a study. The usual order lets the environment override a config file. We reversed it because a team lead pins validation.engine_path so that every programmer runs the same rule build; a stale environment variable on one machine would silently give different QC findings. The environment variable still applies outside a study, and every report prints the engine path and version it used.
  • Official and custom rules run in two engine runs. CORE 0.15.0 treats -lr as a replacement for its rule set, not an addition: one AE file ran 430 official rules without -lr and 2 local rules with it. One run would drop every CDISC rule as soon as a study sets validation.custom_rules. The two results join into one report and each finding names its source.
  • A sweep is one engine run per standard, because the engine takes one standard per run. SDTM and ADaM results still join into one report and one exit code.
  • The IG version list is fixed in Fleet, not read from core list-rule-sets, so that fleet check gives the same answer in CI, where no engine is installed, as on a programmer's machine.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep resolution on each surface and share helpers. Rejected: the drift came from four call sites choosing which helpers to call, and helpers do not stop a fifth surface from skipping one.
  • Let the environment variable win, as today. Rejected for the reason above.
  • Keep the engine's -lr behaviour and warn that official rules did not run. Rejected: one line in a long report is easy to miss at delivery.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A study with custom rules takes about twice as long to validate.
  • A new CORE release that adds an IG version needs a Fleet release before Fleet accepts it.
  • A setup problem (unclear standard, unsupported IG version) is its own outcome, "could not run": exit 2 on the CLI, an exception on the verb, and an outcome field on the MCP tool.

docs.title: A compare that checks no values keeps the two-value verdict and warns
docs.text: When the two sides share only their keys, or both have no observations, a compare checks no values. Before this decision, fleet.compare and the .compare() verb returned a verdict, but fleet compare exited 2 ("could not run"), because the CLI held its own check. ADR-0002 makes the CLI, the function and the verb thin callers over one engine, so we decided that the engine alone gives the verdict and the callers only translate it. The verdict keeps its two values, EQUAL and NOT EQUAL. A key-only compare follows the observations: the same key values on both sides are EQUAL, and a one-sided key or variable is NOT EQUAL. Two empty sides are EQUAL. In both cases the report warns that no values were checked. The warning does not change the verdict and does not trigger on_fail. A variables= restriction that names only keys is an argument mistake, so the engine refuses it with ComparisonError.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Raise ComparisonError whenever nothing is compared. This breaks a subject-list check (USUBJID only on both sides), and it hides the variables summary that shows why nothing matched. PROC COMPARE lists the common and the one-sided variables in this case, and does not stop.
  • A third verdict, NOT COMPARABLE. Every caller, on_fail, the JSON consumers and the VS Code extension would need to learn a third state, and is_equal would no longer answer the whole question.
  • A new flag, for example no_observations. An empty domain early in a study (ADAE with no AEs yet) would fail on every rerun. Programmers would learn to ignore the flag, and that hides the real flags next to it.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• fleet compare now exits 1, and prints the full report, when the sides share only keys but carry other variables. Before, it exited 2 with a message on stderr only.
  • A script that checks only the verdict or the exit code passes a key-only or an empty compare. The warning is the only signal, so a QC reviewer reads it.

docs.title: Summary specs are the engine contract
docs.text: Every summary table in fleet.tlg goes through one engine, summarize_ard, and before this decision 21 namespace methods restated its contract by forwarding 13 to 16 keyword arguments each, in 8 different shapes, with two template rules hidden in method bodies: the fill of uncoded terms and the exclusion of the baseline record. We decided that the summary spec is the engine contract. A seam function, summarize_spec(df, spec, *, groupby, adsl), resolves the group column, validates the frame, prepares it from the spec, and calls the engine from the spec's fields. The two hidden rules become spec fields, uncoded and prefilter, with a default per template, visible in the YAML and settable through the builder. The cards context string and the nested flag are class attributes of the spec class, not YAML fields, because one spec class serves exactly one template method.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Route every method through the seam, composites included. Seven methods do real work between the filter and the engine: the deaths table calls the engine twice on different populations, the shift table builds its own worst-case frame, the demographics table adds a continuous block, and the AE severity, grade and relationship tables reduce to the worst record per subject before counting. Pushing that logic into a spec hides an algorithm in data. These seven keep the keyword engine and share only the preparation step.
  • Keep the uncoded fill and the baseline guard as template facts in code. An SAP can specify the uncoded label and whether baseline is excluded. A spec that cannot say so is not a spec of the table.
  • Typed switches instead of a prefilter expression. exclude_baseline: true reads well, but every new template would add a boolean to the shared base, and a QC programmer still could not see the exact rule. The expression uses the same whitelisted parser as dataset_filter and the SDTM specs.
  • Concentrate every spec class in the shared specs module. The review's deletion test pointed there. With the domain modules kept as the typed public surface, a domain's spec next to its three-line method is the smaller file to open, so the shared module keeps only the base classes and the building blocks.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Every column a prefilter names is a required column of the template. A change-from-baseline table on an ADLB or ADEG without ABLFL, and an exposure table on an ADEX without PARCAT1, now refuse to run. Before, the guard was skipped without a message and baseline or per-period records were counted. prefilter: null in the spec is the visible escape hatch.
  • The order of the preparation step is fixed: uncoded fill, then dataset filter, then prefilter. A dataset filter may therefore reference the uncoded label.
  • A composite applies the dataset filter before its own reduction. On the lab shift table the filter used to run after the worst-case reduction, so a filtered-out record could decide a subject's worst range indicator; it no longer can.
  • Every column a prefilter names is required through prefilter_columns(), read from the expression at validation time, not through the static required_columns list. Setting prefilter=None lifts the requirement with the rule.
  • A user-registered template keeps its signature, fn(df, *, adsl, spec, groupby), and may call the seam or the engine.

docs.title: A study run carries only derivation-free columns from its inputs, and pins every input
docs.text: fleet run left-joined every column a dataset declares from its extra inputs on USUBJID, and pinned nothing, so a define that uses merge, lookup, first_date, last_date or count_events ran from Python and failed from the CLI (#86). We decided that a study run pins every input under its dataset name, and that the implicit join brings only the carry-through columns: the declared variables that have no derivation. A variable with a derivation comes from its algorithm alone.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep the join of every declared column, and pin as well. Rejected: a variable declared with lookup from ADSL would arrive twice, and the overwrite guard in from_spec would stop the run on the second arrival.
  • No implicit join, pins only. Rejected: every carried column would need a derivation line. The pilot study alone has 41 such columns across ADVS, ADAE and ADEX, and the Define-XML would gain 41 methods that say "copied".

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• "No derivation" has one meaning in a define: carried from an input, unchanged. The glossary entry is "carry-through column".
  • A define that declares a column with no derivation and expects Python code to compute it later gets the input's value instead. The column must be left out of the define or given a derivation.
  • The join on USUBJID runs only when a step has carry-through columns to bring, so a step with none needs no USUBJID.

docs.title: Spec parameter facts come from the verb signature, and the spec may be stricter than the verb but never looser
docs.text:
Status: superseded by ADR-0008 on 2026-10-16. The verb is the algorithm, so the Param tables and the five rules below go with the implementation of ADR-0008. The consequence that survives: the spec is never looser than the verb, and a define.yaml names its inputs.

Every spec algorithm in fleet.core.spec_registry restated its verb's parameters in a hand-written Param table: the name, the type, the default, and whether the field is required. The parity test checked that the algorithm names and the JSON schema matched the registry, but it never compared the parameter tables with the verb signatures. A renamed keyword or a changed default on the verb passed green, and the inline form and the define.yaml form of one derivation then produced different numbers. On 2026-10-14 we measured the two sides: 48 algorithms, 24 of them with a Param table equal to the signature, 73 individual differences on the other 24. Most of the differences were deliberate, so "the signature is the declaration" was not true of the registry as it stood, and we had to decide what the registry is allowed to say that the signature does not.

We decided that the registry keeps two vocabularies (the spec algorithm names a data-standards reviewer reads, assign_ct, hardcode_no_ct, mapped onto one verb per intent) and that within one algorithm the spec fields take their default and required facts from the verb signature. A Param declares only what a signature cannot say: the spec field name when it differs from the keyword (kwarg), the YAML type (annotation), a legacy alias, a dispatch-time conversion (convert), whether the target name is the default (default_to_target), and required=True where the spec is stricter than the verb. The registry reads the signature on first lookup, not at import, so spec_registry never imports the namespace classes at module load. The description falls back to the Args: line of the verb docstring when the Param does not state one.

The rule the parity test enforces, for every algorithm with default dispatch and every Param:

  1. The keyword exists in the verb signature.
  2. A Param marked default-to-target skips the default check.
  3. The spec may be stricter than the verb: required=True where the signature has a default. The spec may never be looser: no spec-only default where the signature requires a value, and no spec-only default that differs from the signature's.
  4. When both sides are optional, the defaults are equal.
  5. Verb arguments absent from the registry are ignored. The spec surface is a curated subset of the signature, widened when a Define-XML method template exists for the new field.

Custom-dispatch algorithms (date, nsv, callable, pick) have no verb signature to derive from and are outside the rule.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• The verb is the algorithm (#146). One name, one declaration, one record: the algorithm: value is the verb name and the YAML keys are its keyword arguments, so the Param tables disappear. This reverses the recorded choice "Two vocabularies, one mapping" in docs/concepts/define-yaml.md, changes the vocabulary a reviewer reads in a define.yaml, and cannot make ct_codelist required for a CT assignment while leaving it absent for a plain copy, because one signature cannot produce five strict models. It stays open as its own decision. If it is taken, it deletes the Param tables and this ADR with them.
  • Keep spec-only defaults as CDISC conventions. nrind in YAML defaulted low to LBSTNRLO while the Python call required low=; merge and lookup in YAML defaulted on to USUBJID while the Python verb raises without it. A submission artefact should name its inputs, and a merge that silently joins on USUBJID when the author meant USUBJID and VISITNUM duplicates rows with no trace in the spec. All ten spec-only defaults go, and the keys become required in YAML. No shipped example, doc or test spec omitted any of them.
  • Derive the YAML type from the Python type. The two type systems differ on purpose: ct is str | type | None in Python and a codelist id in YAML, agg is a list of Polars expressions in Python and a list of strings in YAML. The convert field exists because of that gap. The annotation is a declaration, not a restatement, so it stays written.
  • A test only, no derivation. The classified parity test closes the live bug on its own. Derivation is what makes drift impossible instead of tested-for, and it turns each of the 48 registrations planned in #90 into one Param per field plus a method template. The test lands first, then derivation.
  • Resolve at import through a finalize() call in fleet/__init__, or a hook on namespace class creation. Both make the import order of fleet/__init__ a hidden contract, or couple the registry to the namespace mixin. Resolution on first lookup follows fleet.introspect.algorithms(), which refuses to cache for the same reason.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• ct_codelist becomes required on assign_ct and hardcode_ct. The concept doc already claimed that a CT derivation missing its codelist is a load-time error, and the registry now makes that true.
  • A define.yaml must state low, high and aval for nrind, the three dates for on_treatment, term_var for atoxgr, and on for merge and lookup. A missing key is a load-time error with a suggestion.
  • A misspelled keyword in a registration surfaces at first lookup, not at import. The parity test touches every entry, so it is still a red test.
  • The review's count "5 of Param's 10 fields become derived" is corrected to 2: default and required. description has a fallback, not a derivation.
  • fleet.introspect.ParamInfo does not change. A default field may be added later under ADR-0001's additive rule.
  • SpecAlgorithm.verb stays the attribute name on the standard's top-level namespace. Sub-namespace verbs need a dotted path, which is #90's design.

docs.title: The verb is the algorithm: one vocabulary for inline code and define.yaml
docs.text:
Status: accepted, 2026-10-16. Proposed and decided the same day in #146. Supersedes ADR-0007.

A derivation has two notations in Fleet. The inline notation is a verb call, .assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=SEX). The spec notation is a derivation: block in a define.yaml, algorithm: assign_ct, source: sex, ct_codelist: C66731. Today the two notations use two vocabularies. The spec registry maps the spec names onto the verbs with a hand-written Param table per algorithm, and ADR-0007 made the table take its default and required facts from the verb signature. The table still exists, and so do the renamed keys, the aliases and the legacy keys.

We decided that the algorithm: value is the verb name and the YAML keys are the keyword arguments of the verb. The rule for the programmer: remove .verb("TARGET", and the last ). What stays is the YAML block. Fleet builds the strict Pydantic model from the verb signature. A short declaration per verb says only what a signature cannot say: which arguments stay out of the spec, which arguments exclude each other, and the Define-XML method text. Lineage already records (verb, target, kwargs). from_spec calls the verb with them, and to_spec_yaml() writes them back unchanged.

docs.title: Measured on 2026-10-16, on main at bb4b878
docs.text:
Fact Value Registered algorithms 46 (16 SDTM, 30 ADaM) Distinct verbs behind them 39 (13 SDTM, 26 ADaM) Verbs with more than one spec name assign (4 names in SDTM, 3 in ADaM), derivation (2), duration (2) Spec names that differ from their only verb if_then_else, condderivation (case_when), lookup (merge), callable (derivation) Renamed keys 13 distinct renames on 22 fields, for example ct_codelist for ct, groups for by, else_value for else_ Algorithm aliases 4: assign_dtc, dataset_level, count, mean_arterial_pressure Legacy key maps 8 Custom dispatch 4: date (SDTM), nsv, pick, callable Registration code in spec_registry.py 941 lines (lines 960 to 1900) Shipped define.yaml files with derivations 4 files, 174 blocks Blocks whose algorithm: value changes 160 of 174 Blocks where a key changes 18 of 174

The 160 name changes are mostly source and assign_no_ct to assign (108 blocks) and assign_dtc to date (14 blocks).

docs.title: Before and after
docs.text:
The DM block for SEX, today and under this proposal. The inline call is .assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=SEX, ct_map={"F": "F", "M": "M"}).

# today
- name: SEX
  codelist: C66731
  derivation:
    algorithm: assign_ct
    source: sex
    ct_codelist: C66731
    ct_mapping: { "F": "F", "M": "M" }

# proposed
- name: SEX
  codelist: C66731
  derivation:
    algorithm: assign
    source: sex
    ct_map: { "F": "F", "M": "M" }
