docs.text:
Mixin providing flag(), its wrappers, and criterion().

Both SDTM (df.sdtm) and all ADaM namespaces inherit from this mixin. The methods rely on _chain(), _with_lazy() and _materialise_then() which every concrete namespace class must provide.

Source code in src/fleet/core/_flag_mixin.py 
class FlagCriterionMixin:
    """Mixin providing ``flag()``, its wrappers, and ``criterion()``.

    Both SDTM (``df.sdtm``) and all ADaM namespaces inherit from this
    mixin.  The methods rely on ``_chain()``, ``_with_lazy()`` and
    ``_materialise_then()`` which every concrete namespace class must
    provide.
    """

    _lazy: pl.LazyFrame

    # Subclasses must provide these — declared here for type-checker only.
    def _chain(self, *exprs: pl.Expr, verb: str | None = None) -> Self: ...  # noqa: E704
    def _materialise_then(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> Self: ...  # noqa: E704
    def _with_lazy(self, lf: pl.LazyFrame) -> Self: ...  # noqa: E704

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Flag — generalised "Y" / null flagging                               #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def flag(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        criteria: str | pl.Expr,
        by: list[str] | None = None,
        order_by: str | list[str] | None = None,
        value_col: str | None = None,
        where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
        from_dataset: pl.DataFrame | list[pl.DataFrame] | None = None,
        on: list[str] | None = None,
        source_filter: pl.Expr | None = None,
        condition: pl.Expr | None = None,
        inclusive: bool = True,
        flag_no_ref_groups: bool = True,
        flag_all: bool = False,
        flag_value: str = "Y",
        false_value: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Set *target* to *flag_value* for records matching *criteria*.

        Supports row-level boolean expressions and built-in shortcuts:

        - ``"first"`` / ``"last"`` — rank-based edge detection within groups.
        - ``"max"`` / ``"min"`` — value-based extreme within groups.
        - ``"exists"`` — set-membership from external dataset(s).
        - ``"before"`` / ``"after"`` — relative to a landmark condition.
        - ``"exists_after"`` / ``"exists_before"`` — temporal/self-join flag.

        Parameters that are irrelevant to the selected criteria mode
        raise :class:`~fleet.core.exceptions.VerbUsageError` instead of
        being silently ignored.  The ``flag_first`` / ``flag_last`` /
        ``flag_extreme`` / ``flag_exists`` / ``flag_relative`` wrappers
        expose each mode with only its own parameters.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag column.
            criteria: A Polars expression, or one of ``"first"``,
                ``"last"``, ``"max"``, ``"min"``, ``"exists"``,
                ``"before"``, ``"after"``, ``"exists_after"``,
                ``"exists_before"``.
            by: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).
            order_by: Sort column(s) required for ``"first"``/``"last"``
                and ``"before"``/``"after"``.  On a tie among candidates,
                ``"last"`` takes the last input record and ``"first"`` the
                first (SAS ``LAST.``/``FIRST.``); add a sequence variable
                to remove the dependence on input order.
            value_col: Value column required for ``"max"``/``"min"``.
            where: Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates;
                rows that fail it take no part, even on a tie.
            from_dataset: External dataset(s) for ``"exists"`` and
                ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"`` criteria.
            on: Join key columns for ``"exists"`` criteria.
            source_filter: Filter applied to *from_dataset* before key
                extraction or join.
            condition: Boolean expression identifying landmark rows for
                ``"before"``/``"after"`` or the current-row condition for
                ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"``.
            inclusive: Whether the landmark row itself is included in the
                flag (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
            flag_no_ref_groups: If ``False``, groups without a landmark
                condition match get ``None`` instead of being flagged
                (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
            flag_all: If ``True``, all tied extreme values receive the
                flag (for ``"first"``/``"last"``). Default ``False``.
            flag_value: Value to assign when condition is met (default
                ``"Y"``).
            false_value: Value to assign when condition is not met.
                Default ``None`` (null).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Raises:
            VerbUsageError: When a parameter irrelevant to the selected
                criteria mode is passed.
            DerivationError: When a mode-required parameter is missing,
                or a bare-identifier *criteria* matches neither a
                keyword nor a column.

        Examples:
            First observation per group::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .flag("ABLFL", criteria="first", order_by="AVISITN",
                          by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                    .to_frame()
                )

            Existence flag from external dataset::

                adsl = (
                    dm.adam.adsl
                    .flag("VSEVALFL", criteria="exists",
                          from_dataset=advs, on=["USUBJID"],
                          source_filter=pl.col("AVISIT") == "BASELINE")
                    .to_frame()
                )

            Relative flag — before first PD::

                result = (
                    response.adam
                    .flag("ANL02FL", criteria="before",
                          condition=pl.col("AVALC") == "PD",
                          order_by="AVISITN", by=["USUBJID"],
                          inclusive=True)
                    .to_frame()
                )

            Population flag from the treatment start date (a population
            flag is never blank, so non-members get ``"N"``)::

                adsl = (
                    adsl.adam.adsl
                    .flag("SAFFL", criteria=pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null(),
                          false_value="N")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

        grps = by or ["USUBJID"]
        order_cols: list[str] | None = None
        if order_by is not None:
            order_cols = [order_by] if isinstance(order_by, str) else list(order_by)

        criteria_lower = criteria.lower() if isinstance(criteria, str) else None
        mode = criteria_lower if criteria_lower in _FLAG_CRITERIA_KEYWORDS else "expression"
        if mode == "expression":
            # Keyword typos ("frist") must surface as a did-you-mean error
            # before any parameter validation blames the wrong thing.
            self._check_flag_criteria_typo(target, criteria)
        self._validate_flag_params(
            target,
            criteria,
            mode,
            {
                "order_by": order_by,
                "value_col": value_col,
                "where": where,
                "from_dataset": from_dataset,
                "on": on,
                "source_filter": source_filter,
                "condition": condition,
                "inclusive": inclusive,
                "flag_no_ref_groups": flag_no_ref_groups,
                "flag_all": flag_all,
                "false_value": false_value,
            },
        )

        where_expr: pl.Expr | None = None
        if where is not None:
            where_expr = where if isinstance(where, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(str(where))

        false_lit = pl.lit(false_value) if false_value is not None else pl.lit(None)

        if mode in ("first", "last"):
            return self._flag_ranked(
                target,
                criteria_lower=mode,
                grps=grps,
                order_cols=order_cols,
                where_expr=where_expr,
                flag_all=flag_all,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_lit=false_lit,
            )
        elif mode in ("max", "min"):
            return self._flag_extreme(
                target,
                criteria_lower=mode,
                grps=grps,
                value_col=value_col,
                where_expr=where_expr,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_lit=false_lit,
            )
        elif mode == "exists":
            return self._flag_exists(
                target,
                grps=grps,
                from_dataset=from_dataset,
                on=on,
                source_filter=source_filter,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_value=false_value,
                false_lit=false_lit,
            )
        elif mode in ("before", "after"):
            return self._flag_relative(
                target,
                criteria_lower=mode,
                grps=grps,
                order_cols=order_cols,
                condition=condition,
                inclusive=inclusive,
                flag_no_ref_groups=flag_no_ref_groups,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_value=false_value,
            )
        elif mode in ("exists_after", "exists_before"):
            return self._flag_temporal_exists(
                target,
                criteria_lower=mode,
                from_dataset=from_dataset,
                on=on,
                order_cols=order_cols,
                condition=condition,
                source_filter=source_filter,
                flag_value=flag_value,
            )
        else:
            return self._flag_expression(
                target,
                criteria=criteria,
                where_expr=where_expr,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_lit=false_lit,
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Discoverable per-mode wrappers                                       #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def flag_first(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        order_by: str | list[str],
        by: list[str] | None = None,
        where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
        flag_all: bool = False,
        flag_value: str = "Y",
        false_value: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Flag the first record per group (``flag(criteria="first")``).

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag column.
            order_by: Sort column(s) defining "first" within each group.
                A tie goes to the first input record.
            by: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).
            where: Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates.
            flag_all: Flag every tied extreme record instead of one.
            flag_value: Value assigned to flagged records (default ``"Y"``).
            false_value: Value assigned otherwise (default null).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Baseline flag on the first visit per subject/parameter::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .flag_first("ABLFL", order_by="AVISITN",
                                by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self.flag(
            target,
            criteria="first",
            order_by=order_by,
            by=by,
            where=where,
            flag_all=flag_all,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
        )

    def flag_last(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        order_by: str | list[str],
        by: list[str] | None = None,
        where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
        flag_all: bool = False,
        flag_value: str = "Y",
        false_value: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Flag the last record per group (``flag(criteria="last")``).

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag column.
            order_by: Sort column(s) defining "last" within each group.
                A tie goes to the last input record.
            by: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).
            where: Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates.
            flag_all: Flag every tied extreme record instead of one.
            flag_value: Value assigned to flagged records (default ``"Y"``).
            false_value: Value assigned otherwise (default null).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Last analysis-eligible record per subject/parameter::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .flag_last("ANL01FL", order_by="ADT",
                               by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self.flag(
            target,
            criteria="last",
            order_by=order_by,
            by=by,
            where=where,
            flag_all=flag_all,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
        )

    def flag_extreme(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        value_col: str,
        mode: Literal["max", "min"] = "max",
        by: list[str] | None = None,
        where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
        flag_value: str = "Y",
        false_value: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Flag the extreme-valued record(s) per group (``criteria="max"/"min"``).

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag column.
            value_col: Column whose extreme value is flagged.
            mode: ``"max"`` (default) or ``"min"``.
            by: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).
            where: Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates.
            flag_value: Value assigned to flagged records (default ``"Y"``).
            false_value: Value assigned otherwise (default null).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Worst-severity record per subject and term::

                adae = (
                    ae_df.adam.occds
                    .flag_extreme("ANL01FL", value_col="AESEVN",
                                  by=["USUBJID", "AETERM"])
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self.flag(
            target,
            criteria=mode,
            value_col=value_col,
            by=by,
            where=where,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
        )

    def flag_exists(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        from_dataset: pl.DataFrame | list[pl.DataFrame],
        on: list[str],
        source_filter: pl.Expr | None = None,
        flag_value: str = "Y",
        false_value: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Flag records with a match in external dataset(s) (``criteria="exists"``).

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag column.
            from_dataset: External dataset(s) to look up keys in.
            on: Join key columns.
            source_filter: Filter applied to *from_dataset* before key
                extraction.
            flag_value: Value assigned when a match exists (default ``"Y"``).
            false_value: Value assigned otherwise (default null).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Subjects with a baseline vital-signs record::

                adsl = (
                    dm.adam.adsl
                    .flag_exists("VSEVALFL", from_dataset=advs,
                                 on=["USUBJID"],
                                 source_filter=pl.col("AVISIT") == "BASELINE")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self.flag(
            target,
            criteria="exists",
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            on=on,
            source_filter=source_filter,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
        )

    def flag_relative(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        when: Literal["before", "after"],
        condition: pl.Expr,
        order_by: str | list[str],
        by: list[str] | None = None,
        inclusive: bool = True,
        flag_no_ref_groups: bool = True,
        flag_value: str = "Y",
        false_value: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Flag records before/after a landmark (``criteria="before"/"after"``).

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag column.
            when: ``"before"`` or ``"after"`` the first landmark record.
            condition: Boolean expression identifying landmark rows.
            order_by: Sort column(s) defining record order within groups.
            by: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).
            inclusive: Whether the landmark row itself is flagged.
            flag_no_ref_groups: Behaviour for groups without a landmark.
            flag_value: Value assigned to flagged records (default ``"Y"``).
            false_value: Value assigned otherwise (default null).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Analysis flag for records up to first disease progression::

                adrs = (
                    rs_df.adam
                    .flag_relative("ANL02FL", when="before",
                                   condition=pl.col("AVALC") == "PD",
                                   order_by="AVISITN", by=["USUBJID"])
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self.flag(
            target,
            criteria=when,
            condition=condition,
            order_by=order_by,
            by=by,
            inclusive=inclusive,
            flag_no_ref_groups=flag_no_ref_groups,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Internal validation / dispatch helpers                               #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _validate_flag_params(
        self,
        target: str,
        criteria: str | pl.Expr,
        mode: str,
        passed: dict[str, object],
    ) -> None:
        """Reject parameters that the selected criteria mode does not use."""
        irrelevant = [
            name
            for name, value in passed.items()
            if value is not _FLAG_PARAM_DEFAULTS[name] and mode not in _FLAG_MODE_PARAMS[name]
        ]
        if not irrelevant:
            return
        crit_repr = repr(criteria) if isinstance(criteria, str) else "<expression>"
        raise VerbUsageError(
            f"flag('{target}', criteria={crit_repr}): parameter(s) "
            f"{', '.join(sorted(irrelevant))} are not used by criteria mode "
            f"'{mode}' and would be silently ignored. Remove them, or pick the "
            "matching mode (see flag_first/flag_last/flag_extreme/flag_exists/"
            "flag_relative for per-mode signatures)."
        )

    def _check_flag_criteria_typo(self, target: str, criteria: str | pl.Expr) -> None:
        """Reject bare-identifier criteria that match neither keyword nor column.

        A string like ``"frist"`` would otherwise fall through to
        expression parsing and blame a nonexistent *column* when the user
        typo'd a *keyword*.  Reports both interpretations.
        """
        if not isinstance(criteria, str):
            return
        bare = criteria.strip()
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*", bare):
            return
        schema_names = self._lazy.collect_schema().names()
        if bare in schema_names:
            return
        parts = [
            f"flag('{target}', criteria={criteria!r}): {bare!r} is neither a "
            "criteria keyword nor a column in the frame."
        ]
        kw_hit = difflib.get_close_matches(bare.lower(), sorted(_FLAG_CRITERIA_KEYWORDS), n=1)
        if kw_hit:
            parts.append(f"Did you mean criteria='{kw_hit[0]}'?")
        col_hit = difflib.get_close_matches(bare, schema_names, n=1)
        if col_hit:
            parts.append(f"Or the column '{col_hit[0]}'?")
        parts.append(f"Valid keywords: {sorted(_FLAG_CRITERIA_KEYWORDS)}.")
        raise DerivationError(" ".join(parts))

    def _flag_ranked(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria_lower,
        grps,
        order_cols,
        where_expr,
        flag_all,
        flag_value,
        false_lit,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle first/last rank-based flag criteria (pure window exprs)."""
        if not order_cols:
            raise DerivationError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires order_by.")
        descending = criteria_lower == "last"
        null_mask = pl.all_horizontal([pl.col(c).is_not_null() for c in order_cols])
        eligible = null_mask if where_expr is None else (where_expr & null_mask)

        if flag_all:
            if len(order_cols) == 1:
                val_expr = pl.col(order_cols[0])
            else:
                val_expr = pl.struct(order_cols)
            candidate = pl.when(eligible).then(val_expr)
            extreme = candidate.max().over(grps) if descending else candidate.min().over(grps)
            row_cond = eligible & (val_expr == extreme)
            expr = pl.when(row_cond).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(false_lit).alias(target)
            return self._chain(expr, verb="flag")

        # Records that fail `where` take no part; a tie goes to the last (first) input row.
        position = pl.int_range(pl.len())
        winner = pl.when(eligible).then(position).otherwise(None).min()
        row_cond = ((position == winner) & eligible).over(
            grps,
            order_by=[*(pl.col(c) for c in order_cols), pl.int_range(pl.len()).alias("__flag_tie")],
            descending=descending,
            nulls_last=True,
        )
        expr = pl.when(row_cond).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(false_lit).alias(target)
        return self._chain(expr, verb="flag")

    def _flag_extreme(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria_lower,
        grps,
        value_col,
        where_expr,
        flag_value,
        false_lit,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle max/min value-based extreme flag criteria."""
        if not value_col:
            raise DerivationError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires value_col.")
        if where_expr is not None:
            masked_val = pl.when(where_expr).then(pl.col(value_col)).otherwise(pl.lit(None))
            agg_val = (
                masked_val.max().over(grps)
                if criteria_lower == "max"
                else masked_val.min().over(grps)
            )
            row_cond = where_expr & (pl.col(value_col) == agg_val)
        else:
            agg_val = (
                pl.col(value_col).max().over(grps)
                if criteria_lower == "max"
                else pl.col(value_col).min().over(grps)
            )
            row_cond = pl.col(value_col) == agg_val
        expr = pl.when(row_cond).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(false_lit).alias(target)
        return self._chain(expr, verb="flag")

    def _flag_exists(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        grps,
        from_dataset,
        on,
        source_filter,
        flag_value,
        false_value,
        false_lit,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle exists set-membership flag criteria."""
        if from_dataset is None or on is None:
            raise DerivationError("flag criteria='exists' requires from_dataset and on.")
        datasets = from_dataset if isinstance(from_dataset, list) else [from_dataset]
        key_frames: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
        for ds in datasets:
            filtered = ds
            if source_filter is not None:
                filtered = ds.filter(source_filter)
            key_frames.append(filtered.select(on).unique())
        all_keys = pl.concat(key_frames).unique()

        if len(on) == 1:
            is_member = pl.col(on[0]).is_in(all_keys[on[0]].implode(), nulls_equal=True)
            expr = pl.when(is_member).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(false_lit).alias(target)
            return self._chain(expr, verb="flag")

        # Multi-column join path
        df = self._lazy.collect()
        df_with_idx = df.with_row_index("__flag_idx__")
        result = (
            (df_with_idx.drop(target) if target in df_with_idx.columns else df_with_idx)
            .join(
                df_with_idx.select(on + ["__flag_idx__"])
                .unique()
                .join(all_keys, on=on, how="semi", nulls_equal=True)
                .with_columns(pl.lit(flag_value).alias(target)),
                on="__flag_idx__",
                how="left",
            )
            .with_columns(
                pl.col(target).fill_null(pl.lit(false_value) if false_value else pl.lit(None))
            )
            .drop("__flag_idx__")
        )
        return self._materialise_then(result)

    def _flag_relative(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria_lower,
        grps,
        order_cols,
        condition,
        inclusive,
        flag_no_ref_groups,
        flag_value,
        false_value,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle before/after relative-to-landmark flag criteria (window exprs)."""
        if condition is None:
            raise DerivationError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires condition.")
        if not order_cols:
            raise DerivationError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires order_by.")

        pos = pl.int_range(pl.len()).over(grps, order_by=[pl.col(c) for c in order_cols])
        cond_bool = condition.cast(pl.Boolean)
        landmark = pl.when(cond_bool).then(pos).otherwise(None).min().over(grps)

        norm_false = pl.lit(false_value) if false_value else pl.lit(None)
        if criteria_lower == "before":
            flagged = (pos <= landmark) if inclusive else (pos < landmark)
            no_ref = pl.lit(flag_value) if flag_no_ref_groups else norm_false
        else:
            flagged = (pos >= landmark) if inclusive else (pos > landmark)
            no_ref = pl.lit(false_value) if flag_no_ref_groups else norm_false

        expr = (
            pl.when(landmark.is_null())
            .then(no_ref)
            .when(flagged)
            .then(pl.lit(flag_value))
            .otherwise(norm_false)
            .alias(target)
        )
        return self._chain(expr, verb="flag")

    def _flag_temporal_exists(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria_lower,
        from_dataset,
        on,
        order_cols,
        condition,
        source_filter,
        flag_value,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle exists_after/exists_before via one aggregate join.

        "Any source record strictly after t" is equivalent to
        "max(source times) > t" (and symmetrically with min for
        exists_before), so a per-key aggregate left join replaces the
        former per-row scan.
        """
        if from_dataset is None or condition is None:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires from_dataset and condition."
            )
        if on is None:
            raise DerivationError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires on.")

        src = from_dataset if isinstance(from_dataset, pl.DataFrame) else pl.concat(from_dataset)
        if source_filter is not None:
            src = src.filter(source_filter)

        if order_cols:
            time_col = order_cols[0]
        else:
            schema_names = self._lazy.collect_schema().names()
            common_time = [
                c
                for c in ["AVISITN", "ADY", "ADT", "ADTM"]
                if c in schema_names and c in src.columns
            ]
            if not common_time:
                raise DerivationError(
                    f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires order_by or a "
                    "common temporal column (AVISITN, ADY, ADT, ADTM)."
                )
            time_col = common_time[0]

        tmp = "__flag_src_time__"
        if criteria_lower == "exists_after":
            src_agg = src.group_by(on).agg(pl.col(time_col).max().alias(tmp))
            cmp = pl.col(tmp) > pl.col(time_col)
        else:
            src_agg = src.group_by(on).agg(pl.col(time_col).min().alias(tmp))
            cmp = pl.col(tmp) < pl.col(time_col)

        flag_expr = (
            pl.when(condition & cmp).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(pl.lit(None)).alias(target)
        )
        lf = (
            self._lazy.join(
                src_agg.lazy(), on=on, how="left", maintain_order="left", nulls_equal=True
            )
            .with_columns(flag_expr)
            .drop(tmp)
        )
        return self._with_lazy(lf)

    def _flag_expression(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria,
        where_expr,
        flag_value,
        false_lit,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle direct expression-based flag criteria."""
        from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

        if isinstance(criteria, pl.Expr):
            row_cond = criteria
        else:
            row_cond = parse_expression(str(criteria))
        final_cond = (where_expr & row_cond) if where_expr is not None else row_cond
        expr = pl.when(final_cond).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(false_lit).alias(target)
        return self._chain(expr, verb="flag")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Criterion — CRITy / CRITyFL / CRITyFN triple-output                 #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def criterion(
        self,
        number: int,
        *,
        condition: pl.Expr,
        description: str | None = None,
        prefix: str = "CRIT",
    ) -> Self:
        """Derive criterion flag triple: CRITy, CRITyFL, CRITyFN.

        Produces three columns following CDISC ADaM conventions:

        - ``{prefix}{number}`` — the criterion description (constant string).
        - ``{prefix}{number}FL`` — ``"Y"`` if condition is met, ``"N"`` otherwise.
        - ``{prefix}{number}FN`` — ``1`` if met, ``0`` otherwise.

        Args:
            number: Criterion number (e.g. 1 → CRIT1, CRIT1FL, CRIT1FN).
            condition: Boolean Polars expression defining the criterion.
            description: Human-readable description stored in CRITy column.
                If ``None``, the column is still created with null values.
            prefix: Column name prefix (default ``"CRIT"``).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with three new columns appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Flag records where AVAL >= 10::

                adlb = (
                    lb_df.adam
                    .criterion(1, condition=pl.col("AVAL") >= 10,
                               description="AVAL >= 10")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        col_crit = f"{prefix}{number}"
        col_fl = f"{prefix}{number}FL"
        col_fn = f"{prefix}{number}FN"

        desc_expr = (
            pl.lit(description).alias(col_crit)
            if description is not None
            else pl.lit(None).cast(pl.String).alias(col_crit)
        )
        fl_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit("N")).alias(col_fl)
        fn_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit(1)).otherwise(pl.lit(0)).alias(col_fn)

        return self._chain(desc_expr, fl_expr, fn_expr, verb="criterion")

  • "exists_after" / "exists_before" — temporal/self-join flag.

def flag(
    self,
    target: str,
    *,
    criteria: str | pl.Expr,
    by: list[str] | None = None,
    order_by: str | list[str] | None = None,
    value_col: str | None = None,
    where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    from_dataset: pl.DataFrame | list[pl.DataFrame] | None = None,
    on: list[str] | None = None,
    source_filter: pl.Expr | None = None,
    condition: pl.Expr | None = None,
    inclusive: bool = True,
    flag_no_ref_groups: bool = True,
    flag_all: bool = False,
    flag_value: str = "Y",
    false_value: str | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """Set *target* to *flag_value* for records matching *criteria*.

    Supports row-level boolean expressions and built-in shortcuts:

    - ``"first"`` / ``"last"`` — rank-based edge detection within groups.
    - ``"max"`` / ``"min"`` — value-based extreme within groups.
    - ``"exists"`` — set-membership from external dataset(s).
    - ``"before"`` / ``"after"`` — relative to a landmark condition.
    - ``"exists_after"`` / ``"exists_before"`` — temporal/self-join flag.

    Parameters that are irrelevant to the selected criteria mode
    raise :class:`~fleet.core.exceptions.VerbUsageError` instead of
    being silently ignored.  The ``flag_first`` / ``flag_last`` /
    ``flag_extreme`` / ``flag_exists`` / ``flag_relative`` wrappers
    expose each mode with only its own parameters.

    Args:
        target: Name of the output flag column.
        criteria: A Polars expression, or one of ``"first"``,
            ``"last"``, ``"max"``, ``"min"``, ``"exists"``,
            ``"before"``, ``"after"``, ``"exists_after"``,
            ``"exists_before"``.
        by: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).
        order_by: Sort column(s) required for ``"first"``/``"last"``
            and ``"before"``/``"after"``.  On a tie among candidates,
            ``"last"`` takes the last input record and ``"first"`` the
            first (SAS ``LAST.``/``FIRST.``); add a sequence variable
            to remove the dependence on input order.
        value_col: Value column required for ``"max"``/``"min"``.
        where: Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates;
            rows that fail it take no part, even on a tie.
        from_dataset: External dataset(s) for ``"exists"`` and
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"`` criteria.
        on: Join key columns for ``"exists"`` criteria.
        source_filter: Filter applied to *from_dataset* before key
            extraction or join.
        condition: Boolean expression identifying landmark rows for
            ``"before"``/``"after"`` or the current-row condition for
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"``.
        inclusive: Whether the landmark row itself is included in the
            flag (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
        flag_no_ref_groups: If ``False``, groups without a landmark
            condition match get ``None`` instead of being flagged
            (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
        flag_all: If ``True``, all tied extreme values receive the
            flag (for ``"first"``/``"last"``). Default ``False``.
        flag_value: Value to assign when condition is met (default
            ``"Y"``).
        false_value: Value to assign when condition is not met.
            Default ``None`` (null).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        VerbUsageError: When a parameter irrelevant to the selected
            criteria mode is passed.
        DerivationError: When a mode-required parameter is missing,
            or a bare-identifier *criteria* matches neither a
            keyword nor a column.

    Examples:
        First observation per group::

            advs = (
                vs_raw.adam
                .flag("ABLFL", criteria="first", order_by="AVISITN",
                      by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                .to_frame()
            )

        Existence flag from external dataset::

            adsl = (
                dm.adam.adsl
                .flag("VSEVALFL", criteria="exists",
                      from_dataset=advs, on=["USUBJID"],
                      source_filter=pl.col("AVISIT") == "BASELINE")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Relative flag — before first PD::

            result = (
                response.adam
                .flag("ANL02FL", criteria="before",
                      condition=pl.col("AVALC") == "PD",
                      order_by="AVISITN", by=["USUBJID"],
                      inclusive=True)
                .to_frame()
            )

        Population flag from the treatment start date (a population
        flag is never blank, so non-members get ``"N"``)::

            adsl = (
                adsl.adam.adsl
                .flag("SAFFL", criteria=pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null(),
                      false_value="N")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

    grps = by or ["USUBJID"]
    order_cols: list[str] | None = None
    if order_by is not None:
        order_cols = [order_by] if isinstance(order_by, str) else list(order_by)

    criteria_lower = criteria.lower() if isinstance(criteria, str) else None
    mode = criteria_lower if criteria_lower in _FLAG_CRITERIA_KEYWORDS else "expression"
    if mode == "expression":
        # Keyword typos ("frist") must surface as a did-you-mean error
        # before any parameter validation blames the wrong thing.
        self._check_flag_criteria_typo(target, criteria)
    self._validate_flag_params(
        target,
        criteria,
        mode,
        {
            "order_by": order_by,
            "value_col": value_col,
            "where": where,
            "from_dataset": from_dataset,
            "on": on,
            "source_filter": source_filter,
            "condition": condition,
            "inclusive": inclusive,
            "flag_no_ref_groups": flag_no_ref_groups,
            "flag_all": flag_all,
            "false_value": false_value,
        },
    )

    where_expr: pl.Expr | None = None
    if where is not None:
        where_expr = where if isinstance(where, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(str(where))

    false_lit = pl.lit(false_value) if false_value is not None else pl.lit(None)

    if mode in ("first", "last"):
        return self._flag_ranked(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            grps=grps,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_all=flag_all,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif mode in ("max", "min"):
        return self._flag_extreme(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            grps=grps,
            value_col=value_col,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif mode == "exists":
        return self._flag_exists(
            target,
            grps=grps,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            on=on,
            source_filter=source_filter,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif mode in ("before", "after"):
        return self._flag_relative(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            grps=grps,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            condition=condition,
            inclusive=inclusive,
            flag_no_ref_groups=flag_no_ref_groups,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
        )
    elif mode in ("exists_after", "exists_before"):
        return self._flag_temporal_exists(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            on=on,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            condition=condition,
            source_filter=source_filter,
            flag_value=flag_value,
        )
    else:
        return self._flag_expression(
            target,
            criteria=criteria,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )

def criterion(
    self,
    number: int,
    *,
    condition: pl.Expr,
    description: str | None = None,
    prefix: str = "CRIT",
) -> Self:
    """Derive criterion flag triple: CRITy, CRITyFL, CRITyFN.

    Produces three columns following CDISC ADaM conventions:

    - ``{prefix}{number}`` — the criterion description (constant string).
    - ``{prefix}{number}FL`` — ``"Y"`` if condition is met, ``"N"`` otherwise.
    - ``{prefix}{number}FN`` — ``1`` if met, ``0`` otherwise.

    Args:
        number: Criterion number (e.g. 1 → CRIT1, CRIT1FL, CRIT1FN).
        condition: Boolean Polars expression defining the criterion.
        description: Human-readable description stored in CRITy column.
            If ``None``, the column is still created with null values.
        prefix: Column name prefix (default ``"CRIT"``).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with three new columns appended; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Examples:
        Flag records where AVAL >= 10::

            adlb = (
                lb_df.adam
                .criterion(1, condition=pl.col("AVAL") >= 10,
                           description="AVAL >= 10")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    col_crit = f"{prefix}{number}"
    col_fl = f"{prefix}{number}FL"
    col_fn = f"{prefix}{number}FN"

    desc_expr = (
        pl.lit(description).alias(col_crit)
        if description is not None
        else pl.lit(None).cast(pl.String).alias(col_crit)
    )
    fl_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit("N")).alias(col_fl)
    fn_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit(1)).otherwise(pl.lit(0)).alias(col_fn)

    return self._chain(desc_expr, fl_expr, fn_expr, verb="criterion")

Immutable pipeline builder for ADSL (one-row-per-subject) derivations.

Also registered as the adsl LazyFrame namespace, so pl.scan_parquet(...).adsl starts a fully lazy ADSL pipeline.

Inherits shared verbs from SharedADaMVerbsMixin (assign, case_when, merge, source, derivation, whereclauses, ...) and adds ADSL-specific verbs that pull summary statistics from event-level datasets (AE, CM, MH, EX…). Discover the full set with .verbs().

Source code in src/fleet/adam/adsl_namespace.py 
@pl.api.register_lazyframe_namespace("adsl")
class ADSLNamespace(SharedADaMVerbsMixin):
    """
    Immutable pipeline builder for ADSL (one-row-per-subject) derivations.

    Also registered as the ``adsl`` LazyFrame namespace, so
    ``pl.scan_parquet(...).adsl`` starts a fully lazy ADSL pipeline.

    Inherits shared verbs from ``SharedADaMVerbsMixin``
    (assign, case_when, merge, source, derivation, whereclauses, ...)
    and adds ADSL-specific verbs that pull summary statistics from
    event-level datasets (AE, CM, MH, EX…).  Discover the full set with
    ``.verbs()``.
    """

    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame | pl.LazyFrame) -> None:
        super().__init__(df)
        self._domain = "ADSL"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ADSL-specific verbs.                                                 #
    # first_date / last_date / count_events moved to                       #
    # SharedADaMVerbsMixin so the spec path (from_spec) can dispatch them. #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ADSL: age_years — unit-aware age conversion                         #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def age_years(
        self,
        target: str = "AAGE",
        *,
        age_col: str = "AGE",
        age_unit_col: str = "AGEU",
    ) -> Self:
        """Convert age to years, handling common unit strings.

        Recognises *AGEU* values: ``YEARS``, ``MONTHS``, ``WEEKS``, ``DAYS``
        (case-insensitive).  Unknown units produce null.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (default ``"AAGE"``).
            age_col: Source age column.
            age_unit_col: Column containing the age unit string.

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive age in years from DM variables::

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam.adsl
                    .age_years("AAGE", age_col="AGE", age_unit_col="AGEU")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from fleet.adam.utils import age_in_years as _age_in_years_expr

        return self._chain(
            _age_in_years_expr(age_col=age_col, age_unit_col=age_unit_col, target=target)
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ADSL: age_from_dates — date-based age calculation                   #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def age_from_dates(
        self,
        target: str = "AAGE",
        *,
        birth_date: str = "BRTHDT",
        reference_date: str = "TRTSDT",
        round_digits: int | None = 1,
    ) -> Self:
        """Compute age in years from two date columns.

        Uses ``(reference_date - birth_date) / 365.25`` for a more precise
        calculation than unit-conversion from ``AGE``.  Null when either
        date is missing.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (default ``"AAGE"``).
            birth_date: Date-of-birth column (``pl.Date``).
            reference_date: Reference date column (``pl.Date``).
            round_digits: Decimal places to round to (default ``1``).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive age from birth and randomisation dates::

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam.adsl
                    .age_from_dates("AAGE", birth_date="BRTHDT",
                                    reference_date="RANDDT")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        days = (
            pl.col(reference_date).cast(pl.Date) - pl.col(birth_date).cast(pl.Date)
        ).dt.total_days()
        expr = days / 365.25
        if round_digits is not None:
            expr = expr.round(round_digits)
        return self._chain(expr.alias(target))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ADSL: derive_period — Subperiod / Phase variables                   #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def derive_period(
        self,
        *,
        periods: list[dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> Self:
        """Create standard Subperiod / Phase variables.

        Generates ``AP{nn}SDT``, ``AP{nn}EDT``, and optionally
        ``TRT{nn:02d}P`` columns for each period.

        Args:
            periods: List of dicts each with ``"number"``, ``"start"``,
                ``"end"``, and optionally ``"treatment"``.

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with period columns appended.

        Examples:
            Define two treatment periods::

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam.adsl
                    .derive_period(
                        periods=[
                            {"number": 1, "start": "AP01SDT",
                             "end": "AP01EDT", "treatment": "TRT01P"},
                            {"number": 2, "start": "AP02SDT",
                             "end": "AP02EDT", "treatment": "TRT02P"},
                        ],
                    )
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        exprs: list[pl.Expr] = []
        for period in periods:
            n = period["number"]
            prefix = f"AP{n:02d}"
            sdt_col = period["start"]
            edt_col = period["end"]

            exprs.append(pl.col(sdt_col).alias(f"{prefix}SDT"))
            exprs.append(pl.col(edt_col).alias(f"{prefix}EDT"))

            trt = period.get("treatment")
            if trt is not None:
                trt_target = f"TRT{n:02d}P"
                if trt in self._lazy.collect_schema().names():
                    exprs.append(pl.col(trt).alias(trt_target))
                else:
                    exprs.append(pl.lit(trt).alias(trt_target))

        return self._chain(*exprs)

docs.title: Verb Cheat Sheet
docs.text:
This cheat sheet summarises the most common verbs across Fleet namespaces. Every verb name in this page is a clickable link to its docstring, rendered directly from the source code in the corresponding namespace page.

Single source of truth

Fleet's documentation is generated directly from Python docstrings via mkdocstrings and cross-linked with autorefs. The verb name you click here resolves to the exact method signature, parameters, and examples that the runtime executes — there is no separately maintained reference that can drift out of sync. Renaming a parameter in the source automatically updates this page on the next build.

docs.title: Core verbs (available everywhere)
docs.text: Verb Description Example .to_frame() Materialises the pipeline into a Polars DataFrame. Must be called at the end. .to_frame() .derivation() Injects an arbitrary Polars expression. .derivation("AGE", expression="pl.col('AGE_RAW').cast(pl.Int64)") .source() Passes a column through (renaming if from_col is provided). .source("USUBJID") .assign() Copy a column (source=) or hardcode a literal (value=). .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM") .inspect() Hard checkpoint — materialises and prints schema/shape/head. .inspect("after rename") .explain() Prints the Polars query plan without materialising. .explain() .compare() Compares the chain (candidate) against a base on keys; keeps chaining. .compare(adsl_prod, keys="USUBJID", on_fail="raise")

docs.title: SDTM namespace (df.sdtm)
docs.text: Verb Description Example .assign() Copy (source=) or hardcode (value=) a variable. .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id") .assign() CT-validated assignment: add ct= and optional ct_map=. .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=SEX, ct_map={"M":"M"}) .date() Normalise dates to ISO 8601 strings or parse to Date/Datetime. .date("RFSTDTC", source="first_dose_dt") .duration() Compute elapsed time or CDISC study day. .duration("SVSTDY", start="RFSTDTC", end="SVSTDTC") .case_when() Derive a value conditionally over multiple branches. .case_when("AGEGR1", when=[...], else_="OTHER") .condition_add() Single-condition assignment. .condition_add("FLAG", condition=..., then_value="Y") .ae_aerel() AE causality mapping. .ae_aerel("AEREL", source="rel_raw", aerel_map={...}) .merge() Join supplementary dataset on key columns. .merge(other, on="USUBJID") .nodup() Detect/remove duplicates with diagnostics. .nodup(subset=["USUBJID","VISIT"]) .group_by() Aggregate rows by group columns. .group_by(by=["USUBJID"], agg=[...]) .seq() Generate sequence number per group. .seq("AESEQ", by=["USUBJID"]) .nsv() Derive a Non-Standard Variable with qualifier metadata. .nsv("SAFETY", source="safety_flag", label="Safety Population Flag") .export_supp() Export NSV columns as vertical SUPPQUAL (IG ≤3.4). .export_supp(spec="define.yaml", dataset="DM") .from_spec() Build the entire pipeline from a define.yaml spec. df.sdtm.from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="DM") .validate() Run CDISC Rules Engine on the resulting frame. .validate("DM")

docs.text: Verb Description Example .derivation() Arbitrary Polars expression. .derivation("AVAL", expression="pl.col('vsorres').cast(pl.Float64)") .recode() Value remapping with default. .recode("PARAM", source="vstest", recode_map={...}) .assign() Copy/rename a column, or hardcode a literal. .assign("PARAMCD", source="vstestcd") .case_when() Multi-branch conditional derivation. .case_when("EOSSTT", when=[...]) .pick() Derive targets from the event with the latest (or first) value across sources. .pick("LSTALVDT", events=[...], by=["USUBJID"], order=["LSTALVDT"], mode="last") .date() Parse --DTC to analysis date or datetime with optional imputation. .date("ADT", source="VSDTC") .duration() CDISC study day, elapsed time, or ISO 8601 duration. .duration("ADY", start="TRTSDT", end="ADT") .merge_adsl() Bring ADSL columns onto a BDS dataset. .merge_adsl(adsl, keep=["TRTSDT","SAFFL"]) .baseline() Find baseline record per group, broadcast to target. .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL") .chg() Change from baseline (AVAL - BASE). .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE") .pchg() Percent change (CHG / BASE) * 100. .pchg("PCHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE") .flag() Assign "Y" per criteria (expression / first / last). .flag("ANL01FL", criteria="last", order_by="ADT") .bmi() BMI = weight / (height/100)². .bmi("BMI", weight="WEIGHT", height="HEIGHT") .bsa() Body Surface Area (Mosteller / DuBois / Haycock / Gehan-George). .bsa("BSA", weight="WEIGHT", height="HEIGHT") .map() Mean Arterial Pressure: DBP + (SBP-DBP)/3. .map("MAP", systolic="SYSBP", diastolic="DIABP") .qtc() Corrected QT (Fridericia / Bazett); QT in ms, RR in ms by default. .qtc("QTCF", qt="QT", rr="RR", rr_unit="ms") .nrind() Normal range indicator: LOW / NORMAL / HIGH. .nrind("ANRIND", value="AVAL", low="LO", high="HI") .on_treatment() On-treatment flag within [TRTSDT, TRTEDT]. .on_treatment("ONTRTFL", adt="ADT", trtsdt="TRTSDT", trtedt="TRTEDT") .shift() Categorical shift string ("NORMAL to HIGH"). .shift("SHIFT1", baseline_cat="BNRIND", post_cat="ANRIND") .merge() Left-join an external dataset on key columns. .merge(other_df, on="USUBJID") .transform() Apply an arbitrary frame-level transformation. .transform(lambda df: df.sort("USUBJID")) .derive_summary_records() Aggregate by group and append summary rows. .derive_summary_records(by=["USUBJID"], ...) .derive_locf_records() LOCF forward-fill within patient groups. .derive_locf_records(by=["USUBJID","PARAMCD"]) .derive_param() Derive a new parameter and append rows (own frame or from_dataset=). .derive_param(by=["USUBJID"], parameter_filter={...}, from_dataset=adlb, ...) .from_spec() Build the entire pipeline from a define.yaml spec. df.adam.from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="ADVS") .validate() Run CDISC Rules Engine on the resulting frame. .validate("ADVS")

docs.title: ADSL namespace (df.adam.adsl)
docs.text: Verb Description Example .first_date() Earliest date per subject from a second dataset. .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex, date_col="EXSTDTC") .last_date() Latest date per subject from a second dataset. .last_date("TRTEDT", from_dataset=ex, date_col="EXENDTC") .duration() Number of elapsed days (start to end). .duration("TRTDURD", start="TRTSDT", end="TRTEDT") .flag() Generalised "Y" flag (first/last/max/min/exists/before/after/expression). .flag("SAFFL", criteria='pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null()', false_value="N") .count_events() Tally events for each subject. .count_events("NUMAE", from_dataset=ae) .age_years() Unit-aware age conversion (YEARS, MONTHS, WEEKS, DAYS). .age_years("AAGE", age_col="AGE", age_unit_col="AGEU") .age_from_dates() Compute age between two dates. .age_from_dates("AGE", birth="BRTHDT", reference="RFSTDTC") .derive_period() Create APxxSDT / APxxEDT / TRTxxP subperiod variables. .derive_period(periods=[{"number": 1, ...}])

docs.title: OCCDS namespace (df.adam.occds)
docs.text: Verb Description Example .treatment_emergent() TRTEMFL flag (admiral derive_var_trtemfl rules). .treatment_emergent("TRTEMFL", start_date="ASTDT", end_date="AENDT", trtsdt="TRTSDT", trtedt="TRTEDT", end_window=30) .onset_recovery() Onset and recovery interval flags. .onset_recovery(...)

docs.title: PK namespace (df.adam.pk)
docs.text: Verb Description Example .blq_flag() Flag BLQ: conc < LLOQ, or no number and a BLQ text in PCSTRESC. .blq_flag("BLQFL", conc_col="PCSTRESN", lloq_col="PCLLOQ") .blq_impute() Impute BLQ concentrations (half_lloq, zero, lloq, missing). .blq_impute("AVAL", conc_col="PCSTRESN", lloq_col="PCLLOQ") .blqfn() Numeric BLQ flag: 1 when BLQ, 0 otherwise. .blqfn("BLQFN", conc_col="PCSTRESN", lloq_col="PCLLOQ") .nominal_time() Nominal elapsed time with unit conversion. .nominal_time("NTIME", from_col="PCTPTNUM") .duration() Actual elapsed time between datetime columns. .duration("ATIME", start="EXSTDTC", end="PCDTC", unit="hours") .predose_flag() Flag pre-dose samples within a window. .predose_flag("PREDFL", time_col="ATIME") .dose_normalized() Dose-normalise concentration: conc / dose. .dose_normalized("AVALDNM", conc_col="AVAL", dose_col="DOSE") .evid() Derive EVID for NONMEM-style datasets. .evid("EVID") .mrrlt() Clip negative ARRLT to 0 for MRRLT. .mrrlt("MRRLT", arrlt_col="ARRLT") .log_conc() Log-transform concentration. .log_conc("DVL", conc_col="DV") .mdv() Derive MDV for PopPK datasets. .mdv("MDV", conc_col="DV", evid_col="EVID") .amt() Derive AMT: dose amount on dosing records. .amt("AMT", dose_col="EXDOSE", evid_col="EVID") .cmt() Derive CMT compartment number (NONMEM). .cmt("CMT", evid_col="EVID", dose_cmt=1, conc_cmt=2) .avalcat() Listing-ready categorised analysis value. .avalcat("AVALCAT1", conc_col="PCSTRESN", lloq_col="PCLLOQ") .anl_flag() Analysis flag (ANL01FL / ANL02FL). .anl_flag("ANL01FL")

docs.title: Time-to-event (df.adam.tte)
docs.text:
Typed EventSource / CensorSource objects describe the candidates; the prebuilt library (DEATH_EVENT, AE_EVENT, ...) is browsable via prebuilt_sources_frame(). Source frames attach by nickname with .pin().

Verb Description Example .param() Derive one TTE parameter: earliest event wins, else latest censor. .param("OS", "Overall Survival", start_date="TRTSDT", events=[...]) .aval() AVAL (+AVALU) from STARTDT/ADT with CDISC unit conventions. .aval(unit="months") .km_data() (duration, event) frame for lifelines / scikit-survival. .km_data("OS", by=["TRT01P"])

docs.title: Trial Design (df.sdtm verbs + fleet.StudyDesign)
docs.text:
TDD verbs live directly on df.sdtm (there is no .tdd sub-namespace). fleet.StudyDesign is the define-once aggregate that derives every TDD domain — see the Trial Design concepts page.

Verb Description Example .fetch_structure() Load domain IG structure (packaged offline for 3.4). df.sdtm.fetch_structure("TA") .study_header() Hardcode STUDYID and DOMAIN. .study_header("STUDY01", "TA") .add_elements() Load a TrialElements collection (TE). .add_elements(te_rows) .add_arms() Load a TrialArms collection (TA), FK vs TE. .add_arms(ta_rows, te=te_rows) .add_visits() Load a TrialVisits collection (TV), FK vs TA. .add_visits(tv_rows, ta=ta_rows) .add_parameters() Load a TrialParameters collection (TS). .add_parameters(ts_rows) .add_criteria() Load a TrialCriteria collection (TI). .add_criteria(ti_rows) .add_disease_assessments() Load a TrialDiseaseAssessments collection (TD). .add_disease_assessments(td_rows) .add_milestones() Load a TrialMilestones collection (TM). .add_milestones(tm_rows) .element_boundaries() Compute element start/end (SE). .element_boundaries("SESTDTC", "SEENDTC", ...) .epoch_assign() Assign EPOCH from date ranges or per-subject SE. .epoch_assign("EPOCH", date_col="AESTDTC", se=se) .visit_map() Map planned ↔ actual visits (SV). .visit_map("VISITNUM", "VISIT", ...) .duration() Derive study day from reference. .duration("SVSTDY", start="RFSTDTC", end="SVSTDTC")

docs.title: How linking works
docs.text:
Click any verb name in the tables above. Your browser navigates to the corresponding namespace API page and scrolls to the auto-generated heading anchor for that method — a heading rendered live from the Python docstring.

This means:

  1. Parameter accuracy — the cheat sheet links never describe a parameter that doesn't exist in code.
  2. Examples stay current — code samples in docstrings are the same ones the test suite exercises.
  3. Discoverability — IDE hover, docs site, and help() in a REPL all read from the same docstring.

If you find a verb missing from this cheat sheet, file an issue or add a row — the link target itself is generated automatically once the method exists in source.

docs.title: Study Codelists (CDISCPILOT01)
docs.text:
This page documents the auto-generated codelist module that ships with the CDISCPILOT01 example study (examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/codelists.py). It is generated from the CDISC Library by CodelistGenerator and is regenerated whenever a new domain is added.

One source of truth — three audiences served

The same Python module powers:

- **IDE auto-completion** for programmers writing pipelines (`SEX.M`, `RACE.WHITE`).
- **Live runtime validation** through
  [`assign(ct=...)`][fleet.core._verb_mixin.SharedVerbsMixin.assign].
- **Direct hyperlinks to the CDISC Library Browser** for reviewers and auditors,
  via the `_cdisc_url` attribute on every codelist class.

No separate spreadsheet, no copy-pasted concept IDs, no drift between code and CT.

docs.title: In a standalone study project (recommended)
docs.text:
When your study lives in its own directory with a study_config.yaml, use import_codelists() to load the generated module without sys.path hacks:

from fleet.ct import import_codelists

# Auto-discovers codelists.py via study_config.yaml in CWD
ct = import_codelists()

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=ct.SEX)
    .assign("RACE", source="race", ct=ct.RACE)
    .assign("AGEU", value="YEARS", ct=ct.AGEU)
    .to_frame()
)

Or register the module so bare from codelists import ... works:

from fleet.ct import import_codelists

import_codelists()  # registers 'codelists' in sys.modules
from codelists import SEX, RACE, AGEU  # now works everywhere in the session

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=SEX)
    .assign("RACE", source="race", ct=RACE)
    .assign("AGEU", value="YEARS", ct=AGEU)
    .to_frame()
)

You can also pass an explicit path if your codelists file lives somewhere non-standard:

ct = import_codelists("path/to/my_codelists.py")

docs.title: Within the Fleet repo (example studies)
docs.text:
from examples.cdiscpilot01.sdtm.codelists import SEX, RACE, AGEU

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=SEX)
    .assign("RACE", source="race", ct=RACE)
    .assign("AGEU", value="YEARS", ct=AGEU)
    .to_frame()
)

Each codelist class exposes:

Attribute Description _concept_id NCI concept ID (e.g. "C66731"). _cdisc_url Deep link to the CDISC Library Browser entry. _preferred_term Preferred term as published by CDISC (when include_docs=True). <TERM> One class attribute per submission value (SEX.M, SEX.F, …).

docs.title: C66726
docs.text:
FRM (C66726).

The form of the completed pharmaceutical product, e.g. tablet, capsule,

injection, elixir, suppository. Dosage form can have a significant effect on the onset, duration and intensity of the pharmacological action of a drug. A pharmaceutical dosage form controls the rate at which the drug is released into the biological fluids. This release rate affects its intrinsic absorption pattern and therefore, the bioavailability of the drug.

See: https://library.cdisc.org/browser/#/mdr/ct/2023-12-15/packages/sdtmct-2023-12-15/codelists/C66726
Source code in examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/codelists.py

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: fleet.compare pairs a candidate dataset against a base on keys, matches variables by name and returns a comparison report; differences never raise. The .compare() verb on every namespace (SharedVerbsMixin) wraps it for pipelines, and fleet compare wraps it for the shell. See Comparing Datasets for the rules of equality and the exit codes. A comparison that cannot run raises ComparisonError, documented with the other exceptions.

docs.title: compare
docs.text: options: show_root_heading: true heading_level: 3

docs.title: fleet.comparison.compare
docs.text:
compare(
    base,
    candidate,
    *,
    keys,
    by=None,
    pairs=None,
    variables=None,
    abs_tol=0.0,
    rel_tol=0.0,
    ignore_trailing_whitespace=False,
    blank_is_missing=False,
    allow_duplicates=False,
    max_print=50,
    base_name=None,
    candidate_name=None
)

Compare a candidate dataset against a base, PROC COMPARE style.

Observations pair on keys; variables match by name. Equality is exact by default: null equals null, NaN equals NaN, null against NaN differs. abs_tol and rel_tol widen it on the numeric variables and ignore_trailing_whitespace on the string ones; nulls and NaN keep their rule under both. Variables of the same kind (numeric, string, temporal, boolean) but a different dtype compare by value after casting to a common supertype and are listed as dtype differences; variables of different kinds are type conflicts, listed and not compared. An all-null column, which Polars types Null, adopts the other side's dtype. Keys of one kind but different dtypes are cast the same way before pairing. Row order and column order are ignored.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default base DataFrame | LazyFrame

The reference dataset, as a DataFrame or LazyFrame.

required candidate DataFrame | LazyFrame

The dataset measured against the base.

required keys str | Sequence[str]

Variable(s) that identify one observation on each side. Required; the compare refuses to run when a key is missing or not unique on either side.

required by str | Sequence[str] | None

Variable(s) the report is sectioned by. They are prepended to keys automatically, so they need not be repeated there, they label the listing's group column, and the observation and values summaries are additionally reported per group. A group present on one side only raises base_only_groups or candidate_only_groups; the verdict stays global.

None pairs Mapping[str, str] | None

Base variable names mapped to the candidate names that carry them, applied on top of the automatic name matching, so a renamed column is compared rather than reported missing. The report names a paired variable by its base name. A pair whose candidate name is absent reports the base variable as missing from the candidate.

None variables str | Sequence[str] | None

Restrict the comparison to these variables, in base names. A variable outside the restriction is ignored on both sides: it is neither compared nor reported as missing. The default compares every variable that is not a key. A restriction that names only keys is refused.

None abs_tol float

Absolute tolerance on the numeric variables. 0.0 (the default) is exact.

0.0 rel_tol float

Relative tolerance on the numeric variables, as a fraction of the base value. 0.0 (the default) is exact. A numeric pair differs when the absolute difference exceeds max(abs_tol, rel_tol * abs(base)); the relative tolerance anchors on the base because the base is the reference, as in SAS and unlike Polars' testing helper. A tolerant comparison is done in Float64, so integers and decimals beyond 2**53 are compared at that precision; the exact default compares them in their own dtype.

0.0 ignore_trailing_whitespace bool

Strip trailing whitespace from both sides of a string before comparing, so SAS's padded character values equal Fleet's stripped ones. Leading whitespace still differs.

False blank_is_missing bool

Read an empty string as null on both sides, keys included, as SAS does: SAS has one character missing value, the blank. Use it when one side comes from a tool that kept "" (an R data frame without convert_blanks_to_na). Off by default, because the two frames then give different is_null() results.

False allow_duplicates bool

Pair duplicate keys by their position within each key group instead of refusing to run. The observation summary then counts the duplicates per side, the duplicate_keys flag is raised and every renderer warns. Order within a key group decides which observations pair, so it is a weaker guarantee than pairing on keys.

False max_print MaxPrint

Print limits for the text renderer (differences per variable, or a (per_variable, total) pair, or None for everything). The listing on the report is never truncated.

50 base_name str | None

Label for the base in the report, when known.

None candidate_name str | None

Label for the candidate in the report, when known.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description A ComparisonReport

class:~fleet.comparison.ComparisonReport. Differences never

ComparisonReport

raise; check report.is_equal and report.flags.

Raises:

Type Description ComparisonError

A key or BY variable is missing, duplicated (without allow_duplicates) or of an incompatible type on one side, a key reuses a listing column name, a pair or a restriction names a variable no side carries, a restriction names only keys, or a tolerance is negative or not finite.

VerbUsageError

An input is not a Polars frame, or an argument has the wrong type.

Examples:

Prove an independently programmed ADAE reached the production result::

report = fleet.compare(
    adae_prod,
    adae_qc,
    keys=["USUBJID", "AESEQ"],
    base_name="adae (prod)",
    candidate_name="adae (qc)",
)
report.print_report()
assert report.is_equal, report.raised_flags

Section the report by treatment arm, so a difference in one arm stands out::

report = fleet.compare(adsl_prod, adsl_qc, keys="USUBJID", by="TRT01P")
report.observations.per_group

Compare a legacy dataset that named two variables differently, on the variables that are finished::

report = fleet.compare(
    advs_legacy,
    advs_wip,
    keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
    pairs={"AVAL": "RESULT"},
    variables=["AVAL", "AVISIT"],
)
Source code in src/fleet/comparison/engine.py

    rel_tol: float = 0.0,
    ignore_trailing_whitespace: bool = False,
    blank_is_missing: bool = False,
    allow_duplicates: bool = False,
    max_print: MaxPrint = 50,

    candidate_name: str | None = None,

    exact by default: null equals null, NaN equals NaN, null against NaN
    differs.  ``abs_tol`` and ``rel_tol`` widen it on the numeric variables
    and ``ignore_trailing_whitespace`` on the string ones; nulls and NaN
    keep their rule under both.  Variables of the same kind (numeric,
    string, temporal, boolean) but a different dtype compare by value after
    casting to a common supertype and are listed as dtype differences;
    variables of different kinds are type conflicts, listed and not
    compared.  An all-null column, which Polars types ``Null``, adopts the
    other side's dtype.  Keys of one kind but different dtypes are cast the
    same way before pairing.  Row order and column order are ignored.

    Args:
        base: The reference dataset, as a DataFrame or LazyFrame.
        candidate: The dataset measured against the base.
        keys: Variable(s) that identify one observation on each side.
            Required; the compare refuses to run when a key is missing or
            not unique on either side.
        by: Variable(s) the report is sectioned by.  They are prepended to
            ``keys`` automatically, so they need not be repeated there,
            they label the listing's ``group`` column, and the observation
            and values summaries are additionally reported per group.  A
            group present on one side only raises ``base_only_groups`` or
            ``candidate_only_groups``; the verdict stays global.
