from_spec(
    spec_path,
    *,
    dataset=None,
    only=None,
    omit=None,
    strict=True,
    overwrite=False
)

Build a derivation pipeline from a YAML specification file.

Reads either a define.yaml (top-level datasets list where each variable carries a derivation block) or a simplified single-dataset spec (top-level variables list). Every algorithm: is resolved through the central spec registry (:mod:fleet.core.spec_registry), validated against its strict per-algorithm model, and executed via the matching namespace verb.

A top-level ct: block opts the spec into controlled-terminology validation::

ct:
  validate: true
  file: ct/cdisc_ct.yaml   # optional — loaded into the CT cache

With validate: true every assign-family derivation that declares a codelist (assign_ct / hardcode_ct) runs with validate_values=True: out-of-codelist values emit the standard warning naming dataset, variable, and codelist.

Inside a study, a ct_codelist: ID resolves to the class of that ID in the study's generated codelists.py (found from the first study_config.yaml above the spec's folder), so a spec step checks the same terms as assign(..., ct=<class>); an ID the file lacks falls back to the CT loaded in :func:fleet.get_validator. A codelists.py that disagrees with the study warns once per process (see :mod:fleet.ct.study_codelists).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default spec_path str | Path

Path to the YAML specification file.

required dataset str | None

Dataset to execute from a multi-dataset define.yaml (e.g. dataset="DM"). May be omitted when the file contains a single dataset.

None only list[str] | None

Optional allow-list — process only these variable names.

None omit list[str] | None

Optional deny-list — skip these variable names; useful to override a spec variable with custom inline logic. Mutually exclusive with only.

None strict bool

When True (default) an unknown algorithm: raises :class:~fleet.core.exceptions.SpecError. Pass False to restore the legacy warn-and-skip behaviour.

True overwrite bool

When True, allow spec variables to overwrite columns that already exist in the frame. By default an overwrite raises SpecError unless the derivation is a declared carry-through (its source column is the target).

False

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

A namespace pre-loaded with all spec-driven derivations; call .to_frame() to materialise.

Raises:

Type Description SpecError

On unknown algorithms (strict mode), invalid or misspelled derivation fields, column overwrites, unknown fleet_spec_version, or any error raised while executing a variable — always naming file, dataset, and variable.

ValueError

When both only and omit are given, or when dataset is required/unknown.

Examples:

Build and materialise the DM domain from a spec::

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .from_spec("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml", dataset="DM")
    .to_frame()
)

Keep an inline derivation for one variable::

adsl = (
    dm_df.adam
    .from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="ADSL", omit=["TRTSDT"])
    .to_frame()
)

          file: ct/cdisc_ct.yaml   # optional — loaded into the CT cache

    With ``validate: true`` every assign-family derivation that
    declares a codelist (``assign_ct`` / ``hardcode_ct``) runs with
    ``validate_values=True``: out-of-codelist values emit the
    standard warning naming dataset, variable, and codelist.

    Inside a study, a ``ct_codelist:`` ID resolves to the class of
    that ID in the study's generated ``codelists.py`` (found from the
    first ``study_config.yaml`` above the spec's folder), so a spec
    step checks the same terms as ``assign(..., ct=<class>)``; an ID
    the file lacks falls back to the CT loaded in
    :func:`fleet.get_validator`.  A ``codelists.py`` that disagrees
    with the study warns once per process (see
    :mod:`fleet.ct.study_codelists`).

    Args:
        spec_path: Path to the YAML specification file.
        dataset: Dataset to execute from a multi-dataset define.yaml
            (e.g. ``dataset="DM"``).  May be omitted when the file
            contains a single dataset.
        only: Optional allow-list — process only these variable names.
        omit: Optional deny-list — skip these variable names; useful to
            override a spec variable with custom inline logic.
            Mutually exclusive with *only*.
        strict: When ``True`` (default) an unknown ``algorithm:`` raises
            :class:`~fleet.core.exceptions.SpecError`.  Pass ``False``
            to restore the legacy warn-and-skip behaviour.
        overwrite: When ``True``, allow spec variables to overwrite
            columns that already exist in the frame.  By default an
            overwrite raises ``SpecError`` unless the derivation is a
            declared carry-through (its source column *is* the target).

    Returns:
        Self: A namespace pre-loaded with all spec-driven derivations;
            call ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        SpecError: On unknown algorithms (strict mode), invalid or
            misspelled derivation fields, column overwrites, unknown
            ``fleet_spec_version``, or any error raised while executing
            a variable — always naming file, dataset, and variable.
        ValueError: When both *only* and *omit* are given, or when
            *dataset* is required/unknown.

    Examples:
        Build and materialise the DM domain from a spec::

            dm = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .from_spec("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml", dataset="DM")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Keep an inline derivation for one variable::

            adsl = (
                dm_df.adam
                .from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="ADSL", omit=["TRTSDT"])
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.core import spec_registry

    if only is not None and omit is not None:
        raise DerivationError(
            "Cannot specify both only= and omit= in from_spec(). "
            "Use only= to allow-list variables, or omit= to deny-list them."
        )

    path = Path(spec_path)
    spec = load_define_spec(path)
    _check_spec_version(spec, source=str(path))
    _import_derivations_module(spec, source=str(path))

    standard = self._VALIDATE_STANDARD
    ds_name, raw_vars = _extract_spec_variables(spec, dataset)

    ns = self

    # Spec-level CT config: `ct: {validate: true, file: <path>}`.
    if spec.ct.enabled:
        ct_file = spec.ct.file
        if ct_file:
            from fleet.ct.validator import get_validator

            ct_path = Path(ct_file)
            if not ct_path.is_absolute():
                ct_path = path.parent / ct_path
            try:
                get_validator().load_ct_file(ct_path)
            except Exception as err:
                raise SpecError(
                    f"{path}: ct.file '{ct_file}' could not be loaded: {err}"
                ) from err
        ns = copy.copy(ns)
        ns._spec_ct_validate = True
    elif "enabled" in spec.ct.model_fields_set:
        # An explicit `ct: {validate: false}` switches the default CT check off.
        ns = copy.copy(ns)
        ns._spec_ct_validate = False

    # ct_codelist IDs resolve to the study's codelists.py classes, as ct=<class> inline.
    if any(drv.get("ct_codelist") for _, drv in raw_vars):
        from fleet.ct.study_codelists import spec_codelists

        codelists = spec_codelists(path)
        if codelists:
            ns = copy.copy(ns)
            ns._spec_codelists = codelists
    for var_name, drv in raw_vars:
        if only is not None and var_name not in only:
            continue
        if omit is not None and var_name in omit:
            continue

        context = f"{path} → dataset {ds_name} → variable {var_name}"
        alg = drv.get("algorithm")
        algo = spec_registry.get_algorithm(standard, str(alg)) if alg else None
        if algo is None:
            hint = spec_registry.suggest_algorithm(standard, str(alg))
            suffix = f" Did you mean '{hint}'?" if hint else ""
            if strict:
                raise SpecError(
                    f"{context}: unknown algorithm '{alg}' for the {standard} "
                    f"spec path.{suffix} Pass strict=False to warn and skip instead."
                )
            warnings.warn(
                f"from_spec: skipping variable '{var_name}' — "
                f"algorithm '{alg}' is not supported in spec-driven mode.{suffix}",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            continue

        try:
            model = spec_registry.model_for(standard, algo.name)
            var = model.model_validate({**drv, "target": var_name})
        except Exception as err:
            raise SpecError(f"{context}: {err}") from err

        columns = ns._lazy.collect_schema().names()

        # Auto-flush when a declared dependency is not yet committed.
        deps = getattr(var, "depends_on", None) or []
        if deps and any(d not in columns for d in deps):
            ns = ns._materialise_then(ns.to_frame())
            columns = ns._lazy.collect_schema().names()

        if (
            algo.takes_target
            and algo.overwrite_guard
            and not overwrite
            and var.target in columns
            and not spec_registry.is_identity_copy(var)
        ):
            raise SpecError(
                f"{context}: would overwrite the existing column "
                f"'{var.target}'. Pass overwrite=True to allow spec "
                f"overwrites, or omit=[{var.target!r}] to keep the "
                f"inline derivation."
            )

        try:
            ns = spec_registry.execute_variable(ns, var)
        except SpecError:
            raise
        except Exception as err:
            raise SpecError(f"{context}: {type(err).__name__}: {err}") from err

    return ns

to_spec_yaml(dataset=None, path=None, *, predecessor=None)

Serialise the pipeline's lineage into a define.yaml spec.

The natural prototype-then-freeze workflow: build the dataset inline, then emit the equivalent derivation: blocks instead of retyping them. Variables are emitted in frame column order: derived variables carry their derivation: block (last derivation wins when a target was re-derived); CDISC-named carry-through columns are listed as metadata-only entries; raw columns that violate the CDISC name pattern are skipped. Verbs covered by the spec registry emit real blocks; verbs that are not spec-expressible (or whose arguments cannot be serialised, e.g. inline Polars expressions) emit an algorithm: callable stub with a # TODO comment carrying the verb name and sources. Auto-generated by-product columns (e.g. --DTF imputation flags) are listed without a derivation.

The output validates against Fleet's define-spec JSON schema; study-level fields are placeholders to review before use.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dataset str | None

Dataset name for the emitted spec. Defaults to the pipeline's domain context (set by assign("DOMAIN", ...)) or "DATASET".

None path str | Path | None

Optional file path — when given, the YAML is also written there (parent directories are created).

None predecessor str | None

Name of the upstream dataset this ADaM pipeline was built from (e.g. "DM"). When given, variables carried through unchanged — metadata-only entries and pure algorithm: source copies of CDISC-named columns — are emitted with origin: Predecessor and predecessor: '<DATASET>.<SOURCE>'. The emitted YAML stays the explicit, reviewable source of truth; Fleet never infers Predecessor at Define-XML generation time. Columns brought in by merge() leave no lineage and are labeled like carry-throughs — when the pipeline contains a join, a review note is added to the header. ADaM pipelines only.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description str str

The define.yaml document.

Examples:

Freeze an inline DM prototype to a spec::

ns = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
)
yaml_text = ns.to_spec_yaml(dataset="DM", path="specs/define_dm.yaml")
dm = raw_df.sdtm.from_spec("specs/define_dm.yaml", dataset="DM").to_frame()

Freeze an ADSL prototype, labelling DM carry-throughs::

adsl_ns.to_spec_yaml(dataset="ADSL", predecessor="DM")
Source code in src/fleet/core/_verb_mixin.py 
def to_spec_yaml(
    self,
    dataset: str | None = None,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    predecessor: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Serialise the pipeline's lineage into a define.yaml spec.

    The natural prototype-then-freeze workflow: build the dataset
    inline, then emit the equivalent ``derivation:`` blocks instead
    of retyping them.  Variables are emitted in frame column order:
    derived variables carry their ``derivation:`` block (last
    derivation wins when a target was re-derived); CDISC-named
    carry-through columns are listed as metadata-only entries; raw
    columns that violate the CDISC name pattern are skipped.  Verbs
    covered by the spec registry emit real blocks; verbs that are
    not spec-expressible (or whose arguments cannot be serialised,
    e.g. inline Polars expressions) emit an ``algorithm: callable``
    stub with a ``# TODO`` comment carrying the verb name and
    sources.  Auto-generated by-product columns (e.g. ``--DTF``
    imputation flags) are listed without a derivation.

    The output validates against Fleet's define-spec JSON schema;
    study-level fields are placeholders to review before use.

    Args:
        dataset: Dataset name for the emitted spec.  Defaults to the
            pipeline's domain context (set by ``assign("DOMAIN",
            ...)``) or ``"DATASET"``.
        path: Optional file path — when given, the YAML is also
            written there (parent directories are created).
        predecessor: Name of the upstream dataset this ADaM pipeline
            was built from (e.g. ``"DM"``).  When given, variables
            carried through unchanged — metadata-only entries and
            pure ``algorithm: source`` copies of CDISC-named columns
            — are emitted with ``origin: Predecessor`` and
            ``predecessor: '<DATASET>.<SOURCE>'``.  The emitted YAML
            stays the explicit, reviewable source of truth; Fleet
            never infers Predecessor at Define-XML generation time.
            Columns brought in by ``merge()`` leave no lineage and
            are labeled like carry-throughs — when the pipeline
            contains a join, a review note is added to the header.
            ADaM pipelines only.

    Returns:
        str: The define.yaml document.

    Examples:
        Freeze an inline DM prototype to a spec::

            ns = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
            )
            yaml_text = ns.to_spec_yaml(dataset="DM", path="specs/define_dm.yaml")
            dm = raw_df.sdtm.from_spec("specs/define_dm.yaml", dataset="DM").to_frame()

        Freeze an ADSL prototype, labelling DM carry-throughs::

            adsl_ns.to_spec_yaml(dataset="ADSL", predecessor="DM")
    """
    from fleet.core import spec_registry
    from fleet.core.lineage import latest_lineage_of
    from fleet.validation.run_setup import DEFAULT_IG_VERSIONS

    standard = self._VALIDATE_STANDARD
    ds_name = (dataset or getattr(self, "_domain", None) or "DATASET").upper()

    pred_ds = predecessor.upper() if predecessor else None
    if pred_ds:
        if standard != "adam":
            raise DerivationError(
                "to_spec_yaml(predecessor=...) applies to ADaM pipelines only — "
                "SDTM variables built from raw data are Collected/Derived, not "
                "Predecessor."
            )
        if not re.match(r"^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,7}$", pred_ds):
            raise DerivationError(
                f"to_spec_yaml(): predecessor {predecessor!r} is not a valid "
                "dataset name (expected e.g. 'DM' or 'ADSL')."
            )

    schema = self._lazy.collect_schema()
    derived = {n.name: n for n in latest_lineage_of(self)}
    name_pattern = re.compile(r"^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,7}$")

    entries: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], str | None]] = []
    for col in schema.names():
        node = derived.get(col)
        if node is None and not name_pattern.match(col):
            continue  # raw scratch column — not part of the dataset spec
        entry: dict[str, Any] = {
            "name": col,
            "label": col,
            "type": _dtype_to_spec_type(schema.get(col)),
        }
        comment: str | None = None
        if node is not None:
            status, block, meta = spec_registry.derivation_from_lineage(standard, node)
            if meta.get("label"):
                entry["label"] = str(meta["label"])[:40]
            if meta.get("origin"):
                entry["origin"] = meta["origin"]
            if status == "ok":
                # A pure copy of a CDISC-named upstream column is a
                # Predecessor in Define-XML terms; an explicit origin
                # captured from the verb call wins.
                source = str(block.get("source") or col) if block else col
                if (
                    pred_ds
                    and "origin" not in entry
                    and block
                    and block.get("algorithm") == "source"
                    and name_pattern.match(source)
                ):
                    entry["origin"] = "Predecessor"
                    entry["predecessor"] = f"{pred_ds}.{source}"
                entry["derivation"] = block
            elif status == "stub":
                srcs = ", ".join(node.sources) if node.sources else "none"
                comment = (
                    f"TODO: verb '{node.verb}' (sources: {srcs}) is not spec-expressible "
                    f"— replace this stub with a registered derivation "
                    f"(algorithm: callable)."
                )
                entry["derivation"] = {
                    "algorithm": "callable",
                    "callable": f"TODO_{col}",
                }
            # status == "byproduct": metadata-only (auto-generated column).
        elif pred_ds:
            # Metadata-only carry-through — flowed in untouched.
            entry["origin"] = "Predecessor"
            entry["predecessor"] = f"{pred_ds}.{col}"
        entries.append((entry, comment))

    if not entries:
        raise DerivationError(
            "to_spec_yaml(): nothing to serialise — the frame has no derived "
            "variables and no CDISC-named columns."
        )

    stubs = [entry["name"] for entry, comment in entries if comment]
    if stubs:
        warnings.warn(
            f"to_spec_yaml: {len(stubs)} variable(s) have no reviewer-facing "
            f"derivation text for Define-XML ({', '.join(stubs)}) — add a "
            "`comment:` in the spec or wrap the logic in a @derivation callable.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    var_names = [e["name"] for e, _ in entries]
    keys = [k for k in ("STUDYID", "USUBJID") if k in var_names] or var_names[:1]

    study = {
        "id": "STUDY",
        "name": "STUDY",
        "description": (
            "Generated by Fleet to_spec_yaml() — replace with the study description."
        ),
        "protocol_name": "STUDY",
        "originator": "Fleet",
        "standard": "SDTMIG" if standard == "sdtm" else "ADAMIG",
        "standard_version": DEFAULT_IG_VERSIONS[standard],
    }
    head = {"fleet_spec_version": SUPPORTED_SPEC_VERSION, "study": study}
    ds_head = {
        "name": ds_name,
        "label": ds_name,
        "structure": "One record per observation (review)",
        "keys": keys,
    }

    lines: list[str] = [
        "# Generated by Fleet to_spec_yaml() — review study fields, labels, keys,",
        "# and TODO stubs before use.",
    ]
    if pred_ds and "JOIN" in self._lazy.explain().upper():
        lines.append(
            f"# predecessor={pred_ds!r}: this pipeline merges other datasets, and "
            "merged-in columns"
        )
        lines.append(
            f"# are indistinguishable from {pred_ds} carry-throughs — review each "
            "predecessor: entry."
        )
    lines += [
        yaml.safe_dump(head, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True).rstrip(),
        "datasets:",
        _indent_yaml(yaml.safe_dump([ds_head], sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True), 2),
        "    variables:",
    ]
    for entry, comment in entries:
        block_text = _indent_yaml(
            yaml.safe_dump([entry], sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True), 6
        )
        if comment:
            block_lines: list[str] = []
            for ln in block_text.splitlines():
                if ln.strip().startswith("derivation:"):
                    pad = ln[: len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip())]
                    block_lines.append(f"{pad}# {comment}")
                block_lines.append(ln)
            block_text = "\n".join(block_lines)
        lines.append(block_text)

    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    if path is not None:
        dest = Path(path)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return text

nodup(*, subset, sort_by=None, keep=None, descending=False)

Detect duplicate rows and optionally deduplicate after sorting.

Materialises the pipeline, logs duplicate diagnostics through the "fleet" logger (stdout by default — see :mod:fleet.core.log), and optionally removes duplicates. When keep is None (default) the verb operates in report-only mode — duplicates are reported but the frame is returned unchanged, making it safe to insert anywhere in a pipeline for auditing purposes. The duplicate rows are also attached to the returned namespace and retrievable via :attr:last_nodup_report.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default subset list[str]

Column(s) that define the uniqueness key.

required sort_by list[str] | None

Column(s) to sort by before deduplication. Required when keep is not None.

None keep Literal['first', 'last'] | None

Which duplicate to retain after sorting: "first", "last", or None (report only, no removal).

None descending bool | list[bool]

Sort direction(s) for sort_by. A single bool applies to all columns; a list must match sort_by length.

False

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

A fresh namespace wrapping the (optionally deduplicated) frame, carrying the duplicates in last_nodup_report; call .to_frame() to materialise.

Raises:

Type Description DerivationError

If keep is set but sort_by is not provided, or keep is not one of the accepted values.

Examples:

Report-only mode (audit duplicates without removing)::

ae = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .nodup(subset=["USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AESTDTC"])
    .to_frame()
)

Sort and deduplicate (keep latest record)::

adae = (
    ae_df.adam.occds
    .nodup(
        subset=["USUBJID", "AEDECOD"],
        sort_by=["ASTDT", "ASEQ"],
        keep="last",
        descending=True,
    )
    .to_frame()
)

def nodup(
    self,
    *,
    subset: list[str],
    sort_by: list[str] | None = None,
    keep: Literal["first", "last"] | None = None,
    descending: bool | list[bool] = False,
) -> Self:
    """Detect duplicate rows and optionally deduplicate after sorting.

    Materialises the pipeline, logs duplicate diagnostics through the
    ``"fleet"`` logger (stdout by default — see :mod:`fleet.core.log`),
    and optionally removes duplicates.  When ``keep`` is ``None``
    (default) the verb operates in report-only mode — duplicates are
    reported but the frame is returned unchanged, making it safe to
    insert anywhere in a pipeline for auditing purposes.  The
    duplicate rows are also attached to the returned namespace and
    retrievable via :attr:`last_nodup_report`.

    Args:
        subset: Column(s) that define the uniqueness key.
        sort_by: Column(s) to sort by before deduplication.  Required
            when ``keep`` is not ``None``.
        keep: Which duplicate to retain after sorting:
            ``"first"``, ``"last"``, or ``None`` (report only, no removal).
        descending: Sort direction(s) for *sort_by*.  A single ``bool``
            applies to all columns; a list must match *sort_by* length.

    Returns:
        Self: A fresh namespace wrapping the (optionally deduplicated)
            frame, carrying the duplicates in ``last_nodup_report``;
            call ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: If ``keep`` is set but ``sort_by`` is not
            provided, or ``keep`` is not one of the accepted values.

    Examples:
        Report-only mode (audit duplicates without removing)::

            ae = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                .nodup(subset=["USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AESTDTC"])
                .to_frame()
            )

        Sort and deduplicate (keep latest record)::

            adae = (
                ae_df.adam.occds
                .nodup(
                    subset=["USUBJID", "AEDECOD"],
                    sort_by=["ASTDT", "ASEQ"],
                    keep="last",
                    descending=True,
                )
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if keep is not None and sort_by is None:
        raise DerivationError("sort_by is required when keep is set.")
    if keep is not None and keep not in ("first", "last"):
        raise DerivationError(f"keep must be 'first', 'last', or None — got {keep!r}.")

    fleet_log.ensure_default_handler()
    df = self._lazy.collect()

    # Detect duplicates
    dup_mask = df.select(pl.struct(subset).is_duplicated()).to_series()
    n_dup = dup_mask.sum()
    dup_rows = df.filter(dup_mask)

    if n_dup == 0:
        logger.info("[NODUP] No duplicates found (subset: %s)", ", ".join(subset))
        new = self._materialise_then(df)
        new._nodup_report = dup_rows
        return new

    # Summarise duplicate groups
    dup_groups = (
        dup_rows.group_by(subset)
        .agg(pl.len().alias("__count"))
        .sort("__count", descending=True)
    )
    n_groups = len(dup_groups)

    logger.info(
        "[NODUP] %d duplicate rows across %d key group(s) (subset: %s)",
        n_dup,
        n_groups,
        ", ".join(subset),
    )
    # Show top offending groups (up to 5)
    top = dup_groups.head(5)
    logger.info("[NODUP] Top offenders:")
    for row in top.iter_rows(named=True):
        count = row.pop("__count")
        key_str = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in row.items())
        logger.info("  %s  (%d rows)", key_str, count)

    # Report-only mode
    if keep is None:
        logger.info("[NODUP] Action: report only (keep=None)")
        new = self._materialise_then(df)
        new._nodup_report = dup_rows
        return new

    # Sort then deduplicate
    df = df.sort(sort_by, descending=descending)
    df = df.unique(subset=subset, keep=keep, maintain_order=True)

    logger.info(
        "[NODUP] Action: keeping '%s' after sorting by %s (descending=%s)",
        keep,
        sort_by,
        descending,
    )
    logger.info("[NODUP] Result: %d rows (removed %d)", len(df), n_dup - n_groups)
    new = self._materialise_then(df)
    new._nodup_report = dup_rows
    return new

docs.title: fleet.core.exceptions
docs.text:
Core exceptions for fleet.

The verb-layer exceptions use dual inheritance so both catch styles work: except FleetError (the Fleet-native style) and the legacy builtin style (except ValueError / except TypeError / except LookupError) that predates the hierarchy.

  • :class:DerivationError — a verb received invalid values or arguments (missing column, unparseable expression, unsupported option, ...). Catchable as ValueError.
  • :class:VerbUsageError — a verb was called with a wrong type. Catchable as TypeError.
  • :class:PinError — a cross-domain verb could not resolve a pinned reference domain. Catchable as LookupError.

docs.title: Controlled Terminology
docs.text:
Fleet provides three layers for working with CDISC Controlled Terminology:

  1. CDISC Library API client — download CT directly from the authoritative source.
  2. Code generator — turn API responses into typed Python constants with IDE auto-completion.
  3. CT validator — validate values at runtime against loaded codelists.

docs.title: CDISC Library API Client
docs.text:
The CDISCClient wraps httpx to authenticate against the CDISC Library REST API. It requires an API key set via a .env file or the CDISC_API_KEY environment variable.

docs.text:
HTTP client for the CDISC Library REST API.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default config CDISCClientConfig

Optional explicit configuration. When omitted the client auto-discovers credentials from the environment / .env.

CDISCClientConfig()

Examples:

Fetch the SEX codelist::

client = CDISCClient()
terms = client.get_codelist("C66731")
Source code in src/fleet/ct/api.py 
@dataclass
class CDISCClient:
    """HTTP client for the CDISC Library REST API.

    Args:
        config: Optional explicit configuration.  When omitted the client
            auto-discovers credentials from the environment / ``.env``.

    Examples:
        Fetch the SEX codelist::

            client = CDISCClient()
            terms = client.get_codelist("C66731")
    """

    config: CDISCClientConfig = field(default_factory=CDISCClientConfig)
    _http: httpx.Client = field(init=False, repr=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.config.api_key:
            raise CTError(
                "CDISC API key is required. Set the CDISC_API_KEY environment "
                "variable, add it to a .env file, or pass it explicitly via "
                "CDISCClientConfig(api_key=...)."
            )
        self._http = httpx.Client(
            base_url=self.config.base_url,
            headers={
                "api-key": self.config.api_key,
                "Accept": "application/json",
            },
            timeout=30.0,
            follow_redirects=True,
        )

    # -- public helpers ------------------------------------------------- #

    def get_packages(self, product: str = "sdtmct") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """List available CT packages for a product.

        Args:
            product: Product key recognised by the CDISC Library
                (e.g. ``"sdtmct"``, ``"adamct"``).

        Returns:
            List of package metadata dicts (keys vary by CDISC version).

        Raises:
            CTError: On network or authentication failure.
        """
        data = self._get(f"/mdr/ct/packages?type={product}")
        packages: list[dict[str, Any]] = data.get("_links", {}).get("packages", [])
        return packages

    def get_codelist(
        self,
        concept_id: str,
        *,
        package: str = "sdtmct-2023-12-15",
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Download a single codelist by NCI concept ID.

        Args:
            concept_id: NCI concept identifier (e.g. ``"C66731"``).
            package: CT package version string.

        Returns:
            Raw JSON dict from the CDISC Library containing
            ``submissionValue``, ``conceptId``, ``terms``, etc.

        Raises:
            CTError: On network, authentication, or 404 errors.
        """
        return self._get(f"/mdr/ct/packages/{package}/codelists/{concept_id}")

    # -- internals ------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _get(self, path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Perform an authenticated GET and return the JSON payload."""
        try:
            response = self._http.get(path)
            response.raise_for_status()
            return response.json()  # type: ignore[no-any-return]
        except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
            status = exc.response.status_code
            if status == 401:
                raise CTError(
                    "CDISC API authentication failed (401). Check your CDISC_API_KEY."
                ) from exc
            if status == 404:
                raise CTNotFoundError(f"Resource not found on CDISC Library: {path}") from exc
            raise CTError(f"CDISC API request failed ({status}): {exc}") from exc
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            raise CTError(f"Network error contacting CDISC Library: {exc}") from exc

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the underlying HTTP transport."""
        self._http.close()

    def __enter__(self) -> CDISCClient:
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:
        self.close()

@dataclass
class CDISCClientConfig:
    """Configuration for the CDISC Library API client.

    Values are resolved in order:
    1. Explicit constructor arguments.
    2. Environment variables (``CDISC_API_KEY``, ``CDISC_BASE_URL``).
    3. A ``.env`` file in the working directory (loaded lazily via *dotenv*
       if the ``python-dotenv`` package is installed).

    Args:
        api_key: CDISC Library API key.
        base_url: Root URL for the CDISC Library API.
    """

    api_key: str = ""
    base_url: str = _DEFAULT_BASE_URL

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.api_key:
            try_load_dotenv()
            self.api_key = os.environ.get("CDISC_API_KEY", "")
        if self.base_url == _DEFAULT_BASE_URL:
            env_url = os.environ.get("CDISC_BASE_URL", "")
            if env_url:
                self.base_url = env_url.rstrip("/")

docs.title: Codelist Code Generator
docs.text: The CodelistGenerator converts CDISC Library JSON responses into a Python module containing typed classes — one per codelist — with human-readable aliases and IDE auto-completion support.

docs.title: Recommended workflow
docs.text:
# Bootstrap from the SDTM IG (source of truth)
fleet add-ct --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --output specs/my_study/sdtm/codelists.py

# Add domains later (preserves existing codelists)
fleet add-ct --domains LB,CM --output specs/my_study/sdtm/codelists.py

docs.title: Programmatic usage
docs.text:
from fleet.ct.api import CDISCClient
from fleet.ct.generator import CodelistGenerator

with CDISCClient() as client:
    # Recommended: derive codelists from the SDTM IG
    gen = CodelistGenerator.from_sdtm_ig(
        client,
        domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"],
        package="sdtmct-2025-09-26",
    )
    gen.write("specs/my_study/sdtm/codelists.py")

docs.title: Generated output
docs.text:
The generated codelists.py contains:

  • One class per codelist with _concept_id, _cdisc_url, and submission-value constants:
class C66731:
    """SEX (C66731).

    The assemblage of physical properties or qualities by which male is
    distinguished from female.

    See: https://library.cdisc.org/browser/#/codelist/C66731
    """

    _concept_id = "C66731"
    _cdisc_url = "https://library.cdisc.org/browser/#/codelist/C66731"
    F = "F"
    M = "M"
    U = "U"

!!! tip "Direct line to the source of truth" The _cdisc_url attribute and the See: line in each docstring point to the codelist's entry in the CDISC Library Browser. When a reviewer or auditor reads pipeline code, hovering SEX in an IDE shows the URL; clicking the link in the docs site takes them straight to the authoritative CDISC definition. There is no separate lookup table to maintain — the URL is constructed from the NCI concept ID at generation time.

  • Human-readable aliases derived from the CDISC submission value:
SEX = C66731
RACE = C74457
  • __all__ for clean wildcard imports:
from codelists import SEX, RACE

# or
from codelists import *
  • __ct_package__ at the top, naming the CT package every class came from (__ct_package__ = "sdtmct-2025-09-26"). A file with codelists from an SDTM and an ADaM package has __ct_packages__ instead (("adamct-2023-06-30", "sdtmct-2023-12-15")). The stale checks compare them with ct.package and ct.adam_package in study_config.yaml.

docs.title: Importing codelists in standalone study projects
docs.text:
When your study lives in its own directory (not inside the Fleet repo), the generated codelists.py isn't on the Python path by default. Use import_codelists() to load it dynamically:

from fleet.ct import import_codelists

# Strategy 1: auto-discover via study_config.yaml in CWD
ct = import_codelists()
SEX = ct.SEX

# Strategy 2: register in sys.modules so bare imports work
import_codelists()  # one-time call
from codelists import SEX, RACE  # works for the rest of the session

# Strategy 3: explicit path (non-standard locations)
ct = import_codelists("/absolute/path/to/codelists.py")

Resolution order

When called without arguments, import_codelists() resolves the file as follows:

  1. study_config.yaml in CWD → reads paths.metadata_sdtm → appends /codelists.py
  2. Falls back to <CWD>/metadata/sdtm/codelists.py

This means cd-ing into your study root before running a script is all you need.

docs.title: Using generated codelists in pipelines
docs.text:
from fleet.ct import import_codelists

ct = import_codelists()

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=ct.SEX)
    .assign("RACE", source="race", ct=ct.RACE)
    .to_frame()
)

assign(ct=...) accepts either a codelist class (SEX) or a raw NCI concept ID string ("C66731"). The class form is preferred for readability and auto-completion.

Accumulates CDISC codelist JSON responses and renders them as Python.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default include_docs bool

If True (default), inject definition and preferredTerm from the CDISC JSON into class/attribute docstrings for richer AI context.

True cdisc_url_template str

URL template used to build the _cdisc_url class attribute and the See: reference in each codelist's docstring. Substitution fields available: {concept_id}, {package} (e.g. sdtmct-2024-12-13), and {date} (the package date suffix). Defaults to the CDISC Library Browser deep link, which requires all three.

'https://library.cdisc.org/browser/#/mdr/ct/{date}/packages/{package}/codelists/{concept_id}' Source code in src/fleet/ct/generator.py 
@dataclass
class CodelistGenerator:
    """Accumulates CDISC codelist JSON responses and renders them as Python.

    Args:
        include_docs: If ``True`` (default), inject ``definition`` and
            ``preferredTerm`` from the CDISC JSON into class/attribute
            docstrings for richer AI context.
        cdisc_url_template: URL template used to build the
            ``_cdisc_url`` class attribute and the ``See:`` reference in
            each codelist's docstring.  Substitution fields available:
            ``{concept_id}``, ``{package}`` (e.g. ``sdtmct-2024-12-13``),
            and ``{date}`` (the package date suffix).  Defaults to the
            CDISC Library Browser deep link, which requires all three.
    """

    include_docs: bool = True
    cdisc_url_template: str = (
        "https://library.cdisc.org/browser/#/mdr/ct/{date}/packages/"
        "{package}/codelists/{concept_id}"
    )
    _codelists: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)

    def add_codelist(
        self,
        codelist_json: dict[str, Any],
        *,
        package: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Register a raw CDISC Library codelist JSON response.

        Args:
            codelist_json: Dict returned by ``CDISCClient.get_codelist``.
                Must contain at least ``conceptId`` and ``terms``.
            package: Optional CT package the codelist was fetched from
                (e.g. ``"sdtmct-2024-12-13"``).  Stored on the codelist
                dict as ``_package`` so the rendered ``_cdisc_url`` can
                include the correct package + date context required by
                the CDISC Library Browser.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If required keys are missing.
        """
        if "conceptId" not in codelist_json:
            raise ValueError("codelist JSON must contain 'conceptId'")
        if package is not None:
            codelist_json = {**codelist_json, "_package": package}
        self._codelists.append(codelist_json)

    @property
    def concept_ids(self) -> set[str]:
        """Return the set of concept IDs already loaded."""
        return {cl["conceptId"] for cl in self._codelists}

    @property
    def codelist_count(self) -> int:
        """Return the number of codelists registered so far."""
        return len(self._codelists)

    @classmethod
    def from_concept_ids(
        cls,
        client: CDISCClient,
        concept_ids: set[str],
        *,
        package: str = "sdtmct-2023-12-15",
        adam_package: str | None = None,
        include_docs: bool = True,
    ) -> CodelistGenerator:
        """Build a generator from an explicit set of NCI concept IDs.

        Each codelist comes from the first package that holds it: *package*
        (SDTM CT), then *adam_package* (ADaM CT, for codelists such as
        DTYPE that only ADaM CT publishes).

        Args:
            client: An authenticated ``CDISCClient`` instance.
            concept_ids: Set of NCI concept ID strings to download.
            package: SDTM CT package version to download from.
            adam_package: ADaM CT package asked second; ``None`` for SDTM only.
            include_docs: Whether to include definitions in generated output.

        Returns:
            A ``CodelistGenerator`` populated with the requested codelists.

        Raises:
            CTError: When no pinned package holds a codelist (each ID is
                named), or on an authentication or network error.

        Examples:
            Generate codelists for specific concept IDs::

                from fleet.ct.api import CDISCClient
                from fleet.ct.generator import CodelistGenerator

                with CDISCClient() as client:
                    gen = CodelistGenerator.from_concept_ids(
                        client,
                        {"C66731", "C81224"},
                        adam_package="adamct-2023-06-30",
                    )
                    gen.write("codelists.py")
        """
        from fleet.core.exceptions import CTError, CTNotFoundError

        pins = [p for p in (package, adam_package) if p]
        gen = cls(include_docs=include_docs)
        missing: list[str] = []
        for cid in sorted(concept_ids):
            for pin in pins:
                try:
                    gen.add_codelist(client.get_codelist(cid, package=pin), package=pin)
                    break
                except CTNotFoundError:
                    continue
            else:
                missing.append(cid)
        if missing:
            raise CTError(
                f"{len(missing)} codelist(s) are in no pinned CT package "
                f"({', '.join(pins)}): {', '.join(missing)}. Correct the codelist id in "
                "define.yaml, or pin the package that holds it in study_config.yaml "
                "(ct.package, ct.adam_package)."
            )
        return gen

    @classmethod
    def from_sdtm_ig(
        cls,
        client: CDISCClient,
        domains: list[str],
        *,
        ig_version: str = "3-4",
        package: str = "sdtmct-2023-12-15",
        include_docs: bool = True,
    ) -> CodelistGenerator:
        """Build a generator from the SDTM IG — the authoritative source of truth.

        Queries the CDISC Library for the specified SDTM IG version,
        extracts every codelist referenced by variables in the requested
        domains, and downloads the corresponding CT definitions.

        Args:
            client: An authenticated ``CDISCClient`` instance.
            domains: List of SDTM domain abbreviations to include
                (e.g. ``["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]``).
            ig_version: SDTM IG version (default ``"3-4"``).
            package: CT package version to download terms from.
            include_docs: Whether to include definitions in generated output.

        Returns:
            A ``CodelistGenerator`` populated with all referenced codelists.

        Examples:
            Generate codelists for DM and AE from SDTM IG 3.4::

                from fleet.ct.api import CDISCClient
                from fleet.ct.generator import CodelistGenerator

                with CDISCClient() as client:
                    gen = CodelistGenerator.from_sdtm_ig(
                        client,
                        domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"],
                    )
                    gen.write("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/codelists.py")
        """
        concept_ids = extract_ig_concept_ids(client, ig_version, domains)
        return cls.from_concept_ids(
            client,
            concept_ids,
            package=package,
            include_docs=include_docs,
        )

    def render(self) -> str:
        """Render accumulated codelists as a Python module string.

        Returns:
            A complete, syntactically valid Python source string.
        """
        sorted_cls = sorted(self._codelists, key=lambda c: c["conceptId"])

        lines: list[str] = [
            '"""Auto-generated CDISC Controlled Terminology constants.',
            "",
            "Do not edit manually — regenerate with ``fleet.ct.generator``.",
            '"""',
            "",
        ]
        # Marker for the stale checks of fleet.ct.study_codelists; two dates of one
        # product (two SDTM CT packages) get none, so check b reports the mix.
        packages = {cl.get("_package") for cl in sorted_cls}
        products = {str(p).split("-", 1)[0] for p in packages}
        if len(packages) == 1 and None not in packages:
            lines += [f"__ct_package__ = {packages.pop()!r}", "", ""]
        elif None not in packages and len(products) == len(packages) > 1:
            lines += [f"__ct_packages__ = {tuple(sorted(packages))!r}", "", ""]

        # Class definitions
        for cl in sorted_cls:
            lines.extend(self._render_class(cl))
            lines.append("")

        # Human-readable aliases  (e.g.  SEX = C66731)
        aliases: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        for cl in sorted_cls:
            concept_id = cl["conceptId"]
            class_name = _safe_identifier(concept_id)
            alias = self._alias_for(cl)
            if alias and alias != class_name:
                aliases.append((alias, class_name))

        if aliases:
            lines.append("")
            lines.append("# Human-readable aliases")
            for alias, class_name in sorted(aliases):
                lines.append(f"{alias} = {class_name}")
            lines.append("")

        # __all__
        all_names: list[str] = [_safe_identifier(cl["conceptId"]) for cl in sorted_cls]
        all_names.extend(alias for alias, _ in sorted(aliases))
        all_names.sort()
        all_repr = ", ".join(f'"{n}"' for n in all_names)
        lines.append(f"__all__ = [{all_repr}]")
        lines.append("")

        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

    def write(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
        """Render and write the module to *path*.

        Parent directories are created if they do not exist.

        Args:
            path: Destination file path.

        Returns:
            Resolved ``Path`` of the written file.
        """
        dest = Path(path)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest.write_text(self.render(), encoding="utf-8")
        return dest.resolve()

    def define_terms(self) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """The ``codelists:`` entry of ``define.yaml`` for each loaded codelist, by concept ID.

        Returns:
            dict[str, dict[str, Any]]: ``{"name": ..., "items": [{"coded_value": ...,
                "decode": ...}]}``; the decode is the NCI preferred term.
        """
        return {
            cl["conceptId"]: {
                "name": cl.get("name") or cl.get("submissionValue") or cl["conceptId"],
                "items": [
                    {
                        "coded_value": t["submissionValue"],
                        "decode": t.get("preferredTerm") or t["submissionValue"],
                    }
                    for t in cl.get("terms", [])
                ],
            }
            for cl in self._codelists
        }

    # -- private -------------------------------------------------------- #

    def _render_class(self, cl: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
        concept_id: str = cl["conceptId"]
        class_name = _safe_identifier(concept_id)
        submission_value: str = cl.get("submissionValue", concept_id)
        preferred_term: str = cl.get("preferredTerm", "")
        definition: str = cl.get("definition", "")
        cdisc_url: str | None = self._build_cdisc_url(cl)

        # Class docstring
        doc_parts = [f"{submission_value} ({concept_id})."]
        if self.include_docs and definition:
            doc_parts.append("")
            doc_parts.append(textwrap.fill(definition, width=76))
        # Always add the CDISC Library reference so reviewers can jump from
        # generated code to the authoritative source-of-truth definition.
        if cdisc_url:
            doc_parts.append("")
            doc_parts.append(f"See: {cdisc_url}")

        class_doc = "\n    ".join(doc_parts)
        lines = [
            f"class {class_name}:",
            f'    """{class_doc}"""',
            "",
            f"    _concept_id = {concept_id!r}",
        ]
        if cdisc_url:
            lines.append(f"    _cdisc_url = {cdisc_url!r}")

        if self.include_docs and preferred_term:
            lines.append(f"    _preferred_term = {preferred_term!r}")
        lines.append("")

        terms: list[dict[str, Any]] = cl.get("terms", [])
        if not terms:
            lines.append("    pass")
            return lines

        submission_values = sorted({t.get("submissionValue", "") for t in terms} - {""})
        # Two terms can share one attribute name (2 and 3 TIMES PER WEEK).
        lines.append(f"    _terms = {tuple(submission_values)!r}")
        lines.append("")

        for term in sorted(terms, key=lambda t: t.get("submissionValue", "")):
            sv: str = term.get("submissionValue", "")
            if not sv:
                continue
            attr = _safe_identifier(sv)
            lines.append(f"    {attr} = {sv!r}")

            if self.include_docs:
                term_def = term.get("definition", "")
                if term_def:
                    comment = textwrap.shorten(term_def, width=72)
                    lines.append(f"    # {comment}")

        return lines

    def _build_cdisc_url(self, cl: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
        """Format the CDISC Library Browser URL for *cl*.

        Returns ``None`` when the template requires a ``{package}`` or
        ``{date}`` field but no package was recorded for this codelist
        (e.g. when ``add_codelist`` was called without ``package=``).
        """
        concept_id: str = cl["conceptId"]
        package: str | None = cl.get("_package")
        date: str | None = None
        if package and "-" in package:
            # e.g. "sdtmct-2024-12-13" -> "2024-12-13"
            _, _, date = package.partition("-")
        # If the template needs package/date context but none was
        # recorded, skip the URL rather than emit a broken link.
        needs_package = "{package}" in self.cdisc_url_template
        needs_date = "{date}" in self.cdisc_url_template
        if (needs_package and not package) or (needs_date and not date):
            return None
        try:
            return self.cdisc_url_template.format(
                concept_id=concept_id,
                package=package or "",
                date=date or "",
            )
        except KeyError:
            return None

    @staticmethod
    def _alias_for(cl: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
        """Derive a human-readable alias from the codelist submission value.

        Returns a valid Python identifier (e.g. ``"SEX"``, ``"RACE"``,
        ``"ETHNIC"``) or ``None`` when no usable name can be derived.
        """
        sv: str = cl.get("submissionValue", "")
        if not sv:
            return None
        return _safe_identifier(sv)

def add_codelist(
    self,
    codelist_json: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    package: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Register a raw CDISC Library codelist JSON response.

    Args:
        codelist_json: Dict returned by ``CDISCClient.get_codelist``.
            Must contain at least ``conceptId`` and ``terms``.
        package: Optional CT package the codelist was fetched from
            (e.g. ``"sdtmct-2024-12-13"``).  Stored on the codelist
            dict as ``_package`` so the rendered ``_cdisc_url`` can
            include the correct package + date context required by
            the CDISC Library Browser.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If required keys are missing.
    """
    if "conceptId" not in codelist_json:
        raise ValueError("codelist JSON must contain 'conceptId'")
    if package is not None:
        codelist_json = {**codelist_json, "_package": package}
    self._codelists.append(codelist_json)

@classmethod
def from_concept_ids(
    cls,
    client: CDISCClient,
    concept_ids: set[str],
    *,
    package: str = "sdtmct-2023-12-15",
    adam_package: str | None = None,
    include_docs: bool = True,
) -> CodelistGenerator:
    """Build a generator from an explicit set of NCI concept IDs.

    Each codelist comes from the first package that holds it: *package*
    (SDTM CT), then *adam_package* (ADaM CT, for codelists such as
    DTYPE that only ADaM CT publishes).

    Args:
        client: An authenticated ``CDISCClient`` instance.
        concept_ids: Set of NCI concept ID strings to download.
        package: SDTM CT package version to download from.
        adam_package: ADaM CT package asked second; ``None`` for SDTM only.
        include_docs: Whether to include definitions in generated output.

    Returns:
        A ``CodelistGenerator`` populated with the requested codelists.

    Raises:
        CTError: When no pinned package holds a codelist (each ID is
            named), or on an authentication or network error.

    Examples:
        Generate codelists for specific concept IDs::

            from fleet.ct.api import CDISCClient
            from fleet.ct.generator import CodelistGenerator

            with CDISCClient() as client:
                gen = CodelistGenerator.from_concept_ids(
                    client,
                    {"C66731", "C81224"},
                    adam_package="adamct-2023-06-30",
                )
                gen.write("codelists.py")
    """
    from fleet.core.exceptions import CTError, CTNotFoundError

    pins = [p for p in (package, adam_package) if p]
    gen = cls(include_docs=include_docs)
    missing: list[str] = []
    for cid in sorted(concept_ids):
        for pin in pins:
            try:
                gen.add_codelist(client.get_codelist(cid, package=pin), package=pin)
                break
            except CTNotFoundError:
                continue
        else:
            missing.append(cid)
    if missing:
        raise CTError(
            f"{len(missing)} codelist(s) are in no pinned CT package "
            f"({', '.join(pins)}): {', '.join(missing)}. Correct the codelist id in "
            "define.yaml, or pin the package that holds it in study_config.yaml "
            "(ct.package, ct.adam_package)."
        )
    return gen

    ig_version: str = "3-4",

    Queries the CDISC Library for the specified SDTM IG version,
    extracts every codelist referenced by variables in the requested
    domains, and downloads the corresponding CT definitions.

    Args:

        domains: List of SDTM domain abbreviations to include
            (e.g. ``["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]``).

def render(self) -> str:
    """Render accumulated codelists as a Python module string.

    Returns:
        A complete, syntactically valid Python source string.
    """
    sorted_cls = sorted(self._codelists, key=lambda c: c["conceptId"])

    lines: list[str] = [
        '"""Auto-generated CDISC Controlled Terminology constants.',
        "",
        "Do not edit manually — regenerate with ``fleet.ct.generator``.",
        '"""',
        "",
    ]
    # Marker for the stale checks of fleet.ct.study_codelists; two dates of one
    # product (two SDTM CT packages) get none, so check b reports the mix.
    packages = {cl.get("_package") for cl in sorted_cls}
    products = {str(p).split("-", 1)[0] for p in packages}
    if len(packages) == 1 and None not in packages:
        lines += [f"__ct_package__ = {packages.pop()!r}", "", ""]
    elif None not in packages and len(products) == len(packages) > 1:
        lines += [f"__ct_packages__ = {tuple(sorted(packages))!r}", "", ""]

    # Class definitions
    for cl in sorted_cls:
        lines.extend(self._render_class(cl))
        lines.append("")

    # Human-readable aliases  (e.g.  SEX = C66731)
    aliases: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for cl in sorted_cls:
        concept_id = cl["conceptId"]
        class_name = _safe_identifier(concept_id)
        alias = self._alias_for(cl)
        if alias and alias != class_name:
            aliases.append((alias, class_name))

    if aliases:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("# Human-readable aliases")
        for alias, class_name in sorted(aliases):
            lines.append(f"{alias} = {class_name}")
        lines.append("")

    # __all__
    all_names: list[str] = [_safe_identifier(cl["conceptId"]) for cl in sorted_cls]
    all_names.extend(alias for alias, _ in sorted(aliases))
    all_names.sort()
    all_repr = ", ".join(f'"{n}"' for n in all_names)
    lines.append(f"__all__ = [{all_repr}]")
    lines.append("")

    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def write(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Render and write the module to *path*.

    Parent directories are created if they do not exist.

    Args:

Dynamically import a generated codelists.py module.

Resolves the codelist module location using these strategies (in order):

def import_codelists(
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    module_name: str = "codelists",
) -> ModuleType:
    """Dynamically import a generated ``codelists.py`` module.

    Resolves the codelist module location using these strategies (in order):

    1. If *path* is given explicitly, use it directly.
    2. Look for ``study_config.yaml`` in the current working directory and
       resolve the SDTM metadata path from it.
    3. Fall back to ``metadata/sdtm/codelists.py`` relative to CWD.

    The module is registered in ``sys.modules`` under *module_name* so that
    subsequent ``from codelists import SEX`` statements work as expected
    throughout the session.

    Args:
        path: Explicit path to the ``codelists.py`` file.  When ``None``,
            auto-discovery is attempted.
        module_name: Name to register the module under in ``sys.modules``.
            Defaults to ``"codelists"``.

    Returns:
        The imported codelists module.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If no ``codelists.py`` could be located.

    Examples:
        Auto-discover from study config::

            from fleet.ct import import_codelists

            ct = import_codelists()
            SEX = ct.SEX

        Or register so bare imports work::

            from fleet.ct import import_codelists

            import_codelists()  # registers as 'codelists' in sys.modules
            from codelists import SEX, RACE  # now works anywhere
    """
    resolved = _resolve_codelists_path(path)
    if not resolved.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Codelists module not found at: {resolved}\n"
            "Run `fleet init ct` to generate it, or pass an explicit path."
        )

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(module_name, resolved)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise ImportError(f"Cannot create module spec for: {resolved}")

    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[module_name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module

docs.title: CT Validator
docs.text: The singleton CTValidator provides runtime validation of values against loaded codelists.

docs.title: How CT validation works
docs.text:
Validation fires at pipeline-build time — when you call .assign(ct=...) in Python, not when you call .to_frame(). The check happens during the method call itself, before any data is processed.

The validator is opt-in via initialization. Fleet ships a module-level singleton that starts empty. You must load CT data into it before using ct= parameters. If the singleton has no data loaded, validation is silently skipped and the value is assigned as-is — no error, no warning.

Failures warn, they do not block. If a value is not a valid CDISC submission term, a Python UserWarning is emitted via warnings.warn(). The pipeline continues and the value is still written to the output. This design keeps pipelines runnable during development even before CT packages are fully loaded.

docs.title: Step-by-step — enabling CT validation
docs.text:
import warnings
from fleet import load_controlled_terminology, get_validator

# 1. Load the CT package once, at script/session start.
#    The file is a YAML or CSV produced by `fleet init ct` or `fleet add-ct`.
load_controlled_terminology("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/ct_package.yaml")

# 2. Import the generated codelist classes.
from fleet.ct import import_codelists

ct = import_codelists()
AGEU = ct.AGEU
SEX = ct.SEX

# 3. Build your pipeline — validation fires here on each verb call.
import warnings

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    dm = (
        raw_df.sdtm.assign("AGEU", value="YEARS", ct=AGEU)  # OK — valid term
        .assign("AGEU", value="YRS", ct=AGEU)  # Warns immediately
        .to_frame()
    )

# Any invalid values produce a warning at the .assign(ct=...) call site,
# not when .to_frame() runs.
for w in caught:
    print(w.message)
# UserWarning: Value 'YRS' not in codelist 'C66781'. Valid values: DAYS, HOURS, MINUTES, MONTHS, WEEKS, YEARS

docs.title: fleet.ct.CTValidator
docs.text:
Validator for CDISC Controlled Terminology.

Provides caching, lazy loading, and validation of SDTM/ADaM values against CDISC controlled terminology codelists. Aliases are resolved at load time: registering {"SEX": "C66731"} rekeys a cache entry loaded under SEX to its NCI concept ID, so every lookup path (assign-family verbs, DatasetChecker, direct API) reaches the same codelist by OID (C66731) or registered name (SEX) interchangeably — see :meth:_resolve for the resolution order.

Usage

from fleet import get_validator validator = get_validator() validator.load_ct_file("ct/cdisc_ct.yaml", aliases={"SEX": "C66731"}) validator.validate_value("SEX", "M") (True, "Value 'M' is valid for codelist 'C66731'")

Source code in src/fleet/ct/validator.py 
class CTValidator:
    """Validator for CDISC Controlled Terminology.

    Provides caching, lazy loading, and validation of SDTM/ADaM values
    against CDISC controlled terminology codelists.  Aliases are
    resolved **at load time**: registering ``{"SEX": "C66731"}`` rekeys
    a cache entry loaded under ``SEX`` to its NCI concept ID, so every
    lookup path (assign-family verbs, ``DatasetChecker``, direct API)
    reaches the same codelist by OID (``C66731``) or registered name
    (``SEX``) interchangeably — see :meth:`_resolve` for the resolution
    order.

    Usage:
        >>> from fleet import get_validator
        >>> validator = get_validator()
        >>> validator.load_ct_file("ct/cdisc_ct.yaml", aliases={"SEX": "C66731"})
        >>> validator.validate_value("SEX", "M")
        (True, "Value 'M' is valid for codelist 'C66731'")
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._lock = Lock()
        self._ct_cache: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        self._codelist_aliases: dict[str, str] = {}
        self._ct_path: Path | None = None
        self._initialized: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def get_instance(cls) -> CTValidator:
        """Return the module-level singleton. Kept for backward compatibility."""
        return _validator

    def load_ct_file(
        self,
        ct_path: Path | str,
        aliases: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Load all codelists from a YAML or CSV file into the cache.

        Args:
            ct_path: Path or URL to the CT file (.yaml, .yml, .csv).
            aliases: Optional mapping of human-readable names to codelist codes,
                     e.g., {"SEX": "C66731", "RACE": "C74457"}.

        Raises:
            CTError: If the file cannot be loaded.
        """
        with self._lock:
            try:
                logger.info("Loading CT file from: %s", ct_path)
                self._ct_cache = load_controlled_terminology(ct_path)
                self._ct_path = Path(ct_path) if isinstance(ct_path, str) else ct_path
                self._initialized = True
                if aliases:
                    self._codelist_aliases.update(aliases)
                for alias, canonical in self._codelist_aliases.items():
                    self._normalise_alias(alias, canonical)
                logger.info("Loaded %d codelists from %s", len(self._ct_cache), ct_path)
            except CTError:
                raise

    def load_codelist(
        self,
        ct_path: Path | str,
        codelist_name: str,
        alias: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Lazy-load a single codelist from a file (skips if already cached).

        Args:
            ct_path: Path or URL to the CT file.
            codelist_name: Name or NCI code of codelist to load.
            alias: Optional human-readable name to register for this codelist.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if codelist_name in self._ct_cache:
                logger.debug("Codelist %s already cached", codelist_name)
                return
            try:
                data = load_controlled_terminology(ct_path, codelist_name)
                self._ct_cache.update(data)
                if alias:
                    self._codelist_aliases[alias] = codelist_name
                    self._normalise_alias(alias, codelist_name)
                logger.info("Lazy-loaded codelist: %s", codelist_name)
            except CTError as e:
                logger.warning(
                    "Could not load codelist '%s': %s. Validation will pass by default.",
                    codelist_name,
                    e,
                )

    def register_alias(self, alias: str, codelist_name: str) -> None:
        """Register a human-readable alias for a codelist code.

        Resolves immediately: when the cache was loaded keyed by the
        alias (e.g. a CT file using ``SEX:`` as the top-level key), the
        entry is rekeyed to the canonical concept ID so both spellings
        hit the same codelist.

        Args:
            alias: Human-readable name, e.g., "SEX".
            codelist_name: NCI codelist code, e.g., "C66731".
        """
        with self._lock:
            self._codelist_aliases[alias] = codelist_name
            self._normalise_alias(alias, codelist_name)

    def _normalise_alias(self, alias: str, canonical: str) -> None:
        """Rekey a cache entry stored under *alias* to *canonical*.

        Callers must hold ``self._lock``.  No-op when the canonical key
        already exists (the alias mapping alone then suffices).
        """
        if alias in self._ct_cache and canonical not in self._ct_cache:
            self._ct_cache[canonical] = self._ct_cache.pop(alias)

    def _resolve(self, codelist_name: str) -> str:
        """Resolve a codelist reference to its cache key.

        Resolution order (documented contract for both the verb path
        and the define/checker path):

        1. **Exact cache key** — the name as stored by the loaded CT
           file (post load-time normalisation this is the concept ID
           whenever an alias declared one).
        2. **Registered alias** — ``SEX`` → ``C66731`` via
           :meth:`register_alias` / the ``aliases=`` load parameter.
        3. **Reverse alias** — the name is the canonical target of a
           registered alias whose cache entry was never rekeyed
           (defensive; load-time normalisation makes this rare).

        Unresolvable names are returned unchanged so callers report the
        original spelling.
        """
        if codelist_name in self._ct_cache:
            return codelist_name
        canonical = self._codelist_aliases.get(codelist_name)
        if canonical is not None and canonical in self._ct_cache:
            return canonical
        for alias, target in self._codelist_aliases.items():
            if target == codelist_name and alias in self._ct_cache:
                return alias
        return codelist_name

    def validate_value(
        self,
        codelist_name: str,
        value: str | None,
        allow_null: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        """Validate a single value against a codelist.

        Args:
            codelist_name: Codelist name or alias (e.g., "SEX" or "C66731").
            value: The value to validate (None is handled by allow_null).
            allow_null: Whether None is considered valid.

        Returns:
            Tuple (is_valid, message).
        """
        if value is None:
            if allow_null:
                return (True, f"Null value allowed for codelist '{codelist_name}'")
            return (False, f"Null value not allowed for codelist '{codelist_name}'")

        actual_cl = self._resolve(codelist_name)

        if actual_cl not in self._ct_cache:
            logger.warning(
                "Codelist '%s' not loaded — validation skipped for value '%s'",
                actual_cl,
                value,
            )
            return (True, f"Codelist '{actual_cl}' not loaded - validation skipped")

        codelist = self._ct_cache[actual_cl]
        if value in codelist:
            return (True, f"Value '{value}' is valid for codelist '{actual_cl}'")

        valid_str = ", ".join(sorted(codelist.keys()))
        return (
            False,
            f"Value '{value}' not in codelist '{actual_cl}'. Valid values: {valid_str}",
        )

    def has_codelist(self, codelist_name: str) -> bool:
        """Return True when a codelist (or alias) is loaded in the cache.

        Args:
            codelist_name: Codelist name, alias, or NCI concept ID.

        Returns:
            True if the codelist is available for validation.
        """
        actual_cl = self._resolve(codelist_name)
        return actual_cl in self._ct_cache

    def get_valid_values(self, codelist_name: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return all valid codes for a codelist.

        Args:
            codelist_name: Codelist name or alias.

        Returns:
            Sorted list of valid code strings, empty if codelist not loaded.
        """
        actual_cl = self._resolve(codelist_name)
        codelist = self._ct_cache.get(actual_cl, {})
        return sorted(codelist.keys())

    def get_cache_info(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Return diagnostic information about the current cache state."""
        return {
            "codelists_loaded": list(self._ct_cache.keys()),
            "aliases": dict(self._codelist_aliases),
            "ct_path": str(self._ct_path) if self._ct_path else None,
            "initialized": self._initialized,
        }

    def apply_ct_mapping(self, codelist_name: str, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        """Map an SDTM code to its decoded CT value (e.g., "M" → "Male").

        Returns the original value if the codelist is not loaded or value not found.
        """
        if value is None:
            return None
        actual_cl = self._resolve(codelist_name)
        codelist = self._ct_cache.get(actual_cl, {})
        return codelist.get(value, value)

    def get_decode_map(self, codelist_name: str) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Return a code-to-preferred-term mapping for a codelist.

        Each key is the submission value (e.g. ``"M"``) and the value is
        the preferred term / decode (e.g. ``"Male"``).  Returns an empty
        dict if the codelist is not loaded.

        Args:
            codelist_name: Codelist name, alias, or NCI concept ID.

        Returns:
            Dictionary mapping coded values to their preferred terms.
        """
        actual_cl = self._resolve(codelist_name)
        codelist = self._ct_cache.get(actual_cl, {})
        return {
            coded: info.get("preferred_term", coded) if isinstance(info, dict) else coded
            for coded, info in codelist.items()
        }

def load_controlled_terminology(
    ct_path: Path | str,
    codelist_name: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    """Load CDISC controlled terminology from a YAML or CSV file (or URL).

    Args:
        ct_path: Path or URL to CT file. Supported formats: .yaml, .yml, .csv.
        codelist_name: If given, only load this specific codelist.

    Returns:
        Nested dict mapping codelist_name -> {code: decoded_value}.

    Raises:
        CTError: If the file cannot be found, read, or is in an unsupported format.
    """
    if isinstance(ct_path, str):
        if ct_path.startswith("http"):
            ct_path = _download_ct(ct_path)
        else:
            ct_path = Path(ct_path)

    if not ct_path.exists():
        raise CTError(f"CT file not found: {ct_path}")

    suffix = ct_path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix in (".yaml", ".yml"):
        return _load_ct_yaml(ct_path, codelist_name)
    elif suffix == ".csv":
        return _load_ct_csv(ct_path, codelist_name)
    else:
        raise CTError(f"Unsupported CT file type: {suffix}. Use .yaml or .csv")
