Fluent builder for constructing TLG ARDs inline.

This is a shared base class composed into every TLG sub-namespace. Domain-specific defaults (required columns, default statistics, context label) are baked into the sub-namespace rather than the builder.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default df DataFrame

The primary analysis DataFrame.

required context str

Domain context label (e.g. "t_ae_summary").

required spec_cls type[TLGSpec]

The spec Pydantic model class for this domain.

required namespace_cls type[Any]

The namespace class that implements t_summary().

required defaults dict[str, Any] | None

Domain-specific default kwargs for spec construction.

None Source code in src/fleet/tlg/_builder.py 
class TLGBuilder:
    """Fluent builder for constructing TLG ARDs inline.

    This is a shared base class composed into every TLG sub-namespace.
    Domain-specific defaults (required columns, default statistics,
    ``context`` label) are baked into the sub-namespace rather than the
    builder.

    Args:
        df: The primary analysis DataFrame.
        context: Domain context label (e.g. ``"t_ae_summary"``).
        spec_cls: The spec Pydantic model class for this domain.
        namespace_cls: The namespace class that implements ``t_summary()``.
        defaults: Domain-specific default kwargs for spec construction.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        df: pl.DataFrame,
        *,
        context: str,
        spec_cls: type[TLGSpec],
        namespace_cls: type[Any],
        defaults: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._df = df
        self._context = context
        self._spec_cls = spec_cls
        self._namespace_cls = namespace_cls
        self._defaults: dict[str, Any] = defaults or {}
        self._method = "t_summary"
        self._adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None
        self._adsl_filter: pl.Expr | str | None = None
        self._dataset_filter: pl.Expr | str | None = None
        self._group_col: str | None = None
        self._header_rows_list: list[OverallStat] = []
        self._rows_fields: list[str | Row] = []
        self._statistics: list[Statistic] | None = None
        self._pools: list[GroupPool] = []
        self._column_order: list[str] = []
        self._value_col: str | None = None
        self._label_col: str | None = None
        self._decimals: dict[str, str] | None = None
        self._uncoded: Uncoded | None = _UNSET
        self._prefilter: pl.Expr | str | None = _UNSET
        self._listing_columns: list[str | Column] | None = None
        self._sort_by: list[str] | None = None
        self._template_id: str | None = None
        self._template_fn: Callable[..., pl.DataFrame] | None = None
        self._interactive: InteractiveBlock | None = None

    def _clone(self) -> TLGBuilder:
        return copy.copy(self)

    def _targets_listing(self) -> bool:
        """True when the current spec class describes a listing layout."""
        field = self._spec_cls.model_fields.get("output_type")
        return field is not None and field.default == "listing"

    def _has_reinterpretable_state(self) -> bool:
        """True when row/stat/format verbs have already accumulated state."""
        return bool(
            self._rows_fields
            or self._statistics is not None
            or self._header_rows_list
            or self._pools
            or self._column_order
            or self._value_col is not None
            or self._label_col is not None
            or self._decimals is not None
            or self._uncoded is not _UNSET
            or self._prefilter is not _UNSET
            or self._listing_columns is not None
            or self._sort_by is not None
        )

    def _require_consumed_field(self, field: str, verb: str) -> None:
        """Raise when builder state maps to a field the target won't consume."""
        cls = self._spec_cls
        if field not in cls.model_fields:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"{verb} maps to spec field '{field}', which {cls.__name__} "
                f"does not define — the target template method "
                f"'{self._method}' would silently ignore it. Remove the verb "
                "or target a template that consumes it."
            )
        if field in cls._unconsumed_spec_fields:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"{verb} maps to spec field '{field}', which the target "
                f"template method '{self._method}' does not consume — it "
                "would be silently ignored. Remove the verb or target a "
                "different template."
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Data input verbs                                                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def population(
        self,
        adsl: pl.DataFrame,
        *,
        adsl_filter: pl.Expr | str | None = None,
    ) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the ADSL population and optional denominator filter.

        Args:
            adsl: ADSL DataFrame for big-N denominators.
            adsl_filter: Optional population filter on ADSL — a
                ``pl.Expr`` or a string expression (the
                YAML-serializable form).  Only the analysis records of
                the selected subjects are counted.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with population set.

        Examples:
            Use ADSL for the big-N denominators::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._adsl = adsl
        new._adsl_filter = adsl_filter
        return new

    def filter(self, expr: pl.Expr | str) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the dataset filter (applied to the primary dataset only).

        Args:
            expr: Polars expression (or string expression — the
                YAML-serializable form) filtering the primary dataset.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with dataset filter set.

        Examples:
            Restrict the table to treatment-emergent events::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .filter('pl.col("TRTEMFL") == "Y"')
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._dataset_filter = expr
        return new

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Grouping verbs                                                       #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def by(self, col: str) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the primary grouping column (treatment arm).

        Args:
            col: Column name for group1 (e.g. ``"TRTA"``).

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with group1 set.

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If *col* is not a single column name —
                multi-column grouping is not implemented, and accepting a
                list would silently read only the first entry.

        Examples:
            Split columns by actual treatment arm::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        if not isinstance(col, str):
            raise SchemaError(
                f"by() takes a single treatment-arm column name, got "
                f"{col!r}. Multi-column grouping is not implemented — move "
                "additional grouping into the row hierarchy (rows())."
            )
        new = self._clone()
        new._group_col = col
        return new

    def template(self, template_id: str) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Target a registered template so materialisation runs its method.

        Resolves *template_id* through the template registry (built-ins
        and user registrations alike): the builder will materialise via
        that template's namespace method (e.g. ``lbt02`` → ``t_chg``) —
        or its registered function for user templates — with the
        template's spec class.  Listing templates (e.g. ``ael01``)
        materialise via :meth:`to_listing`.

        **Ordering**: call ``template()`` *before* row/stat/format verbs.
        It swaps the builder's spec class, so state accumulated earlier
        is re-validated against — and interpreted by — the new target's
        spec; a ``UserWarning`` is emitted when that happens.

        Args:
            template_id: Registry id (e.g. ``"aet02"``, ``"lbt02"``).

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder targeting the template's method and spec.

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If the id is unknown, belongs to a different
                namespace, or is a graph template.

        Examples:
            Materialise the AET02 shell::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .template("aet02")
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        from ._registry import TEMPLATES, OutputType

        meta = TEMPLATES.get(template_id)
        if meta is None:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Unknown template id {template_id!r}. Known ids: {sorted(TEMPLATES)}"
            )
        if meta.output_type is OutputType.GRAPH:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Template {template_id!r} is a graph, which the inline builder cannot materialise."
            )
        new = self._clone()
        if meta.func is not None:
            # User-registered template: self-contained function, not bound
            # to a namespace method.
            new._template_fn = meta.func
            new._spec_cls = meta.spec_cls or SummarySpecBase
        else:
            spec_classes = getattr(self._namespace_cls, "_builder_specs", {})
            if meta.method not in spec_classes:
                raise SchemaError(
                    f"Template {template_id!r} ({meta.namespace}.{meta.method}) does "
                    f"not belong to this namespace ({self._context})."
                )
            new._method = meta.method
            new._spec_cls = meta.spec_cls or spec_classes[meta.method]
        new._template_id = meta.id
        if self._has_reinterpretable_state():
            warnings.warn(
                f"template({template_id!r}) was called after row/stat/format "
                "verbs — the accumulated state will be reinterpreted by "
                f"{new._spec_cls.__name__}. Call .template() first to avoid "
                "surprises.",
                UserWarning,
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        return new

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Row / stat / format verbs                                            #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def header_rows(self, overall_stats: list[OverallStat]) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set header rows (whole-dataset aggregate rows).

        Args:
            overall_stats: List of ``OverallStat`` definitions.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with header rows set.

        Examples:
            Add a whole-dataset aggregate row::

                from fleet.tlg import OverallStat

                ard = (
                    adlb.tlg.lb
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .header_rows([OverallStat(label="Any abnormal")])
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._header_rows_list = list(overall_stats)
        return new

    def rows(self, fields: list[str | Row]) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the row hierarchy fields.

        A single field maps to ``variable``.  Two fields drive two-level
        nesting: the first maps to ``variable``, the second to ``group2``.
        Entries may be plain column names or full ``Row`` objects
        carrying ``label`` / ``filter_value`` / ``decimals``.

        Args:
            fields: One or two field names (or ``Row`` objects) for the
                row hierarchy.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with row fields set.

        Examples:
            Two-level SOC → preferred-term hierarchy::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._rows_fields = list(fields)
        return new

    def value(self, col: str) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the analysis-value column for continuous statistics.

        Maps to the spec's ``value_col`` — point it at ``CHG``, ``PCHG``
        or ``BASE`` to summarize those without pre-renaming.

        Args:
            col: Analysis-value column name (e.g. ``"CHG"``).

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with the value column set.

        Examples:
            Summarise change from baseline instead of AVAL::

                ard = (
                    advs.tlg.vs
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .value("CHG")
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._value_col = col
        return new

    def label(self, col: str) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the display-label column for the first row field's values.

        Maps to the spec's ``label_col`` — e.g. ``"PARAM"`` when the row
        field is ``"PARAMCD"`` so stubs show display names, not codes.

        Args:
            col: Column holding display labels.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with the label column set.

        Examples:
            Show PARAM display names for PARAMCD rows::

                ard = (
                    advs.tlg.vs
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .rows(["PARAMCD"])
                    .label("PARAM")
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._label_col = col
        return new

    def decimals(self, mapping: dict[str, str]) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set per-statistic display-format overrides.

        Maps to the spec's ``decimals`` — ARD ``stat_name`` (e.g.
        ``"mean"``) to format string (e.g. ``"xx.xx"``).

        Args:
            mapping: Stat-name → format-string overrides.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with format overrides set.

        Examples:
            Report means with two decimal places::

                ard = (
                    advs.tlg.vs
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .decimals({"mean": "xx.xx"})
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._decimals = dict(mapping)
        return new

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Record-rule verbs                                                    #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def uncoded(self, columns: list[str] | None, *, label: str = NO_CODING_LABEL) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the uncoded rule: the coding columns whose nulls become a level.

        Maps to the spec's ``uncoded``.  Each template has its own
        default (the AE tables fill ``AEBODSYS`` and ``AEDECOD`` with
        ``"No Coding Available"``); ``uncoded(None)`` switches the rule
        off so uncoded records are not counted.

        Args:
            columns: Coding columns to fill when null, or ``None`` to
                switch the rule off.
            label: Replacement level for a null coding term.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with the uncoded rule set.

        Examples:
            Use the sponsor's label for uncoded events::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .uncoded(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"], label="UNCODED")
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._uncoded = None if columns is None else Uncoded(columns=list(columns), label=label)
        return new

    def prefilter(self, expr: pl.Expr | str | None) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the template's own record filter, applied after ``filter()``.

        Maps to the spec's ``prefilter``.  Each template has its own
        default (the change-from-baseline tables drop the ``ABLFL`` = Y
        record); every column the expression names becomes a required
        column.  ``prefilter(None)`` switches the rule off.

        Args:
            expr: Polars expression, string expression (the
                YAML-serializable form), or ``None``.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with the prefilter set.

        Examples:
            Keep on-treatment records only in a change table::

                ard = (
                    adlb.tlg.lb
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .template("lbt02")
                    .prefilter('pl.col("ONTRTFL") == "Y"')
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._prefilter = expr
        return new

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Listing verbs                                                        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def columns(self, cols: list[str | Column]) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the display columns for a listing.

        Entries may be plain column names or full ``Column`` objects
        carrying display labels.  Applies to the listing path only —
        for table grouping use :meth:`by`.

        Args:
            cols: Ordered listing columns.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with listing columns set.

        Examples:
            A subject-level AE listing::

                listing = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .template("ael01")
                    .columns(["USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AESEV"])
                    .to_listing()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._listing_columns = list(cols)
        return new

    def sort_by(self, cols: list[str]) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the sort order for a listing.

        Args:
            cols: Column names to sort the listing by, in order.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with the sort order set.

        Examples:
            Sort the listing by subject then onset date::

                listing = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .template("ael01")
                    .sort_by(["USUBJID", "ASTDT"])
                    .to_listing()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._sort_by = list(cols)
        return new

    def stats(self, statistics: list[Statistic]) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the statistics to compute.

        Args:
            statistics: List of ``Statistic`` enum values.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with statistics set.

        Examples:
            Report subject counts and percentages::

                from fleet.tlg import Statistic

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._statistics = list(statistics)
        return new

    def pools(self, pool_defs: list[GroupPool]) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set pooled treatment group definitions.

        Args:
            pool_defs: List of ``GroupPool`` definitions.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with pools set.

        Examples:
            Add a pooled Total column across all arms::

                from fleet.tlg import GroupPool

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .pools([GroupPool(label="Total", arms="*")])
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._pools = list(pool_defs)
        return new

    def column_order(self, order: list[str]) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Set the display column order.

        Args:
            order: Ordered list of arm labels.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with column order set.

        Examples:
            Force placebo first::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .column_order(["Placebo", "Low Dose", "High Dose"])
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._column_order = list(order)
        return new

    def interactive(
        self,
        *,
        groupby: Any | None = None,
        population: list[Any] | None = None,
        dataset_filter: list[Any] | None = None,
        stats: list[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Declare the explorer's degrees of freedom (``interactive:`` block).

        Each axis maps onto an existing spec field — ``groupby`` →
        ``columns``, ``population`` → ``adsl_filter``, ``dataset_filter``
        → ``dataset_filter``, ``stats`` → ``statistics`` — so every
        explorer variant runs through the same engine as the batch
        output.  Values may be plain dicts (the YAML shapes) or
        ``GroupbyChoice``/``ChoiceOption`` instances.

        Args:
            groupby: ``{"choices": [...], "default": ...}`` — candidate
                treatment-arm columns.
            population: ADSL filter presets, each
                ``{"label": ..., "filter": ..., "default": ...}``.
            dataset_filter: Analysis-dataset filter presets (same shape).
            stats: Statistics presets, each
                ``{"label": ..., "statistics": [...], "default": ...}``.

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder with the interactive block set.

        Examples:
            Declare a two-axis explorer and save the spec::

                spec = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl, adsl_filter='pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"')
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .template("aet01")
                    .interactive(
                        groupby={"choices": ["TRTA", "TRT01A"], "default": "TRTA"},
                        stats=[
                            {"label": "n (%)", "statistics": ["n_subjects", "n_pct"],
                             "default": True},
                            {"label": "+ events",
                             "statistics": ["n_subjects", "n_pct", "n_events"]},
                        ],
                    )
                    .to_spec()
                )
        """
        new = self._clone()
        new._interactive = InteractiveBlock(
            groupby=groupby,
            population=population,
            dataset_filter=dataset_filter,
            stats=stats,
        )
        return new

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Materialisation                                                      #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def to_spec(self) -> TLGSpec:
        """Serialise accumulated builder state to the equivalent spec.

        Every verb the user called must land on a spec field the target
        template's method actually consumes — otherwise this raises
        instead of silently dropping state (e.g. ``rows()`` on the
        fixed-hierarchy ``lbt03`` shift table).

        Returns:
            TLGSpec: A spec instance matching the builder configuration
                (carrying ``template=<id>`` when targeted via
                :meth:`template`).

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If accumulated builder state maps to a spec
                field the target template's method does not consume, or
                to no field at all.

        Examples:
            Capture the builder state as a reusable spec::

                spec = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .template("aet02")
                    .to_spec()
                )
        """
        is_listing = self._targets_listing()
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = dict(self._defaults)

        if self._template_id is not None:
            kwargs["template"] = self._template_id
        if self._adsl_filter is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("adsl_filter", "population(adsl_filter=...)")
            kwargs["adsl_filter"] = self._adsl_filter
        if self._dataset_filter is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("dataset_filter", "filter()")
            kwargs["dataset_filter"] = self._dataset_filter
        if self._header_rows_list:
            self._require_consumed_field("header_rows", "header_rows()")
            kwargs["header_rows"] = self._header_rows_list
        if self._group_col:
            if is_listing:
                raise SchemaError(
                    "by() sets a grouping column, but the target template is "
                    "a listing — listings have no column grouping. Remove "
                    "by() or target a table template."
                )
            if "columns" in self._spec_cls.model_fields:
                kwargs["columns"] = [self._group_col]
        if self._rows_fields:
            kwargs.update(self._rows_kwargs())
        if self._statistics is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("statistics", "stats()")
            kwargs["statistics"] = self._statistics
        if self._pools:
            self._require_consumed_field("pools", "pools()")
            kwargs["pools"] = self._pools
        if self._column_order:
            self._require_consumed_field("column_order", "column_order()")
            kwargs["column_order"] = self._column_order
        if self._value_col is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("value_col", "value()")
            kwargs["value_col"] = self._value_col
        if self._label_col is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("label_col", "label()")
            kwargs["label_col"] = self._label_col
        if self._decimals is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("decimals", "decimals()")
            kwargs["decimals"] = self._decimals
        if self._uncoded is not _UNSET:
            self._require_consumed_field("uncoded", "uncoded()")
            kwargs["uncoded"] = self._uncoded
        if self._prefilter is not _UNSET:
            self._require_consumed_field("prefilter", "prefilter()")
            kwargs["prefilter"] = self._prefilter
        if self._listing_columns is not None:
            if not is_listing:
                raise SchemaError(
                    "columns() defines listing display columns, but the "
                    "target template is a table. Use by() for the grouping "
                    'column, or target a listing template (.template("ael01") '
                    "/ .to_listing())."
                )
            kwargs["columns"] = [
                c if isinstance(c, Column) else Column(field=c) for c in self._listing_columns
            ]
        if self._sort_by is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("sort_by", "sort_by()")
            kwargs["sort_by"] = list(self._sort_by)
        if self._interactive is not None:
            kwargs["interactive"] = self._interactive

        return self._spec_cls(**kwargs)

    def _rows_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Map ``rows()`` state onto the target spec's row field(s).

        DM summarises independent categorical variables, not a row
        hierarchy — map the builder's rows() onto ``categorical_vars``
        (merging any ``Row.label`` into ``category_labels``).
        """
        row_objs = [f if isinstance(f, Row) else Row(field=f) for f in self._rows_fields]
        if "categorical_vars" not in self._spec_cls.model_fields:
            self._require_consumed_field("rows", "rows()")
            return {"rows": row_objs}
        unsupported = [
            r.field for r in row_objs if r.filter_value is not None or r.decimals is not None
        ]
        if unsupported:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"rows() entries {unsupported} carry filter_value/decimals, "
                f"which {self._spec_cls.__name__}'s categorical breakdown "
                "does not consume — they would be silently ignored."
            )
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"categorical_vars": [r.field for r in row_objs]}
        labels = {r.field: r.label for r in row_objs if r.label}
        if labels:
            default_field = self._spec_cls.model_fields["category_labels"]
            defaults = default_field.get_default(call_default_factory=True) or {}
            kwargs["category_labels"] = {**defaults, **labels}
        return kwargs

    def to_ard(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Materialise the builder to an ARD DataFrame.

        Constructs the equivalent spec and delegates to the targeted
        namespace method — ``t_summary()`` by default, the method
        selected via :meth:`template`, or the registered function for a
        user template.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: Long-format {cards}-compatible ARD.

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If the target template is a listing — call
                :meth:`to_listing` instead.

        Examples:
            Inline AE summary::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl, adsl_filter=pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y")
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                    .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        if self._template_fn is not None:
            return self._template_fn(
                self._df,
                adsl=self._adsl,
                spec=self.to_spec(),
                groupby=self._group_col,
            )
        if self._targets_listing():
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Template {self._template_id!r} is a listing — call "
                ".to_listing() instead of .to_ard()."
            )
        spec = self.to_spec()
        ns = self._namespace_cls(self._df)
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"adsl": self._adsl, "spec": spec}
        if self._group_col is not None:
            kwargs["groupby"] = self._group_col
        return getattr(ns, self._method)(**kwargs)

    def to_listing(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Materialise the builder to a listing DataFrame.

        Uses the listing template targeted via :meth:`template` (e.g.
        ``ael01``), or the namespace's default listing when none was
        targeted.  Listings ignore population/grouping by design, so
        ``by()`` and ``population(adsl_filter=...)`` state raises here.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: A plain DataFrame with the requested columns,
                sorted per spec.

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If a table template was targeted, or the
                namespace ships no listing template.

        Examples:
            Inline AE listing::

                listing = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .columns(["USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AESEV"])
                    .sort_by(["USUBJID"])
                    .to_listing()
                )
        """
        builder = self
        if not self._targets_listing():
            if self._template_id is not None or self._template_fn is not None:
                raise SchemaError(
                    f"Template {self._template_id!r} is not a listing — call "
                    ".to_ard() instead of .to_listing()."
                )
            spec_classes = getattr(self._namespace_cls, "_builder_specs", {})
            listing_cls = spec_classes.get("l_listing")
            if listing_cls is None:
                raise SchemaError(
                    f"{self._context}: this namespace ships no listing "
                    "template, so .to_listing() is unavailable."
                )
            builder = self._clone()
            builder._method = "l_listing"
            builder._spec_cls = listing_cls
        spec = builder.to_spec()
        ns = self._namespace_cls(self._df)
        return getattr(ns, builder._method)(spec=spec)

    def to_html(
        self,
        path: str | Path | None = None,
        *,
        metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
        html_wrapper: str | None = None,
    ) -> str:
        """Render the builder result as a pharma-style HTML table.

        Materialises the ARD via ``.to_ard()``, shapes it into a
        ``TableModel``, and renders to HTML.

        Args:
            path: Optional file path.  If given, HTML is written to disk.
            metadata: Optional ``RenderMetadata`` for title, subtitle,
                footnotes, etc.
            html_wrapper: Optional HTML template with ``{table}``
                placeholder for injection.

        Returns:
            str: The rendered HTML string.

        Examples:
            Inline AE summary to HTML::

                html = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                    .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                    .to_html(metadata=RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1"))
                )
        """
        from pathlib import Path as _Path

        from .render._models import RenderMetadata as _RM
        from .render._models import ard_to_table_model
        from .render.html import render_html

        ard = self.to_ard()
        meta = metadata or _RM()
        model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
        html = render_html(model, html_wrapper=html_wrapper)

        if path is not None:
            p = _Path(path)
            p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            p.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")

        return html

    def to_rtf(
        self,
        path: str | Path | None = None,
        *,
        metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
    ) -> str:
        """Render the builder result as a pharma-style RTF table.

        Materialises the ARD via ``.to_ard()``, shapes it into a
        ``TableModel``, and renders to RTF (Courier New 9pt, cell
        borders, repeated headers, ``Page X of Y``) — the de facto
        submission/QC format.  Pure stdlib.

        Args:
            path: Optional file path.  If given, RTF is written to disk.
            metadata: Optional ``RenderMetadata`` for title, subtitle,
                footnotes, etc.

        Returns:
            str: The rendered RTF document.

        Examples:
            Inline AE summary to a submission RTF::

                rtf = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                    .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                    .to_rtf("t_ae_summary.rtf",
                            metadata=RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1"))
                )
        """
        from .render._models import RenderMetadata as _RM
        from .render._models import ard_to_table_model
        from .render.rtf import render_rtf

        ard = self.to_ard()
        meta = metadata or _RM()
        model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
        return render_rtf(model, path)

    def to_pdf(
        self,
        path: str | Path,
        *,
        metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
    ) -> Path:
        """Render the builder result as a PDF file via WeasyPrint.

        Args:
            path: Output PDF file path.
            metadata: Optional ``RenderMetadata`` for title, subtitle,
                footnotes, etc.

        Returns:
            Path: The written PDF path.

        Raises:
            ImportError: If WeasyPrint is not installed.

        Examples:
            Inline AE summary to PDF::

                path = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                    .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                    .to_pdf("ae_summary.pdf",
                            metadata=RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1"))
                )
        """

        from .render._models import RenderMetadata as _RM
        from .render._models import ard_to_table_model
        from .render.pdf import render_pdf

        ard = self.to_ard()
        meta = metadata or _RM()
        model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
        return render_pdf(model, path)

    def to_pptx(
        self,
        path: str | Path,
        *,
        metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
        theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> Path:
        """Render the builder result as an editable PPTX slide deck.

        Args:
            path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
            metadata: Optional ``RenderMetadata`` for title, subtitle,
                footnotes, etc.
            theme: Optional dict of style overrides (font, colours, sizes).

        Returns:
            Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

        Raises:
            ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

        Examples:
            Inline AE summary to editable slides::

                path = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                    .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                    .to_pptx("ae_summary.pptx",
                             metadata=RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1"))
                )
        """

        from .render._models import RenderMetadata as _RM
        from .render._models import ard_to_table_model
        from .render.slides import render_pptx

        ard = self.to_ard()
        meta = metadata or _RM()
        model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
        return render_pptx(model, path, theme=theme)

Resolves template_id through the template registry (built-ins and user registrations alike): the builder will materialise via that template's namespace method (e.g. lbt02 → t_chg) — or its registered function for user templates — with the template's spec class. Listing templates (e.g. ael01) materialise via :meth:to_listing.

If the id is unknown, belongs to a different namespace, or is a graph template.

Materialise the AET02 shell::

ard = (
    adae.tlg.ae

    .template("aet02")
    .to_ard()

def template(self, template_id: str) -> TLGBuilder:
    """Target a registered template so materialisation runs its method.

    Resolves *template_id* through the template registry (built-ins
    and user registrations alike): the builder will materialise via
    that template's namespace method (e.g. ``lbt02`` → ``t_chg``) —
    or its registered function for user templates — with the
    template's spec class.  Listing templates (e.g. ``ael01``)
    materialise via :meth:`to_listing`.

    **Ordering**: call ``template()`` *before* row/stat/format verbs.
    It swaps the builder's spec class, so state accumulated earlier
    is re-validated against — and interpreted by — the new target's
    spec; a ``UserWarning`` is emitted when that happens.

    Args:
        template_id: Registry id (e.g. ``"aet02"``, ``"lbt02"``).

    Returns:
        TLGBuilder: Builder targeting the template's method and spec.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If the id is unknown, belongs to a different
            namespace, or is a graph template.

    Examples:
        Materialise the AET02 shell::

            ard = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .population(adsl)
                .by("TRTA")
                .template("aet02")
                .to_ard()
            )
    """
    from ._registry import TEMPLATES, OutputType

    meta = TEMPLATES.get(template_id)
    if meta is None:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Unknown template id {template_id!r}. Known ids: {sorted(TEMPLATES)}"
        )
    if meta.output_type is OutputType.GRAPH:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Template {template_id!r} is a graph, which the inline builder cannot materialise."
        )
    new = self._clone()
    if meta.func is not None:
        # User-registered template: self-contained function, not bound
        # to a namespace method.
        new._template_fn = meta.func
        new._spec_cls = meta.spec_cls or SummarySpecBase
    else:
        spec_classes = getattr(self._namespace_cls, "_builder_specs", {})
        if meta.method not in spec_classes:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Template {template_id!r} ({meta.namespace}.{meta.method}) does "
                f"not belong to this namespace ({self._context})."
            )
        new._method = meta.method
        new._spec_cls = meta.spec_cls or spec_classes[meta.method]
    new._template_id = meta.id
    if self._has_reinterpretable_state():
        warnings.warn(
            f"template({template_id!r}) was called after row/stat/format "
            "verbs — the accumulated state will be reinterpreted by "
            f"{new._spec_cls.__name__}. Call .template() first to avoid "
            "surprises.",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    return new

def to_spec(self) -> TLGSpec:
    """Serialise accumulated builder state to the equivalent spec.

    Every verb the user called must land on a spec field the target
    template's method actually consumes — otherwise this raises
    instead of silently dropping state (e.g. ``rows()`` on the
    fixed-hierarchy ``lbt03`` shift table).

    Returns:
        TLGSpec: A spec instance matching the builder configuration
            (carrying ``template=<id>`` when targeted via
            :meth:`template`).

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If accumulated builder state maps to a spec
            field the target template's method does not consume, or
            to no field at all.

    Examples:
        Capture the builder state as a reusable spec::

            spec = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .population(adsl)
                .by("TRTA")
                .template("aet02")
                .to_spec()
            )
    """
    is_listing = self._targets_listing()
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = dict(self._defaults)

    if self._template_id is not None:
        kwargs["template"] = self._template_id
    if self._adsl_filter is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("adsl_filter", "population(adsl_filter=...)")
        kwargs["adsl_filter"] = self._adsl_filter
    if self._dataset_filter is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("dataset_filter", "filter()")
        kwargs["dataset_filter"] = self._dataset_filter
    if self._header_rows_list:
        self._require_consumed_field("header_rows", "header_rows()")
        kwargs["header_rows"] = self._header_rows_list
    if self._group_col:
        if is_listing:
            raise SchemaError(
                "by() sets a grouping column, but the target template is "
                "a listing — listings have no column grouping. Remove "
                "by() or target a table template."
            )
        if "columns" in self._spec_cls.model_fields:
            kwargs["columns"] = [self._group_col]
    if self._rows_fields:
        kwargs.update(self._rows_kwargs())
    if self._statistics is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("statistics", "stats()")
        kwargs["statistics"] = self._statistics
    if self._pools:
        self._require_consumed_field("pools", "pools()")
        kwargs["pools"] = self._pools
    if self._column_order:
        self._require_consumed_field("column_order", "column_order()")
        kwargs["column_order"] = self._column_order
    if self._value_col is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("value_col", "value()")
        kwargs["value_col"] = self._value_col
    if self._label_col is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("label_col", "label()")
        kwargs["label_col"] = self._label_col
    if self._decimals is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("decimals", "decimals()")
        kwargs["decimals"] = self._decimals
    if self._uncoded is not _UNSET:
        self._require_consumed_field("uncoded", "uncoded()")
        kwargs["uncoded"] = self._uncoded
    if self._prefilter is not _UNSET:
        self._require_consumed_field("prefilter", "prefilter()")
        kwargs["prefilter"] = self._prefilter
    if self._listing_columns is not None:
        if not is_listing:
            raise SchemaError(
                "columns() defines listing display columns, but the "
                "target template is a table. Use by() for the grouping "
                'column, or target a listing template (.template("ael01") '
                "/ .to_listing())."
            )
        kwargs["columns"] = [
            c if isinstance(c, Column) else Column(field=c) for c in self._listing_columns
        ]
    if self._sort_by is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("sort_by", "sort_by()")
        kwargs["sort_by"] = list(self._sort_by)
    if self._interactive is not None:
        kwargs["interactive"] = self._interactive

    return self._spec_cls(**kwargs)

def to_ard(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Materialise the builder to an ARD DataFrame.

    Constructs the equivalent spec and delegates to the targeted
    namespace method — ``t_summary()`` by default, the method
    selected via :meth:`template`, or the registered function for a
    user template.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: Long-format {cards}-compatible ARD.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If the target template is a listing — call
            :meth:`to_listing` instead.

    Examples:
        Inline AE summary::

            ard = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .population(adsl, adsl_filter=pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y")
                .by("TRTA")
                .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                .to_ard()
            )
    """
    if self._template_fn is not None:
        return self._template_fn(
            self._df,
            adsl=self._adsl,
            spec=self.to_spec(),
            groupby=self._group_col,
        )
    if self._targets_listing():
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Template {self._template_id!r} is a listing — call "
            ".to_listing() instead of .to_ard()."
        )
    spec = self.to_spec()
    ns = self._namespace_cls(self._df)
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"adsl": self._adsl, "spec": spec}
    if self._group_col is not None:
        kwargs["groupby"] = self._group_col
    return getattr(ns, self._method)(**kwargs)

def to_listing(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Materialise the builder to a listing DataFrame.

    Uses the listing template targeted via :meth:`template` (e.g.
    ``ael01``), or the namespace's default listing when none was
    targeted.  Listings ignore population/grouping by design, so
    ``by()`` and ``population(adsl_filter=...)`` state raises here.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: A plain DataFrame with the requested columns,
            sorted per spec.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If a table template was targeted, or the
            namespace ships no listing template.

    Examples:
        Inline AE listing::

            listing = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .columns(["USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AESEV"])
                .sort_by(["USUBJID"])
                .to_listing()
            )
    """
    builder = self
    if not self._targets_listing():
        if self._template_id is not None or self._template_fn is not None:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Template {self._template_id!r} is not a listing — call "
                ".to_ard() instead of .to_listing()."
            )
        spec_classes = getattr(self._namespace_cls, "_builder_specs", {})
        listing_cls = spec_classes.get("l_listing")
        if listing_cls is None:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"{self._context}: this namespace ships no listing "
                "template, so .to_listing() is unavailable."
            )
        builder = self._clone()
        builder._method = "l_listing"
        builder._spec_cls = listing_cls
    spec = builder.to_spec()
    ns = self._namespace_cls(self._df)
    return getattr(ns, builder._method)(spec=spec)

def to_html(
    self,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render the builder result as a pharma-style HTML table.

    Materialises the ARD via ``.to_ard()``, shapes it into a
    ``TableModel``, and renders to HTML.

    Args:
        path: Optional file path.  If given, HTML is written to disk.
        metadata: Optional ``RenderMetadata`` for title, subtitle,
            footnotes, etc.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template with ``{table}``
            placeholder for injection.

    Returns:
        str: The rendered HTML string.

    Examples:
        Inline AE summary to HTML::

            html = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .population(adsl)
                .by("TRTA")
                .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                .to_html(metadata=RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1"))
            )
    """
    from pathlib import Path as _Path

    from .render._models import RenderMetadata as _RM
    from .render._models import ard_to_table_model
    from .render.html import render_html

    ard = self.to_ard()
    meta = metadata or _RM()
    model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
    html = render_html(model, html_wrapper=html_wrapper)

    if path is not None:
        p = _Path(path)
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")

    return html

Every axis maps onto one existing :class:TLGSpec field (groupby→columns, population→adsl_filter, dataset_filter→dataset_filter, stats→statistics), so the interactive variant space is spanned by the same engine that produces the batch output — no second body of table logic exists. class InteractiveBlock(BaseModel):
    """Declared degrees of freedom for the TLG explorer.

    Every axis maps onto one existing :class:`TLGSpec` field
    (``groupby``→``columns``, ``population``→``adsl_filter``,
    ``dataset_filter``→``dataset_filter``, ``stats``→``statistics``), so
    the interactive variant space is spanned by the same engine that
    produces the batch output — no second body of table logic exists.
    An absent axis stays fixed at the spec's value.
    """

    groupby: GroupbyChoice | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Treatment-arm column choices (→ spec ``columns``).",
    )
    population: list[ChoiceOption] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="ADSL population presets (→ spec ``adsl_filter``).",
    )
    dataset_filter: list[ChoiceOption] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Analysis-dataset filter presets (→ spec ``dataset_filter``).",
    )
    stats: list[ChoiceOption] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Statistics presets (→ spec ``statistics``).",
    )

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_axes(self) -> InteractiveBlock:
        """Require at least one axis, one default per axis, stats lists."""
        if all(v is None for v in (self.groupby, self.population, self.dataset_filter, self.stats)):
            raise ValueError("interactive: declare at least one axis (or drop the block).")
        for axis in ("population", "dataset_filter", "stats"):
            options = getattr(self, axis)
            if options is None:
                continue
            n_default = sum(o.default for o in options)
            if n_default != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"interactive.{axis}: exactly one option must set "
                    f"'default: true' (got {n_default}) — the default variant "
                    "is the batch/submission output."
                )
        if self.stats is not None:
            missing = [o.label for o in self.stats if not o.statistics]
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"interactive.stats: options {missing} must declare a 'statistics' list."
                )
        return self

class SummarySpecBase(TLGSpec):
    """Shared fields for every summary-table spec.

    Domain specs subclass this and override only their defaults (rows,
    statistics, required columns, the uncoded rule, the prefilter) —
    one declaration of the shared shape instead of nine divergent
    copies.  Every field is also settable inline through
    [`TLGBuilder`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder].  The spec is the whole engine
    contract: [`summarize_spec()`][fleet.tlg.summarize_spec] reads every
    engine argument from it (ADR-0005).
    """

    #: The cards ``context`` tag written to every ARD row.  One spec
    #: class serves one template method, so the tag is a class fact,
    #: not a YAML field.
    context: ClassVar[str] = ""
    #: ``True`` when ``rows`` is a hierarchy (SOC → PT, PARAM → visit);
    #: ``False`` when each row field is an independent flat breakdown.
    nested: ClassVar[bool] = False
    #: Extra text for the missing-prefilter-column error (e.g. how to
    #: state a post-baseline rule without ONTRTFL).
    prefilter_hint: ClassVar[str] = ""

    output_type: str = "summary"
    rows: list[Row] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Row groupings (hierarchy for nested templates).  Set inline "
            "via [`TLGBuilder.rows()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.rows]."
        ),
    )
    uncoded: Uncoded | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The uncoded rule: coding columns whose nulls become a "
            "visible level before counting.  Each template sets its own "
            "default; ``null`` switches the rule off.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.uncoded()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.uncoded]."
        ),
    )
    prefilter: Any | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The template's own record filter, applied after "
            "``dataset_filter`` — a ``pl.Expr`` or a string expression "
            '(e.g. ``\'pl.col("ABLFL").ne_missing("Y")\'`` on a '
            "change-from-baseline table).  Each template sets its own "
            "default; ``null`` switches it off.  Every column it names "
            "is a required column.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.prefilter()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.prefilter]."
        ),
    )

    _validate_prefilter = field_validator("prefilter")(_check_filter_field)
    columns: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: ["TRTA"],
        description=(
            "Column-grouping variables (typically a treatment column).  "
            "Exactly one entry — multi-column grouping is not implemented "
            "yet, and the engine would silently read only the first.  "
            "Set inline via [`TLGBuilder.by()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.by]."
        ),
    )
    statistics: list[Statistic] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: [Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT],
        description=(
            "Statistics computed for each row.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.stats()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.stats]."
        ),
    )
    pools: list[GroupPool] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Composite (pooled) treatment groups.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.pools()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.pools]."
        ),
    )
    column_order: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Explicit ordering of column labels in the rendered output.  "
            "Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.column_order()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.column_order]."
        ),
    )
    value_col: str = Field(
        default="AVAL",
        description=(
            "Analysis-value column used for continuous statistics "
            "(mean/SD/median/…).  Summarize ``CHG``, ``PCHG`` or ``BASE`` "
            "by pointing this at the column — no pre-renaming needed.  "
            "When the column is missing but continuous statistics are "
            "requested, the engine raises instead of emitting null stats."
        ),
    )
    label_col: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Column holding display labels for the first row field's "
            'values (e.g. ``"PARAM"`` when the row field is '
            '``"PARAMCD"``) so stubs show display names instead of '
            "codes.  ``None`` shows the raw values."
        ),
    )
    decimals: dict[str, str] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Per-statistic format overrides — ARD ``stat_name`` (e.g. "
            '``"mean"``, ``"sd"``, ``"pct"``) to format string (e.g. '
            '``"xx.xx"``).  Overrides the built-in defaults for this '
            "table; individual rows may override again via "
            ":attr:`Row.decimals`."
        ),
    )

    def prefilter_columns(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return the columns the spec's prefilter names.

        Every one of them is a required column of the template, so a
        change table's ``ABLFL`` guard makes ``ABLFL`` required and
        ``prefilter=None`` lifts that requirement with it.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Column names in first-seen order; empty when the
                prefilter is ``None``.

        Examples:
            ``LBChgSpec().prefilter_columns() == ["ABLFL", "CHG"]``
        """
        expr = resolve_filter(self.prefilter)
        if expr is None:
            return []
        return list(dict.fromkeys(expr.meta.root_names()))

    def check(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> list[str]:
        """Run the pre-validation diagnostic without computing.

        The base checks (required columns, prefilter columns, required
        flag values) plus one warning per row field absent from *df*,
        whose sub-analysis the engine would skip.

        Args:
            df: The DataFrame to check.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if all checks pass).

        Examples:
            ``MHSummarySpec().check(admh)``
        """
        diagnostics = super().check(df)
        available = set(df.columns)
        for row_def in self.rows:
            if row_def.field not in available:
                diagnostics.append(
                    f"WARNING: Column '{row_def.field}' not present — "
                    f"'{row_def.label or row_def.field}' sub-analysis will be skipped."
                )
        return diagnostics

    @field_validator("columns")
    @classmethod
    def _single_group_column(cls, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        """Reject multi-column (or empty) grouping loudly.

        The engine reads only ``columns[0]``; accepting more would
        silently discard the rest of the grouping.
        """
        if len(value) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'columns' must contain exactly one treatment-arm column "
                f"(got {value!r}). Multi-column grouping is not implemented "
                "— the engine would silently read only the first entry. "
                "Move additional grouping into the row hierarchy ('rows') "
                "or file a feature request."
            )
        return value

class TLGSpec(BaseModel):
    """Base specification for all TLG outputs.

    Subclasses define output-type-specific defaults and required
    columns.  Every field below is also settable inline through the
    fluent [`TLGBuilder`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder] — the cross-references
    in each field's description point to the matching builder method.
    """

    #: Spec fields defined on the model but ignored by the owning
    #: template method (e.g. ``rows`` on the fixed-hierarchy shift
    #: table).  ``TLGBuilder.to_spec()`` raises when accumulated builder
    #: state maps onto one of these instead of silently dropping it.
    _unconsumed_spec_fields: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset()

    template: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            'Registry template id (e.g. ``"aet01"``).  Carrying it in '
            "the YAML makes the file self-executing: "
            "[`load_spec()`][fleet.tlg.load_spec] resolves the spec "
            "class and [`run_spec()`][fleet.tlg.run_spec] dispatches to "
            "the template's method through the registry."
        ),
    )
    schema_version: Literal[1] = Field(
        default=1,
        description=(
            "TLG spec schema version.  Bump-guarded so a future breaking "
            "layout change can be detected at load time."
        ),
    )
    output_type: str = Field(
        default="base",
        description=(
            "Discriminator distinguishing summary vs listing layouts. "
            "Subclasses override this default."
        ),
    )
    adsl_filter: Any | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Population filter on ADSL — a "
            "``pl.Expr`` or a string expression such as "
            '``\'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"\'`` (the YAML-serializable form).  '
            "It selects the subjects for the big N, and only their "
            "analysis records are counted (ADR-0016).  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.population()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.population]."
        ),
    )
    dataset_filter: Any | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Filter applied to the analysis dataset (e.g. ADAE) — a "
            "``pl.Expr`` or a string expression (the YAML-serializable "
            "form).  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.filter()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.filter]."
        ),
    )
    header_rows: list[OverallStat] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Whole-dataset aggregate rows rendered above the hierarchy.  "
            "Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.header_rows()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.header_rows]."
        ),
    )
    required_columns: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Columns that must be present in the dataset; checked by :meth:`validate_dataframe`."
        ),
    )
    required_flags: dict[str, list[str]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description=(
            "Per-column lists of values that must be present in the data "
            "(content validation).  Empty by default."
        ),
    )
    interactive: InteractiveBlock | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Declared degrees of freedom for the explorer "
            "(``fleet tlg explore``).  Each axis maps onto one existing "
            "spec field; the all-defaults variant is the batch output.  "
            "Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.interactive()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.interactive]."
        ),
    )

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid", "arbitrary_types_allowed": True}

    _validate_filters = field_validator("adsl_filter", "dataset_filter")(_check_filter_field)

    #: interactive axis name → the spec field its choices map onto.
    _INTERACTIVE_AXIS_FIELDS: ClassVar[dict[str, str]] = {
        "groupby": "columns",
        "population": "adsl_filter",
        "dataset_filter": "dataset_filter",
        "stats": "statistics",
    }

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_interactive_applies(self) -> TLGSpec:
        """Reject interactive axes mapping to fields this spec cannot consume.

        Variants are built with ``model_copy(update=...)`` (no
        re-validation), so an axis targeting a missing or unconsumed
        field must fail here, at construction, naming the axis.
        """
        if self.interactive is None:
            return self
        fields = type(self).model_fields
        for axis, target in self._INTERACTIVE_AXIS_FIELDS.items():
            if getattr(self.interactive, axis) is None:
                continue
            if target not in fields or target in self._unconsumed_spec_fields:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"interactive.{axis} maps to spec field {target!r}, which "
                    f"{type(self).__name__} does not consume — the axis would "
                    "be silently ignored. Remove it or target a template that "
                    "consumes it."
                )
        if self.interactive.groupby is not None and "statistics" not in fields:
            raise ValueError(
                "interactive.groupby needs a summary spec — listings have no "
                "column grouping. Remove the axis."
            )
        return self

    @field_validator("schema_version", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _coerce_schema_version(cls, value: Any) -> Any:
        """Accept ``schema_version: "1"`` (string form) as version 1."""
        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip().isdigit():
            return int(value.strip())
        return value

    def validate_dataframe(self, df: pl.DataFrame, *, group_col: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Run structural + content validation against *df*.

        Args:
            df: The analysis DataFrame.
            group_col: Effective treatment-arm column.  When it overrides
                the spec's default arm column (``columns[0]``), the
                default is substituted in the required-columns check so
                ``groupby="TRT01A"`` works on data without ``TRTA``.

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If required columns are missing, required flag
                values are absent, or other data constraints are violated.
        """
        self._validate_structural(df, group_col=group_col)
        self._validate_content(df)

    def _validate_structural(self, df: pl.DataFrame, *, group_col: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Tier 1: check required columns exist."""
        required = list(self.required_columns)
        default_group = getattr(self, "columns", None)
        if group_col and default_group and isinstance(default_group[0], str):
            required = [group_col if c == default_group[0] else c for c in required]
        available = set(df.columns)
        missing = [c for c in required if c not in available]
        if missing:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"{self.__class__.__name__} requires columns {required} "
                f"but DataFrame is missing {missing}. "
                f"Available: {sorted(available)}"
            )
        prefilter_missing = [c for c in self.prefilter_columns() if c not in available]
        if prefilter_missing:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"{self.__class__.__name__}'s prefilter names columns "
                f"{self.prefilter_columns()} but DataFrame is missing "
                f"{prefilter_missing}. Add the column, or set prefilter=None "
                "to switch the rule off (visible in the spec)."
                f"{getattr(self, 'prefilter_hint', '')} "
                f"Available: {sorted(available)}"
            )

    def prefilter_columns(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return the columns the spec's prefilter names.

        Every one of them is a required column of the template.  A
        listing has no prefilter, so the base returns none; summary
        specs override this.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Column names in first-seen order; empty here.

        Examples:
            ``AEListingSpec().prefilter_columns() == []``
        """
        return []

    def _validate_content(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
        """Tier 2: check required flag/PARAMCD values exist in data."""
        for col, required_vals in self.required_flags.items():
            if col not in df.columns:
                raise SchemaError(
                    f"{self.__class__.__name__} requires column '{col}' for "
                    f"content validation but it is missing."
                )
            actual = set(df[col].drop_nulls().unique().to_list())
            missing = [v for v in required_vals if v not in actual]
            if missing:
                raise SchemaError(
                    f"{self.__class__.__name__} requires {col} values "
                    f"{required_vals} but data is missing {missing}. "
                    f"Available: {sorted(actual)}"
                )

    def check(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> list[str]:
        """Pre-validation diagnostic — returns warnings without raising.

        Args:
            df: The DataFrame to check.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if all checks pass).
        """
        diagnostics: list[str] = []
        available = set(df.columns)
        missing = [c for c in self.required_columns if c not in available]
        if missing:
            diagnostics.append(
                f"MISSING COLUMNS: {missing} required by {self.__class__.__name__} are not present."
            )
        prefilter_missing = [c for c in self.prefilter_columns() if c not in available]
        if prefilter_missing:
            diagnostics.append(
                f"MISSING PREFILTER COLUMNS: {prefilter_missing} named by the "
                f"{self.__class__.__name__} prefilter are not present."
            )
        for col, required_vals in self.required_flags.items():
            if col not in available:
                diagnostics.append(f"MISSING FLAG COLUMN: '{col}' not in DataFrame.")
            else:
                actual = set(df[col].drop_nulls().unique().to_list())
                absent = [v for v in required_vals if v not in actual]
                if absent:
                    diagnostics.append(f"MISSING VALUES: {col} missing {absent}.")
        return diagnostics

    def to_yaml(self) -> str:
        """Serialize this spec to a YAML string.

        Filters (``adsl_filter``, ``dataset_filter``, ``prefilter``,
        header-row ``filter``) serialize only in their string-expression form.  A
        live ``pl.Expr`` cannot be serialized faithfully, and silently
        dropping it would change the numbers a reloaded spec computes —
        so it raises instead.

        Returns:
            str: YAML representation of the spec.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If any filter field holds a ``pl.Expr``.  Pass
                the filter as a string, e.g. ``'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"'``.
        """
        for field_name in ("adsl_filter", "dataset_filter", "prefilter"):
            value = getattr(self, field_name, None)
            if value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{field_name} holds a {type(value).__name__} and cannot be "
                    "YAML-serialized. Use a string expression instead, e.g. "
                    'adsl_filter=\'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"\'.'
                )
        for hr in getattr(self, "header_rows", []):
            if hr.filter is not None and not isinstance(hr.filter, str):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"header_rows[{hr.label!r}].filter holds a "
                    f"{type(hr.filter).__name__} and cannot be YAML-serialized. "
                    "Use a string expression instead."
                )
        data = self.model_dump(exclude_none=True, exclude_defaults=False)
        # An explicit prefilter=None switches a template's default rule
        # off; dropping it would bring the default back on reload.
        if "prefilter" in self.model_fields_set and getattr(self, "prefilter", 0) is None:
            data["prefilter"] = None
        # Convert enums to their values
        data = _enum_to_value(data)
        return yaml.dump(data, default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=False)

    @classmethod
    def from_yaml(cls, yaml_str: str) -> Self:
        """Deserialize a spec from a YAML string.

        Args:
            yaml_str: YAML text.

        Returns:
            Self: The reconstructed spec instance (the class it is called on).
        """
        data = yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
        return cls.model_validate(data)

class Uncoded(BaseModel):
    """The uncoded rule: give a null coding term a visible level.

    GDSR templates recode a missing MedDRA or ATC term to
    ``"No Coding Available"`` instead of dropping the record, so a
    subject whose only events are uncoded is still counted.  A spec
    carries one ``Uncoded`` (or ``None`` to switch the rule off); set
    inline via [`TLGBuilder.uncoded()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.uncoded].
    """

    columns: list[str] = Field(
        ...,
        description=(
            "Coding columns to fill when null (e.g. ``AEBODSYS`` and "
            "``AEDECOD``).  Names absent from the dataset are skipped."
        ),
    )
    label: str = Field(
        default=NO_CODING_LABEL,
        description="Replacement level written into every null coding column.",
    )

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}
