def paginate(
    model: TableModel,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> list[TableModel]:
    """Split a ``TableModel`` into display pages.

    Pagination lives in the model layer so every renderer (HTML, PDF,
    RTF, PPTX) inherits identical page composition: each page repeats
    the title, subtitle, column headers, and footnote blocks.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page.  A stub-only row
            (group/section heading) is never left orphaned at the bottom
            of a page.  ``None`` means no row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable whose stub rows force a page break (e.g.
            ``"PARAMCD"`` → one page per parameter).  Defaults to
            ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Returns:
        list[TableModel]: One model per page (a single-element list when
        no pagination applies).

    Examples:
        One page per lab parameter, at most 20 rows each::

            from fleet.tlg.render import ard_to_table_model, paginate

            model = ard_to_table_model(ard)
            pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=20, page_by="PARAMCD")
    """
    effective_page_by = page_by or model.metadata.page_by
    if rows_per_page is None and not effective_page_by:
        return [model]

    # ── 1. Split into blocks at page_by stub boundaries ──
    blocks: list[list[TableRow]] = [[]]
    for row in model.rows:
        if (
            effective_page_by
            and row.variable == effective_page_by
            and row.row_type in ("group", "section")
            and blocks[-1]
        ):
            blocks.append([])
        blocks[-1].append(row)

    # ── 2. Split blocks by row count ──
    pages_rows: list[list[TableRow]] = []
    for block in blocks:
        if not block:
            continue
        if rows_per_page is None:
            pages_rows.append(block)
        else:
            pages_rows.extend(_chunk_rows(block, rows_per_page))

    if not pages_rows:
        return [model]
    return [
        TableModel(
            metadata=model.metadata,
            columns=model.columns,
            rows=rows,
            stub_label=model.stub_label,
        )
        for rows in pages_rows
    ]

def paginate_listing(
    model: ListingModel,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
) -> list[ListingModel]:
    """Split a ``ListingModel`` into display pages of *rows_per_page* rows.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model.
        rows_per_page: Maximum data rows per page; ``None`` disables
            splitting.

    Returns:
        list[ListingModel]: One model per page.

    Examples:
        Split a long listing into 40-row pages::

            pages = paginate_listing(model, rows_per_page=40)
    """
    if rows_per_page is None or len(model.data) <= rows_per_page:
        return [model]
    return [
        ListingModel(
            metadata=model.metadata,
            column_labels=model.column_labels,
            data=model.data[i : i + rows_per_page],
        )
        for i in range(0, len(model.data), rows_per_page)
    ]

def render_explorer(
    entries: Sequence[ExplorerEntry],
    path: str | Path | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render the declared variant space of one or more specs to HTML.

    For every entry, enumerates its ``interactive:`` variants
    ([`enumerate_variants`][fleet.tlg._variants.enumerate_variants]),
    runs each through the identical engine path used by ``fleet tlg
    run`` (``run_spec`` → ``ard_to_table_model`` → ``render_html``), and
    embeds the pre-rendered fragments — plus each variant's ARD as
    downloadable JSON and its exact spec YAML in a "show definition"
    panel — into one self-contained HTML file.  The client-side script
    only toggles fragment visibility.

    Args:
        entries: One :class:`ExplorerEntry` per spec.
        path: Optional output file path; the HTML is also returned.

    Returns:
        str: The complete explorer HTML document.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If a spec has no template id, or its variant space
            exceeds the hard cap (500).

    Examples:
        Build a two-axis AE overview explorer::

            import fleet.tlg as tlg
            from fleet.tlg.render.explorer import ExplorerEntry, render_explorer

            spec = tlg.load_spec("specs/aet01.yaml")
            render_explorer(
                [ExplorerEntry(name="aet01", spec=spec, df=adae, adsl=adsl)],
                path="explorer.html",
            )
    """
    body: list[str] = []
    tabs: list[str] = []
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()

    for idx, entry in enumerate(entries):
        entry_id = _slug(entry.name)
        if entry_id in seen_ids:
            entry_id = f"{entry_id}-{idx}"
        seen_ids.add(entry_id)
        if entry.spec.template is None or entry.spec.template not in TEMPLATES:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Explorer entry {entry.name!r}: spec needs a registered "
                f"'template:' id to dispatch through run_spec(). Known ids: "
                f"{sorted(TEMPLATES)}"
            )
        meta = TEMPLATES[entry.spec.template]
        is_listing = meta.output_type is OutputType.LISTING
        variants = enumerate_variants(entry.spec)
        axis_order = list(variants[0].axis_labels)

        hidden = "" if idx == 0 else " hidden"
        body.append(f'<section class="fleet-entry" data-entry="{entry_id}"{hidden}>')
        body.append(_widget_bar(entry_id, variants, entry.spec))
        for variant in variants:
            fragment, result = _variant_fragment(entry, variant, is_listing=is_listing)
            body.append(
                _variant_section(
                    entry_id, entry.name, variant, fragment, result.write_json(), axis_order
                )
            )
        body.append("</section>")
        active = " active" if idx == 0 else ""
        tabs.append(
            f'<button class="fleet-tab{active}" data-entry="{entry_id}">{_esc(entry.name)}</button>'
        )

    tab_bar = f'<nav class="fleet-tabs">{"".join(tabs)}</nav>' if len(entries) > 1 else ""
    html = "\n".join(
        [
            "<!DOCTYPE html>",
            '<html lang="en">',
            '<head><meta charset="utf-8">',
            "<title>Fleet TLG Explorer</title>",
            _EXPLORER_CSS,
            "</head>",
            "<body>",
            f'<header class="fleet-explorer-header"><h1>Fleet TLG Explorer</h1>{tab_bar}</header>',
            "<main>",
            *body,
            "</main>",
            _EXPLORER_JS,
            "</body>",
            "</html>",
        ]
    )
    if path is not None:
        p = Path(path)
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
    return html

def render_html(
    model: TableModel,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style HTML table.

    Pagination happens in the model layer (:func:`~fleet.tlg.render.paginate`):
    each page repeats title, column headers, and footnotes, carries a
    ``Page X of Y`` footer, and breaks on a real page in print/PDF media.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template string.  If given, the
            generated ``<table>`` block replaces the ``{table}`` placeholder,
            enabling embedding in sponsor portals, Quarto documents, or
            interactive dashboards.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page; ``None`` disables
            row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable to page-break on (e.g. ``"PARAMCD"``).
            Defaults to ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Returns:
        str: Complete HTML string (with ``<style>`` block) or injected
            into *html_wrapper*.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary to HTML::

            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
            html = render_html(model)
    """
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page, page_by=page_by)

    parts: list[str] = ['<div class="fleet-table-container">', _SUMMARY_CSS]
    if len(pages) == 1:
        parts += _table_page_parts(pages[0])
    else:
        for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
            parts.append('<div class="fleet-page">')
            parts += _table_page_parts(page, page_footer=f"Page {idx} of {len(pages)}")
            parts.append("</div>")
    parts.append("</div>")

    html = "\n".join(parts)

    if html_wrapper is not None:
        return html_wrapper.replace("{table}", html)

    return html

def render_listing_pdf(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` to a PDF file via WeasyPrint.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model.
        path: Output PDF file path.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template with ``{table}`` placeholder.
        rows_per_page: Maximum data rows per page; ``None`` renders one
            continuous listing.

    Returns:
        Path: The written PDF path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If WeasyPrint is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE listing to PDF::

            listing = adae.tlg.ae.template("ael01").to_listing()
            model = listing_to_model(listing, RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.7"))
            render_listing_pdf(model, "ae_listing.pdf")
    """
    try:
        import weasyprint  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "WeasyPrint is required for PDF export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add weasyprint\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pdf]"
        ) from None

    html = render_listing_html(model, html_wrapper=html_wrapper, rows_per_page=rows_per_page)
    doc = (
        "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
        '<html><head><meta charset="utf-8">'
        "<style>"
        "@page { size: landscape; margin: 1cm; }"
        "body { font-family: 'Courier New', Courier, monospace; font-size: 9pt; }"
        "</style></head><body>\n"
        f"{html}\n"
        "</body></html>"
    )
    p = Path(path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    weasyprint.HTML(string=doc).write_pdf(str(p))
    return p

def render_listing_pptx(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` to a PPTX slide deck.

    Each slide contains a flat data listing as an editable PowerPoint
    table.  Long listings are chunked across slides (title, headers,
    and footnotes repeat per slide).  The listing can be modified after
    export.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.
        rows_per_page: Data rows per slide (default 15).

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE listing to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import listing_to_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_listing_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.7.1", subtitle="AE Listing")
            model = listing_to_model(listing_df, meta)
            render_listing_pptx(model, "ae_listing.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)
    pages = paginate_listing(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page or _MAX_ROWS_PER_SLIDE)

    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    for page in pages:
        slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

        # ── Title + subtitle ──
        top = Inches(0.3)
        if page.metadata.title:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.title
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.45)

        if page.metadata.subtitle:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.subtitle
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.4)

        top += Inches(0.1)

        # ── Table ──
        n_cols = len(page.column_labels)
        n_rows = 1 + len(page.data)  # header + data

        table_width = Inches(12.3)
        table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
        table_left = Inches(0.5)

        tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(
            n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height
        )
        table = tbl_shape.table

        col_width = int(table_width / max(n_cols, 1))
        for ci in range(n_cols):
            table.columns[ci].width = Emu(col_width)

        # Headers
        for ci, lbl in enumerate(page.column_labels):
            cell = table.cell(0, ci)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = lbl
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_bg"])
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_fg"])

        # Data rows
        for ri, row_data in enumerate(page.data, start=1):
            bg = th["alt_row_bg"] if ri % 2 == 0 else None
            for ci, lbl in enumerate(page.column_labels):
                cell = table.cell(ri, ci)
                cell.text = ""
                p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
                p.text = row_data.get(lbl, "")
                p.font.name = th["font_name"]
                p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
                p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
                if bg:
                    cell.fill.solid()
                    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)

        # ── Footnotes ──
        if page.metadata.footnotes:
            fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
            fn_text = "\n".join(page.metadata.footnotes)
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = fn_text
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

def render_listing_rtf(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = _DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` as a pharma-style RTF listing.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Optional output file path; the RTF is written when given.
        rows_per_page: Maximum data rows per page (default 40).  ``None``
            renders one continuous listing.

    Returns:
        str: The complete RTF document.

    Examples:
        Lab abnormalities listing to RTF::

            listing = adlb.tlg.lb.l_listing()
            model = listing_to_model(listing, RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.8.1"))
            render_listing_rtf(model, "outputs/l_lb_abnormal.rtf")
    """
    pages = paginate_listing(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page)

    n_cols = max(len(model.column_labels), 1)
    col_w = _USABLE_W // n_cols
    positions = _cell_positions([col_w] * n_cols)
    aligns = [r"\ql"] * n_cols

    parts: list[str] = [_DOC_HEADER]
    for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
        if idx > 1:
            parts.append(r"\page")
        parts += _title_block(page.metadata.title, page.metadata.subtitle)

        parts.append(
            _row_rtf(
                list(page.column_labels),
                positions,
                aligns,
                header=True,
                border_top=_BDR_HEAVY,
                border_bottom=_BDR_LIGHT,
            )
        )

        for r_idx, row_data in enumerate(page.data):
            cells = [row_data.get(label, "") for label in page.column_labels]
            parts.append(
                _row_rtf(
                    cells,
                    positions,
                    aligns,
                    border_bottom=_BDR_HEAVY if r_idx == len(page.data) - 1 else None,
                )
            )

        parts += _footer_block(page.metadata.footnotes, f"Page {idx} of {len(pages)}")

    parts.append("}")
    return _write("\n".join(parts), path)

def render_pdf(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` to a PDF file via WeasyPrint.

    Pagination comes from the model layer: pages break on real PDF
    pages with repeated title, column headers, and footnotes, plus a
    ``Page X of Y`` footer.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model.
        path: Output PDF file path.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template with ``{table}`` placeholder.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page; ``None`` disables
            row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable to page-break on (e.g. ``"PARAMCD"``).
            Defaults to ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Raises:

    Examples:

            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
            render_pdf(model, "ae_summary.pdf")
    """

        import weasyprint  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "WeasyPrint is required for PDF export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add weasyprint\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pdf]"
        ) from None

    html = render_html(
        model, html_wrapper=html_wrapper, rows_per_page=rows_per_page, page_by=page_by
    )
    # Wrap in a minimal HTML document for WeasyPrint
    doc = (
        "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
        '<html><head><meta charset="utf-8">'
        "<style>"
        "@page { size: landscape; margin: 1cm; }"
        "body { font-family: 'Courier New', Courier, monospace; font-size: 9pt; }"
        "</style></head><body>\n"
        f"{html}\n"
        "</body></html>"
    )
    p = Path(path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    weasyprint.HTML(string=doc).write_pdf(str(p))
    return p

Each slide contains a fully editable PowerPoint table with: - Title and subtitle from RenderMetadata - Column headers with optional (N=xx) display - Row hierarchy with indentation and bold formatting - Footnotes rendered below the table

def render_pptx(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` to a PPTX slide deck.

    Each slide contains a fully editable PowerPoint table with:
    - Title and subtitle from ``RenderMetadata``
    - Column headers with optional (N=xx) display
    - Row hierarchy with indentation and bold formatting
    - Footnotes rendered below the table

    Long tables are chunked across slides via the model-layer paginator
    (title, headers, and footnotes repeat per slide), so a 300-row table
    never lands on one unreadable slide.

    The output is editable: users can modify fonts, colours, text, and
    layout in PowerPoint or LibreOffice Impress after export.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.  Keys include
            ``font_name``, ``font_size_body``, ``header_bg``, etc.
            See ``_DEFAULT_THEME`` for all available keys.
        rows_per_page: Body rows per slide (default 15 — what fits a
            16:9 slide at the default body font).

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary ARD to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import ard_to_table_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1", subtitle="AE Summary")
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
            render_pptx(model, "ae_summary.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page or _MAX_ROWS_PER_SLIDE)

    prs = Presentation()
    # Landscape 16:9
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    for page in pages:
        slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank layout
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

        # ── Title + subtitle ──
        top = Inches(0.3)
        if page.metadata.title:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.title
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.45)

        if page.metadata.subtitle:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.subtitle
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.4)

        top += Inches(0.1)

        # ── Table dimensions ──
        n_cols = 1 + len(page.columns)  # stub + arms
        n_rows = 1 + len(page.rows)  # header + data rows

        table_width = Inches(12.3)
        table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
        table_left = Inches(0.5)

        tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(
            n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height
        )
        table = tbl_shape.table

        # Distribute column widths: stub gets 30%, rest evenly split
        stub_width = int(table_width * 0.30)
        arm_width = int((table_width - stub_width) / max(len(page.columns), 1))
        table.columns[0].width = Emu(stub_width)
        for ci in range(1, n_cols):
            table.columns[ci].width = Emu(arm_width)

        # ── Helper: set cell text + style ──
        def _set_cell(
            row_idx: int,
            col_idx: int,
            text: str,
            *,
            bold: bool = False,
            font_size: int | None = None,
            bg: str | None = None,
            fg: str | None = None,
            align: Any = PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
            indent: int = 0,
            table: Any = table,
        ) -> None:
            cell = table.cell(row_idx, col_idx)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = text
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(font_size or th["font_size_body"])
            p.font.bold = bold
            p.alignment = align
            if fg:
                p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(fg)
            if bg:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)
            if indent:
                p.level = min(indent, 8)

        # ── Column headers ──
        _set_cell(0, 0, page.stub_label, bold=True, bg=th["header_bg"], fg=th["header_fg"])
        for ci, col in enumerate(page.columns, start=1):
            _set_cell(
                0,
                ci,
                col.display,
                bold=True,
                bg=th["header_bg"],
                fg=th["header_fg"],
                align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
            )

        # ── Data rows ──
        for ri, row in enumerate(page.rows, start=1):
            # Row background
            if row.row_type in ("group", "section"):
                bg = th["group_bg"]
            elif ri % 2 == 0:
                bg = th["alt_row_bg"]
            else:
                bg = None

            # Stub cell
            indent_spaces = "  " * row.indent
            _set_cell(
                ri,
                0,
                f"{indent_spaces}{row.label}",
                bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
                bg=bg,
            )

            # Value cells
            for ci, col in enumerate(page.columns, start=1):
                val = row.cells.get(col.label, "")
                _set_cell(
                    ri,
                    ci,
                    val,
                    bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
                    bg=bg,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
                )

        # ── Footnotes ──
        if page.metadata.footnotes:
            fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
            fn_text = "\n".join(page.metadata.footnotes)
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = fn_text
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

def render_rtf(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = _DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style RTF table.

    Every page carries the title block, the column-header row (also
    flagged ``\\trhdr`` so word processors repeat it on overflow), the
    footnote block, and a ``Page X of Y`` footer.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        path: Optional output file path; the RTF is written when given.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page (default 40, sized for
            9pt landscape letter).  ``None`` disables row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable to page-break on (e.g. ``"PARAMCD"``).
            Defaults to ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Returns:
        str: The complete RTF document.

    Examples:
        Inline AE summary to a submission RTF::

            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
            render_rtf(model, "outputs/t_ae_summary.rtf")
    """
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page, page_by=page_by)

    stub_w = int(_USABLE_W * 0.34)
    arm_w = (_USABLE_W - stub_w) // max(len(model.columns), 1)
    positions = _cell_positions([stub_w] + [arm_w] * len(model.columns))
    aligns = [r"\ql"] + [r"\qc"] * len(model.columns)

    parts: list[str] = [_DOC_HEADER]
    for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
        if idx > 1:
            parts.append(r"\page")
        parts += _title_block(page.metadata.title, page.metadata.subtitle)

        # Column headers: heavy rule above, light rule below.
        header_cells = [page.stub_label] + [col.display for col in page.columns]
        parts.append(
            _row_rtf(
                header_cells,
                positions,
                aligns,
                header=True,
                border_top=_BDR_HEAVY,
                border_bottom=_BDR_LIGHT,
            )
        )

        for r_idx, row in enumerate(page.rows):
            cells = [row.label] + [row.cells.get(col.label, "") for col in page.columns]
            parts.append(
                _row_rtf(
                    cells,
                    positions,
                    aligns,
                    bold=row.bold,
                    indent=row.indent,
                    border_bottom=_BDR_HEAVY if r_idx == len(page.rows) - 1 else None,
                )
            )

        parts += _footer_block(page.metadata.footnotes, f"Page {idx} of {len(pages)}")

    parts.append("}")
    return _write("\n".join(parts), path)

class TLGBuilder:
    """Fluent builder for constructing TLG ARDs inline.

    This is a shared base class composed into every TLG sub-namespace.
    Domain-specific defaults (required columns, default statistics,
    ``context`` label) are baked into the sub-namespace rather than the
    builder.

    Args:
        df: The primary analysis DataFrame.
        context: Domain context label (e.g. ``"t_ae_summary"``).
        spec_cls: The spec Pydantic model class for this domain.
        namespace_cls: The namespace class that implements ``t_summary()``.
        defaults: Domain-specific default kwargs for spec construction.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        df: pl.DataFrame,
        *,
        context: str,
        spec_cls: type[TLGSpec],
        namespace_cls: type[Any],
        defaults: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._df = df
        self._context = context
        self._spec_cls = spec_cls
        self._namespace_cls = namespace_cls
        self._defaults: dict[str, Any] = defaults or {}
        self._method = "t_summary"
        self._adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None
        self._adsl_filter: pl.Expr | str | None = None
        self._dataset_filter: pl.Expr | str | None = None
        self._group_col: str | None = None
        self._header_rows_list: list[OverallStat] = []
        self._rows_fields: list[str | Row] = []
        self._statistics: list[Statistic] | None = None
        self._pools: list[GroupPool] = []
        self._column_order: list[str] = []
        self._value_col: str | None = None
        self._label_col: str | None = None
        self._decimals: dict[str, str] | None = None
        self._uncoded: Uncoded | None = _UNSET
        self._prefilter: pl.Expr | str | None = _UNSET
        self._listing_columns: list[str | Column] | None = None
        self._sort_by: list[str] | None = None
        self._template_id: str | None = None
        self._template_fn: Callable[..., pl.DataFrame] | None = None
        self._interactive: InteractiveBlock | None = None

    def _clone(self) -> TLGBuilder:
        return copy.copy(self)

    def _targets_listing(self) -> bool:
        """True when the current spec class describes a listing layout."""
        field = self._spec_cls.model_fields.get("output_type")
        return field is not None and field.default == "listing"

    def _has_reinterpretable_state(self) -> bool:
        """True when row/stat/format verbs have already accumulated state."""
        return bool(
            self._rows_fields
            or self._statistics is not None
            or self._header_rows_list
            or self._pools
            or self._column_order
            or self._value_col is not None
            or self._label_col is not None
            or self._decimals is not None
            or self._uncoded is not _UNSET
            or self._prefilter is not _UNSET
            or self._listing_columns is not None
            or self._sort_by is not None
        )

    def _require_consumed_field(self, field: str, verb: str) -> None:
        """Raise when builder state maps to a field the target won't consume."""
        cls = self._spec_cls
        if field not in cls.model_fields:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"{verb} maps to spec field '{field}', which {cls.__name__} "
                f"does not define — the target template method "
                f"'{self._method}' would silently ignore it. Remove the verb "
                "or target a template that consumes it."
            )

    def by(self, col: str) -> TLGBuilder:

        Returns:

    def template(self, template_id: str) -> TLGBuilder:
        """Target a registered template so materialisation runs its method.

        Resolves *template_id* through the template registry (built-ins
        and user registrations alike): the builder will materialise via
        that template's namespace method (e.g. ``lbt02`` → ``t_chg``) —
        or its registered function for user templates — with the
        template's spec class.  Listing templates (e.g. ``ael01``)
        materialise via :meth:`to_listing`.

        **Ordering**: call ``template()`` *before* row/stat/format verbs.
        It swaps the builder's spec class, so state accumulated earlier
        is re-validated against — and interpreted by — the new target's
        spec; a ``UserWarning`` is emitted when that happens.

        Args:
            template_id: Registry id (e.g. ``"aet02"``, ``"lbt02"``).

        Returns:
            TLGBuilder: Builder targeting the template's method and spec.

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If the id is unknown, belongs to a different
                namespace, or is a graph template.

        Examples:
            Materialise the AET02 shell::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .template("aet02")
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        from ._registry import TEMPLATES, OutputType

        meta = TEMPLATES.get(template_id)
        if meta is None:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Unknown template id {template_id!r}. Known ids: {sorted(TEMPLATES)}"
            )
        if meta.output_type is OutputType.GRAPH:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Template {template_id!r} is a graph, which the inline builder cannot materialise."
            )
        new = self._clone()
        if meta.func is not None:
            # User-registered template: self-contained function, not bound
            # to a namespace method.
            new._template_fn = meta.func
            new._spec_cls = meta.spec_cls or SummarySpecBase
        else:
            spec_classes = getattr(self._namespace_cls, "_builder_specs", {})
            if meta.method not in spec_classes:
                raise SchemaError(
                    f"Template {template_id!r} ({meta.namespace}.{meta.method}) does "
                    f"not belong to this namespace ({self._context})."
                )
            new._method = meta.method
            new._spec_cls = meta.spec_cls or spec_classes[meta.method]
        new._template_id = meta.id
        if self._has_reinterpretable_state():
            warnings.warn(
                f"template({template_id!r}) was called after row/stat/format "
                "verbs — the accumulated state will be reinterpreted by "
                f"{new._spec_cls.__name__}. Call .template() first to avoid "
                "surprises.",
                UserWarning,
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        return new

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Materialisation                                                      #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def to_spec(self) -> TLGSpec:
        """Serialise accumulated builder state to the equivalent spec.

        Every verb the user called must land on a spec field the target
        template's method actually consumes — otherwise this raises
        instead of silently dropping state (e.g. ``rows()`` on the
        fixed-hierarchy ``lbt03`` shift table).

        Returns:
            TLGSpec: A spec instance matching the builder configuration
                (carrying ``template=<id>`` when targeted via
                :meth:`template`).

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If accumulated builder state maps to a spec
                field the target template's method does not consume, or
                to no field at all.

        Examples:
            Capture the builder state as a reusable spec::

                spec = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .template("aet02")
                    .to_spec()
                )
        """
        is_listing = self._targets_listing()
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = dict(self._defaults)

        if self._template_id is not None:
            kwargs["template"] = self._template_id
        if self._adsl_filter is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("adsl_filter", "population(adsl_filter=...)")
            kwargs["adsl_filter"] = self._adsl_filter
        if self._dataset_filter is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("dataset_filter", "filter()")
            kwargs["dataset_filter"] = self._dataset_filter
        if self._header_rows_list:
            self._require_consumed_field("header_rows", "header_rows()")
            kwargs["header_rows"] = self._header_rows_list
        if self._group_col:
            if is_listing:
                raise SchemaError(
                    "by() sets a grouping column, but the target template is "
                    "a listing — listings have no column grouping. Remove "
                    "by() or target a table template."
                )
            if "columns" in self._spec_cls.model_fields:
                kwargs["columns"] = [self._group_col]
        if self._rows_fields:
            kwargs.update(self._rows_kwargs())
        if self._statistics is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("statistics", "stats()")
            kwargs["statistics"] = self._statistics
        if self._pools:
            self._require_consumed_field("pools", "pools()")
            kwargs["pools"] = self._pools
        if self._column_order:
            self._require_consumed_field("column_order", "column_order()")
            kwargs["column_order"] = self._column_order
        if self._value_col is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("value_col", "value()")
            kwargs["value_col"] = self._value_col
        if self._label_col is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("label_col", "label()")
            kwargs["label_col"] = self._label_col
        if self._decimals is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("decimals", "decimals()")
            kwargs["decimals"] = self._decimals
        if self._uncoded is not _UNSET:
            self._require_consumed_field("uncoded", "uncoded()")
            kwargs["uncoded"] = self._uncoded
        if self._prefilter is not _UNSET:
            self._require_consumed_field("prefilter", "prefilter()")
            kwargs["prefilter"] = self._prefilter
        if self._listing_columns is not None:
            if not is_listing:
                raise SchemaError(
                    "columns() defines listing display columns, but the "
                    "target template is a table. Use by() for the grouping "
                    'column, or target a listing template (.template("ael01") '
                    "/ .to_listing())."
                )
            kwargs["columns"] = [
                c if isinstance(c, Column) else Column(field=c) for c in self._listing_columns
            ]
        if self._sort_by is not None:
            self._require_consumed_field("sort_by", "sort_by()")
            kwargs["sort_by"] = list(self._sort_by)
        if self._interactive is not None:
            kwargs["interactive"] = self._interactive

        return self._spec_cls(**kwargs)

    def _rows_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Map ``rows()`` state onto the target spec's row field(s).

        DM summarises independent categorical variables, not a row
        hierarchy — map the builder's rows() onto ``categorical_vars``
        (merging any ``Row.label`` into ``category_labels``).
        """
        row_objs = [f if isinstance(f, Row) else Row(field=f) for f in self._rows_fields]
        if "categorical_vars" not in self._spec_cls.model_fields:
            self._require_consumed_field("rows", "rows()")
            return {"rows": row_objs}
        unsupported = [
            r.field for r in row_objs if r.filter_value is not None or r.decimals is not None
        ]
        if unsupported:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"rows() entries {unsupported} carry filter_value/decimals, "
                f"which {self._spec_cls.__name__}'s categorical breakdown "
                "does not consume — they would be silently ignored."
            )
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"categorical_vars": [r.field for r in row_objs]}
        labels = {r.field: r.label for r in row_objs if r.label}
        if labels:
            default_field = self._spec_cls.model_fields["category_labels"]
            defaults = default_field.get_default(call_default_factory=True) or {}
            kwargs["category_labels"] = {**defaults, **labels}
        return kwargs

    def to_ard(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Materialise the builder to an ARD DataFrame.

        Constructs the equivalent spec and delegates to the targeted
        namespace method — ``t_summary()`` by default, the method
        selected via :meth:`template`, or the registered function for a
        user template.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: Long-format {cards}-compatible ARD.

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If the target template is a listing — call
                :meth:`to_listing` instead.

        Examples:
            Inline AE summary::

                ard = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl, adsl_filter=pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y")
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                    .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                    .to_ard()
                )
        """
        if self._template_fn is not None:
            return self._template_fn(
                self._df,
                adsl=self._adsl,
                spec=self.to_spec(),
                groupby=self._group_col,
            )
        if self._targets_listing():
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Template {self._template_id!r} is a listing — call "
                ".to_listing() instead of .to_ard()."
            )
        spec = self.to_spec()
        ns = self._namespace_cls(self._df)
        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"adsl": self._adsl, "spec": spec}
        if self._group_col is not None:
            kwargs["groupby"] = self._group_col
        return getattr(ns, self._method)(**kwargs)

    def to_listing(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Materialise the builder to a listing DataFrame.

        Uses the listing template targeted via :meth:`template` (e.g.
        ``ael01``), or the namespace's default listing when none was
        targeted.  Listings ignore population/grouping by design, so
        ``by()`` and ``population(adsl_filter=...)`` state raises here.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: A plain DataFrame with the requested columns,
                sorted per spec.

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If a table template was targeted, or the
                namespace ships no listing template.

        Examples:
            Inline AE listing::

                listing = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .columns(["USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AESEV"])
                    .sort_by(["USUBJID"])
                    .to_listing()
                )
        """
        builder = self
        if not self._targets_listing():
            if self._template_id is not None or self._template_fn is not None:
                raise SchemaError(
                    f"Template {self._template_id!r} is not a listing — call "
                    ".to_ard() instead of .to_listing()."
                )
            spec_classes = getattr(self._namespace_cls, "_builder_specs", {})
            listing_cls = spec_classes.get("l_listing")
            if listing_cls is None:
                raise SchemaError(
                    f"{self._context}: this namespace ships no listing "
                    "template, so .to_listing() is unavailable."
                )
            builder = self._clone()
            builder._method = "l_listing"
            builder._spec_cls = listing_cls
        spec = builder.to_spec()
        ns = self._namespace_cls(self._df)
        return getattr(ns, builder._method)(spec=spec)

    def to_html(
        self,
        path: str | Path | None = None,
        *,
        metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
        html_wrapper: str | None = None,
    ) -> str:
        """Render the builder result as a pharma-style HTML table.

        Materialises the ARD via ``.to_ard()``, shapes it into a
        ``TableModel``, and renders to HTML.

        Args:
            path: Optional file path.  If given, HTML is written to disk.
            metadata: Optional ``RenderMetadata`` for title, subtitle,
                footnotes, etc.
            html_wrapper: Optional HTML template with ``{table}``
                placeholder for injection.

        Returns:
            str: The rendered HTML string.

        Examples:
            Inline AE summary to HTML::

                html = (
                    adae.tlg.ae
                    .population(adsl)
                    .by("TRTA")
                    .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                    .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                    .to_html(metadata=RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1"))
                )
        """
        from pathlib import Path as _Path

        from .render._models import ard_to_table_model
        from .render.html import render_html

        ``TableModel``, and renders to RTF (Courier New 9pt, cell
        borders, repeated headers, ``Page X of Y``) — the de facto
        submission/QC format.  Pure stdlib.

                footnotes, etc.

        from .render.rtf import render_rtf

template(template_id)

Target a registered template so materialisation runs its method.

Resolves template_id through the template registry (built-ins and user registrations alike): the builder will materialise via that template's namespace method (e.g. lbt02 → t_chg) — or its registered function for user templates — with the template's spec class. Listing templates (e.g. ael01) materialise via :meth:to_listing.

Ordering: call template() before row/stat/format verbs. It swaps the builder's spec class, so state accumulated earlier is re-validated against — and interpreted by — the new target's spec; a UserWarning is emitted when that happens.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default template_id str

Registry id (e.g. "aet02", "lbt02").

required

Returns:

Name Type Description TLGBuilder TLGBuilder

Builder targeting the template's method and spec.

Raises:

Type Description SchemaError

If the id is unknown, belongs to a different namespace, or is a graph template.

Examples:

Materialise the AET02 shell::

ard = (
    adae.tlg.ae
    .population(adsl)
    .by("TRTA")
    .template("aet02")
    .to_ard()
)
Source code in src/fleet/tlg/_builder.py 
def template(self, template_id: str) -> TLGBuilder:
    """Target a registered template so materialisation runs its method.

    Resolves *template_id* through the template registry (built-ins
    and user registrations alike): the builder will materialise via
    that template's namespace method (e.g. ``lbt02`` → ``t_chg``) —
    or its registered function for user templates — with the
    template's spec class.  Listing templates (e.g. ``ael01``)
    materialise via :meth:`to_listing`.

    **Ordering**: call ``template()`` *before* row/stat/format verbs.
    It swaps the builder's spec class, so state accumulated earlier
    is re-validated against — and interpreted by — the new target's
    spec; a ``UserWarning`` is emitted when that happens.

    Args:
        template_id: Registry id (e.g. ``"aet02"``, ``"lbt02"``).

    Returns:
        TLGBuilder: Builder targeting the template's method and spec.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If the id is unknown, belongs to a different
            namespace, or is a graph template.

    Examples:
        Materialise the AET02 shell::

            ard = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .population(adsl)
                .by("TRTA")
                .template("aet02")
                .to_ard()
            )
    """
    from ._registry import TEMPLATES, OutputType

    meta = TEMPLATES.get(template_id)
    if meta is None:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Unknown template id {template_id!r}. Known ids: {sorted(TEMPLATES)}"
        )
    if meta.output_type is OutputType.GRAPH:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Template {template_id!r} is a graph, which the inline builder cannot materialise."
        )
    new = self._clone()
    if meta.func is not None:
        # User-registered template: self-contained function, not bound
        # to a namespace method.
        new._template_fn = meta.func
        new._spec_cls = meta.spec_cls or SummarySpecBase
    else:
        spec_classes = getattr(self._namespace_cls, "_builder_specs", {})
        if meta.method not in spec_classes:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Template {template_id!r} ({meta.namespace}.{meta.method}) does "
                f"not belong to this namespace ({self._context})."
            )
        new._method = meta.method
        new._spec_cls = meta.spec_cls or spec_classes[meta.method]
    new._template_id = meta.id
    if self._has_reinterpretable_state():
        warnings.warn(
            f"template({template_id!r}) was called after row/stat/format "
            "verbs — the accumulated state will be reinterpreted by "
            f"{new._spec_cls.__name__}. Call .template() first to avoid "
            "surprises.",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    return new

def to_spec(self) -> TLGSpec:
    """Serialise accumulated builder state to the equivalent spec.

    Every verb the user called must land on a spec field the target
    template's method actually consumes — otherwise this raises
    instead of silently dropping state (e.g. ``rows()`` on the
    fixed-hierarchy ``lbt03`` shift table).

    Returns:
        TLGSpec: A spec instance matching the builder configuration
            (carrying ``template=<id>`` when targeted via
            :meth:`template`).

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If accumulated builder state maps to a spec
            field the target template's method does not consume, or
            to no field at all.

    Examples:
        Capture the builder state as a reusable spec::

            spec = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .population(adsl)
                .by("TRTA")
                .template("aet02")
                .to_spec()
            )
    """
    is_listing = self._targets_listing()
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = dict(self._defaults)

    if self._template_id is not None:
        kwargs["template"] = self._template_id
    if self._adsl_filter is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("adsl_filter", "population(adsl_filter=...)")
        kwargs["adsl_filter"] = self._adsl_filter
    if self._dataset_filter is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("dataset_filter", "filter()")
        kwargs["dataset_filter"] = self._dataset_filter
    if self._header_rows_list:
        self._require_consumed_field("header_rows", "header_rows()")
        kwargs["header_rows"] = self._header_rows_list
    if self._group_col:
        if is_listing:
            raise SchemaError(
                "by() sets a grouping column, but the target template is "
                "a listing — listings have no column grouping. Remove "
                "by() or target a table template."
            )
        if "columns" in self._spec_cls.model_fields:
            kwargs["columns"] = [self._group_col]
    if self._rows_fields:
        kwargs.update(self._rows_kwargs())
    if self._statistics is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("statistics", "stats()")
        kwargs["statistics"] = self._statistics
    if self._pools:
        self._require_consumed_field("pools", "pools()")
        kwargs["pools"] = self._pools
    if self._column_order:
        self._require_consumed_field("column_order", "column_order()")
        kwargs["column_order"] = self._column_order
    if self._value_col is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("value_col", "value()")
        kwargs["value_col"] = self._value_col
    if self._label_col is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("label_col", "label()")
        kwargs["label_col"] = self._label_col
    if self._decimals is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("decimals", "decimals()")
        kwargs["decimals"] = self._decimals
    if self._uncoded is not _UNSET:
        self._require_consumed_field("uncoded", "uncoded()")
        kwargs["uncoded"] = self._uncoded
    if self._prefilter is not _UNSET:
        self._require_consumed_field("prefilter", "prefilter()")
        kwargs["prefilter"] = self._prefilter
    if self._listing_columns is not None:
        if not is_listing:
            raise SchemaError(
                "columns() defines listing display columns, but the "
                "target template is a table. Use by() for the grouping "
                'column, or target a listing template (.template("ael01") '
                "/ .to_listing())."
            )
        kwargs["columns"] = [
            c if isinstance(c, Column) else Column(field=c) for c in self._listing_columns
        ]
    if self._sort_by is not None:
        self._require_consumed_field("sort_by", "sort_by()")
        kwargs["sort_by"] = list(self._sort_by)
    if self._interactive is not None:
        kwargs["interactive"] = self._interactive

    return self._spec_cls(**kwargs)

def to_ard(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Materialise the builder to an ARD DataFrame.

    Constructs the equivalent spec and delegates to the targeted
    namespace method — ``t_summary()`` by default, the method
    selected via :meth:`template`, or the registered function for a
    user template.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: Long-format {cards}-compatible ARD.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If the target template is a listing — call
            :meth:`to_listing` instead.

    Examples:
        Inline AE summary::

            ard = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .population(adsl, adsl_filter=pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y")
                .by("TRTA")
                .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                .to_ard()
            )
    """
    if self._template_fn is not None:
        return self._template_fn(
            self._df,
            adsl=self._adsl,
            spec=self.to_spec(),
            groupby=self._group_col,
        )
    if self._targets_listing():
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Template {self._template_id!r} is a listing — call "
            ".to_listing() instead of .to_ard()."
        )
    spec = self.to_spec()
    ns = self._namespace_cls(self._df)
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"adsl": self._adsl, "spec": spec}
    if self._group_col is not None:
        kwargs["groupby"] = self._group_col
    return getattr(ns, self._method)(**kwargs)

def to_listing(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Materialise the builder to a listing DataFrame.

    Uses the listing template targeted via :meth:`template` (e.g.
    ``ael01``), or the namespace's default listing when none was
    targeted.  Listings ignore population/grouping by design, so
    ``by()`` and ``population(adsl_filter=...)`` state raises here.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: A plain DataFrame with the requested columns,
            sorted per spec.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If a table template was targeted, or the
            namespace ships no listing template.

    Examples:
        Inline AE listing::

            listing = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .columns(["USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AESEV"])
                .sort_by(["USUBJID"])
                .to_listing()
            )
    """
    builder = self
    if not self._targets_listing():
        if self._template_id is not None or self._template_fn is not None:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Template {self._template_id!r} is not a listing — call "
                ".to_ard() instead of .to_listing()."
            )
        spec_classes = getattr(self._namespace_cls, "_builder_specs", {})
        listing_cls = spec_classes.get("l_listing")
        if listing_cls is None:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"{self._context}: this namespace ships no listing "
                "template, so .to_listing() is unavailable."
            )
        builder = self._clone()
        builder._method = "l_listing"
        builder._spec_cls = listing_cls
    spec = builder.to_spec()
    ns = self._namespace_cls(self._df)
    return getattr(ns, builder._method)(spec=spec)

def to_html(
    self,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render the builder result as a pharma-style HTML table.

    Materialises the ARD via ``.to_ard()``, shapes it into a
    ``TableModel``, and renders to HTML.

    Args:
        path: Optional file path.  If given, HTML is written to disk.
        metadata: Optional ``RenderMetadata`` for title, subtitle,
            footnotes, etc.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template with ``{table}``
            placeholder for injection.

    Returns:
        str: The rendered HTML string.

    Examples:
        Inline AE summary to HTML::

            html = (
                adae.tlg.ae
                .population(adsl)
                .by("TRTA")
                .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
                .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
                .to_html(metadata=RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1"))
            )
    """
    from pathlib import Path as _Path

    from .render._models import RenderMetadata as _RM
    from .render._models import ard_to_table_model
    from .render.html import render_html

    ard = self.to_ard()
    meta = metadata or _RM()
    model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
    html = render_html(model, html_wrapper=html_wrapper)

    if path is not None:
        p = _Path(path)
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")

    return html

class CDISCClass(str, Enum):  # noqa: UP042

Every axis maps onto one existing :class:TLGSpec field (groupby→columns, population→adsl_filter, dataset_filter→dataset_filter, stats→statistics), so the interactive variant space is spanned by the same engine that produces the batch output — no second body of table logic exists. class InteractiveBlock(BaseModel):
    """Declared degrees of freedom for the TLG explorer.

    Every axis maps onto one existing :class:`TLGSpec` field
    (``groupby``→``columns``, ``population``→``adsl_filter``,
    ``dataset_filter``→``dataset_filter``, ``stats``→``statistics``), so
    the interactive variant space is spanned by the same engine that
    produces the batch output — no second body of table logic exists.
    An absent axis stays fixed at the spec's value.
    """

    groupby: GroupbyChoice | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Treatment-arm column choices (→ spec ``columns``).",
    )
    population: list[ChoiceOption] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="ADSL population presets (→ spec ``adsl_filter``).",
    )
    dataset_filter: list[ChoiceOption] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Analysis-dataset filter presets (→ spec ``dataset_filter``).",
    )
    stats: list[ChoiceOption] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Statistics presets (→ spec ``statistics``).",
    )

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_axes(self) -> InteractiveBlock:
        """Require at least one axis, one default per axis, stats lists."""
        if all(v is None for v in (self.groupby, self.population, self.dataset_filter, self.stats)):
            raise ValueError("interactive: declare at least one axis (or drop the block).")
        for axis in ("population", "dataset_filter", "stats"):
            options = getattr(self, axis)
            if options is None:
                continue
            n_default = sum(o.default for o in options)
            if n_default != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"interactive.{axis}: exactly one option must set "
                    f"'default: true' (got {n_default}) — the default variant "
                    "is the batch/submission output."
                )
        if self.stats is not None:
            missing = [o.label for o in self.stats if not o.statistics]
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"interactive.stats: options {missing} must declare a 'statistics' list."
                )
        return self

class SummarySpecBase(TLGSpec):
    """Shared fields for every summary-table spec.

    Domain specs subclass this and override only their defaults (rows,
    statistics, required columns, the uncoded rule, the prefilter) —
    one declaration of the shared shape instead of nine divergent
    copies.  Every field is also settable inline through
    [`TLGBuilder`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder].  The spec is the whole engine
    contract: [`summarize_spec()`][fleet.tlg.summarize_spec] reads every
    engine argument from it (ADR-0005).
    """

    #: The cards ``context`` tag written to every ARD row.  One spec
    #: class serves one template method, so the tag is a class fact,
    #: not a YAML field.
    context: ClassVar[str] = ""
    #: ``True`` when ``rows`` is a hierarchy (SOC → PT, PARAM → visit);
    #: ``False`` when each row field is an independent flat breakdown.
    nested: ClassVar[bool] = False
    #: Extra text for the missing-prefilter-column error (e.g. how to
    #: state a post-baseline rule without ONTRTFL).
    prefilter_hint: ClassVar[str] = ""

    output_type: str = "summary"
    rows: list[Row] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Row groupings (hierarchy for nested templates).  Set inline "
            "via [`TLGBuilder.rows()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.rows]."
        ),
    )
    uncoded: Uncoded | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The uncoded rule: coding columns whose nulls become a "
            "visible level before counting.  Each template sets its own "
            "default; ``null`` switches the rule off.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.uncoded()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.uncoded]."
        ),
    )
    prefilter: Any | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The template's own record filter, applied after "
            "``dataset_filter`` — a ``pl.Expr`` or a string expression "
            '(e.g. ``\'pl.col("ABLFL").ne_missing("Y")\'`` on a '
            "change-from-baseline table).  Each template sets its own "
            "default; ``null`` switches it off.  Every column it names "
            "is a required column.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.prefilter()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.prefilter]."
        ),
    )

    _validate_prefilter = field_validator("prefilter")(_check_filter_field)
    columns: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: ["TRTA"],
        description=(
            "Column-grouping variables (typically a treatment column).  "
            "Exactly one entry — multi-column grouping is not implemented "
            "yet, and the engine would silently read only the first.  "
            "Set inline via [`TLGBuilder.by()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.by]."
        ),
    )
    statistics: list[Statistic] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: [Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT],
        description=(
            "Statistics computed for each row.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.stats()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.stats]."
        ),
    )
    pools: list[GroupPool] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Composite (pooled) treatment groups.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.pools()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.pools]."
        ),
    )
    column_order: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Explicit ordering of column labels in the rendered output.  "
            "Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.column_order()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.column_order]."
        ),
    )
    value_col: str = Field(
        default="AVAL",
        description=(
            "Analysis-value column used for continuous statistics "
            "(mean/SD/median/…).  Summarize ``CHG``, ``PCHG`` or ``BASE`` "
            "by pointing this at the column — no pre-renaming needed.  "
            "When the column is missing but continuous statistics are "
            "requested, the engine raises instead of emitting null stats."
        ),
    )
    label_col: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Column holding display labels for the first row field's "
            'values (e.g. ``"PARAM"`` when the row field is '
            '``"PARAMCD"``) so stubs show display names instead of '
            "codes.  ``None`` shows the raw values."
        ),
    )
    decimals: dict[str, str] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Per-statistic format overrides — ARD ``stat_name`` (e.g. "
            '``"mean"``, ``"sd"``, ``"pct"``) to format string (e.g. '
            '``"xx.xx"``).  Overrides the built-in defaults for this '
            "table; individual rows may override again via "
            ":attr:`Row.decimals`."
        ),
    )

    def prefilter_columns(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return the columns the spec's prefilter names.

        Every one of them is a required column of the template, so a
        change table's ``ABLFL`` guard makes ``ABLFL`` required and
        ``prefilter=None`` lifts that requirement with it.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Column names in first-seen order; empty when the
                prefilter is ``None``.

        Examples:
            ``LBChgSpec().prefilter_columns() == ["ABLFL", "CHG"]``
        """
        expr = resolve_filter(self.prefilter)
        if expr is None:
            return []
        return list(dict.fromkeys(expr.meta.root_names()))

    def check(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> list[str]:
        """Run the pre-validation diagnostic without computing.

        The base checks (required columns, prefilter columns, required
        flag values) plus one warning per row field absent from *df*,
        whose sub-analysis the engine would skip.

        Args:
            df: The DataFrame to check.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if all checks pass).

        Examples:
            ``MHSummarySpec().check(admh)``
        """
        diagnostics = super().check(df)
        available = set(df.columns)
        for row_def in self.rows:
            if row_def.field not in available:
                diagnostics.append(
                    f"WARNING: Column '{row_def.field}' not present — "
                    f"'{row_def.label or row_def.field}' sub-analysis will be skipped."
                )
        return diagnostics

    @field_validator("columns")
    @classmethod
    def _single_group_column(cls, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        """Reject multi-column (or empty) grouping loudly.

        The engine reads only ``columns[0]``; accepting more would
        silently discard the rest of the grouping.
        """
        if len(value) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'columns' must contain exactly one treatment-arm column "
                f"(got {value!r}). Multi-column grouping is not implemented "
                "— the engine would silently read only the first entry. "
                "Move additional grouping into the row hierarchy ('rows') "
                "or file a feature request."
            )
        return value
