def render_html(
    model: TableModel,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style HTML table.

    Pagination happens in the model layer (:func:`~fleet.tlg.render.paginate`):
    each page repeats title, column headers, and footnotes, carries a
    ``Page X of Y`` footer, and breaks on a real page in print/PDF media.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template string.  If given, the
            generated ``<table>`` block replaces the ``{table}`` placeholder,
            enabling embedding in sponsor portals, Quarto documents, or
            interactive dashboards.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page; ``None`` disables
            row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable to page-break on (e.g. ``"PARAMCD"``).
            Defaults to ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Returns:
        str: Complete HTML string (with ``<style>`` block) or injected
            into *html_wrapper*.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary to HTML::

            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
            html = render_html(model)
    """
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page, page_by=page_by)

    parts: list[str] = ['<div class="fleet-table-container">', _SUMMARY_CSS]
    if len(pages) == 1:
        parts += _table_page_parts(pages[0])
    else:
        for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
            parts.append('<div class="fleet-page">')
            parts += _table_page_parts(page, page_footer=f"Page {idx} of {len(pages)}")
            parts.append("</div>")
    parts.append("</div>")

    html = "\n".join(parts)

    if html_wrapper is not None:
        return html_wrapper.replace("{table}", html)

    return html

Render an AE listing to editable slides::

def render_listing_pptx(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` to a PPTX slide deck.

    Each slide contains a flat data listing as an editable PowerPoint
    table.  Long listings are chunked across slides (title, headers,
    and footnotes repeat per slide).  The listing can be modified after
    export.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.
        rows_per_page: Data rows per slide (default 15).

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE listing to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import listing_to_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_listing_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.7.1", subtitle="AE Listing")
            model = listing_to_model(listing_df, meta)
            render_listing_pptx(model, "ae_listing.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)
    pages = paginate_listing(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page or _MAX_ROWS_PER_SLIDE)

    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    for page in pages:
        slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

        # ── Title + subtitle ──
        top = Inches(0.3)
        if page.metadata.title:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.title
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.45)

        if page.metadata.subtitle:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.subtitle
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.4)

        top += Inches(0.1)

        # ── Table ──
        n_cols = len(page.column_labels)
        n_rows = 1 + len(page.data)  # header + data

        table_width = Inches(12.3)
        table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
        table_left = Inches(0.5)

        tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(
            n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height
        )
        table = tbl_shape.table

        col_width = int(table_width / max(n_cols, 1))
        for ci in range(n_cols):
            table.columns[ci].width = Emu(col_width)

        # Headers
        for ci, lbl in enumerate(page.column_labels):
            cell = table.cell(0, ci)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = lbl
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_bg"])
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_fg"])

        # Data rows
        for ri, row_data in enumerate(page.data, start=1):
            bg = th["alt_row_bg"] if ri % 2 == 0 else None
            for ci, lbl in enumerate(page.column_labels):
                cell = table.cell(ri, ci)
                cell.text = ""
                p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
                p.text = row_data.get(lbl, "")
                p.font.name = th["font_name"]
                p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
                p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
                if bg:
                    cell.fill.solid()
                    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)

        # ── Footnotes ──
        if page.metadata.footnotes:
            fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
            fn_text = "\n".join(page.metadata.footnotes)
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = fn_text
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

def render_listing_rtf(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = _DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` as a pharma-style RTF listing.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Optional output file path; the RTF is written when given.
        rows_per_page: Maximum data rows per page (default 40).  ``None``
            renders one continuous listing.

    Returns:
        str: The complete RTF document.

    Examples:
        Lab abnormalities listing to RTF::

            listing = adlb.tlg.lb.l_listing()
            model = listing_to_model(listing, RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.8.1"))
            render_listing_rtf(model, "outputs/l_lb_abnormal.rtf")
    """
    pages = paginate_listing(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page)

    n_cols = max(len(model.column_labels), 1)
    col_w = _USABLE_W // n_cols
    positions = _cell_positions([col_w] * n_cols)
    aligns = [r"\ql"] * n_cols

    parts: list[str] = [_DOC_HEADER]
    for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
        if idx > 1:
            parts.append(r"\page")
        parts += _title_block(page.metadata.title, page.metadata.subtitle)

        parts.append(
            _row_rtf(
                list(page.column_labels),
                positions,
                aligns,
                header=True,
                border_top=_BDR_HEAVY,
                border_bottom=_BDR_LIGHT,
            )
        )

        for r_idx, row_data in enumerate(page.data):
            cells = [row_data.get(label, "") for label in page.column_labels]
            parts.append(
                _row_rtf(
                    cells,
                    positions,
                    aligns,
                    border_bottom=_BDR_HEAVY if r_idx == len(page.data) - 1 else None,
                )
            )

        parts += _footer_block(page.metadata.footnotes, f"Page {idx} of {len(pages)}")

    parts.append("}")
    return _write("\n".join(parts), path)

        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.  Keys include
            ``font_name``, ``font_size_body``, ``header_bg``, etc.
            See ``_DEFAULT_THEME`` for all available keys.
        rows_per_page: Body rows per slide (default 15 — what fits a
            16:9 slide at the default body font).

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary ARD to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import ard_to_table_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1", subtitle="AE Summary")
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
            render_pptx(model, "ae_summary.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page or _MAX_ROWS_PER_SLIDE)

    prs = Presentation()
    # Landscape 16:9
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    for page in pages:
        slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank layout
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

        # ── Title + subtitle ──
        top = Inches(0.3)
        if page.metadata.title:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.title
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.45)

        if page.metadata.subtitle:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.subtitle
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.4)

        top += Inches(0.1)

        # ── Table dimensions ──
        n_cols = 1 + len(page.columns)  # stub + arms
        n_rows = 1 + len(page.rows)  # header + data rows

        table_width = Inches(12.3)
        table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
        table_left = Inches(0.5)

        tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(
            n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height
        )
        table = tbl_shape.table

        # Distribute column widths: stub gets 30%, rest evenly split
        stub_width = int(table_width * 0.30)
        arm_width = int((table_width - stub_width) / max(len(page.columns), 1))
        table.columns[0].width = Emu(stub_width)
        for ci in range(1, n_cols):
            table.columns[ci].width = Emu(arm_width)

        # ── Helper: set cell text + style ──
        def _set_cell(
            row_idx: int,
            col_idx: int,
            text: str,
            *,
            bold: bool = False,
            font_size: int | None = None,
            bg: str | None = None,
            fg: str | None = None,
            align: Any = PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
            indent: int = 0,
            table: Any = table,
        ) -> None:
            cell = table.cell(row_idx, col_idx)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = text
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(font_size or th["font_size_body"])
            p.font.bold = bold
            p.alignment = align
            if fg:
                p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(fg)
            if bg:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)
            if indent:
                p.level = min(indent, 8)

        # ── Column headers ──
        _set_cell(0, 0, page.stub_label, bold=True, bg=th["header_bg"], fg=th["header_fg"])
        for ci, col in enumerate(page.columns, start=1):
            _set_cell(
                0,
                ci,
                col.display,
                bold=True,
                bg=th["header_bg"],
                fg=th["header_fg"],
                align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
            )

        # ── Data rows ──
        for ri, row in enumerate(page.rows, start=1):
            # Row background
            if row.row_type in ("group", "section"):
                bg = th["group_bg"]
            elif ri % 2 == 0:
                bg = th["alt_row_bg"]
            else:
                bg = None

            # Stub cell
            indent_spaces = "  " * row.indent
            _set_cell(
                ri,
                0,
                f"{indent_spaces}{row.label}",
                bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
                bg=bg,
            )

            # Value cells
            for ci, col in enumerate(page.columns, start=1):
                val = row.cells.get(col.label, "")
                _set_cell(
                    ri,
                    ci,
                    val,
                    bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
                    bg=bg,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
                )

        # ── Footnotes ──
        if page.metadata.footnotes:
            fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
            fn_text = "\n".join(page.metadata.footnotes)
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = fn_text
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

Inline AE summary to a submission RTF::

ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)

def render_rtf(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = _DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style RTF table.

    Every page carries the title block, the column-header row (also
    flagged ``\\trhdr`` so word processors repeat it on overflow), the
    footnote block, and a ``Page X of Y`` footer.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        path: Optional output file path; the RTF is written when given.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page (default 40, sized for
            9pt landscape letter).  ``None`` disables row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable to page-break on (e.g. ``"PARAMCD"``).
            Defaults to ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Returns:
        str: The complete RTF document.

    Examples:
        Inline AE summary to a submission RTF::

            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
            render_rtf(model, "outputs/t_ae_summary.rtf")
    """
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page, page_by=page_by)

    stub_w = int(_USABLE_W * 0.34)
    arm_w = (_USABLE_W - stub_w) // max(len(model.columns), 1)
    positions = _cell_positions([stub_w] + [arm_w] * len(model.columns))
    aligns = [r"\ql"] + [r"\qc"] * len(model.columns)

    parts: list[str] = [_DOC_HEADER]
    for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
        if idx > 1:
            parts.append(r"\page")
        parts += _title_block(page.metadata.title, page.metadata.subtitle)

        # Column headers: heavy rule above, light rule below.
        header_cells = [page.stub_label] + [col.display for col in page.columns]
        parts.append(
            _row_rtf(
                header_cells,
                positions,
                aligns,
                header=True,
                border_top=_BDR_HEAVY,
                border_bottom=_BDR_LIGHT,
            )
        )

        for r_idx, row in enumerate(page.rows):
            cells = [row.label] + [row.cells.get(col.label, "") for col in page.columns]
            parts.append(
                _row_rtf(
                    cells,
                    positions,
                    aligns,
                    bold=row.bold,
                    indent=row.indent,
                    border_bottom=_BDR_HEAVY if r_idx == len(page.rows) - 1 else None,
                )
            )

        parts += _footer_block(page.metadata.footnotes, f"Page {idx} of {len(pages)}")

    parts.append("}")
    return _write("\n".join(parts), path)

Shape an ARD for rendering::

def ard_to_table_model(
    ard: pl.DataFrame,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
) -> TableModel:
    """Shape a long-format ARD into a display-ready ``TableModel``.

    This is the core Phase 2 shaping function.  It:
    1. Extracts big-N from ``stat_name == "N"`` rows → column headers.
    2. Identifies header rows (``variable == ""``) → ``TableRow(row_type="header")``.
    3. Emits parent stubs (``"group"``), flat-block headings
       (``"section"`` from ``variable_label``), and level rows.
    4. Merges ``n`` + ``pct`` count stats into single display cells;
       expands continuous statistics into one display row per statistic
       under the level stub (the universal pharma layout).

    Args:
        ard: A {cards}-compatible ARD DataFrame.
        metadata: Optional render metadata.  If ``None``, a blank
            ``RenderMetadata`` is used.

    Returns:
        TableModel: A display-ready table model suitable for any renderer.

    Examples:
        Shape an ARD for rendering::

            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
    """
    meta = metadata or RenderMetadata()

    # ── 1. Extract column order (arms) ──
    # Respect the order already present in the ARD (set by column_order in spec)
    arm_order: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for val in ard["group1_level"].to_list():
        if val and val not in seen:
            arm_order.append(val)
            seen.add(val)

    # ── 2. Extract big-N for column headers ──
    big_n_rows = ard.filter((pl.col("stat_name") == "N") & (pl.col("variable") == ""))
    big_n_map: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in big_n_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
        arm = row["group1_level"]
        val = row["stat"]
        if arm and val is not None:
            big_n_map[arm] = int(val)

    columns = [ColumnHeader(label=arm, big_n=big_n_map.get(arm)) for arm in arm_order]

    # ── 3. Get non-big-N rows ──
    data_rows = ard.filter(~((pl.col("stat_name") == "N") & (pl.col("variable") == "")))

    # ── 4. Display-row identity in appearance order ──
    # Nested ARDs emit the same child level once per parent, so the
    # parent lineage must be part of the display-row identity or cells
    # from different parents collapse into one row (last-write-wins).
    row_keys: list[_RowKey] = []
    row_keys_seen: set[_RowKey] = set()
    var_labels: dict[str, str] = {}
    has_var_label = "variable_label" in ard.columns
    for row in data_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
        key = (
            row.get("group2") or "",
            row.get("group2_level") or "",
            row["variable"],
            row["variable_level"],
        )
        if key not in row_keys_seen:
            row_keys.append(key)
            row_keys_seen.add(key)
        if has_var_label and row["variable"] not in var_labels:
            var_labels[row["variable"]] = row.get("variable_label") or ""

    variable_set = {k[2] for k in row_keys}
    parent_vars = {k[0] for k in row_keys if k[0]}
    explicit_parents = parent_vars & variable_set

    # Stub column heading: one line per hierarchy level, top level first
    # and each child indented ("System Organ Class" / "  Preferred Term").
    # Non-breaking spaces survive the renderers' whitespace collapsing.
    stub_label = ""
    for k in row_keys:
        if not k[0] and k[2] in explicit_parents:
            parent = k[2]
            lines = [var_labels.get(parent, "")]
            for child in dict.fromkeys(kk[2] for kk in row_keys if kk[0] == parent):
                if child != parent and var_labels.get(child):
                    lines.append("  " + var_labels[child])
            stub_label = "\n".join(line for line in lines if line.strip())
            break

    # ── 5. Build display rows ──
    table_rows: list[TableRow] = []
    current_section: str | None = None
    current_synth_parent: tuple[str, str] | None = None

    for g2, g2l, variable, variable_level in _ordered_display_keys(row_keys):
        vl_rows = data_rows.filter(
            (pl.col("group2").fill_null("") == g2)
            & (pl.col("group2_level").fill_null("") == g2l)
            & (pl.col("variable") == variable)
            & (pl.col("variable_level") == variable_level)
        )
        stat_order, stat_labels, per_arm = _collect_cell_stats(vl_rows, arm_order)
        continuous = any(s not in _COUNT_STAT_NAMES for s in stat_order)
        empty_cells = {arm: "" for arm in arm_order}

        # ── Structure: header / group stub / synthetic parent / section ──
        if variable == "":
            # Header row (OverallStat)
            current_section = None
            current_synth_parent = None
            row_type, indent, bold = "header", 0, False
        elif variable in explicit_parents and not g2:
            # Parent stub row (SOC / PARAMCD): label only, no cells.
            current_section = None
            current_synth_parent = None
            table_rows.append(
                TableRow(
                    label=variable_level,
                    row_type="group",
                    indent=0,
                    cells=dict(empty_cells),
                    bold=True,
                    variable=variable,
                )
            )
            continue
        elif g2:
            # Child level inside a hierarchy.
            current_section = None
            if g2 not in explicit_parents:
                # No explicit parent rows — synthesise the stub from the
                # parent level so children don't float unanchored.
                if current_synth_parent != (g2, g2l):
                    table_rows.append(
                        TableRow(
                            label=g2l,
                            row_type="group",
                            indent=0,
                            cells=dict(empty_cells),
                            bold=True,
                            variable=g2,
                        )
                    )
                    current_synth_parent = (g2, g2l)
            else:
                current_synth_parent = None
            row_type, indent, bold = "data", 1, False
        else:
            # Flat block — emit the variable label as a section heading.
            current_synth_parent = None
            section_label = var_labels.get(variable, "")
            if section_label:
                if current_section != variable:
                    table_rows.append(
                        TableRow(
                            label=section_label,
                            row_type="section",
                            indent=0,
                            cells=dict(empty_cells),
                            bold=True,
                            variable=variable,
                        )
                    )
                    current_section = variable
                row_type, indent, bold = "data", 1, False
            else:
                current_section = None
                row_type, indent, bold = "flat", 0, False

        # ── Cells: merged count cell, or one row per statistic ──
        if continuous:
            table_rows.append(
                TableRow(
                    label=variable_level,
                    row_type=row_type,
                    indent=indent,
                    cells=dict(empty_cells),
                    bold=bold,
                    variable=variable,
                )
            )
            table_rows += _stat_rows(
                stat_order,
                stat_labels,
                arm_order,
                per_arm,
                indent=indent + 1,
                variable=variable,
            )
        else:
            table_rows.append(
                TableRow(
                    label=variable_level,
                    row_type=row_type,
                    indent=indent,
                    cells=_merged_cells(arm_order, per_arm),
                    bold=bold,
                    variable=variable,
                )
            )

    return TableModel(metadata=meta, columns=columns, rows=table_rows, stub_label=stub_label)

def listing_to_model(
    listing: pl.DataFrame,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
) -> ListingModel:
    """Shape a listing DataFrame into a display-ready ``ListingModel``.

    Args:
        listing: A Polars DataFrame from ``l_listing()``.
        metadata: Optional render metadata.

    Returns:
        ListingModel: A display-ready listing model.

    Examples:
        Shape a listing for rendering::

            listing = adae.tlg.ae.template("ael01").to_listing()
            model = listing_to_model(listing, RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.7"))
    """
    meta = metadata or RenderMetadata()
    col_labels = list(listing.columns)

    data: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for row in listing.iter_rows(named=True):
        data.append({col: str(v) if v is not None else "" for col, v in row.items()})

    return ListingModel(metadata=meta, column_labels=col_labels, data=data)

    model: TableModel,

    html_wrapper: str | None = None,

    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style HTML table.

    Pagination happens in the model layer (:func:`~fleet.tlg.render.paginate`):
    each page repeats title, column headers, and footnotes, carries a
    ``Page X of Y`` footer, and breaks on a real page in print/PDF media.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template string.  If given, the
            generated ``<table>`` block replaces the ``{table}`` placeholder,
            enabling embedding in sponsor portals, Quarto documents, or
            interactive dashboards.

def render_rtf(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = _DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style RTF table.

    Every page carries the title block, the column-header row (also
    flagged ``\\trhdr`` so word processors repeat it on overflow), the
    footnote block, and a ``Page X of Y`` footer.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        path: Optional output file path; the RTF is written when given.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page (default 40, sized for
            9pt landscape letter).  ``None`` disables row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable to page-break on (e.g. ``"PARAMCD"``).
            Defaults to ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Returns:
        str: The complete RTF document.

    Examples:
        Inline AE summary to a submission RTF::

            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
            render_rtf(model, "outputs/t_ae_summary.rtf")
    """
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page, page_by=page_by)

    stub_w = int(_USABLE_W * 0.34)
    arm_w = (_USABLE_W - stub_w) // max(len(model.columns), 1)
    positions = _cell_positions([stub_w] + [arm_w] * len(model.columns))
    aligns = [r"\ql"] + [r"\qc"] * len(model.columns)

    parts: list[str] = [_DOC_HEADER]
    for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
        if idx > 1:
            parts.append(r"\page")
        parts += _title_block(page.metadata.title, page.metadata.subtitle)

        # Column headers: heavy rule above, light rule below.
        header_cells = [page.stub_label] + [col.display for col in page.columns]
        parts.append(
            _row_rtf(
                header_cells,
                positions,
                aligns,
                header=True,
                border_top=_BDR_HEAVY,
                border_bottom=_BDR_LIGHT,
            )
        )

        for r_idx, row in enumerate(page.rows):
            cells = [row.label] + [row.cells.get(col.label, "") for col in page.columns]
            parts.append(
                _row_rtf(
                    cells,
                    positions,
                    aligns,
                    bold=row.bold,
                    indent=row.indent,
                    border_bottom=_BDR_HEAVY if r_idx == len(page.rows) - 1 else None,
                )
            )

        parts += _footer_block(page.metadata.footnotes, f"Page {idx} of {len(pages)}")

    parts.append("}")
    return _write("\n".join(parts), path)

def render_listing_rtf(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = _DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` as a pharma-style RTF listing.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Optional output file path; the RTF is written when given.
        rows_per_page: Maximum data rows per page (default 40).  ``None``
            renders one continuous listing.

    Returns:
        str: The complete RTF document.

    Examples:
        Lab abnormalities listing to RTF::

            listing = adlb.tlg.lb.l_listing()
            model = listing_to_model(listing, RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.8.1"))
            render_listing_rtf(model, "outputs/l_lb_abnormal.rtf")
    """
    pages = paginate_listing(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page)

    n_cols = max(len(model.column_labels), 1)
    col_w = _USABLE_W // n_cols
    positions = _cell_positions([col_w] * n_cols)
    aligns = [r"\ql"] * n_cols

    parts: list[str] = [_DOC_HEADER]
    for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
        if idx > 1:
            parts.append(r"\page")
        parts += _title_block(page.metadata.title, page.metadata.subtitle)

        parts.append(
            _row_rtf(
                list(page.column_labels),
                positions,
                aligns,
                header=True,
                border_top=_BDR_HEAVY,
                border_bottom=_BDR_LIGHT,
            )
        )

        for r_idx, row_data in enumerate(page.data):
            cells = [row_data.get(label, "") for label in page.column_labels]
            parts.append(
                _row_rtf(
                    cells,
                    positions,
                    aligns,
                    border_bottom=_BDR_HEAVY if r_idx == len(page.data) - 1 else None,
                )
            )

        parts += _footer_block(page.metadata.footnotes, f"Page {idx} of {len(pages)}")

    parts.append("}")
    return _write("\n".join(parts), path)

One page per lab parameter, at most 20 rows each::

def paginate(
    model: TableModel,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> list[TableModel]:
    """Split a ``TableModel`` into display pages.

    Pagination lives in the model layer so every renderer (HTML, PDF,
    RTF, PPTX) inherits identical page composition: each page repeats
    the title, subtitle, column headers, and footnote blocks.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page.  A stub-only row
            (group/section heading) is never left orphaned at the bottom
            of a page.  ``None`` means no row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable whose stub rows force a page break (e.g.
            ``"PARAMCD"`` → one page per parameter).  Defaults to
            ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Returns:
        list[TableModel]: One model per page (a single-element list when
        no pagination applies).

    Examples:
        One page per lab parameter, at most 20 rows each::

            from fleet.tlg.render import ard_to_table_model, paginate

            model = ard_to_table_model(ard)
            pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=20, page_by="PARAMCD")
    """
    effective_page_by = page_by or model.metadata.page_by
    if rows_per_page is None and not effective_page_by:
        return [model]

    # ── 1. Split into blocks at page_by stub boundaries ──
    blocks: list[list[TableRow]] = [[]]
    for row in model.rows:
        if (
            effective_page_by
            and row.variable == effective_page_by
            and row.row_type in ("group", "section")
            and blocks[-1]
        ):
            blocks.append([])
        blocks[-1].append(row)

    # ── 2. Split blocks by row count ──
    pages_rows: list[list[TableRow]] = []
    for block in blocks:
        if not block:
            continue
        if rows_per_page is None:
            pages_rows.append(block)
        else:
            pages_rows.extend(_chunk_rows(block, rows_per_page))

    if not pages_rows:
        return [model]
    return [
        TableModel(
            metadata=model.metadata,
            columns=model.columns,
            rows=rows,
            stub_label=model.stub_label,
        )
        for rows in pages_rows
    ]

def render_pdf(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` to a PDF file via WeasyPrint.

    Pagination comes from the model layer: pages break on real PDF
    pages with repeated title, column headers, and footnotes, plus a
    ``Page X of Y`` footer.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model.
        path: Output PDF file path.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template with ``{table}`` placeholder.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page; ``None`` disables
            row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable to page-break on (e.g. ``"PARAMCD"``).
            Defaults to ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Returns:
        Path: The written PDF path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If WeasyPrint is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary to PDF::

            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
            render_pdf(model, "ae_summary.pdf")
    """
    try:
        import weasyprint  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "WeasyPrint is required for PDF export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add weasyprint\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pdf]"
        ) from None

    html = render_html(
        model, html_wrapper=html_wrapper, rows_per_page=rows_per_page, page_by=page_by
    )
    # Wrap in a minimal HTML document for WeasyPrint
    doc = (
        "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
        '<html><head><meta charset="utf-8">'
        "<style>"
        "@page { size: landscape; margin: 1cm; }"
        "body { font-family: 'Courier New', Courier, monospace; font-size: 9pt; }"
        "</style></head><body>\n"
        f"{html}\n"
        "</body></html>"
    )
    p = Path(path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    weasyprint.HTML(string=doc).write_pdf(str(p))
    return p

        rows_per_page: Body rows per slide (default 15 — what fits a
            16:9 slide at the default body font).

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary ARD to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import ard_to_table_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1", subtitle="AE Summary")
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
            render_pptx(model, "ae_summary.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page or _MAX_ROWS_PER_SLIDE)

    prs = Presentation()
    # Landscape 16:9
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    for page in pages:
        slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank layout
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

        # ── Title + subtitle ──
        top = Inches(0.3)
        if page.metadata.title:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.title
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.45)

        if page.metadata.subtitle:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.subtitle
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.4)

        top += Inches(0.1)

        # ── Table dimensions ──
        n_cols = 1 + len(page.columns)  # stub + arms
        n_rows = 1 + len(page.rows)  # header + data rows

        table_width = Inches(12.3)
        table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
        table_left = Inches(0.5)

        tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(
            n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height
        )
        table = tbl_shape.table

        # Distribute column widths: stub gets 30%, rest evenly split
        stub_width = int(table_width * 0.30)
        arm_width = int((table_width - stub_width) / max(len(page.columns), 1))
        table.columns[0].width = Emu(stub_width)
        for ci in range(1, n_cols):
            table.columns[ci].width = Emu(arm_width)

        # ── Helper: set cell text + style ──
        def _set_cell(
            row_idx: int,
            col_idx: int,
            text: str,
            *,
            bold: bool = False,
            font_size: int | None = None,
            bg: str | None = None,
            fg: str | None = None,
            align: Any = PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
            indent: int = 0,
            table: Any = table,
        ) -> None:
            cell = table.cell(row_idx, col_idx)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = text
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(font_size or th["font_size_body"])
            p.font.bold = bold
            p.alignment = align
            if fg:
                p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(fg)
            if bg:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)
            if indent:
                p.level = min(indent, 8)

        # ── Column headers ──
        _set_cell(0, 0, page.stub_label, bold=True, bg=th["header_bg"], fg=th["header_fg"])
        for ci, col in enumerate(page.columns, start=1):
            _set_cell(
                0,
                ci,
                col.display,
                bold=True,
                bg=th["header_bg"],
                fg=th["header_fg"],
                align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
            )

        # ── Data rows ──
        for ri, row in enumerate(page.rows, start=1):
            # Row background
            if row.row_type in ("group", "section"):
                bg = th["group_bg"]
            elif ri % 2 == 0:
                bg = th["alt_row_bg"]
            else:
                bg = None

            # Stub cell
            indent_spaces = "  " * row.indent
            _set_cell(
                ri,
                0,
                f"{indent_spaces}{row.label}",
                bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
                bg=bg,
            )

            # Value cells
            for ci, col in enumerate(page.columns, start=1):
                val = row.cells.get(col.label, "")
                _set_cell(
                    ri,
                    ci,
                    val,
                    bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
                    bg=bg,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
                )

        # ── Footnotes ──
        if page.metadata.footnotes:
            fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
            fn_text = "\n".join(page.metadata.footnotes)
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = fn_text
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

Examples:

Render an AE listing to editable slides::

from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_listing_pptx

render_listing_pptx(model, "ae_listing.pptx")
Source code in src/fleet/tlg/render/slides.py 
def render_listing_pptx(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` to a PPTX slide deck.

    Each slide contains a flat data listing as an editable PowerPoint
    table.  Long listings are chunked across slides (title, headers,
    and footnotes repeat per slide).  The listing can be modified after
    export.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.
        rows_per_page: Data rows per slide (default 15).

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE listing to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import listing_to_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_listing_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.7.1", subtitle="AE Listing")
            model = listing_to_model(listing_df, meta)
            render_listing_pptx(model, "ae_listing.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)
    pages = paginate_listing(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page or _MAX_ROWS_PER_SLIDE)

    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    for page in pages:
        slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

        # ── Title + subtitle ──
        top = Inches(0.3)
        if page.metadata.title:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.title
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.45)

        if page.metadata.subtitle:
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = page.metadata.subtitle
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            top += Inches(0.4)

        top += Inches(0.1)

        # ── Table ──
        n_cols = len(page.column_labels)
        n_rows = 1 + len(page.data)  # header + data

        table_width = Inches(12.3)
        table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
        table_left = Inches(0.5)

        tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(
            n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height
        )
        table = tbl_shape.table

        col_width = int(table_width / max(n_cols, 1))
        for ci in range(n_cols):
            table.columns[ci].width = Emu(col_width)

        # Headers
        for ci, lbl in enumerate(page.column_labels):
            cell = table.cell(0, ci)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = lbl
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_bg"])
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_fg"])

        # Data rows
        for ri, row_data in enumerate(page.data, start=1):
            bg = th["alt_row_bg"] if ri % 2 == 0 else None
            for ci, lbl in enumerate(page.column_labels):
                cell = table.cell(ri, ci)
                cell.text = ""
                p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
                p.text = row_data.get(lbl, "")
                p.font.name = th["font_name"]
                p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
                p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
                if bg:
                    cell.fill.solid()
                    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)

        # ── Footnotes ──
        if page.metadata.footnotes:
            fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
            fn_text = "\n".join(page.metadata.footnotes)
            txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
            tf = txbox.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = fn_text
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

docs.title: Advanced Patterns
docs.text: Fleet provides significant flexibility to handle complex clinical trial scenarios that don't fit perfectly into standard CDISC verbs.

docs.title: Custom Derivations with Polars Expressions
docs.text: While Fleet provides verbs like .study_day() or .baseline(), you will often need custom logic to derive variables specific to a study.

docs.title: Simple Inline Derivations
docs.text:
For row-by-row logic or straightforward column math, use the .derivation() verb. It accepts four forms:

String expression (YAML-compatible, AST-sandboxed):

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "AGEGR1",
    expression="pl.when(pl.col('AGE') < 65).then(pl.lit('<65 yrs')).otherwise(pl.lit('>=65 yrs'))",
).to_frame()

Direct pl.Expr (full Polars power):

import polars as pl

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "AGEGR1",
    expression=(
        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 18)
        .then(pl.lit("<18"))
        .when(pl.col("AGE") <= 65)
        .then(pl.lit("18-65"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit(">65"))
    ),
).to_frame()

Lambda returning pl.Expr (inline, IDE auto-complete, no string sandbox):

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "AGEGR1",
    expression=lambda: (
        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 65).then(pl.lit("<65 yrs")).otherwise(pl.lit(">=65 yrs"))
    ),
).to_frame()

docs.title: @derivation — File-Based, Lineage-Tracked Derivations
docs.text: For study-specific logic that should be versioned, reused, and automatically documented in Define-XML, use the @derivation decorator. This is the primary escape-hatch pattern for anything too complex for a one-liner.

docs.title: Three kind values
docs.text:
Kind When to use Signature column Row-by-row expression (no DataFrame needed) () -> pl.Expr frame Multi-column or aggregation logic (df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame param By-group reshape (e.g. tall/narrow BDS rows) (df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame + by= / set_values_to=

What the function receives and returns:

  • column — the function takes no arguments and returns a pl.Expr. Fleet splices the expression into the lazy pipeline, so nothing is materialised: it behaves exactly like an inline .derivation(expression=...), just versioned in its own file.
  • frame — the df parameter is the pipeline's current state, materialised as a plain pl.DataFrame at the point the derivation runs (every column derived by earlier verbs is present). The function returns a pl.DataFrame — usually df.with_columns(...) — and Fleet wraps the result back into the namespace so the chain continues.
  • param — same in/out contract as frame (upstream pl.DataFrame in, pl.DataFrame out), but tagged for BDS parameter derivation: the by= / set_values_to= metadata drives the by-group reshape and the PARAMCD/PARAM stamping of the appended rows.

You rarely need to pass kind= yourself — it is inferred from the signature: a return annotation of pl.Expr (or a zero-argument function) means column; by=/set_values_to= means param; everything else is frame.

docs.title: kind="column" example
docs.text:
# examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/derivations/AGEGR1.py
from fleet.core.derivation import derivation
import polars as pl


@derivation
def AGEGR1() -> pl.Expr:
    """Classify AGE into pooled age groups for ADSL."""
    return (
        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 65).then(pl.lit("<65 yrs")).otherwise(pl.lit(">=65 yrs"))
    ).alias("AGEGR1")

Use it directly in a pipeline:

from examples.cdiscpilot01.adam.derivations import AGEGR1

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.derivation(AGEGR1).to_frame()

docs.title: kind="frame" example
docs.text:
@derivation(targets=["SAFFL", "ITTFL"])
def add_pop_flags(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Add SAFFL and ITTFL population flags."""
    return df.with_columns(
        pl.lit("Y").alias("SAFFL"),
        pl.lit("Y").alias("ITTFL"),
    )

docs.title: kind="param" example
docs.text:
@derivation(
    by=["USUBJID", "ADT"],
    set_values_to={"PARAMCD": "BMI", "PARAM": "Body Mass Index"},
)
def BMI(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Compute BMI per subject visit."""
    return df.with_columns((pl.col("WEIGHT") / (pl.col("HEIGHT") / 100) ** 2).alias("AVAL"))

docs.title: Derivations folder convention
docs.text:
Study derivations live under the study's configured programs tree:

programs/derivations/       # <programs dir from study_config.yaml>
    __init__.py
    AGEGR1.py
    BMI.py

Scaffold a new derivation with the CLI (config-context — run it anywhere inside the study workspace):

fleet derivation add AGEGR1 --dataset ADSL --kind column

The convention is standard-agnostic: the same @derivation objects and algorithm: callable escape hatch work in SDTM pipelines and specs exactly as in ADaM — both dispatch through the shared core registry.

docs.title: Complex Multi-Dataset Derivations (Escaping the Pipeline)
docs.text:
For highly complex, advanced logic—such as derivations requiring customized multi-dataset joins, complex rolling window aggregations, or logic that simply cannot be expressed linearly in standard verbs—the recommended pattern is to "escape" the automated pipeline.

Because Fleet is built securely on Polars DataFrames, you can drop out to native Polars, compute your advanced logic, merge it back, and then seamlessly resume your Fleet pipeline.

import polars as pl

# 1. Start by compiling your base ADSL dataset to a Polars DataFrame
# (Assuming you already have adsl base and adverse events dataframes)
base_adsl = (
    adsl_pipeline.to_frame()
)  # or dm.adam.from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="ADSL").to_frame()

# 2. Compute complex custom logic using pure Polars (e.g. tracking a multi-step clinical event pattern)
# Here we find patients who had a Severe AE specifically after taking a certain concomitant medication.
complex_events = (
    base_adsl.select(["USUBJID", "TRTSDT"])
    .join(ae_df.filter(pl.col("AESEV") == "SEVERE"), on="USUBJID", how="inner")
    .join(cm_df.filter(pl.col("CMINDC") == "NAUSEA"), on="USUBJID", how="left")
    .group_by("USUBJID")
    .agg(
        [
            pl.when(pl.col("AESTDTC").min() > pl.col("CMSTDTC").min())
            .then(pl.lit("Y"))
            .otherwise(pl.lit("N"))
            .alias("CUSTFL")
        ]
    )
)

# 3. Merge the result natively using Polars
merged_adsl = base_adsl.join(complex_events, on="USUBJID", how="left")

# 4. Jump back into Fleet if you need to finalize any remaining standard derivations or metadata
final_adsl = merged_adsl.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "CUSTFL", expression=pl.col("CUSTFL").fill_null("N")
).to_frame()

This pattern ensures you are never bottlenecked by the package API: if you can write it in Polars, you can execute it in Fleet.

docs.title: Subclassing Namespaces
docs.text:
If your organisation uses standard proprietary derivations across multiple datasets, you can extend Fleet namespaces by subclassing them.

from fleet.adam.namespace import AdamNamespace
import polars as pl


class CompanyAdamNamespace(AdamNamespace):
    def proprietary_flag(self, target_col: str, condition: str) -> "CompanyAdamNamespace":
        """Re-usable custom flag for your company."""
        expr = pl.when(pl.col(condition) == "Y").then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit(None))
        return self._chain(expr.alias(target_col))


# You can register this as a custom accessor using Polars
@pl.api.register_dataframe_namespace("company_adam")
class _CompanyAdamPolarsAccessor(CompanyAdamNamespace):
    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame):
        super().__init__(df)

docs.title: Handling Non-CDISC Raw Sources
docs.text:
If you are pulling in non-standard vendor files, rename and map columns directly inside the pipeline — no intermediate Polars .rename() call needed. .assign(target, source=...) is the canonical rename verb in both SDTM and ADaM; the ADaM .source(*cols) verb is the variadic pass-through for carrying already-named columns as-is:

import polars as pl

raw_labs = pl.read_csv("vendor_labs.csv")

# Rename non-standard columns inline, then continue the derivation
adlb = (
    raw_labs.adam.assign("USUBJID", source="Subject_ID")
    .assign("AVAL", source="Lab_Result")
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL")
    .to_frame()
)

Same verb, same spelling in SDTM:

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign("SUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .to_frame()
)

Only fall back to raw Polars for pre-processing that genuinely cannot be expressed as a Fleet verb (e.g. pivoting wide vendor files, multi-file concatenation), and re-enter the Fleet pipeline immediately afterwards.

docs.title: Cross-Domain Derivations with .pin()
docs.text: Many CDISC derivations require data from sibling domains — SDTM study day needs DM's RFSTDTC, ADaM datasets need ADSL columns like TRTSDT and population flags. Fleet's Pipeline Passport (.pin()) lets verbs see reference data without polluting the frame.

docs.title: Pinning a reference domain
docs.text:
# Build DM first
dm = dm_raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM").to_frame()  # ...plus the rest of DM

# Pin DM to the VS pipeline — verbs can now resolve RFSTDTC
vs = (
    vs_raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="VS")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("VSTESTCD", source="vs_test_code")
    .assign("VSORRES", source="vs_result")
    .date("VSDTC", source="vs_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)  # ← attach reference (join_on="USUBJID" by default)
    .study_day("VSDY", date_col="VSDTC")  # ← consumes the pin
    .baseline_flag("VSBLFL", date_col="VSDTC", testcd_col="VSTESTCD")  # ← also consumes it
    .to_frame()
)

You don't see RFSTDTC in the call because .study_day() fills it in from its SDTM defaults: ref_pin="DM" and ref_col="RFSTDTC" — i.e. "look up RFSTDTC in the pinned DM, joined on the pin's key". Spelled out in full, the call above is:

vs_ns.study_day("VSDY", date_col="VSDTC", ref_pin="DM", ref_col="RFSTDTC")

On ADaM namespaces the same defaults become ref_pin="ADSL" / ref_col="TRTSDT". Resolution order: an explicit ref_df=/dm=/adsl= frame wins, then the pinned domain, then a ref_col already present in the frame — and a LookupError tells you what to pin when none of those hold.

The pinned DataFrame is not merged into the frame — it stays beside it. Verbs borrow what they need, compute, and drop temp columns. The output frame stays clean.

docs.title: Multiple pins
docs.text:
You can pin as many domains as you need:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.pin("DM", dm_df)  # join on USUBJID (default)
    .pin("TV", tv_df, join_on="VISITNUM")  # different join key
    .pin("EX", ex_df, join_on=["USUBJID", "EXTRT"])  # compound key
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")  # ← reads DM.RFSTDTC via the DM pin
    .to_frame()
)

Datasets sharing a join key can be declared in one call — the keyword form mirrors the define.yaml inputs: block (kwarg name = dataset name):

adae = (
    ae_df.adam.occds("ADAE")
    .pin(ADSL=adsl_df, EX=ex_df)  # both join on USUBJID (default)
    .join_adsl("TRTSDT", "SAFFL")
    .to_frame()
)

Each verb names the pin it consumes (or falls back to its default ref_pin), and the join uses that pin's stored join_on — so the TV and EX pins above sit untouched until a visit- or exposure-consuming verb asks for them.

docs.title: Inspecting pins
docs.text:
ae_ns = ae_raw.sdtm.pin("DM", dm).pin("TV", tv, join_on="VISITNUM")
ae_ns.pins()
# {'DM': {'df': ..., 'join_on': ['USUBJID']},
#  'TV': {'df': ..., 'join_on': ['VISITNUM']}}

docs.title: ADaM: .join_adsl() and .study_day()
docs.text:
For ADaM datasets, pin ADSL and use .join_adsl() to carry forward columns, and .study_day() with the ADaM-standard default (TRTSDT):

adae = (
    ae_df.adam.occds("ADAE")
    .pin("ADSL", adsl)  # join_on="USUBJID" unless overridden
    .source("USUBJID")
    .join_adsl("TRTSDT", "TRTEDT", "SAFFL")  # left-join on the ADSL pin's key (USUBJID)
    .study_day("ASTDY", date_col="AESTDTC", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .to_frame()
)

.join_adsl() has no by= parameter on purpose: the merge key is whatever the ADSL pin was registered with — USUBJID by default, or .pin("ADSL", adsl, join_on=["STUDYID", "USUBJID"]) for a compound key — so the join key is declared once, next to the data it belongs to. The pin-free alternative .merge_adsl(adsl, by=["USUBJID"], keep=[...]) takes an explicit frame and defaults by= to ["USUBJID"].

docs.title: FK validation
docs.text:
When a pin exists, Fleet can automatically check foreign-key integrity. By default it emits warnings for orphan values; use .fk_policy() to make it strict or silent:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.pin("DM", dm)
    .fk_policy("error")  # raise on FK violations
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")  # FK auto-checked vs DM
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Lineage tracing
docs.text:
Every derivation — including cross-domain pin access — is recorded automatically. Print the origin of every derived variable with the .trail() verb (detailed in the Observability section below), without breaking the chain:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
    .trail()  # prints the origin table; pipeline continues
    .to_frame()
)

The cross-domain pin is attributed in the Origin column as DM.RFSTDTC.

docs.title: Pipeline Debugging & Observability
docs.text: Fleet pipelines are lazy — all derivations accumulate until .to_frame() collects the result. This can make it hard to pinpoint which step introduced bad data or types — or to see where each variable came from. Three chainable verbs help:

docs.title: .inspect() — Hard Checkpoint
docs.text:
Materialises the pipeline at that point, prints schema, shape, and first rows, then returns a fresh namespace wrapping the collected frame. The pipeline resumes from this checkpoint.

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID")
    .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex, date_col="EXSTDTC")
    .inspect(prefix="After TRTSDT")  # prints and checkpoints
    .duration("TRTDURD", start="TRTSDT", end="TRTEDT")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: .explain() — Query Plan
docs.text:
Prints the Polars logical plan without materialising. Useful for understanding how Polars optimises the accumulated derivation pipeline.

advs = (
    vs_raw.adam.source("USUBJID")
    .derivation("AVAL", expression="VSSTRESN")
    .explain()  # shows optimised plan
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: .trail() — Variable Origin
docs.text:
Prints a table of every derived variable: the verb that produced it and the source columns it consumed, including cross-domain pin sources shown as DOMAIN.COLUMN. Nothing is materialised — the trail is metadata captured automatically on every verb — so it can sit anywhere in the chain, though it is most complete just before .to_frame().

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
    .trail()  # prints the table below, pipeline continues
    .to_frame()
)

Variable trail (4 derivation(s)):
┌───┬──────────┬────────────────┬─────────────────────┬────────┐
│ # ┆ Variable ┆ Verb           ┆ Origin              ┆ Domain │
╞═══╪══════════╪════════════════╪═════════════════════╪════════╡
│ 1 ┆ DOMAIN   ┆ assign         ┆ (literal)           ┆ —      │
│ 2 ┆ USUBJID  ┆ assign         ┆ patient_number      ┆ AE     │
│ 3 ┆ AESTDTC  ┆ assign         ┆ ae_start_date       ┆ AE     │
│ 4 ┆ AESTDY   ┆ study_day      ┆ AESTDTC, DM.RFSTDTC ┆ AE     │
└───┴──────────┴────────────────┴─────────────────────┴────────┘

Variables with no source column (e.g. hardcoded constants) are marked (literal); a variable derived more than once appears once per derivation, in pipeline order. Passthrough columns that no verb touched are not listed.

All three verbs are available on df.sdtm, df.adam, and all ADaM sub-namespaces.

docs.title: Comparing Datasets
docs.text:
Every QC step ends with the same question: is this dataset the same as that one, and if not, where exactly does it differ? SAS answers it with PROC COMPARE. Fleet answers it with compare — one engine in pure Polars, reachable as a Python function, as a pipeline verb, and as a CLI command.

A compare pairs two datasets observation by observation on their keys and variable by variable on their names, then reports where they differ. It is distinct from validation, which checks one dataset against CDISC conformance rules.

Term Meaning Base The reference dataset the comparison is measured against (production, legacy SAS, last release). Candidate The dataset being measured against the base (the independent QC programming, the migrated output). Keys The variables that together identify one observation on each side. Mandatory; never looked up. Comparison report The outcome: which variables and observations were common or one-sided, and every value that differed.

docs.title: Three surfaces, one engine
docs.text:
From Python, fleet.compare takes DataFrames or LazyFrames on either side and returns a ComparisonReport. Differences never raise — the report says what was found:

import fleet

report = fleet.compare(adae_prod, adae_qc, keys=["USUBJID", "AESEQ"])
report.print_report()
assert report.is_equal, report.raised_flags

At the end of a pipeline, the .compare() verb is available on df.sdtm, df.adam, df.adam.adsl and df.adam.occds. The chain is the candidate and the argument is the base; the verb prints the report, keeps it on the namespace as last_comparison, and returns a namespace copy so the chain continues:

adae_qc = (
    ae_df.adam.occds.source("USUBJID")
    .source("AESEQ")
    .compare(adae_prod, keys=["USUBJID", "AESEQ"])
    .to_frame()
)

From a shell, fleet compare loads both files through the raw-data loader (parquet, CSV, and XPT or sas7bdat with the io extra), prints the report, and turns the verdict into the exit code:

uv run fleet compare adae_prod.parquet adae_qc.parquet --keys USUBJID,AESEQ
uv run fleet compare legacy/adae.xpt outputs/adam/adae.parquet --keys USUBJID,AESEQ --all
Exit code Meaning 0 The datasets are equal. 1 The datasets differ; the report on stdout says where. 2 The comparison could not run: unreadable file, missing or duplicate keys, a negative tolerance, a --variables list that names only keys, or an --out or --report path that cannot be written. The reason is on stderr.

A compare that checks no values still gives a verdict. When the two sides share only their keys, the verdict follows the observations: the same key values on both sides are EQUAL, a one-sided key or variable is NOT EQUAL. When both sides have no observations, the verdict is EQUAL. In both cases the report warns above the first number, so an EQUAL that checked no values never reads as a full pass (ADR-0004).

--keys is required. --by TRT01P sections the report per BY group and --allow-duplicates pairs duplicate keys by position. --pairs and --variables rename and restrict what is compared. --abs-tol, --rel-tol and --ignore-trailing-whitespace widen equality (see tolerances and whitespace). --all lifts the print limits so every unequal value is listed. --report adae_compare.html writes the HTML report for a reviewer. --format json prints one JSON document and nothing else on stdout, and --out differences.parquet writes the complete value listing; both are described under machine-readable outputs. See the CLI reference for the full usage.

docs.title: What the report contains
docs.text:
The text report follows the PROC COMPARE section order, so a SAS programmer reads it without a legend:

  1. Data set summary — name, observations and variables per side, the keys, and the settings line naming the equality rule in effect (exact, or the tolerances and the whitespace rule).
  2. Variables summary — variables in common, in the base only, in the candidate only, type conflicts, dtype differences.
  3. Observation summary — matched observations and the key values of the ones found on one side only.
  4. Values summary — how many values differ, per variable.
  5. Summary statistics — for each differing numeric variable, how far apart the two sides are (see summary statistics).
  6. Value listing — every unequal value, grouped per observation so one subject's differences read together, with the base value, the candidate value, and the difference and percent difference for numeric variables.
  7. Verdict — EQUAL, or NOT EQUAL followed by the raised flags.

The report object carries the same content as data: report.listing is a long Polars frame (keys, group, variable, base, candidate, difference, percent_difference) that is never truncated, report.statistics is the summary statistics frame, and report.flags replaces SAS's SYSINFO integer with names — base_only_variables, candidate_only_variables, type_conflicts, base_only_observations, candidate_only_observations, values_differ, duplicate_keys, base_only_groups, candidate_only_groups. report.is_equal is true only when no flag is raised. report.warnings holds the lines every renderer prints above the report — today only the duplicate-key one.

docs.title: Summary statistics
docs.text:
Counting differences says how many, not whether the candidate runs systematically a little high or scatters at random. report.statistics says which: one row per differing variable and, for a numeric one, the shape of both sides, of their difference, and of that difference as a percentage of the base.

report = fleet.compare(advs_prod, advs_qc, keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVISITN"])
offset = report.statistics.filter(pl.col("difference_mean").abs() > 0.5)
Column Content variable The differing variable, by its base name, in compared order. differences How many matched observations differ on it. base_n, base_mean, base_std, base_min, base_max The base values. candidate_n … candidate_max The same five, of the candidate values. difference_n … difference_max The same five, of candidate − base. percent_difference_n … percent_difference_max The same five, of (candidate − base) ÷ base × 100.

Two things decide what the numbers mean:

  • The measures span every matched observation, not only the unequal ones. A mean difference near zero over a thousand observations with three differences reads as noise; a mean difference of exactly 0.5 across all of them reads as an offset. Only observations null, NaN or infinite on either side are dropped, because a difference needs two finite values — which is why n can be smaller than the matched count, and smaller again for the percent, which drops a zero base as the listing does. No measure is ever NaN or infinite, so the text report, the HTML page and the JSON document show the same numbers.
  • Only numeric variables carry them. A string, a date or a boolean contributes its differences count and nulls for the rest; there is no mean of "F" against "M".

The statistics are on every surface: their own section in the text report after the values summary, the statistics key of the JSON document, and a table at the top of each variable's block in the HTML page. An equal comparison has an empty frame and an empty section.

Deliberately absent are PROC COMPARE's correlation, R² and t statistic: they answer a modelling question rather than a QC one, and the value listing answers the QC one exactly.

docs.title: The HTML report
docs.text:
A study lead reviews without a Python environment. report.to_html() renders one self-contained page and report.save_html_report(path) writes it; from the shell, fleet compare --report adae_compare.html does the same next to the text report:

uv run fleet compare adae_prod.parquet adae_qc.parquet --keys USUBJID,AESEQ --report build/adae_compare.html

The page opens offline: its style is embedded and it fetches no script, font or image. It reads top-down the way a review goes:

  1. Verdict — EQUAL or NOT EQUAL, with the one-line summary and the raised flags.
  2. Chips — one per raised flag, so structural problems are visible before value details: the variables found on one side only, the type conflicts with their dtypes, the observations on one side only (the first few named by their key values), how many values differ. Dtype differences appear as an information chip, never as a finding.
  3. Summary — name, observations and variables per side, the keys, the equality rule in effect, and how many observations matched.
  4. Observations on one side only — the key values of every observation found only in the base or only in the candidate.
  5. Unequal values — only the mismatched observations, one collapsible block per differing variable. Each block opens on the variable's summary statistics, then lists every unequal row: the key values, the base value and the candidate value side by side with both cells highlighted, and the difference and percent difference for numeric variables. Blocks start open when there are five or fewer, closed beyond that, so a report over fifty variables stays navigable.

The page is never truncated: every unequal value is on it, whatever max_print the comparison ran with. With BY groups it gains a Groups section with the per-group counts and sections the unequal values per group. For listings beyond a few thousand rows, the parquet listing is the better archive.

docs.title: Machine-readable outputs
docs.text:
An agent or a CI job consumes the comparison without parsing prose. report.to_json() renders one JSON document, report.save_json(path) writes it, and report.save_listing(path) writes the complete value listing as parquet. From the shell, fleet compare --format json prints the document and nothing else on stdout (the exit code is still the verdict, and a comparison that could not run still leaves stdout empty with the reason on stderr), and --out writes the listing:

uv run fleet compare adae_prod.parquet adae_qc.parquet --keys USUBJID,AESEQ --format json > adae_compare.json
uv run fleet compare adae_prod.parquet adae_qc.parquet --keys USUBJID,AESEQ --out build/adae_differences.parquet

docs.title: The JSON contract
docs.text:
Field names mirror the report attributes. The document is additive-only within a major version, in the spirit of ADR 0001: keys may be added, never removed or renamed, so a comparison view built on them (the editor extension is the intended consumer) declares a minimum Fleet version and no ceiling. The top-level keys, in order (fleet.comparison.JSON_KEYS):

Key Content is_equal The verdict: true only when no flag is raised. summary The one-line summary, as report.summary. flags The raised flags, in their documented order. warnings The lines every renderer prints above the report; empty on an ordinary comparison. datasets base and candidate, each with name, rows and variables. variables common, compared, base_only, candidate_only, then type_conflicts and dtype_differences as {variable, base_dtype, candidate_dtype} with the dtypes as text. observations matched, base_only, candidate_only, the one-sided key values as base_only_keys and candidate_only_keys (capped at the per-variable print limit; truncated says whether a cap applied), base_duplicates and candidate_duplicates, the per-group counts as per_group, and the one-sided group labels as base_only_groups and candidate_only_groups. values per_variable as {variable, differences}, variables_with_differences, observations_with_differences, total_differences, and per_group. statistics One object per differing variable, with the columns of fleet.comparison.STATISTICS_COLUMNS; the measures are null for a variable that is not numeric. See summary statistics. listing columns, rows (one object per differing value, within the print limits), shown, total and truncated. settings Every option the comparison ran with: keys, by, pairs, variables, abs_tol, rel_tol, ignore_trailing_whitespace, allow_duplicates, max_print, base_name, candidate_name. version The Fleet version that produced the report.

The document is strict JSON: non-finite numbers are null and temporal key values are ISO 8601 strings. max_print governs the listing inside the document exactly as it governs the text (--all or max_print=None lifts it); the parquet listing is never truncated.

import json

document = json.loads(report.to_json())
if not document["is_equal"]:
    for row in document["listing"]["rows"]:
        print(row["USUBJID"], row["variable"], row["base"], "->", row["candidate"])

docs.title: The parquet listing
docs.text: save_listing writes report.listing as is: the key columns in their own dtypes, then group (String, the BY group label or null), variable, base and candidate (String), difference and percent_difference (Float64). An equal comparison writes an empty frame with the same schema, so a downstream scan_parquet always finds the documented columns.

docs.title: Rules of equality
docs.text:
• Keys are mandatory and must be unique on each side. A missing or duplicated key stops the compare with a ComparisonError that names the side and the offending key values, because a broken key is the first thing to fix. allow_duplicates is the deliberate way past it.
  • Equality is exact by default. Null equals null, NaN equals NaN, and null against NaN differs, so a missing value that became a NaN is surfaced. Tolerances widen it on the numeric variables and trailing-whitespace stripping on the strings; the null and NaN rule holds under both.
  • Same kind, different dtype is information, not a failure. An Int64 next to a Float64, a String next to a Categorical, or a Date next to a Datetime is compared by value after casting to a common type and listed as a dtype difference. A numeric next to a string is a type conflict: listed, not compared.
  • A blank is not a missing value unless you say so. A SAS file reads a blank as null, so XPT against Parquet needs nothing.
