A file from another tool can keep "" (an R data frame without convert_blanks_to_na), and "" against null differs by default. blank_is_missing=True (or --blank-is-missing) reads "" as null on both sides, keys included, and the settings line says blank equals missing.
  • A CSV file holds no types. fleet compare reads a CSV side as text and types each column across both sides: the other side's type when that side is not a CSV file; otherwise text when a value on either side has a leading zero or is not a number, and a number in every other case. So SITEID 001 against 1 differs, and AVAL 1.10 against 1.1 is equal, as in PROC COMPARE. --text LBORRES keeps a column text, the $ informat. The text report starts with the type each CSV column was read as.
  • Row order and column order are ignored. A re-sorted or re-ordered dataset is not a different dataset.
  • Print limits only affect what is rendered. By default the text report and the JSON document show 50 differences per variable and 500 overall; max_print=None (or --all) shows everything. The listing frame and the parquet always hold every difference.

docs.title: Tolerances and trailing whitespace
docs.text:
A migration programmer comparing Fleet output against a legacy SAS dataset has to absorb engine noise without hiding a real difference. Three options do that, and they are the same three on every surface:

Option Applies to Effect abs_tol / --abs-tol Numeric variables Absolute tolerance. Default 0.0 — exact. rel_tol / --rel-tol Numeric variables Relative tolerance, as a fraction of the base value. Default 0.0 — exact. ignore_trailing_whitespace / --ignore-trailing-whitespace String variables Strip trailing whitespace from both sides before comparing. Default False.

A numeric pair differs when the absolute difference exceeds max(abs_tol, rel_tol × |base|), so the wider of the two tolerances is the one that decides. The relative tolerance anchors on the base, because the base is the reference the candidate is measured against — this follows PROC COMPARE and deliberately not Polars' testing helper, which anchors on its right-hand frame. The choice is visible: at rel_tol=0.095 a base of 100 against a candidate of 110 differs (10 > 9.5), while the same pair with the sides swapped is equal (10 ≤ 10.45).

report = fleet.compare(
    advs_legacy,
    advs_fleet,
    keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVISITN"],
    rel_tol=1e-9,
    ignore_trailing_whitespace=True,
)

uv run fleet compare legacy/advs.xpt outputs/adam/advs.parquet \
  --keys USUBJID,PARAMCD,AVISITN --rel-tol 1e-9 --ignore-trailing-whitespace

What the options do not change:

  • Exact stays the default. Both tolerances are 0.0 and whitespace counts until you say otherwise.
  • Tolerances only reach the numeric variables. A string, a date or a boolean is compared exactly however wide abs_tol is, and stripping only reaches the string ones.
  • Nulls and NaN keep their rule. Null still equals null, NaN still equals NaN, and null against NaN — or NaN against a number — still differs, however wide the tolerance. A NaN is never within a tolerance of a number.
  • Only trailing whitespace is ignored. "M " equals "M" when asked; " M" never does.
  • The listing shows the values as they are. A difference that survives the tolerance is reported with the original base and candidate values, unstripped.
  • A tolerant comparison is arithmetic in Float64. Integers and decimals beyond 2**53 are therefore compared at that precision; the exact default compares them in their own dtype.

The rule in effect is on every surface: the settings line of the text report (Settings: abs_tol=1e-09, rel_tol=0, ignoring trailing whitespace, or Settings: exact), the header of the HTML report, and the settings block of the JSON document as the three raw fields.

docs.title: Duplicate keys
docs.text:
Keys that do not identify one observation per side stop the compare, because a broken key is usually the bug. When the duplication is expected — a dataset with no sequence variable, a legacy extract — allow_duplicates forces the comparison through:

report = fleet.compare(adae_prod, adae_qc, keys=["USUBJID"], allow_duplicates=True)

uv run fleet compare adae_prod.parquet adae_qc.parquet --keys USUBJID --allow-duplicates

Duplicates then pair by their position within each key group: the first base observation for USUBJID=01 against the first candidate one, the second against the second, and so on. An unpaired one — three on the base, two on the candidate — is reported as an observation found on one side only.

That is a weaker guarantee than pairing on keys, so it is never silent:

  • the observation summary counts the duplicates per side;
  • the duplicate_keys flag is raised, so the comparison is never is_equal;
  • report.warnings carries a line every renderer prints above the report, and the JSON document repeats it under warnings.

Row order stops being irrelevant under the override, and only within a duplicated key group: which base observation meets which candidate one is decided by the order the two datasets arrive in.

docs.title: BY groups
docs.text:
A reviewer looking at a study with several treatment arms wants to know where the differences are, not just how many. by sections the report:

report = fleet.compare(adsl_prod, adsl_qc, keys="USUBJID", by="TRT01P")
report.observations.per_group  # group, matched, base_only, candidate_only
report.values.per_group  # group, variables_with_differences, observations_with_differences, differences

uv run fleet compare adsl_prod.parquet adsl_qc.parquet --keys USUBJID --by TRT01P

The BY variables are prepended to the keys automatically, so they need not be repeated in keys (repeating them is harmless). Everything else follows from that:

  • Every difference carries its group in the listing's group column, labelled TRT01P=A (and TRT01P=A, AVISIT=2 with several BY variables), and the listing is sorted by group first.
  • The observation summary and the values summary are reported per group as well as in total, in the text report, the JSON document and the HTML page.
  • A group present on one side only raises base_only_groups or candidate_only_groups and is listed by name, so a missing arm reads as a missing arm rather than as a thousand missing observations.
  • The verdict stays global. is_equal is still true only when no flag is raised anywhere.

docs.title: Variable pairs and restriction
docs.text:
Two datasets rarely line up by name alone. A legacy extract calls a variable WEIGHT where the candidate calls it WT, and a candidate that is still being written has columns nobody wants compared yet. pairs and variables say so:

report = fleet.compare(
    advs_legacy,
    advs_wip,
    keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
    pairs={"WEIGHT": "WT"},  # base name: candidate name
    variables=["WEIGHT", "AVISIT"],  # base names
)

uv run fleet compare legacy/advs.xpt outputs/adam/advs.parquet \
  --keys USUBJID,PARAMCD --pairs WEIGHT=WT --variables WEIGHT,AVISIT

pairs maps base names to candidate names, on top of the automatic name matching rather than instead of it: everything not named in pairs still matches by name. A paired variable is compared by value and no longer reported missing on either side, and the report — the values summary, the listing, the HTML blocks — names it by its base name throughout. A pair is otherwise an ordinary common variable: same kind but a different dtype is a dtype difference, a different kind is a type conflict.

A pair whose candidate variable is absent reports the base one as missing from the candidate, exactly as an unpaired variable would. A pair whose base variable the base does not carry, one that renames a key, and two pairs pointing at the same candidate variable are refused with a ComparisonError: the pairing could not be honoured as written.

variables restricts the universe, in base names. What is outside the list is ignored entirely, on both sides: not compared, and not reported as missing or extra either — a work-in-progress candidate is checked on the columns that are finished without its unfinished ones raising a flag. What is on the list still is: a restricted variable the candidate does not carry is still reported as missing from it. Keys are never restricted; they pair observations whatever the list says. A restriction naming a variable neither side carries is refused, because a comparison that silently compares nothing would report two datasets as equal.

Both options are recorded in report.settings (pairs and variables) and shown wherever a run is described: the data set summary of the text report, the header of the HTML page, and the settings block of the JSON document.

docs.title: Gating a pipeline on the outcome
docs.text:
The verb speaks the same failure vocabulary as .validate():

on_fail Behaviour when the datasets differ "warn" (default) Emit a UserWarning and continue the chain. "raise" Raise ComparisonError (a FleetError). "ignore" Continue silently; the report is still on last_comparison. 
adsl = (
    dm_df.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID")
    .assign("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .compare(adsl_prod, keys="USUBJID", on_fail="raise")
    .to_frame()
)

Any other value fails fast with a DerivationError, exactly as .validate() does.

docs.title: Where it stops today
docs.text: The engine compares values, not metadata: a Polars frame carries no labels, formats or lengths, so comparing those would need a define.yaml-aware mode. Keys are mandatory on all three surfaces — there is no positional matching, and no lookup of keys from define.yaml or the study configuration. A comparison takes exactly two datasets, never a batch of directories. The compare spec tracks what is deliberately left out and what may follow it, including an MCP tool and a diff view in the editor extension built on the JSON contract above.

docs.title: Custom Validation Rules
docs.text: Custom rules are Fleet's extension mechanism for CORE — start with Validation with CORE for the base engine setup and the official rule sets. When the standard CDISC CORE conformance rules do not cover a study-specific requirement — a sponsor SOP constraint, an FDA Technical Conformance Guide (TCG) gap, a protocol-specific range check, or ADaM checks while the official ADaMIG rule set remains unpublished — you author custom rules and run them next to the official rules.

docs.title: Official and custom rules both run
docs.text:
CORE runs only the -lr rules when it gets a rules directory: one AE file ran 430 official rules without -lr and only the 2 custom rules with it. So Fleet runs the engine twice per standard when custom rules are set:

  1. one run without -lr: the official CDISC rules,
  2. one run with -lr: the custom rules only.

The findings of both runs join into one report per dataset. Each finding names its source, official or custom:

1. [CORE-000001] (official) AESTDTC is after AEENDTC
2. [FLEET-AE-001] (custom) AESEV is missing for a serious AE

The source is also on ValidationIssue.source, in the HTML reports, and in the MCP fleet_validate output. Without custom rules, the engine runs once per standard.

docs.title: When to write custom rules
docs.text:
• Sponsor SOPs require checks not covered by CDISC CORE (e.g. mandatory SUPPQUAL variables).
  • FDA TCG requirements that have not yet been formalised as CORE rules.
  • Protocol-specific constraints such as custom reference ranges, visit windows, or dose limits.
  • Interim quality gates during study setup before official validation.

docs.title: 1. Configure the custom rules directory
docs.text:
In your study_config.yaml, set the custom_rules path:

validation:
  custom_rules: metadata/custom_rules  # directory for your .yaml rule files

fleet init cfg sets this up by default. The engine loads all .yaml files in this directory.

docs.title: 2. Scaffold a new rule
docs.text:
# Auto-increments ID: FLEET-AE-001, FLEET-AE-002, …
uv run fleet add-rule --domain AE --description "AESEV must be populated when AESER = Y"

# Custom prefix
uv run fleet add-rule --domain AE --prefix ACME --description "Severity required for serious AEs"

# Explicit ID (skips auto-increment)
uv run fleet add-rule --domain VS --id ACME-VS-010 --description "VSORRES range check"

# Output to a specific directory (overrides study_config)
uv run fleet add-rule --domain AE --description "Custom check" --output ./my_rules/

docs.title: 3. Edit the Check block
docs.text:
Open the generated YAML and fill in your validation logic in the Check: section:

Check:
  all:
    - name: AESER
      operator: equal_to
      value: "Y"
      value_is_literal: true
    - name: AESEV
      operator: empty

docs.title: 4. Run validation
docs.text:
# Inline in a pipeline: inside the study, validation.custom_rules applies
ae = raw_df.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="AE").validate("AE").to_frame()

# Or name the directory explicitly
ae = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .validate("AE", custom_rules="metadata/custom_rules")
    .to_frame()
)

# Or via the ValidationService
from fleet.validation.service import ValidationService

svc = ValidationService()
result = svc.validate_sdtm(ae, domain="AE", version="3.4", custom_rules="metadata/custom_rules")
result.print_report()

docs.title: Rule anatomy
docs.text:
A custom rule follows the same YAML schema as CDISC CORE rules. Here is an annotated example:

Core:
  Id: FLEET-AE-001          # Unique ID (auto-generated by fleet add-rule)
  Status: Draft
  Version: "1"

Rule Type: Record Data       # Record-level check

Scope:
  Classes:
    Include: [EVENTS]
  Domains:
    Include: [AE]            # Restrict to the AE domain

Check:                       # The validation logic (what you write)
  all:
    - name: AESER
      operator: equal_to
      value: "Y"
      value_is_literal: true
    - name: AESEV
      operator: empty

Outcome:
  Message: >-
    AESEV is empty for a record where AESER = 'Y'. Serious adverse events
    must have severity documented.
  Output Variables: [USUBJID, AETERM, AESER, AESEV]

Description: >-
  AESEV must be populated when AESER = 'Y'.

Authorities:
  - Organization: Fleet
    Standards:
      - Name: SDTMIG
        Version: "3.4"
        References:
          - Origin: Sponsor SOP
            Rule Identifier:
              Id: FLEET-AE-001
              Version: "1"

Sensitivity: Record
Executability: Fully Executable

docs.title: The check DSL
docs.text:
CDISC CORE rules use a JSON/YAML check DSL built from composable operators:

Combinator Meaning all All conditions must be true (AND) any At least one condition is true (OR) not Negates the enclosed condition

Each leaf condition specifies a variable name, an operator, and optionally a value:

Check:
  all:
    - name: AESEV
      operator: is_contained_by
      value: ["MILD", "MODERATE", "SEVERE"]
    - name: AESER
      operator: equal_to
      value: "Y"
      value_is_literal: true

docs.title: Available operators
docs.text:
Operator Description equal_to Exact match not_equal_to Not equal empty Variable is null/blank non_empty Variable has a value less_than / greater_than Numeric/date comparison less_than_or_equal_to / greater_than_or_equal_to Inclusive comparison contains / does_not_contain Substring check is_contained_by Value is in a list starts_with / ends_with Prefix/suffix check matches_regex Regex pattern match date_less_than / date_greater_than Date comparison

For the full operator reference, see the CDISC CORE Rule Editor.

docs.title: Configuration and resolution order
docs.text:
Fleet resolves custom rules from multiple sources. The first match wins:

  1. Explicit custom_rules= parameter on .validate() or ValidationService methods.
  2. validation.custom_rules in study_config.yaml (team-wide default). The .validate() verb finds the study config from the working directory.
  3. None — no custom rules are loaded.

A directory that does not exist is refused before the engine starts: the verb raises ValidationSetupError. The report header shows the directory used and its source.

docs.title: Storing custom rules
docs.text:
Place custom rule files in the configured directory (default: metadata/custom_rules/):

my_study/
  study_config.yaml
  metadata/
    custom_rules/          ← Your sponsor-specific rules (all .yaml files loaded)
      FLEET-AE-001.yaml
      FLEET-AE-002.yaml
      ACME-VS-001.yaml
    sdtm/
      rules/               ← CDISC CORE rules (from fleet init rules)
    adam/
      rules/

Commit the directory to VCS so the complete rule inventory is versioned alongside the study.

docs.title: ID naming convention
docs.text:
Pattern Example Owner CORE-XXXXXX CORE-000001 CDISC (official — never reuse) <COMPANY>-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> ACME-AE-001 Your organisation FLEET-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> FLEET-DM-003 Default prefix

The --prefix flag on fleet add-rule controls the prefix. Auto-increment scans existing rules in the target directory to determine the next available sequence number.

docs.title: Uniqueness guarantee
docs.text: fleet add-rule checks all existing .yaml files in the target directory and refuses to create a rule if the Core.Id already exists. This prevents accidental overwrites.

docs.title: Validating rule schema locally
docs.text:
Before running rules through the engine, you can validate them against the vendored CDISC JSON Schema:

import json
import yaml
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
from pathlib import Path

schema_path = Path("src/fleet/validation/schemas/cdisc_rule_schema.json")
schema = json.loads(schema_path.read_text())

with open("metadata/custom_rules/FLEET-AE-001.yaml") as f:
    rule = yaml.safe_load(f)

validator = Draft202012Validator(schema)
errors = list(validator.iter_errors(rule))
# errors == [] means the rule is schema-valid

docs.title: Contributing upstream
docs.text: If your custom rule addresses a gap that would benefit the broader CDISC community, consider contributing it back via the CDISC Rule Editor or the CORE GitHub repository.

docs.title: How define.yaml Drives DataFrame Creation
docs.text:
define.yaml is the single source of truth for a Fleet study. One file simultaneously:

  1. Declares all output variables (fed to Define-XML 2.1 generation)
  2. Specifies how each variable is derived (executed as a pipeline)
  3. Declares codelists and controlled terminology references
  4. Defines structural metadata (keys, class, structure label)

docs.title: File Layout
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../src/fleet/define_xml/schemas/define_spec_schema.json
fleet_spec_version: 1
study:
  id:             CDISCPILOT01
  standard:       ADAMIG
  standard_version: "1.1"

codelists:
  - oid: C66731
    name: Sex
    type: text
    items:
      - coded_value: "M"
        decode: MALE
      - coded_value: "F"
        decode: FEMALE

datasets:
  - name: ADSL
    label: Subject-Level Analysis Dataset
    structure: One record per subject
    keys: [STUDYID, USUBJID]
    inputs:
      - name: DM
        type: dataset
    variables:
      - name: STUDYID
        ...

The spec is validated against the bundled JSON Schema (define_spec_schema.json), which is generated from the algorithm registry — its algorithm: enum and per-algorithm required fields always match what from_spec() actually executes (a CI sync test enforces this). The top-level fleet_spec_version: 1 pins the spec dialect; a future incompatible version is rejected with a clear message rather than silently misinterpreted.

fleet lsp reads that schema straight from the installed package, so the Fleet VS Code extension gives you inline errors with no setup. Without it, a generic YAML language server can read the same schema from a $schema comment — fleet init define prints the exact line, resolved against your install. Adding it alongside the Fleet extension reports every schema error twice, so use one or the other.

docs.title: Derivation Algorithms
docs.text:
Every spec-executable algorithm is declared once in the central registry (fleet.core.spec_registry), which drives the from_spec executor, the discriminated-union validation models, and the JSON schema.

Two vocabularies, one mapping. The spec dialect deliberately keeps define-spec terminology (assign_ct, hardcode_no_ct, …) — the language a data-standards reviewer reads in a metadata document — while the runtime API keeps one verb per intent (assign). The two are not competing spellings: every algorithm is declared with its runtime verb, the mapping below is machine-checkable (fleet.spec_coverage()), and a CI test fails if they drift. Splitting assign_ct / assign_no_ct in the spec is also what makes validation strict — each algorithm gets its own required-field model, so a CT derivation missing its codelist is a load-time error, not a runtime surprise. A representative subset:

algorithm Namespace verb What it does assigned .assign(target, value=...) Constant literal for all rows source .assign(target, source=...) Copy column from predecessor assign_ct .assign(target, source=..., ct=..., ct_map=...) Copy + CT validate/decode derivation .derivation(target, expression=...) Arbitrary Polars expression first_date .first_date(target, from_dataset=..., date_col=..., where=...) Earliest event date per subject last_date .last_date(...) Latest event date per subject count_events .count_events(target, from_dataset=..., where=...) Integer event count duration .duration(target, start=..., end=...) Integer day count / elapsed time flag .flag(target, criteria=...) "Y" / null flag baseline / chg / pchg .baseline(...) / .chg(...) / .pchg(...) Baseline value & change callable .derivation(drv_obj) Study-specific escape hatch

The complete, always-current list is one call away (and df.sdtm.verbs() / df.adam.verbs() gives the runtime-verb counterpart):

import fleet

print(sorted(fleet.spec_algorithms("adam")))
print(sorted(fleet.spec_algorithms("sdtm")))

docs.title: The verb-coverage matrix
docs.text:
Not every inline verb is spec-expressible. fleet.spec_coverage() returns the full algorithm ↔ verb ↔ required-fields mapping, and fleet.SPEC_UNSUPPORTED is the machine-checked allowlist of verbs that have no spec algorithm (e.g. transform, derive_summary_records, the TDD add_* verbs) — so "which subset is spec-safe" has a definite answer instead of a guess:

import fleet

matrix = fleet.spec_coverage()  # algorithm ↔ verb ↔ required fields
inline_only = fleet.SPEC_UNSUPPORTED  # {"sdtm": {...}, "adam": {...}}
print(len(matrix), "algorithms;", len(inline_only["adam"]), "adam verbs are inline-only")

docs.title: Study-specific callables (callable:)
docs.text:
When no built-in verb fits, point derivation: at a registered derivation name or a fully qualified Python dotted path. The runtime dispatch depends on the callable's kind:

  • kind="column" (zero-arg, returns pl.Expr) — stays fully lazy, no DataFrame materialisation.
  • kind="frame" or kind="param" (receives upstream DataFrame, returns pl.DataFrame) — the pipeline is materialised at that point, the function is called, and the result is wrapped back into the namespace.
- name: AGEGR1
  derivation:
    algorithm: callable
    callable: examples.cdiscpilot01.adam.derivations.AGEGR1

Or use the registered short name (if the derivations module was imported):

- name: AGEGR1
  derivation:
    callable: AGEGR1 # algorithm: callable injected automatically

docs.title: Derivations folder convention
docs.text:
fleet derivation add AGEGR1 --dataset ADSL scaffolds a derivation file under the study's configured programs tree:

programs/derivations/       # <programs dir from study_config.yaml>
    __init__.py
    AGEGR1.py
    BMI.py

The convention is shared across standards — algorithm: callable works identically in SDTM and ADaM specs, because both dispatch through the same core registry and resolver. The resolver itself does no folder scanning: a callable is found either (a) by short name, when its module has been imported and the function is @derivation-registered, or (b) by fully qualified dotted path. Declare derivations_module: at the top of the spec and from_spec() imports it for you, so short names always resolve.

Both algorithm: and callable: plug into the Define-XML methods: DefineSpecGenerator(spec) (or fleet define-xml) emits one <MethodDef> per Derived variable, named Algorithm for <VARIABLE>. The <Description> is submission text, resolved in this order:

  1. the variable's comment: — always wins;
  2. for callable: derivations, the study callable's docstring (@derivation objects use their own fn docstring) — this is study-authored text; reST markup is stripped;
  3. the registry's submission-facing template for the algorithm, with the spec params filled in (e.g. chg renders Change from baseline: AVAL - BASE.).

Fleet's verb docstrings are never used — they are API documentation, identical across studies and unstable across Fleet versions. The <FormalExpression Context="Python/Fleet"> carries the faithful call (the verb the algorithm runs plus the spec params, or the callable's dotted_path), giving a verifiable link between the regulatory submission and the exact code that produced the data. The verb is named after the class that defines it, the way the run's lineage records it in VariableNode.method, so an ADaM study_day reads fleet.core._verb_mixin.SharedVerbsMixin.duration('ADY', end='ASTDT', start='TRTSDT') in the define and in the lineage of the dataset it documents.

docs.title: Example — TRTSDT (date of first dose)
docs.text:
first_date is a real spec algorithm — this example runs end to end. In the spec, from_dataset: names a pinned dataset (attach it with .pin("EX", ex) before calling from_spec); the runtime resolves the name to the pinned frame.

fleet_spec_version: 1
study:
  id: CDISCPILOT01
  standard: ADAMIG
  standard_version: "1.1"
datasets:
  - name: ADSL
    label: Subject-Level Analysis Dataset
    structure: One record per subject
    keys: [STUDYID, USUBJID]
    variables:
      - name: TRTSDT
        label: Date of First Exposure to Treatment
        type: date
        origin: Derived
        derivation:
          algorithm: first_date
          from_dataset: EX
          date_col: EXSTDTC
          # admiral template exposure rule: a placebo dose of 0 counts. The SAP decides.
          where: >-
            (pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0) | ((pl.col("EXDOSE") == 0)
            & pl.col("EXTRT").str.to_uppercase().str.contains("PLACEBO"))

Run it by pinning EX and calling from_spec (the harness writes the YAML above to define.yaml first):

import polars as pl
import fleet  # noqa: F401

dm = pl.DataFrame({"STUDYID": ["CDISCPILOT01"] * 2, "USUBJID": ["S1", "S2"]})
ex = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "USUBJID": ["S1", "S1", "S2"],
        "EXTRT": ["XANOMELINE", "XANOMELINE", "XANOMELINE"],
        "EXSTDTC": ["2014-01-05", "2014-01-02", "2014-02-01"],
        "EXDOSE": [54.0, 0.0, 54.0],  # the 0-dose active row is filtered out by where=
    }
)

adsl = dm.adam.pin("EX", ex).from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="ADSL").to_frame()
print(adsl)  # TRTSDT = 2014-01-05 for S1 (earliest dosed date), 2014-02-01 for S2

The equivalent hand-written pipeline calls the same verb directly:

treated = (
    '(pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0) | '
    '((pl.col("EXDOSE") == 0) & pl.col("EXTRT").str.to_uppercase().str.contains("PLACEBO"))'
)
adsl = dm.adam.adsl.first_date(
    "TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex, date_col="EXSTDTC", where=treated
).to_frame()

docs.title: End-to-End Flow
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[define.yaml] -->|parsed + validated| B[spec_registry]
    B -->|derivation specs| D[namespace.from_spec]
    D -->|applies verbs| E[Polars pipeline]
    E -->|calls .to_frame| F[ADSL DataFrame]
    A -->|variable metadata| C[DefineSpecGenerator]
    C --> G[define_adam.xml]
    F --> H[adsl.parquet / adsl.json]
    F --> I[DatasetChecker / ValidationService]

docs.title: Running the full pipeline programmatically
docs.text:
from_spec is the execution entry point. Pin any datasets the spec references by name, then build each dataset:

import polars as pl
import fleet  # noqa: F401

dm = pl.read_parquet("outputs/sdtm/dm.parquet")
ex = pl.read_parquet("outputs/sdtm/ex.parquet")

adsl = (
    dm.adam.pin("EX", ex)
    .from_spec("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml", dataset="ADSL")
    .to_frame()
)

StudyContext (via load_study_context(config_path)) resolves the configured raw_data, sdtm_data, adam_data, and metadata directories so you don't hard-code paths; it exposes sdtm_spec / adam_spec / raw_file(...) helpers.

docs.title: Generating Define-XML from the same spec
docs.text:
One CLI command — inside a study workspace, spec and output default from study_config.yaml:

uv run fleet define-xml --standard adam                 # config-based defaults
uv run fleet define-xml -s specs/define.yaml -o out.xml --strict

The same generation from Python:

from fleet import DefineSpecGenerator

DefineSpecGenerator("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml").generate(
    "outputs/cdiscpilot01/define_adam.xml"
)

DefineSpecGenerator emits a <MethodDef> per Derived variable (see the method text rule above); variables with origin: Collected, Assigned, Protocol, or Predecessor never reference a method. Generated documents are validated on the way out — against the vendored CDISC XSDs and a semantic lint (fleet.define_xml.semantic_errors) that rejects reviewer-facing defects such as a MethodOID on a non-Derived variable or API markup inside TranslatedText; validate_xml=False bypasses both.

docs.title: Define-XML gaps: warning or refusal
docs.text:
Define-XML 2.1 requires three things that a spec can leave out:

  • a MethodOID on each Derived ItemRef, so a Derived variable needs a comment: or a derivation: block that gives method text;
  • a Length on text, integer and float items (characters for text, digits for numbers);
  • a SignificantDigits on float items (significant_digits: in the spec, on a variable or on a value-level entry).

The generator names each gap, one line per item:

specs/define.yaml: 2 Define-XML gap(s):
  DM.SAFFL: no method text (add a comment: or a derivation: block)
  VS.AVAL (PARAMCD = SYSBP): no SignificantDigits (required on float)
Entry point A gap gives fleet define-xml, DefineSpecGenerator(spec) the file, and one warning with the list fleet define-xml --strict, DefineSpecGenerator(spec, strict=True) SpecError, exit code 1, no file fleet check a FAIL row define (sdtm) or define (adam) with the list

The schema refuses significant_digits: on a type other than float, and length: on date and datetime.

The spec keys below apply to every generation:

  • fleet_spec_version: 1 — spec dialect version (checked on load).
  • derivations_module: — a dotted module that from_spec imports itself, so callable: derivations register without a manual import.
  • output_format: — per-dataset or spec-level export format (parquet, json, xpt) recorded in the DAG and Define-XML leaf hrefs.
  • value_level: — value-level metadata entries emitted as Define-XML <ValueListDef> / where-clause elements.
  • ct: {validate: true, file: ...} — opt the spec into CT validation (see below).

docs.title: Codelist References
docs.text:
Variables can reference codelists declared in the codelists block:

- name: SEX
  label: Sex
  type: text
  codelist: C66731 # references the oid in codelists[]
  derivation:
    algorithm: source
    source: SEX

docs.title: Controlled terminology in the spec path
docs.text:
A spec step and its inline call check the same terms. Inside a study, a ct_codelist: ID resolves to the class of that ID in the study's codelists.py, the module fleet init ct generates. So this entry:

- name: AESEV
  codelist: C66769
  derivation:
    algorithm: assign_ct
    source: ae_severity
    ct_codelist: C66769

runs as .assign("AESEV", source="ae_severity", ct=AESEV) with the AESEV class of codelists.py, and a raw Mild gives the same warning in both notations: AE.AESEV: column 'ae_severity' contains values not in codelist 'C66769': ['Mild'].

  • The study is the first study_config.yaml above the folder of the define.yaml, never the working directory.
  • When the CT loaded in fleet.get_validator() holds the codelist (for example through ct: file:, below), it checks the values in both notations. A literal (hardcode_ct) is checked against the loaded CT only.
  • Outside a study, before fleet init ct, or for an ID without a class, only the loaded CT can check the values.

Because both notations then trust codelists.py, Fleet checks the file against the study:

Check Problem Fix Package A package in the __ct_packages__ or __ct_package__ marker of the file (for older files, the package in each class's _cdisc_url) is not pinned in study_config.yaml (ct.package, ct.adam_package). fleet init ct --force Mixed packages The classes name two packages of one product, for example two SDTM CT dates. An SDTM and an ADaM package together are correct. fleet init ct --force Missing codelist A codelist: or ct_codelist: ID of a define.yaml has no class in the file. fleet add-ct --domains AE (SDTM); fleet init ct --force (ADaM), after you set ct.adam_package Missing file The define.yaml files reference codelists, but the file does not exist. fleet init ct

from_spec warns once per process about all but the missing codelist, and still checks the values against the file. An inline ct= class from another package gives the package warning too. fleet check fails on all four, and fleet doctor prints one codelists.py line.

docs.title: Two CT packages: SDTM CT and ADaM CT
docs.text:
CDISC publishes ADaM CT on its own dates, and some codelists are only in ADaM CT (DTYPE, C81224). A study with ADaM datasets pins both packages in study_config.yaml:

ct:
  package: sdtmct-2023-12-15
  adam_package: adamct-2023-06-30
  • fleet init cfg and fleet new with ADaM datasets pin adamct-2023-06-30, the latest ADaM CT package on or before the default SDTM package. With another --package, give --adam-package too.
  • fleet init ct takes each codelist from the first pinned package that holds it, SDTM CT first. When no pinned package holds a codelist, it names the ID, writes no file and exits with code 1.
  • fleet init ct also writes the terms and decodes (the NCI preferred term) into each codelists: entry of the define.yaml files that has no terms yet; with --force, into every entry. The file is rewritten, so only its header comment stays. A Define-XML CodeList needs its terms, and fleet define-xml names each codelist without them.
  • The ADaM define.yaml states both dates: ct_version (SDTM CT, for SEX) and adam_ct_version (ADaM CT, for DTYPE). Its Define-XML lists two CT standards, with the publishing sets SDTM and ADaM.

docs.title: Opting the spec into CT validation
docs.text:
Without a ct: block, an assign_ct without ct_mapping checks its values (pass-through), and one with ct_mapping maps them without a check. Add a top-level ct: block to check every assign_ct / hardcode_ct derivation of the spec, mapped ones included; out-of-codelist values emit a warning naming the dataset, variable, and codelist:

ct:
  validate: true
  file: ct/cdisc_ct.yaml   # optional — loaded into the CT cache before the run
datasets:
  - name: DM
    variables:
      - name: SEX
        codelist: C66731
        derivation:
          algorithm: assign_ct
          source: sex
          ct_codelist: C66731

When datasets are checked with DatasetChecker(spec, check_ct=True), the values are also verified against the spec's own inline codelists:, and codelist lookups are normalised to concept IDs — so a spec cannot ship values that contradict the conformance it asserts in the generated Define-XML.

docs.title: Schema Validation — What, When, and How
docs.text: Fleet has two independent layers of schema validation for define.yaml. They run at different points and catch different classes of error.

docs.title: Layer 1 — Registry model validation (pipeline-build time)
docs.text:
When you call .from_spec(), Fleet resolves each variable's algorithm: through the spec registry and validates its derivation block against a discriminated-union Pydantic model generated for that algorithm. The model declares exactly which fields are required and sets extra="forbid", so a misspelled field is a loud error — not a silent column of nulls. This runs immediately when .from_spec() is called, before any data is materialised.

What it catches:

  • Unknown algorithm names (with a did-you-mean suggestion)
  • Misspelled or unexpected fields (extra="forbid")
  • Missing required fields for a given algorithm
  • Wrong field types (e.g. a list where a string is expected)

Errors are wrapped in a SpecError that names file → dataset → variable. Here is the real message for a typo'd field (ct_codelst instead of ct_codelist):

# derivation block with a typo:
#   - name: SEX
#     derivation:
#       algorithm: assign_ct
#       source: sex
#       ct_codelst: C66731        # ← typo: should be ct_codelist

dm = raw_df.sdtm.from_spec("specs/define.yaml", dataset="DM")
# fleet.core.exceptions.SpecError:
# specs/define.yaml → dataset DM → variable SEX: 1 validation error for SDTMAssignCtSpec
# ct_codelst
#   Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value='C66731', input_type=str]

(Note: a well-formed assign_ct without any codelist does not error — it copies the value through and emits a UserWarning that CT could not be validated. assign never fabricates a missing-field error for an optional field.)

docs.title: Layer 2 — Define-XML generation in strict mode (fleet check)
docs.text:
fleet check generates the Define-XML of every define.yaml the study config points at, in strict mode, and writes no file. The row passes only when the generator gives a valid document. This layer fires on demand, not automatically during pipeline execution.

uv run fleet check

What it catches:

  • a spec that does not conform to define_spec_schema.json (SpecSchemaError, with the path of the bad entry);
  • a codelist: reference to a codelist that the spec does not declare;
  • a Define-XML gap: method text, Length or SignificantDigits (see Define-XML gaps above);
  • a generated document that fails the CDISC XSDs or the semantic lint.

The same check from Python: DefineSpecGenerator(path, strict=True).to_xml_string() raises on the first of these problems and returns the XML text otherwise.

docs.title: When to run each layer
docs.text: Layer When it fires Blocks execution? Registry models Automatically on .from_spec() call Yes — raises SpecError (file → dataset → variable) fleet check Manually or in CI, before submission Yes — a FAIL row and exit code 1 CDISC Rules Engine Manually, after datasets are materialised No — report only

docs.title: JSON Schema & Editor Support
docs.text:
The YAML spec is validated against the bundled schema at:

src/fleet/define_xml/schemas/define_spec_schema.json

This schema is generated from the algorithm registry — its algorithm: enum, per-algorithm required fields, and the fleet_spec_version / derivations_module properties are derived from the same declarations that drive execution, and a CI test fails if the checked-in schema drifts. So the editor red-squiggles you see match exactly what from_spec() will accept — including the callable escape hatch and every algorithm the engine can run. Regenerate it after registry changes with:

uv run python -m fleet.define_xml.schema_builder

Add this comment to the top of every spec file to activate YAML language-server auto-complete in VS Code or any LSP-enabled editor:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../src/fleet/define_xml/schemas/define_spec_schema.json

docs.title: CRF Page References
docs.text:
Variables with origin: Collected can include page references to the annotated Case Report Form PDF. Fleet emits these as <def:DocumentRef> / <def:PDFPageRef> elements inside <def:Origin> in the Define-XML, and the standard define2-1.xsl stylesheet renders them as clickable links.

One origin vocabulary

origin: uses the Define-XML 2.1 Origin Types — Collected, Derived, Assigned, Protocol, Predecessor — and the same values flow into QORIG in generated SUPPQUAL datasets. Collected values also carry def:Source, which defaults to Investigator (CRF data); override it with origin_source: Vendor | Sponsor | Subject. The Define-XML 2.0 spellings CRF and eDT are not valid.

How the Origin description renders, per origin type:

  • Predecessor requires predecessor: DATASET.VARIABLE (schema-enforced); the define renders Predecessor: DM.COUNTRY. In an ADaM spec, a variable carried with algorithm: source but still marked Collected triggers a generation-time warning suggesting the Predecessor form. When freezing an inline pipeline, to_spec_yaml(dataset="ADSL", predecessor="DM") pre-fills these entries for carry-through columns and pure source copies — the emitted YAML stays the explicit, reviewable source of truth.
  • Derived describes the derivation in its MethodDef.
  • Assigned / Protocol show the comment: — e.g. comment: DM.ARM renders Assigned: DM.ARM.
  • Collected with CRF pages renders the page links; Investigator-collected variables without pages fall back to a Case Report Form description.
  • A variable with value-level metadata and no comment: renders See Value Level Metadata.
- name: COUNTRY
  label: Country
  type: text
  origin: Predecessor
  predecessor: DM.COUNTRY

docs.title: Setup: declare the aCRF document
docs.text:
Scaffold the block with one command (config-context: it edits the study's own define.yaml; --standard adam|both covers the ADaM spec too):

uv run fleet add-acrf --href blankcrf.pdf
uv run fleet add-acrf --href blankcrf.pdf --page-map acrf_pages.yaml --standard both

Which adds a documents block to the study: section:

study:
  id: CDISCPILOT01
  standard: SDTMIG
  standard_version: "3.4"
  documents:
    annotated_crf:
      href: blankcrf.pdf # path in the submission package
      title: Annotated Case Report Form # displayed in Define-XML

This emits the top-level <def:AnnotatedCRF> container and the <def:leaf> element that the XSLT needs to render document links.

docs.title: Layer 1 — Simple page strings (most common)
docs.text:
Add crf_pages to any collected variable:

variables:
  - name: SEX
    label: Sex
    type: text
    origin: Collected
    crf_pages: "8" # single page
    derivation:
      algorithm: assign_ct
      source: sex
      ct_codelist: C66731

  - name: RACE
    label: Race
    type: text
    origin: Collected
    crf_pages: "8 9" # space-separated multiple pages

The string value maps directly to the PageRefs attribute with Type="PhysicalRef".

docs.title: Layer 2 — Rich references (named destinations, page ranges)
docs.text:
For PDF bookmarks or page ranges, use the dict form:

- name: SEX
  origin: Collected
  crf_pages:
    pages: "DM_SEX" # PDF bookmark name
    type: NamedDestination # or PhysicalRef (default)

- name: RACE
  origin: Collected
  crf_pages:
    pages: "8 9"
    type: PhysicalRef
    first_page: "8" # optional range attributes
    last_page: "9"

docs.title: Layer 3 — External page map (EDC-driven workflows)
docs.text:
For studies where CRF annotations are extracted from an EDC system, point to an external YAML file:

study:
  documents:
    annotated_crf:
      href: blankcrf.pdf
      page_map: acrf_pages.yaml # relative to the define.yaml directory

The page map file uses DOMAIN.VARIABLE keys:

# acrf_pages.yaml — auto-generated from EDC export
DM.SEX: "7"
DM.BRTHDTC: "8"
AE.AETERM: "12 13"
VS.VSTESTCD: "20"

Inline crf_pages on individual variables always take precedence over the external page map.

docs.title: Supplemental documents
docs.text:
Additional supporting documents (reviewer's guide, protocol, etc.) can be declared alongside the annotated CRF:

study:
  documents:
    annotated_crf:
      href: blankcrf.pdf
    supplemental_docs:
      - id: LF.ReviewerGuide
        href: reviewers-guide.pdf
        title: Reviewer's Guide

These emit <def:SupplementalDoc> and corresponding <def:leaf> elements.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• The inputs block declares which upstream datasets the pipeline should join/merge.
  • Variables with no derivation block are expected to flow in via the source dataset — they appear in Define-XML as origin: Collected.
  • Run uv run fleet check (or fleet define-xml --strict) to catch schema errors and Define-XML gaps before submission.

docs.title: Exporting Datasets
docs.text:
Fleet writes datasets in three formats, selected the same way everywhere — one --format flag on the CLI, one output_format: key in the spec, one writer function per format in Python.

Format File When to use Requires Parquet (default) .parquet Working format: fast, typed, compressed; ideal between pipeline steps and for QC — SAS XPT (v5 Transport) .xpt Regulatory submission datasets; SAS interop io extra (pyreadstat) CDISC Dataset-JSON v1.1 .json The emerging submission exchange format; typed, metadata-rich —

docs.title: From the CLI
docs.text:
Every dataset-writing command takes the same flag and resolves its output directory from study_config.yaml:

uv run fleet run --format xpt                 # define.yaml pipelines → <sdtm_data>/<adam_data>
uv run fleet run --format dataset-json --dataset ADSL
uv run fleet tdd build --format xpt           # trial design domains → <sdtm_data>

docs.title: From the spec (output_format:)
docs.text:
Declare the format once in define.yaml — per dataset or spec-wide. The choice is recorded in the pipeline DAG and drives the Define-XML leaf hrefs, so the metadata always points at the files you actually ship:

output_format: parquet          # spec-level default
datasets:
  - name: ADSL
    output_format: xpt          # per-dataset override

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
from fleet import save_parquet, save_dataset_json
from fleet.io import save_xpt

save_parquet(adsl, Path("data/adam/adsl.parquet"))
save_xpt(adsl, Path("data/adam/adsl.xpt"))
save_dataset_json(
    adsl, "data/adam/adsl.json", domain="ADSL", label="Subject-Level Analysis Dataset"
)

Format-specific behaviour worth knowing:

  • XPT is SAS transport version 5, the submission format of FDA TCG 3.1.1, and the member is named as the file (adsl.xpt holds ADSL). Names are upper-cased. A pl.Date is stored as a SAS date with DATE9, a pl.Datetime with DATETIME20 and a pl.Time with TIME8. NaN and infinity become SAS missing. Nothing is cut: a name over 8 characters, a label over 40 or a value over 200 bytes stops the write. A value that is not ASCII is written as UTF-8 bytes, with a warning. Pass label= and column_labels= for the dataset and variable labels; fleet run takes them from define.yaml. Install the writer with uv add "fleet-cdisc[io]".
  • Dataset-JSON embeds dataset metadata (domain, label, originator, file OID) alongside typed column data — pass them as keyword arguments.
  • Parquet forwards any keyword arguments to Polars' write_parquet (compression, statistics, ...).

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
The mirror-image loaders auto-detect format from the extension — CSV, Parquet, XPT, and SAS7BDAT all land as LazyFrames:

from fleet import load_raw_data, load_datasets

dm_raw = load_raw_data("data/raw/dm_raw.csv")  # one file → LazyFrame
frames = load_datasets(
    {"DM": "data/sdtm/dm.parquet", "AE": "data/sdtm/ae.xpt"}  # many files → dict
)

What the readers decide for you:

  • A SAS blank is a missing value. SAS has one character missing value, the blank, so a blank in an XPT or SAS7BDAT file reads as null and is_null() finds it. A variable with no value keeps its SAS type.
  • A CSV file holds no types. Polars infers them from every row. A column with a leading zero (SITEID 001) stays text, with a warning, because a number would lose the zero. schema_overrides={"LBORRES": pl.String} is the $ informat; your types always win. fleet run reads the variables of define type text, and their raw source columns, as text.
  • The encoding is yours to name. A file from a WLATIN1 SAS session needs load_raw_data(path, encoding="iso-8859-1"), or --encoding iso-8859-1 on fleet compare and fleet validate. A keyword the reader does not take raises; it is never dropped.

In a join on keys a missing key matches a missing key, as SAS MERGE BY does, in every verb that joins (merge, pick, first_date, derive_param, ...).

docs.title: Not to be confused with TLG render formats
docs.text: Tables, listings, and graphs render to display formats — HTML, RTF, PDF, PPTX — via fleet tlg run --format .... Those are outputs for humans; this page covers dataset files for machines and submissions. See TLG from a Spec.

docs.title: Interactive Explorer — One Definition, Two Run Modes
docs.text: Interactive exploration apps and batch TLG programs usually drift apart because the table definition lives twice — once in the app's modules, once in the production scripts. Fleet avoids that structurally: the TLG spec YAML is the definition, and both run modes consume the same file through the same engine.

docs.title: Declare degrees of freedom on the spec
docs.text:
Add an interactive: block to a TLG spec. Every choice is just a value for an existing spec field — a widget is a spec-field selector, nothing more:

template: aet01
schema_version: 1
adsl_filter: 'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"'
statistics: [n_subjects, n_pct]

interactive:
  population:                            # -> adsl_filter
    - {label: Safety, filter: 'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"', default: true}
    - {label: All subjects, filter: null}
  dataset_filter:                        # -> dataset_filter
    - {label: All AEs, filter: null, default: true}
    - {label: Serious only, filter: 'pl.col("AESER") == "Y"'}
  stats:                                 # -> statistics
    - {label: "n (%)", statistics: [n_subjects, n_pct], default: true}
    - {label: "+ events", statistics: [n_subjects, n_pct, n_events]}

Axes: groupby (arm column), population (ADSL filter presets), dataset_filter, and stats. Each axis needs exactly one default: true; an absent axis stays fixed at the spec value.

docs.title: Two run modes, same artifact
docs.text:
# Batch — renders the default variant (submission output):
fleet tlg run examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml --data adae.parquet --adsl adsl.parquet -o out/

# Interactive — one self-contained HTML file, no server, no new dependencies:
fleet tlg explore examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml --data adae.parquet --adsl adsl.parquet -o explorer.html

The explorer pre-renders every declared variant through the identical spec → ARD → render path and embeds, per variant: the HTML fragment, the ARD as downloadable JSON (for QC), and the exact spec YAML in a "show definition" panel. The embedded JavaScript only shows/hides pre-rendered fragments — no statistics or layout logic exists client-side, so there is no second implementation that could drift. Works from a shared drive; makes no network requests.

docs.title: Why drift is impossible
docs.text:
• The batch output is the explorer's default variant — same functions, same build. A golden test pins them byte-identical.
  • Promotion needs no transcription: the "show definition" panel displays the current view's spec YAML; adopting it means saving that YAML into your specs directory, which the batch run then consumes.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Variant space is the cartesian product of declared choices: hard error above 500 variants, warning above 100. This is not an engine bottleneck — the Polars pipeline renders hundreds of variants in seconds. The cap protects the artifact: the explorer is one self-contained HTML file with every variant pre-rendered and embedded (fragment + ARD JSON + spec YAML), so the file grows linearly with the variant count and a 500-variant page is unusable to open, review, and share — which defeats its purpose. Beyond that scale, a live server that renders on demand is the right tool (a future fleet tlg serve); the static explorer deliberately trades variant count for zero-infrastructure portability.
  • Views are sanctioned-only (declared choices, not free-form filtering) — every number a reviewer sees was produced by the validated engine at build time.

docs.title: Multi-Source Event Derivation with pick()
docs.text: Many ADaM variables scan several data sources and keep one value per subject: the latest date over all sources, or the first source that has a value. Admiral calls this pattern derive_vars_extreme_event / event(). Fleet provides pick(), one verb that replaces multi-step joins, coalesces, and manual priority logic.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Consider LSTALVDT (Last Date Known Alive). The derivation spec typically reads:

Set LSTALVDT to the latest date from:

  1. Death date (DTHDT) — if the subject died
  2. Last AE end date (AEENDTC)
  3. Last AE start date (AESTDTC)
  4. Treatment end date (TRTEDT) — fallback

Each "event" has its own source dataset, filter condition, and column to extract. The latest date over all events wins for each subject, whatever the list position.

Without pick(), you'd need:

# Manual approach — 3 last_date lookups + a row-wise maximum
adsl = (
    adsl.adam.adsl.last_date("_dth", from_dataset=adsl_df, date_col="DTHDT")
    .last_date("_ae_end", from_dataset=ae, date_col="AEENDTC")
    .last_date("_ae_start", from_dataset=ae, date_col="AESTDTC")
    .derivation(
        "LSTALVDT", expression='pl.max_horizontal("_dth", "_ae_end", "_ae_start", "TRTEDT")'
    )
    .to_frame()
    .drop(["_dth", "_ae_end", "_ae_start"])
)

This is verbose, error-prone, and loses traceability: the record behind each date is gone.

docs.title: The Solution: pick()
docs.text:
adsl = adsl.adam.adsl.pick(
    "LSTALVDT",
    events=[
        {
            "when": pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "DTHDT"},
            "source": adsl_df,
            "label": "Death date",
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("AEENDTC").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "AEENDTC"},
            "source": ae,
            "label": "AE end date",
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("AESTDTC").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "AESTDTC"},
            "source": ae,
            "label": "AE start date",
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("TRTEDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "TRTEDT"},
            "label": "Treatment end (self)",
        },
    ],
    by=["USUBJID"],
    order=["LSTALVDT"],
    mode="last",
).to_frame()

order=["LSTALVDT"], mode="last" at top level makes every event compete on the date: the latest one wins. Each event's "label" documents intent. No temporary columns needed.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Events list] --> PE

    subgraph PE["For each event"]
        direction TB
        C[Filter source by 'when' condition]
        D[Apply 'set' mappings to targets]
        E[Group by 'by' vars]
        F[Select record per mode / order]
        G[Tag with event list position]
        C --> D --> E --> F --> G
    end

    PE --> H[Stack all candidate records]
    H --> I[Sort by top-level order, then list position]
    I --> J[Keep first per group = winner]
    J --> K[Left-join targets back to base frame]

Key properties:

  1. Within-event selection uses the event's mode and order, or the top-level ones.
  2. With a top-level order, every event's record competes on that order and mode, as admiral derive_vars_extreme_event does. order=["LSTALVDT"], mode="last" gives the latest date over all sources. A tie goes to the first listed event.
  3. With no top-level order, the first listed event that has a record wins: a priority cascade, as the admiral DTHCAUS template.
  4. Subjects with no matching events get null for all targets.

docs.title: Event Dict Reference
docs.text:
Each event is a Python dict with these keys:

Key Required Type Description "when" Yes str \| pl.Expr Boolean filter — which records qualify "set" Yes dict[str, str \| pl.Expr \| Any] Maps each target to a source column name, expression, or literal "source" No pl.DataFrame External dataset to scan. Omit to use the current pipeline frame "mode" No str Override top-level mode for this event ("first" / "last") "order" No str \| list[str] Override top-level sort for this event "label" No str Documentation-only description (ignored at runtime)

docs.title: Multiple Targets
docs.text:
pick() can derive several columns simultaneously from the same events:

adsl = adsl.adam.adsl.pick(
    ["LSTALVDT", "DTHFL"],
    events=[
        {
            "when": pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "DTHDT", "DTHFL": pl.lit("Y")},
            "source": adsl_df,
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("AEENDTC").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "AEENDTC", "DTHFL": pl.lit("N")},
            "source": ae,
        },
    ],
    by=["USUBJID"],
    order=["LSTALVDT"],
    mode="last",
).to_frame()

When an event only sets some targets, the others remain null for that event's candidates.

docs.title: String Conditions (YAML-Compatible)
docs.text:
For spec-driven pipelines, conditions can be strings that get evaluated safely:

events = [
    {"when": 'pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null()', "set": {"LSTALVDT": "DTHDT"}},
]

This is equivalent to passing a pl.Expr directly and enables full round-tripping through define.yaml.

docs.title: Admiral Comparison
docs.text:
Admiral Fleet event(dataset, condition, set_values_to, order, mode) Event dict in events list derive_vars_extreme_event(events, source_datasets, by_vars, order, mode, check_type) .pick(targets, events=..., by=..., order=..., mode=...) order = exprs(LSTALVDT), mode = "last": latest value over all events order=["LSTALVDT"], mode="last" Ties on order go to the first event in the list Ties on order go to the first event in events DTHCAUS template: first listed event with a record No top-level order: first listed event with a record Requires pre-built event objects + explicit dataset references Inline dicts with optional "source" — current frame used by default

Fleet's pick() is semantically equivalent but:

  • Eliminates the need for a separate event() constructor
  • Supports per-event mode/order overrides
  • Accepts literals (pl.lit("Y")) directly in "set" alongside column references
  • Chains naturally into the ADaM pipeline without materialisation breaks

docs.title: When to Use pick() vs @derivation
docs.text:
Scenario Use Multi-source extreme value or first-source cascade (LSTALVDT, DTHCAUS, LDDTHELD) pick() Simple conditional (AGEGR1, EOSSTT) case_when() Complex cross-record logic within one source (CBOR confirmation rules) @derivation(kind="frame") Aggregation that needs custom grouping (derived parameters) derive_param()

Rule of thumb: If your logic is "the latest (or first) value over sources A, B and C", or "try source A, then B, then C", use pick(). If it requires comparing multiple records within the same subject to determine a single result (e.g., sustained response confirmation), use a @derivation.

docs.title: Spec-Driven Usage
docs.text:
In a define.yaml, the pick algorithm maps directly:

variables:
  - name: LSTALVDT
    label: Last Date Known Alive
    algorithm: pick
    targets: [LSTALVDT]
    events:
      - when: 'pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null()'
        set: {LSTALVDT: DTHDT}
        source: ADSL
      - when: 'pl.col("AEENDTC").is_not_null()'
        set: {LSTALVDT: AEENDTC}
        source: AE
    by: [USUBJID]
    order: [LSTALVDT]
    mode: last

Fleet's from_spec() dispatches to .pick() automatically when algorithm: pick is detected.

docs.title: Namespace Pipeline Architecture
docs.text: Fleet lets you write the same pipeline in two notations: Code-driven (chaining verbs in Python) or Spec-driven (declaring the same verbs in a define.yaml that Fleet executes for you). Verb names and argument names are identical in both, so a step can move between them.

docs.title: The Recommended Approach: Spec-First with Custom Extensions
docs.text:
For the majority of modern statistical programming tasks, we highly recommend a hybrid "Spec-First" workflow.

In this approach, you let AI or your documentation team generate the define.yaml. Fleet consumes this YAML to automatically manage 90% of the derivations, dependencies, traceability, and Define-XML generation. Then, for the 10% of highly complex, proprietary derivations that do not fit neatly into a YAML file, you apply a thin layer of manual Polars python code on top of the built data step.

This hybrid approach ensures high reproducibility and documentation sync, while leaving an "escape hatch" open for when code must take over.

docs.title: 1. Code-Driven (Inline Python)
docs.text:
Best for: Quick exploration, ad-hoc analysis, smaller studies, or initial data discovery.

You construct your pipelines entirely in Python by chaining namespace verbs on Polars DataFrames. All logic is embedded directly in your scripts.

Example:

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID").duration("ADY", start="TRTSDT", end="ADT").to_frame()

docs.title: 2. Spec-Driven (define.yaml)
docs.text:
Best for: Production clinical trials, regulatory submissions, repeatability across projects.

You define metadata, controlled terminology, and derivations in a central define.yaml file. Fleet reads the specification and automatically builds the datasets. In this model, your Python scripts simply load the study context and call .build().

Example of the Hybrid Escape Hatch:

# The standard derivations live in define.yaml.
import polars as pl
import fleet  # noqa: F401

dm = pl.read_parquet("outputs/sdtm/dm.parquet")
base_adsl = dm.adam.from_spec("specs/study01/adam/define.yaml", dataset="ADSL").to_frame()

# Add custom logic for the 10% of edge-case scenarios not covered by the spec:
final_adsl = base_adsl.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "CUSTOM_FLAG", expression=pl.when(pl.col("AGE") > 80).then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit("N"))
).to_frame()

docs.title: How the pipeline works underneath
docs.text:
Every Fleet namespace (sdtm, adam, adsl, occds) follows the same pattern:

  1. Access the namespace on a Polars DataFrame: df.sdtm
  2. Chain verb calls — each returns a new namespace object accumulating pl.Expr objects
  3. Materialise with .to_frame() — executes a single df.with_columns(...) pass
result = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")  # 1. access  # 2. chain
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=SEX, ct_map={"Male": "M", "Female": "F"})
    .to_frame()  # 3. materialise
)

assign is the one canonical assignment verb (source= copies, value= hardcodes, ct=/ct_map= add CT). Most verbs only build an internal expression list at step 2; a few window/cross-domain verbs checkpoint internally but keep the chain going.

To inspect intermediate state or the query plan during development, use the chainable debug verbs .inspect() (hard checkpoint with diagnostic output) and .explain() (print the Polars query plan). See Advanced Patterns for details.

docs.title: Lazy evaluation
docs.text:
df.sdtm
  │
  ├─ .assign("USUBJID", source=...)  →  [Expr("patient_id".alias("USUBJID"))]
  ├─ .assign("SEX", ct=...)          →  [..., Expr(when/then.alias("SEX"))]
  └─ .to_frame()
       │
       └─ df.with_columns(*exprs)   ← single Polars pass

This means you pay no cost for columns you don't chain. Expression ordering mirrors declaration order.

docs.title: SDTM verbs at a glance
docs.text: Verb Purpose assign(target, source=) Copy raw column assign(target, value=) Constant literal for all rows assign(target, source=, ct=, ct_map=) Copy + validate/recode through a codelist case_when(target, when=, else_=) Multi-branch conditional date(target, source=) Normalise to ISO 8601 date or datetime derivation(target, expression=) Arbitrary pl.Expr merge(dataset, on=, keep=) Join a reference dataset to_frame() Materialise

docs.title: ADaM verbs at a glance
docs.text: Verb Purpose source(*targets) Variadic pass-through column(s) derivation(target, expression=) Arbitrary pl.Expr assign(target, value=) Constant literal date(target, source=) Parse DTC → Date/Datetime with imputation duration(target, start=, end=) CDISC study day / elapsed time flag(target, criteria=, by=) Per-group boolean flag baseline(target, aval=, baseline_flag=, by=) Carry baseline AVAL within groups chg(target, aval, base) Change from baseline pchg(target, aval, base) Percent change from baseline bmi(target, weight, height) Body Mass Index nrind(target, value, low, high) Normal range indicator (LOW/NORMAL/HIGH) on_treatment(target, adt, trtsdt, trtedt) On-treatment flag shift(target, baseline_cat, post_cat) Categorical shift string bsa(target, weight, height, method) Body Surface Area (4 methods) map(target, systolic, diastolic) Mean Arterial Pressure qtc(target, qt, rr, method, rr_unit) Corrected QT (QT in ms, RR in ms by default) derive_summary_records(by_vars, ...) Aggregate by group, append summary rows derive_locf_records(by_vars, ...) Forward-fill (LOCF) within patient groups derive_param(by_vars, ...) Derive a new parameter and append as rows to_frame() Materialise

docs.title: ADSL verbs at a glance
docs.text: Verb Purpose source(target) Pass-through column first_date(target, from_dataset, date_col, where) Earliest event date per subject last_date(target, from_dataset, date_col, where) Latest event date per subject duration(target, start, end) Elapsed days / duration flag(target, criteria) "Y" flag (expression, first/last/max/min/exists) count_events(target, from_dataset, where) Event count per subject age_years(target, age_col, age_unit_col) Unit-aware age conversion to years derive_period(periods, start_date) Subperiod/Phase variables (APxxSDT, etc.) to_frame() Materialise

docs.title: OCCDS verbs at a glance
docs.text: Verb Purpose source(target) Pass-through column first_occ(target, date_col, groups) Flag first occurrence within group flag(target, criteria, value_col, groups) Generalised \"Y\" flag (max/min/first/last/exists/expression) any_flag(target, col, value, groups) "Y" if event exists in group to_frame() Materialise

docs.title: StudyContext — workspace initialisation
docs.text:
The recommended way to start a new study is the bootstrapping pipeline via the Fleet CLI:

fleet init cfg --study-id STUDY01 --company "Acme Pharma" \
  --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS --root ./studies/STUDY01
fleet init define --config ./studies/STUDY01/study_config.yaml  # queries CDISC Library IG → define.yaml
fleet init ct     --config ./studies/STUDY01/study_config.yaml  # reads define.yaml → codelists.py

Note

When --root points to a non-current directory, pass --config <root>/study_config.yaml to init define and init ct, or cd into the root directory before running them.

See the CLI Reference for full details.

StudyContext.init() can also be used programmatically — it creates the folder tree and writes study_config.yaml. Define specs and codelists are produced by the subsequent pipeline steps (fleet init define, fleet init ct).

from fleet import StudyContext, SDTMConfig, ADAMConfig, load_study_context
from pathlib import Path

# ── Once, when starting a new study ──────────────────────────────────────
ctx = StudyContext.init(
    "./studies/STUDY01",
    study_id="STUDY01",
    company="Acme Pharma",
    sdtm=SDTMConfig(ig_version="3-4", domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]),
    adam=ADAMConfig(ig_version="1-1", datasets=["ADSL", "ADVS"]),
)

# ── Every subsequent session ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ctx = load_study_context(Path("./studies/STUDY01/study_config.yaml"))
Outcome Behaviour Directories already exist Silently skipped (mkdir -p semantics) study_config.yaml exists Raises StudyConfigError — use load_study_context() instead

docs.title: Trial Design Domains
docs.text:
Fleet provides first-class support for all nine CDISC Trial Design Model (TDD) domains through two complementary paths:

  1. fleet.StudyDesign — a typed aggregate: define the design once, derive every domain, audit it, and round-trip through YAML / Mermaid / USDM.
  2. Row-level pipeline — a fixed-sequence verb chain with rich Pydantic models and collection-level validators, for full row control.

SDTMIG 3.4 structures for the TDD domains ship with Fleet, so everything on this page runs offline — no CDISC Library API key required.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Domain Full Name Structure Type TE Trial Elements 1 rec/element Protocol-reference TA Trial Arms 1 rec/element/arm Protocol-reference TV Trial Visits 1 rec/visit/arm Protocol-reference TS Trial Summary 1 rec/parameter/seq Protocol-reference TI Trial Inclusion/Exclusion 1 rec/criterion Protocol-reference TD Trial Disease Assessments 1 rec/assessment plan Protocol-reference TM Trial Disease Milestones 1 rec/milestone type Protocol-reference SV Subject Visits 1 rec/subject/visit Subject-level SE Subject Elements 1 rec/subject/element Subject-level

docs.title: StudyDesign — define once, derive everything
docs.text:
fleet.StudyDesign is the single source of truth for a study's structure. Arms are declared as element paths; TAETORD, ELEMENT, EPOCH, and TABRANCH (at the randomization branch point) are derived mechanically:

import fleet

design = fleet.StudyDesign(
    study_id="CDISCPILOT01",
    elements=[
        {
            "etcd": "SCRN",
            "element": "Screening",
            "tedur": "P14D",
            "epoch": "SCREENING",
            "testrl": "INFORMED CONSENT",
            "teenrl": "RANDOMIZATION - 1",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "PBO",
            "element": "Placebo Treatment",
            "tedur": "P84D",
            "epoch": "TREATMENT",
            "testrl": "RANDOMIZATION",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "XANLO",
            "element": "Xanomeline Low Dose",
            "tedur": "P84D",
            "epoch": "TREATMENT",
            "testrl": "RANDOMIZATION",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "FU",
            "element": "Follow-up",
            "tedur": "P28D",
            "epoch": "FOLLOW-UP",
            "testrl": "END OF TREATMENT + 1",
        },
    ],
    arms={"PBO": ["SCRN", "PBO", "FU"], "XAN_LO": ["SCRN", "XANLO", "FU"]},
    arm_names={"PBO": "Placebo", "XAN_LO": "Xanomeline Low Dose"},
)

te = design.to_te()  # one domain at a time
frames = design.domains()  # or every populated domain: {"TE": df, "TA": df, ...}

Referential integrity is validated at construction: arm paths must reference defined elements, visit armcd values must reference defined arms, and element codes must be unique.

docs.title: Interchange formats
docs.text: Method Direction Use case StudyDesign.from_yaml(path) / design.to_yaml(path) YAML ⇄ trial_design.yaml spec, versioned next to define.yaml StudyDesign.from_mermaid(text, study_id=...) / design.to_mermaid() Mermaid ⇄ Diagram-as-code; protocol review decks StudyDesign.from_usdm(json_dict) USDM → Import a CDISC USDM / DDF export (e.g. from OpenStudyBuilder): arms, epochs, elements, study cells, encounters, eligibility criteria TrialParameters.from_ctgov("NCT...") ctgov → Seed TS from the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API

docs.title: Conformance audit — a P21 dry-run, offline
docs.text:
One CLI command (config-context — the design spec resolves from study_config.yaml; exit code 1 on errors, so it drops straight into CI):

uv run fleet tdd audit

The same audit from Python — design.audit(), or the standalone fleet.sdtm.trial_design_audit(te=..., ta=..., tv=..., ts=..., ti=..., dm=...) — checks the domains against published P21/FDA rule IDs and returns a findings DataFrame (rule_id, severity, domain, message):

findings = design.audit(dm=dm)
errors = findings.filter(pl.col("severity") == "error")

Encoded checks include:

Area Rules TE ETCD length (SD1009), TEENRL/TEDUR presence (SD0089), duplicates (SD1271) TA TAETORD unique per arm (SD1052), ARM↔ARMCD one-to-one (SD1033/SD1034), reserved ARMCDs (SD1053), ARMCD length (SD1004) TA↔TE ETCD/ELEMENT consistency, UNPLAN-aware (SD0067); unused elements (SD1378) TV VISITNUM uniqueness (SD1064), ARMCD FK vs TA TI IETESTCD format (SD0018), uniqueness within TIVERS (SD1286) DM↔TA Undefined arms, arms without subjects (SD1354) TS The FDA Technical Conformance Guide required-parameter profile (SD22xx — a missing SSTDTC is flagged as rejection-level TRC 1734) and conditional rules (e.g. INTMODEL/INTTYPE/PCLAS when STYPE=INTERVENTIONAL — SD1310/11/12)

The audit is a curated high-signal subset; run fleet validate (CDISC Rules Engine) for exhaustive coverage.

docs.title: Visit schedules
docs.text:
Build TV from day offsets relative to an anchor event. VISITNUM, VISITDY (CDISC no-day-zero convention), and deterministic TVSTRL rule text are derived:

from fleet.sdtm.tdd import TrialVisits

tv_rows = TrialVisits.from_schedule(
    [("Screening", -14), ("Baseline", 0), ("Week 4", 28), ("Week 8", 56)],
    anchor="RANDOMIZATION",
    window=3,  # or (before, after)
)

docs.title: CLI: fleet tdd
docs.text:
Like every Fleet command, fleet tdd runs in the context of the discovered study_config.yaml (git-style parent walk, --config to override): the design spec defaults to <metadata_sdtm>/trial_design.yaml and the output directory to the config's sdtm_data path — so the command works from any subdirectory of any company's folder structure. The YAML mirrors the StudyDesign schema; a top-level trial_design: wrapper key is accepted.

uv run fleet tdd audit                       # conformance pre-check
uv run fleet tdd build --format xpt          # audit + write to <sdtm_data>/
uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705           # print TS parameters from ClinicalTrials.gov
uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705 --write   # ...or merge them into trial_design.yaml
uv run fleet tdd build --design specs/td.yaml --out /tmp/out   # explicit overrides

build writes every populated domain (parquet, xpt, or dataset-json) and refuses to write when the audit reports errors (--force overrides).

docs.title: Protocol-Reference Domains
docs.text:
Protocol-reference domains (TE, TA, TV, TS, TI, TD, TM) follow a fixed sequence:

fetch_structure() → study_header() → add_*() → to_frame()

Each step validates that the previous step was completed. Calling verbs out of order raises a ValueError with a descriptive message.

import polars as pl
from fleet.sdtm.tdd import TrialElement, TrialElements, Epoch

te_rows = TrialElements(
    elements=[
        TrialElement(
            etcd="SCRN",
            element="Screening",
            testrl="INFORMED CONSENT",
            teenrl="RANDOMIZATION - 1",
            tedur="P14D",
            epoch=Epoch.SCREENING,
        ),
        TrialElement(
            etcd="TRT",
            element="Treatment",
            testrl="RANDOMIZATION",
            teenrl="END OF TREATMENT",
            tedur="P84D",
            epoch=Epoch.TREATMENT,
        ),
    ]
)

te = (
    pl.DataFrame()
    .sdtm.fetch_structure("TE", ig_version="3-4")
    .study_header(study_id="CDISCPILOT01", domain="TE")
    .add_elements(te_rows)
    .to_frame()
)

fetch_structure() resolves the domain structure in priority order: define_path= → save_to= cache → packaged SDTMIG 3.4 metadata → online CDISC Library. Discrepancies between the IG and Fleet's models are reported as UserWarning (schema reconciliation).

docs.title: Subject-Level Domains
docs.text:
Subject-level domains (SV, SE) use derivation verbs that freely mix with existing SDTM verbs:

sv = (
    raw_visits.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="SV")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .date("SVSTDTC", source="visit_date")
    .visit_map(
        "VISITNUM",
        "VISIT",
        date_col="SVSTDTC",
        planned_visits=tv_rows,
        ref_date="RFSTDTC",
        tolerance={"before": 3, "after": 3},
    )
    .study_day("SVSTDY", date_col="SVSTDTC", ref_date_col="RFSTDTC")
    .to_frame()
)

For SE, derive boundaries with element_boundaries() and the sequence number with the standard seq() verb:

se = (
    disposition_df.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="SE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .element_boundaries(
        "SESTDTC", "SEENDTC", milestones={"SCRN": "screening_date", "TRT": "first_dose_date"}
    )
    .seq("SESEQ", order_by=["SESTDTC"])
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: EPOCH stamped from SE
docs.text:
epoch_assign(se=...) derives EPOCH for any domain from the subject's own element intervals — the cross-domain consistency that P21 checks against SE. (The study-level epoch_ranges= form remains available.)

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .date("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .epoch_assign("EPOCH", date_col="AESTDTC", se=se)
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Collection Models
docs.text:
Every add_*() verb requires a collection model (not a bare list). Collections enforce integrity at construction time:

Collection Checks TrialElements Unique ETCD, epoch consistency TrialArms Sequential TAETORD per arm, FK to TE (opt.) TrialVisits Unique VISITNUM, VISITDY ordering, FK to TA (opt.) TrialParameters Unique (TSPARMCD, TSSEQ) TrialCriteria Unique IETESTCD TrialDiseaseAssessments Unique TDORDER TrialMilestones Unique MIDSTYPE

docs.title: Cross-domain FK validation
docs.text:
ta = (
    pl.DataFrame()
    .sdtm.fetch_structure("TA")
    .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TA")
    .add_arms(ta_rows, te=te_rows)  # TA.ETCD ∈ TE.ETCD
    .to_frame()
)

tv = (
    pl.DataFrame()
    .sdtm.fetch_structure("TV")
    .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TV")
    .add_visits(tv_rows, ta=ta_rows)  # TV.ARMCD ∈ TA.ARMCD
    .to_frame()
)

Omit te= / ta= to skip the FK check during iterative development.

docs.title: TS: TSSEQ and dictionary-bound values
docs.text:
TrialParameter covers the full SDTMIG 3.4 variable set: TSSEQ for repeating parameters (one row per country for FCNTRY, per primary outcome for OUTMSPRI, ...) plus TSGRPID, TSVCDREF, TSVCDVER for dictionary-bound values (SNOMED, UNII, MED-RT):

TrialParameter(
    tsparmcd="INDIC",
    tsparm="Trial Disease/Condition Indication",
    tsval="Alzheimer's disease",
    tsvalcd="26929004",
    tsvcdref="SNOMED CT",
    tsvcdver="2014-03-01",
)

TrialParameters.from_ctgov("NCT00048217") seeds the registry-derivable parameters (REGID, TITLE, TPHASE, STYPE, INTMODEL, RANDOM, TBLIND, NARMS, PLANSUB, AGEMIN/AGEMAX, SEXPOP, HLTSUBJI, SSTDTC/SENDTC, SPONSOR, OUTMSPRI, FCNTRY) from the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API. It is a starting point — dictionary-bound parameters are deliberately not guessed.

The same flow from the CLI — print the parameters: YAML block, or merge it directly into the study's trial_design.yaml (new TSPARMCD/TSSEQ rows only, existing entries untouched), then rebuild:

uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705           # print the parameters: YAML
uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705 --write   # merge into trial_design.yaml
uv run fleet tdd build                       # → ts.parquet in <sdtm_data>/

docs.title: Epoch values
docs.text:
The Epoch enum is bound to NCI C99079 with all 14 standard values. C99079 is extensible: sponsor-defined terms are accepted as plain upper-case strings anywhere an epoch is expected:

from fleet.sdtm.tdd import Epoch, TrialElement

TrialElement(etcd="TRT", element="Treatment", epoch=Epoch.TREATMENT)
TrialElement(etcd="ESC", element="Escalation", epoch="DOSE ESCALATION")  # sponsor term

Note: TrialElement.epoch is a design-time attribute — it drives the element→epoch mapping when deriving TA and SE, but is not written to the TE dataset (SDTMIG 3.4 has no EPOCH variable in TE).

docs.title: Mermaid parser
docs.text:
Parse a Mermaid flowchart directly into a design (or use the lower-level parse_trial_design() for raw TE/TA collections):

design = fleet.StudyDesign.from_mermaid(
    """
    flowchart TD
    subgraph SCR[SCREENING]
        SCRN["Screening<br/>P14D"]
    end
    subgraph TRT[TREATMENT]
        DRUG["Drug Treatment<br/>P84D"]
