        PBO["Placebo<br/>P84D"]
    end
    SCRN -->|DRUG_ARM| DRUG
    SCRN -->|PBO_ARM| PBO
""",
    study_id="CDISCPILOT01",
)

print(design.to_mermaid())  # and back out — protocol-vs-datasets QC

docs.title: Validation with CORE (CDISC Rules Engine)
docs.text: Fleet's conformance validation is built on CORE — the open-source CDISC Rules Engine, the official executable implementation of CDISC's conformance rules. Fleet manages the engine lifecycle (download, discovery, health check) and wraps execution behind one CLI command and one namespace verb, so validation runs with the same rules a regulator's reviewer tooling references.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
uv run fleet install-engine     # downloads the CORE binary to ~/.fleet
uv run fleet doctor             # confirms engine + extras are healthy

fleet install-engine installs CORE 0.15.0 (GitHub tag v0.15), the version that Fleet is tested with. --version latest installs the newest CORE release, but Fleet prints a warning, because that version is not tested with Fleet. Newer releases can fail on data that 0.15.0 validates.

fleet doctor prints the engine that validation will use, where it came from, and its version. It takes them from the same run setup as the verb and fleet validate.

Teams can pin a shared engine instead via validation.engine_path in study_config.yaml. Inside a study, validation.engine_path beats the FLEET_RULES_ENGINE environment variable, so that every programmer runs the same engine build. Outside a study, FLEET_RULES_ENGINE still applies.

docs.title: Engine version
docs.text:
Every report header prints the engine version, so a QC programmer can check that two runs used the same rule build. Fleet takes the version from the first source that gives it:

  1. the engine's own core version command (0.15.0),
  2. the fleet-release-tag.txt file that fleet install-engine writes next to the managed binary (tag v0.15, printed as 0.15),
  3. else unknown.

docs.title: Running validation
docs.text:
Everything resolves from the discovered study_config.yaml:

uv run fleet validate                          # all datasets in <sdtm_data> and <adam_data>
uv run fleet validate data/sdtm/ae.parquet     # one dataset
uv run fleet validate --report findings.html   # HTML findings report
  • Sweep: the engine runs once for all SDTM datasets and once for all ADaM datasets, so rules that span several datasets of one standard can execute. The report shows one result per dataset.
  • Standard detection: a dataset in the configured sdtm_data or adam_data directory takes the standard of that directory. For any other path, AD* datasets validate as ADaM and everything else as SDTM. --standard overrides both.
  • IG versions come from the config's sdtm.ig_version / adam.ig_version (--version overrides).
  • Custom rules load automatically from validation.custom_rules (--custom-rules overrides). They run in a second engine run next to the official rules, so a sweep of both standards with custom rules makes four engine runs. See Custom Validation Rules.
  • The report header of each dataset shows every input with its source, as on the verb.
  • HTML report: --report findings.html writes one page: a status row per dataset, then one row per finding and per dataset that could not run. ValidationResult.save_html_report() writes the same page for one dataset. Every cell is HTML-escaped.
  • Could not run: a dataset whose directory and file name disagree (data/sdtm/adsl.parquet), or an unsupported IG version, is not validated. The reason is printed, and the other datasets still run. An engine that crashes, writes no report, or does not finish within the timeout also gives "could not run", not a data failure.
  • Timeout: --timeout SECONDS, else validation.timeout in the study config, else 300 s. On timeout Fleet stops the engine and its workers.
  • Every finding blocks (ADR-0017). CORE gives no severity, so Fleet does not invent one. A finding stops blocking only when validation.accepted lists its rule and dataset with a reason, as an SDRG explanation does:
validation:
  accepted:
    - rule: CORE-000767
      dataset: AE
      reason: No FA domain in this study; see SDRG section 4.2.
  • Status words: PASS (at least one rule executed, no finding), FINDINGS (n) (every finding accepted), NOT ASSESSED (no rule executed), FAIL (a finding blocks), COULD NOT RUN. Study-level findings (dataset STUDY) get their own block in a sweep. In a single-dataset run (the verb, the MCP tool) they are information only, because one dataset cannot show what the study lacks.
  • Exit codes: 0 nothing blocks, 1 a finding blocks, 2 a dataset could not run. So fleet validate drops straight into CI. The last line counts each status and the findings.
  • Engine version: fleet install-engine installs the newest tested CORE release. The report header and fleet doctor name a version Fleet is not tested with. A weekly CI job runs Fleet on the newest CORE release.

docs.title: The CI gate: fleet check
docs.text:
fleet check builds the same run setup for SDTM and ADaM, with no datasets. It catches a setup error before delivery, without an engine:

  • sdtm.ig_version: 3-5, or any IG version not in the supported list, fails the gate.
  • A validation.custom_rules directory that does not exist fails the gate.
  • A codelists.py that disagrees with ct.package, ct.adam_package or the define.yaml files fails the gate; each row names the fix command. See controlled terminology in the spec path.
  • No engine found is a warning only, because CI installs no engine.

docs.title: The MCP tool
docs.text:
fleet_validate(dataset_path, standard=None, version=None, custom_rules=None) builds the same run setup. It looks for study_config.yaml from the directory of the dataset, not from the working directory of the server. A refused setup returns {"outcome": "could not run", "reason": ...} and does not raise. See IDE tooling.

The same run from Python, chainable at the end of a pipeline:

result = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    # ... derivations ...
    .validate("AE")  # runs CORE on the materialised frame
)

docs.title: Where the verb takes its inputs
docs.text:
The verb builds a run setup before the engine starts. Each input comes from the first source that gives it:

Input Argument Study config Environment Default Standard (none) (none) (none) the namespace: .sdtm or .adam IG version version= sdtm.ig_version / adam.ig_version (none) SDTMIG 3.4, ADaMIG 1.3 Custom rules custom_rules= validation.custom_rules (none) none Engine rules_engine_path= validation.engine_path FLEET_RULES_ENGINE managed install

The verb looks for study_config.yaml from the working directory, then each parent. version= accepts "3-4" and "3.4". The supported versions are SDTMIG 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 and ADaMIG 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3.

The report header prints each input with its source and the study config used:

Standard:     SDTMIG (namespace)
IG version:   3.3 (study config)
Custom rules: /study/metadata/custom_rules (study config)
Engine:       /study/tools/core/core (study config)
CORE version: 0.15.0
Study config: /study/study_config.yaml

docs.title: Could not run
docs.text:
Some setups are refused before the engine starts. The verb then raises ValidationSetupError in every on_fail mode, because no rule ran:

  • the dataset name belongs to the other standard: adae.adam.validate("AE") or ae.sdtm.validate("ADAE"),
  • the IG version is not supported, for example SDTMIG 3.1.3,
  • the custom rules directory does not exist.

docs.title: Which rules actually exist upstream
docs.text:
CORE executes the rule sets CDISC has published to its Library. As of mid-2026 that means:

Standard Published executable rules SDTMIG 3.2 / 3.3 / 3.4 ✅ full SD-series rule sets SENDIG 3.0 / 3.1 / 3.1.1 (+DART, GENETOX, AR) ✅ FDA Business Rules ✅ (SDTM/SEND-oriented) TIG 1.0 (incl. its ADaM substandard) ✅ USDM ✅ ADaMIG 1.0–1.3 ⚠️ selection plumbing exists (engine ≥ v0.13.0), but no executable ADaMIG rule set is published yet — ADaM Conformance Rules v5.0 remains a document, not machine rules

Practical consequence: an ADaM fleet validate run today executes your custom rules (plus any TIG-ADaM rules you opt into), while SDTM runs get the full official battery. Fleet tracks the upstream catalog — when CDISC publishes executable ADaMIG rules, the same command picks them up through the engine's standard/version selection with no Fleet change.

docs.title: Where CORE sits in Fleet's validation stack
docs.text:
Validation is layered — each layer fires at a different moment and catches a different error class:

Layer When What it catches Spec registry models from_spec() load time unknown algorithms, misspelled/missing derivation fields fleet check on demand / CI gate Define-XML generation in strict mode (schema, codelists, method text, Length, SignificantDigits), run setup (IG versions, custom rules directory) Trial-design audit (fleet tdd audit) on demand, offline P21-style SD-series + FDA TS profile for TDD domains CORE (fleet validate) after datasets materialise official CDISC conformance rules against the data itself

See Custom Validation Rules for extending CORE with sponsor-, study-, or TCG-specific checks — they run next to the official rules, report in the same format with their source, and live in version control next to the study.

docs.text:
Interactive Playground — Click the badge above to launch this notebook in Google Colab and experiment with Fleet live, no local setup needed.

This notebook demonstrates building clinical datasets entirely in Python code. It is best suited for quick ad-hoc analysis, smaller studies, or initial data discovery.

docs.title: 1. Derive SDTM¶
docs.text: We use the .sdtm namespace to standardize the raw inputs.

docs.title: 2. Derive ADaM¶
docs.text: We use the .adam namespace. Notice how easily we define a custom derivation to flag subjects who are older than 40.

docs.title: Spec-Driven Pipeline with Code Extensions¶
docs.text:
Interactive Playground — Click the badge above to launch this notebook in Google Colab and experiment with Fleet live, no local setup needed.

This notebook demonstrates the standard workflow for Fleet in a production environment: Spec-First.

  1. You define as much as possible in define.yaml.
  2. Fleet automatically executes it.
  3. You write a thin layer of Python code for complex custom rules.

docs.title: Extending the Built Data¶
docs.text: Suppose define.yaml generated our base ADSL pipeline, but we have a completely proprietary calculation that the specification does not natively handle via its algorithms. We simply extend the resulting dataframe!

docs.title: ADTTE: Time-to-Event in One Chain
docs.text: A time-to-event parameter answers one question per subject: how long until X happened — and if it never did, how long did we watch? This walkthrough builds a two-parameter ADTTE (overall survival + time to first adverse event) in a single chain, shows why every subject got their row, and hands the result straight to a Kaplan-Meier fit. Every output below is real.

docs.title: The model in 30 seconds
docs.text:
• An EventSource says: in this dataset, these rows, this date column — if selected, the clock stops here with CNSR = 0.
  • A CensorSource says the same for censoring (CNSR ≥ 1).
  • .param() plays referee per parameter: pool the events, the earliest wins; no event → the latest censor. STARTDT comes from the pinned ADSL; dates before it are floored to it.
  • .aval() turns ADT − STARTDT into AVAL (+AVALU) afterwards.

Datasets attach by nickname through the pin system — a source saying dataset="ADAE" reads whatever you pinned as ADAE.

Choosing the time origin (start_date=)

TRTSDT (ADaMIG: Date of First Exposure to Treatment) is the conventional origin for safety endpoints like time to first AE. For ITT efficacy endpoints in randomized trials — overall survival in particular — use the randomization date (RANDDT): ITT time starts at randomization, not at first dose. start_date= accepts any ADSL date column, so pick per parameter.

docs.title: 1. Input data
docs.text:
from datetime import date

import polars as pl
import fleet
from fleet.adam.tte import AE_EVENT, CensorSource, DEATH_EVENT, LASTALIVE_CENSOR

adsl = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "USUBJID": ["01", "02", "03"],
        "TRT01P": ["Drug A", "Placebo", "Drug A"],
        "TRTSDT": [date(2023, 1, 1), date(2023, 1, 2), date(2023, 1, 3)],
        "DTHFL": ["Y", None, None],
        "DTHDT": [date(2023, 3, 1), None, None],
        "LSTALVDT": [date(2023, 3, 1), date(2023, 6, 30), None],
        "EOSDT": [date(2023, 3, 1), date(2023, 6, 30), date(2023, 2, 1)],
    }
)
adae = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "USUBJID": ["01", "01", "02"],
        "TRTEMFL": ["Y", "Y", "Y"],
        "ASTDT": [date(2023, 1, 20), date(2023, 1, 10), date(2023, 2, 5)],
        "AESEQ": [2, 1, 1],
    }
)

Note the traps this tiny study contains: subject 01 has an earlier and a later AE (tie-break needed), subject 03 has no death, no last-alive date, and no AE (the classic silently-dropped subject), and dates must be typed Date — a DTC string column is rejected with instructions to .date() it first.

docs.title: 2. Sources — typed, reusable, and inspectable
docs.text:
DEATH_EVENT, LASTALIVE_CENSOR, and AE_EVENT ship with Fleet (the full prebuilt registry: prebuilt_sources_frame()). Custom ones are one constructor call — and unlike admiral's opaque source objects, every source renders as a DataFrame:

from fleet.adam.tte import sources_frame

EOS = CensorSource(dataset="ADSL", date="EOSDT", set={"EVNTDESC": "END OF STUDY"})
print(sources_frame(DEATH_EVENT, LASTALIVE_CENSOR, AE_EVENT))

┌────────┬─────────┬──────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────┬────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ kind   ┆ dataset ┆ date     ┆ where                    ┆ order ┆ censor ┆ set                      │
╞════════╪═════════╪══════════╪══════════════════════════╪═══════╪════════╪══════════════════════════╡
│ event  ┆ ADSL    ┆ DTHDT    ┆ pl.col("DTHFL") == "Y"   ┆ null  ┆ null   ┆ EVNTDESC='DEATH'         │
│ censor ┆ ADSL    ┆ LSTALVDT ┆ null                     ┆ null  ┆ 1      ┆ EVNTDESC='ALIVE'         │
│ event  ┆ ADAE    ┆ ASTDT    ┆ pl.col("TRTEMFL") == "Y" ┆ AESEQ ┆ null   ┆ EVNTDESC='ADVERSE EVENT' │
└────────┴─────────┴──────────┴──────────────────────────┴───────┴────────┴──────────────────────────┘

In set=, strings are literals (EVNTDESC="DEATH" is never a column lookup); reference source columns with a pl.Expr. SRCDOM/SRCVAR/ SRCSEQ are stamped automatically from the source's own declaration.

docs.title: 3. Derive both parameters in one chain
docs.text:
adtte_ns = (
    adsl.adam.tte.pin("ADSL", adsl)
    .pin("ADAE", adae)
    .param(
        "OS",
        "Overall Survival",
        start_date="TRTSDT",
        events=[DEATH_EVENT],
        censors=[LASTALIVE_CENSOR],
        retain="censor_at_start",
    )  # keep subject 03, censored at STARTDT
    .param(
        "TTAE",
        "Time to First Adverse Event",
        start_date="TRTSDT",
        events=[AE_EVENT],
        censors=[EOS],
        explain=True,
    )  # ← prints the decision trace below
    .aval(unit="days")  # AVAL = ADT − STARTDT + 1, AVALU stamped
    .seq("ASEQ", order_by=["PARAMCD"])
)
adtte = adtte_ns.to_frame()

┌─────────┬─────────┬─────────────────────────────┬────────────┬────────────┬──────┬───────────────────┬────────┬──────────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬──────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ PARAMCD ┆ PARAM                       ┆ STARTDT    ┆ ADT        ┆ CNSR ┆ EVNTDESC          ┆ SRCDOM ┆ SRCVAR   ┆ SRCSEQ ┆ AVAL  ┆ AVALU ┆ ASEQ │
╞═════════╪═════════╪═════════════════════════════╪════════════╪════════════╪══════╪═══════════════════╪════════╪══════════╪════════╪═══════╪═══════╪══════╡
│ 01      ┆ OS      ┆ Overall Survival            ┆ 2023-01-01 ┆ 2023-03-01 ┆ 0    ┆ DEATH             ┆ ADSL   ┆ DTHDT    ┆ null   ┆ 60.0  ┆ DAYS  ┆ 1    │
│ 02      ┆ OS      ┆ Overall Survival            ┆ 2023-01-02 ┆ 2023-06-30 ┆ 1    ┆ ALIVE             ┆ ADSL   ┆ LSTALVDT ┆ null   ┆ 180.0 ┆ DAYS  ┆ 1    │
│ 03      ┆ OS      ┆ Overall Survival            ┆ 2023-01-03 ┆ 2023-01-03 ┆ 1    ┆ NO EVENT OBSERVED ┆ ADSL   ┆ TRTSDT   ┆ null   ┆ 1.0   ┆ DAYS  ┆ 1    │
│ 01      ┆ TTAE    ┆ Time to First Adverse Event ┆ 2023-01-01 ┆ 2023-01-10 ┆ 0    ┆ ADVERSE EVENT     ┆ ADAE   ┆ ASTDT    ┆ 1      ┆ 10.0  ┆ DAYS  ┆ 2    │
│ 02      ┆ TTAE    ┆ Time to First Adverse Event ┆ 2023-01-02 ┆ 2023-02-05 ┆ 0    ┆ ADVERSE EVENT     ┆ ADAE   ┆ ASTDT    ┆ 1      ┆ 35.0  ┆ DAYS  ┆ 2    │
│ 03      ┆ TTAE    ┆ Time to First Adverse Event ┆ 2023-01-03 ┆ 2023-02-01 ┆ 1    ┆ END OF STUDY      ┆ ADSL   ┆ EOSDT    ┆ null   ┆ 30.0  ┆ DAYS  ┆ 2    │
└─────────┴─────────┴─────────────────────────────┴────────────┴────────────┴──────┴───────────────────┴────────┴──────────┴────────┴───────┴───────┴──────┘

Worth noticing:

  • Subject 01's TTAE picked the earlier AE, with order=["AESEQ"] breaking same-date ties deterministically (SRCSEQ = 1).
  • Subject 03 survived the OS derivation thanks to retain="censor_at_start" — without it Fleet warns with a count instead of silently dropping, admiral-style.
  • SRCDOM/SRCVAR are filled in without anyone typing them.
  • AVALU is stamped by .aval() — unit="months"/"years" use the CDISC conversions (30.4375 / 365.25).

docs.title: 4. Why did subject 03 get censored? — the decision trace
docs.text:
explain=True prints every candidate per subject with the winner and the reason (the inspectability admiral's quosure objects can't offer):

TTE decision trace — TTAE (Time to First Adverse Event):
┌─────────┬────────┬────────┬────────────┬──────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ kind   ┆ SRCDOM ┆ date       ┆ selected ┆ reason                   │
╞═════════╪════════╪════════╪════════════╪══════════╪══════════════════════════╡
│ 01      ┆ event  ┆ ADAE   ┆ 2023-01-10 ┆ true     ┆ earliest event           │
│ 02      ┆ event  ┆ ADAE   ┆ 2023-02-05 ┆ true     ┆ earliest event           │
│ 01      ┆ censor ┆ ADSL   ┆ 2023-03-01 ┆ false    ┆ not selected             │
│ 02      ┆ censor ┆ ADSL   ┆ 2023-06-30 ┆ false    ┆ not selected             │
│ 03      ┆ censor ┆ ADSL   ┆ 2023-02-01 ┆ true     ┆ latest censor (no event) │
└─────────┴────────┴────────┴────────────┴──────────┴──────────────────────────┘

Typos never make it this far: a source naming DTHDTT fails at declaration with Did you mean 'DTHDT'?, before a single row is computed.

docs.title: 5. Straight into a survival fit
docs.text:
km_data() returns exactly what lifelines / scikit-survival consume — and group columns you ask for resolve from the pinned ADSL automatically:

km = adtte_ns.km_data("OS", by=["TRT01P"])

┌─────────┬──────────┬───────┬─────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ duration ┆ event ┆ TRT01P  │
╞═════════╪══════════╪═══════╪═════════╡
│ 01      ┆ 60.0     ┆ true  ┆ Drug A  │
│ 02      ┆ 180.0    ┆ false ┆ Placebo │
│ 03      ┆ 1.0      ┆ false ┆ Drug A  │
└─────────┴──────────┴───────┴─────────┘

from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter  # optional — not a Fleet dependency

kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
for (arm,), grp in km.group_by("TRT01P"):
    kmf.fit(grp["duration"], grp["event"], label=arm)

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Window truncation (admiral 1.5 parity): end_dates=[CensorSource(...)] closes the observation window — events after it don't count, and the end source supplies its own CNSR/EVNTDESC. event_type="positive" covers favorable events (time to response): subjects without one censor at the window end.
  • Strata: by=["AEDECOD"] derives one parameter per term, with per-stratum PARAMCD built via an expression in set_values_to (a static PARAMCD across strata is rejected — the 1:1 mapping guard).
  • The full verb reference lives in the cheat sheet and the TA API page.

docs.title: End-to-End Walkthrough: Multi-Domain Pipeline
docs.text:
Interactive Playground — Click the badge above to launch a notebook in Google Colab and experiment with Fleet live, no local setup needed.

This guide walks the whole journey, in the order a study actually runs: scaffold the workspace, generate metadata and codelists, derive SDTM and ADaM, prove traceability with .trail(), validate against the CDISC Rules Engine, and generate the Define-XML with an annotated CRF. The code-only core of this flow lives in examples/full_pipeline_example.py.

docs.title: 1. Scaffold the study workspace
docs.text:
One command creates the folder tree, study_config.yaml, the IG-derived define.yaml skeletons, and the typed codelists.py (requires a CDISC Library API key in .env):

uv run fleet new STUDY01 --domains DM,VS,AE --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS
cd STUDY01

or step by step:

uv run fleet init cfg --study-id STUDY01 --company "Acme Pharma" \
  --domains DM,VS,AE --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS --root ./STUDY01
uv run fleet init define   # CDISC Library IG → metadata/*/define.yaml
uv run fleet init ct       # define.yaml codelists → metadata/sdtm/codelists.py
uv run fleet init rules    # conformance rules cache (optional)

Every Fleet command from here on discovers study_config.yaml by walking up from wherever you run it — paths below (data/sdtm, metadata/...) come from that config, not from hard-coding.

docs.title: DM (Demographics)
docs.text:
dm = (
    raw_dm.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="STUDY01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign("ARM", source="arm")
    .assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=SEX, ct_map={"Male": "M", "Female": "F"})
    .date("BRTHDTC", source="dob")
    .date("RFSTDTC", source="first_dose")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: VS (Vital Signs) — with a cross-domain pin
docs.text:
study_day() needs DM's RFSTDTC; instead of merging DM in, pin it — the reference stays beside the frame and the output stays clean:

vs = (
    raw_vs.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="STUDY01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="VS")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign(
        "VSTESTCD",
        source="test_name",
        ct=VSTESTCD,
        ct_map={"Weight": "WEIGHT", "Heart Rate": "HR"},
    )
    .assign("VSSTRESN", source="result")
    .date("VSDTC", source="date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("VSDY", date_col="VSDTC")  # resolves DM.RFSTDTC via the pin
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: AE (Adverse Events)
docs.text:
ae = (
    raw_ae.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="STUDY01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign("AEDECOD", source="ae_term")
    .date("AESTDTC", source="start_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: ADSL (Subject-Level Analysis)
docs.text:
adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl.source("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "ARM", "SEX")
    .assign("TRT01P", source="ARM")
    .date("TRTSDT", source="RFSTDTC")
    .first_date("AESTDT", from_dataset=ae, date_col="AESTDTC")  # first AE date
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: ADVS (BDS) — pin ADSL, carry columns, derive baseline
docs.text:
advs = (
    vs.adam.pin("ADSL", adsl)
    .source("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "VSTESTCD")
    .assign("PARAMCD", source="VSTESTCD")
    .assign("AVAL", source="VSSTRESN")
    .join_adsl("TRT01P", "TRTSDT")  # carry forward on the ADSL pin's key
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria='pl.col("VSDY") <= 1', by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 5. Prove traceability — .trail()
docs.text:
Drop .trail() anywhere in a chain (typically just before .to_frame()) and Fleet prints the origin of every derived variable — including cross-domain pin reads, attributed as DOMAIN.COLUMN:

advs_ns = (
    vs.adam.pin("ADSL", adsl)
    .source("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "VSTESTCD")
    .assign("AVAL", source="VSSTRESN")
    .join_adsl("TRTSDT")
    .trail()  # ← prints the table below; the pipeline continues
)

Variable trail (5 derivation(s)):
┌───┬──────────┬───────────┬───────────────────────────┬────────┐
│ # ┆ Variable ┆ Verb      ┆ Origin                    ┆ Domain │
╞═══╪══════════╪═══════════╪═══════════════════════════╪════════╡
│ 1 ┆ STUDYID  ┆ source    ┆ STUDYID                   ┆ ADVS   │
│ 2 ┆ USUBJID  ┆ source    ┆ USUBJID                   ┆ ADVS   │
│ 3 ┆ VSTESTCD ┆ source    ┆ VSTESTCD                  ┆ ADVS   │
│ 4 ┆ AVAL     ┆ assign    ┆ VSSTRESN                  ┆ ADVS   │
│ 5 ┆ TRTSDT   ┆ join_adsl ┆ ADSL.TRTSDT [carry_forward] ┆ ADVS │
└───┴──────────┴───────────┴───────────────────────────┴────────┘

This is the machine-checkable answer to "where did this number come from" — the same lineage feeds to_spec_yaml() (pipeline → define.yaml round-trip) and the Define-XML method descriptions.

docs.title: 6. Validate — are we CDISC compliant?
docs.text:
Validation is a verb — chain .validate() right where the dataset is born and the CDISC Rules Engine report prints without breaking the pipeline (fleet install-engine once, first). Revisiting the AE chain from step 3:

ae = (
    raw_ae.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="STUDY01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign("AEDECOD", source="ae_term")
    .date("AESTDTC", source="start_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
    .validate("AE")  # ← CORE report prints here; the chain continues
    .to_frame()
)

======================================================================
CDISC Validation Report: AE
======================================================================
Dataset Type: sdtmig v3.4
Status: PASS
Total Issues: 0
----------------------------------------------------------------------

For a CI pipeline, make compliance a hard gate — on_fail="raise" turns a finding that validation.accepted does not list into a ValidationError instead of a warning:

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl.source("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "ARM", "SEX")
    .assign("TRT01P", source="ARM")
    .date("TRTSDT", source="RFSTDTC")
    .validate("ADSL", on_fail="raise")  # ← a finding not accepted stops the build
    .to_frame()
)

The full ValidationResult stays retrievable via the namespace's last_validation property when you need programmatic access to findings. To sweep every written dataset at once (e.g. a nightly job), the batch equivalent is uv run fleet validate --report outputs/validation.html. (Note: official executable ADaMIG rules are not yet published by CDISC — ADaM datasets run your custom rules; see Validation with CORE.)

docs.title: 7. Define-XML with an annotated CRF
docs.text:
Declare the aCRF once (it edits metadata/sdtm/define.yaml in place — point --href at your real annotated CRF; blankcrf.pdf is the conventional placeholder name in a submission package):

uv run fleet add-acrf --href blankcrf.pdf --standard both

Tag CRF-collected variables with their page numbers in the define.yaml (origin: Collected + crf_pages: "8" — see CRF Page References), then generate:

uv run fleet define-xml --standard sdtm
uv run fleet define-xml --standard adam

Each Derived variable gets a <MethodDef> with its method text: a verifiable link between the submission metadata and the exact code above. Add --strict to refuse a define with a gap (a Derived variable with no method text, or a numeric variable with no length:).

docs.title: 8. Bonus: hand the pipeline to an orchestrator
docs.text:
The same define.yaml files describe the dependency graph — export it as an executable Snakefile or Airflow DAG (each rule/task shells out to fleet run --dataset ...):

from fleet import build_dag

dag = build_dag("metadata/sdtm/define.yaml", "metadata/adam/define.yaml", output_dir="data")
dag.to_snakefile("Snakefile")  # → snakemake -j1
dag.to_airflow_dag(dag_id="study01", path="dags/study01.py")

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: One workspace bootstrap, ~60 lines of pipeline code, and four CLI commands took us from raw EDC extracts to validated SDTM/ADaM datasets with variable-level traceability and a submission-ready Define-XML — with every path resolved from study_config.yaml, so the same flow runs unchanged in any company folder structure.

docs.title: One file. One domain. Raw to Render.
docs.text:
The Raw-to-Render (R2R) strategy collapses the traditional multi-program pharma workflow into a single, self-contained script that takes raw source data all the way to a rendered clinical table:

flowchart LR
    RAW["Raw AE CSV"] --> SDTM["SDTM AE<br/>df.sdtm"]
    SDTM --> ADAE["ADaM ADAE<br/>df.adam · df.adam.occds"]
    ADSL[("ADSL<br/>pre-built, governed")] -.-> ADAE
    ADAE --> QC["QC<br/>.compare()"]
    QC --> VAL["Validate<br/>.validate()"]
    VAL --> TLG["AE summary table<br/>df.tlg.ae → HTML"]

DM and ADSL are assumed to already exist — they are governed, shared artefacts produced by separate programs. The R2R script focuses on one domain end-to-end: raw AE data through SDTM, ADaM, QC, validation, and table rendering.

Instead of maintaining separate programs for each layer — with hand-offs, naming conventions to remember, and scattered data lineage — an R2R script keeps the complete derivation chain for a single domain visible in one place.

docs.title: The traditional model
docs.text:
In conventional clinical programming, the AE deliverable involves at least four separate programs, often written by different people. The last column is the R2R layer that replaces each:

Program Input Output Owner R2R layer ae.sas Raw AE extract SDTM AE SDTM prog. 1 — df.sdtm adae.sas SDTM AE + ADSL ADaM ADAE ADaM prog. 2 — df.adam.occds adae_qc.sas SDTM AE + ADSL PROC COMPARE listing QC prog. 3 — .compare() t_ae.sas ADAE + ADSL AE summary table TLG prog. 5 — df.tlg.ae

Each program runs independently. Context about why a particular derivation exists often lives only in the developer's head or in a Word document. When the table looks wrong, you debug backwards across four files, hoping the variable names haven't drifted.

docs.title: The R2R model
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph R2R["r2r_ae.py — one script, one review"]
        direction LR
        L1["Layer 1<br/>SDTM AE"] --> L2["Layer 2<br/>ADAE"]
        L2 --> L3["Layer 3<br/>QC compare"]
        L3 --> L4["Layer 4<br/>Validate"]
        L4 --> L5["Layer 5<br/>Render HTML"]
    end
    RAWAE["Raw AE"] --> L1
    ADSL[("ADSL<br/>pre-built input")] -.-> L2

One script. One review. When cell (3, 2) in the table looks wrong, scroll up — the derivation that produced it is in the same file.

DM and ADSL remain separate, governed programs — they are shared by many domains. The R2R script consumes ADSL as a pre-built input and owns everything else.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• Full lineage visibility — every transformation from raw value to table cell is traceable in a single scroll.
  • Faster debugging — no need to run four programs and cross-reference intermediate datasets; breakpoints anywhere in the chain.
  • Atomic reviews — a reviewer sees the complete picture; intent and implementation live together.
  • Agent-native — an AI coding agent can reason about the entire pipeline in one context window, generate it end-to-end, and fix issues without switching files.
  • Reproducible — one command (uv run python r2r_ae.py) regenerates everything from source.

docs.title: When to use R2R
docs.text:
R2R shines when:

  • You need to prototype fast — get a table on screen from raw data in minutes.
  • The domain is self-contained — AE, VS, LB, CM — where the analysis dataset depends only on its own SDTM domain plus ADSL.
  • You're working with an AI agent that benefits from seeing the full pipeline in one prompt.
  • You want a living specification — the code is the documentation of how raw data becomes a regulatory table.

docs.title: When NOT to use R2R
docs.text:
• Shared derivations — ADSL is consumed by many domains; it deserves its own program with governed outputs. The R2R script loads ADSL as an input — it does not derive it.
  • Large teams — when SDTM and ADaM are programmed by different people on different timelines, separation makes sense.
  • Validated production — regulatory submissions may require individual program-level sign-off; R2R is ideal for exploratory and rapid development before refactoring into governed programs.

docs.title: The Layers
docs.text: An R2R script is organised into clearly labelled layers. Each layer uses a different Fleet namespace:

docs.title: Layer 0 — Inputs
docs.text:
Load the pre-built ADSL and the raw AE extract:

import polars as pl
import fleet  # registers .sdtm / .adam / .tlg namespaces

# ADSL is produced by a separate governed program
adsl = pl.read_csv("outputs/cdiscpilot01/adsl_admiral.csv", try_parse_dates=True)
adsl = adsl.with_columns(pl.col("TRT01P").alias("TRTA"))

# Raw AE — the only raw data this script owns (your study's file)
ae_raw = pl.read_csv("data/raw/ae_raw.csv")

docs.title: Layer 1 — SDTM (.sdtm namespace)
docs.text:
Standardise raw columns into CDISC-compliant SDTM variables:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="CDISCPILOT01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AETERM", source="ae_term")
    .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .assign("AEENDTC", source="ae_end_date")
    .assign("AESEV", source="ae_severity")
    .assign("AESER", source="ae_serious")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Layer 2 — ADaM ADAE (.adam / .adam.occds namespaces)
docs.text:
Merge ADSL treatment dates into SDTM AE, then derive analysis dates, treatment-emergent flags, and worst-severity flags:

# Merge ADSL treatment dates & population flags into SDTM AE
_adsl_trt = adsl.select(["USUBJID", "TRTSDT", "TRTEDT", "TRT01P", "TRTA", "SAFFL"])
ae_with_trt = ae.join(_adsl_trt, on="USUBJID", how="left")

adae = (
    ae_with_trt.adam.source("STUDYID")
    .source("USUBJID")
    .source("AETERM")
    .source("TRTA")
    .source("SAFFL")
    .date("ASTDT", source="AESTDTC")
    .study_day("ADY", date_col="ASTDT", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .to_frame()
    .adam.occds.treatment_emergent(
        "TRTEMFL",
        start_date="ASTDT",
        end_date="AEENDTC",
        trtsdt="TRTSDT",
        trtedt="TRTEDT",
        end_window=0,  # the SAP decides the window after the last dose
    )
    .recode("AESEVN", source="AESEV", recode_map={"MILD": 1, "MODERATE": 2, "SEVERE": 3})
    .flag(
        "ANL01FL",
        criteria="max",
        value_col="AESEVN",
        by=["USUBJID", "AETERM"],
    )
    .seq("ASEQ", by=["USUBJID"])
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Layer 3 — QC (.compare())
docs.text:
This is adae_qc.sas. A second programmer re-derives the analysis variables from the same SDTM AE and ADSL inputs — in plain Polars expressions rather than the first-class verbs the production chain used — and ends the chain in .compare(), Fleet's PROC COMPARE. The chain is the candidate, the production ADAE is the base, and on_fail="raise" turns a difference into a stopped script:

adae_qc = (
    ae_with_trt.adam.occds("ADAE")
    .derivation("ASTDT", expression=pl.col("AESTDTC").str.to_date(strict=False))
    .derivation(
        "TRTEMFL",
        expression=pl.when(
            pl.col("AESTDTC")
            .str.to_date(strict=False)
            .is_between(
                pl.col("TRTSDT").str.to_date(strict=False),
                pl.col("TRTEDT").str.to_date(strict=False),
            )
        ).then(pl.lit("Y")),
    )
    # ... AENDT, ADY, ANL01FL, ASEQ, AEDECOD and AEBODSYS likewise
    .compare(
        adae,
        keys=["USUBJID", "AESEQ"],
        variables=["ASTDT", "AENDT", "ADY", "TRTEMFL", "ANL01FL", "ASEQ", "AEDECOD", "AEBODSYS"],
        base_name="ADAE (production)",
        candidate_name="ADAE (QC)",
        on_fail="raise",
    )
    .to_frame()
)

variables= states the QC scope, so production's imputation-flag by-products are neither compared nor reported as missing. The report is printed and kept on the namespace as last_comparison:

Comparison report: ADAE (production) vs ADAE (QC)
======================================================================

Data set summary
----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Base:      ADAE (production)  (5 observations, 37 variables)
  Candidate: ADAE (QC)  (5 observations, 34 variables)
  Keys:      USUBJID, AESEQ
  Variables: ASTDT, AENDT, ADY, TRTEMFL, ANL01FL, ASEQ, AEDECOD, AEBODSYS  (restricted)
  Settings:  exact

Verdict
----------------------------------------------------------------------
  EQUAL: no differences found.

docs.title: Layer 4 — Validate
docs.text:
Call .validate() directly in the pipeline chain — it prints the conformance report and returns the namespace unchanged so derivations can continue:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="CDISCPILOT01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AETERM", source="ae_term")
    .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .assign("AEENDTC", source="ae_end_date")
    .assign("AESEV", source="ae_severity")
    .assign("AESER", source="ae_serious")
    .validate("AE")  # ← prints report, chain continues
    .to_frame()
)

adae = (
    ae_with_trt.adam.source("STUDYID")
    .source("USUBJID")
    .source("AETERM")
    .source("TRTA")
    .source("SAFFL")
    .date("ASTDT", source="AESTDTC")
    .study_day("ADY", date_col="ASTDT", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .to_frame()
    .adam.occds.treatment_emergent(
        "TRTEMFL",
        start_date="ASTDT",
        end_date="AEENDTC",
        trtsdt="TRTSDT",
        trtedt="TRTEDT",
        end_window=0,
    )
    .recode("AESEVN", source="AESEV", recode_map={"MILD": 1, "MODERATE": 2, "SEVERE": 3})
    .flag(
        "ANL01FL",
        criteria="max",
        value_col="AESEVN",
        by=["USUBJID", "AETERM"],
    )
    .seq("ASEQ", by=["USUBJID"])
    .validate("ADAE")  # ← prints report, chain continues
    .to_frame()
)

The report printed to stdout makes conformance issues immediately visible:

======================================================================
CDISC Validation Report: AE
======================================================================
Dataset Type: sdtmig v3.4
Status: FAIL
Rules executed: 93
Total Issues: 2
  Errors: 2, Warnings (accepted): 0, Info: 0
----------------------------------------------------------------------

ERRORS (2 unique, 2 total):

1. [CORE-000355] (official) At least one required variable is missing from dataset
   Variable: AESEQ

2. [CORE-000328] (official) The Study Day of Start of Observation (AESTDY) is not present in the dataset when Start Date/Time of Observation (AESTDTC) is present

======================================================================

======================================================================
CDISC Validation Report: ADAE
======================================================================
Dataset Type: adamig v1.3
Status: PASS
Total Issues: 0
  Errors: 0, Warnings (accepted): 0, Info: 0
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  No issues found.

======================================================================

Every CORE finding blocks until the study config accepts it with a reason (validation.accepted, ADR-0017). An accepted finding gives Status: FINDINGS (1) and shows its reason.

docs.title: Layer 4b — Trace an issue back to its verb
docs.text:
.validate() cross-links each finding to the chain's own variable lineage, so the report says not just what failed but which verb produced it. Nothing extra to call — .trail() shows the same lineage on demand:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="CDISCPILOT01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AETERM", source="ae_term")
    .trail()  # ← the lineage .validate() reads from
    .validate("AE")
    .to_frame()
)

The join is name-exact: ValidationIssue.variable is matched against VariableNode.name, so an issue only gains a Producing verb when the chain derived that same column. A finding on AETERM carries its origin — the verb name plus the dotted path to its implementation:

2. [SDTM.AE.R0004] AETERM must not be empty
   Variable: AETERM
   Rows affected: 7 (1 occurrences)
   Producing verb: assign (fleet.core._verb_mixin.SharedVerbsMixin.assign)

AEBODSYS above stays bare: nothing in the chain derives it, so there is no lineage node to match.

docs.title: Layer 5 — Render (.tlg.ae namespace)
docs.text:
Compute the Analysis Results Dataset and render to HTML:

from fleet.tlg import (
    AESummarySpec,
    Row,
    Statistic,
    RenderMetadata,
    ard_to_table_model,
    render_html,
)

spec = AESummarySpec(
    rows=[
        Row(field="AEBODSYS", label="System Organ Class"),
        Row(field="AEDECOD", label="Preferred Term"),
    ],
    statistics=[Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT],
)

ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)

meta = RenderMetadata(
    title="Table 14.3.1.1",
    subtitle="AE Summary by SOC and PT",
    footnotes=["Source: ADAE", "Population: Safety"],
)
html = render_html(ard_to_table_model(ard, meta))
Path("outputs/ae_r2r.html").write_text(html)

docs.title: R2R and Agentic Coding
docs.text:
R2R was designed for a reviewable human workflow — one file, one reading order, one visible output. AI agents happen to need exactly the same things, which is why they do well with it:

  1. Single-context reasoning — The entire derivation fits in one file (and one prompt). An agent doesn't need to discover dependencies across a file tree.

  2. End-to-end generation — Given a raw dataset schema and a target table shell, an agent can generate a complete R2R script in one pass — no multi-turn orchestration.

  3. Instant feedback — The script produces a visible output (HTML table). The agent (or user) can inspect the result and iterate without leaving the file.

  4. Self-documenting — The layered structure doubles as executable documentation. An agent reading the file can explain every derivation decision from raw to table.

  5. Deterministic re-execution — One uv run python r2r_ae.py reproduces the full artefact. No DAG scheduler, no Makefile, no external state.

docs.title: Agent prompt pattern
docs.text:
"Using Fleet's R2R pattern, write a single Python script that takes ae_raw.csv and a pre-built ADSL (adsl_admiral.csv) and produces an HTML AE summary table (Table 14.3.1.1). Include SDTM AE, ADAE with treatment-emergent flags, pre-validation, and a rendered HTML output."

The agent returns a complete, runnable script — no follow-up questions needed.

docs.title: Running the Example
docs.text:
The full working example is at examples/r2r_ae_example.py:

uv run python examples/r2r_ae_example.py

Output:

━━ Layer 0 · Inputs ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ADSL (pre-built) : 5 subjects × 33 variables
  ae_raw           :   5 rows × 9 cols

━━ Layer 1 · SDTM AE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  AE : 5 records × 21 variables

━━ Layer 2 · ADaM ADAE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ADAE : 5 records × 37 variables

━━ Layer 3 · QC ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  EQUAL: no differences found.

━━ Layer 4 · Validate ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ✓ TLG pre-validation passed

━━ Layer 5 · Render ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ARD: 155 rows × 15 cols → ae_r2r.html

━━ R2R Complete ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ADaM → QC        : 8 variables compared → EQUAL
  One file. One domain. Raw to Render.

docs.title: Trial Design, Fully Offline
docs.text: Trial Design is the one corner of a study you can build before any data exists — and in Fleet it needs no API key either: SDTMIG 3.4 structures for all nine TDD domains ship with the package. This walkthrough goes from a design definition to audited, submission-shaped datasets in five steps. The runnable script is examples/tdd_example.py.

docs.title: 1. Define the design once
docs.text:
Arms are element paths — TAETORD, ELEMENT, EPOCH, and TABRANCH (at the randomization branch) are derived, never typed by hand:

import fleet
from fleet.sdtm.tdd import TrialVisits

design = fleet.StudyDesign(
    study_id="MYSTUDY01",
    elements=[
        {
            "etcd": "SCRN",
            "element": "Screening",
            "tedur": "P14D",
            "epoch": "SCREENING",
            "testrl": "INFORMED CONSENT",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "TRTA",
            "element": "Drug A Treatment",
            "tedur": "P84D",
            "epoch": "TREATMENT",
            "testrl": "RANDOMIZATION",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "TRTB",
            "element": "Drug B Treatment",
            "tedur": "P84D",
            "epoch": "TREATMENT",
            "testrl": "RANDOMIZATION",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "FU",
            "element": "Follow-up",
            "tedur": "P28D",
            "epoch": "FOLLOW-UP",
            "testrl": "END OF TREATMENT + 1",
        },
    ],
    arms={"DRGA": ["SCRN", "TRTA", "FU"], "DRGB": ["SCRN", "TRTB", "FU"]},
    arm_names={"DRGA": "Drug A", "DRGB": "Drug B"},
    visits=TrialVisits.from_schedule(
        [("Screening", -14), ("Baseline", 0), ("Week 4", 28), ("Week 8", 56)],
        anchor="RANDOMIZATION",
        window=3,
    ).visits,
)

docs.title: 3. Audit before anyone else does
docs.text:
design.audit() runs the P21-style conformance battery offline — findings carry the public rule IDs, and a missing FDA-required TS parameter is flagged before a validator ever sees the data:

findings = design.audit()
print(findings.head(3))

┌─────────┬──────────┬────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ rule_id ┆ severity ┆ domain ┆ message                                        │
╞═════════╪══════════╪════════╪════════════════════════════════════════════════╡
│ SD2213  ┆ error    ┆ TS     ┆ Required TS parameter 'TITLE' is missing       │
│ SD2214  ┆ error    ┆ TS     ┆ Required TS parameter 'TPHASE' is missing      │
│ SD2232  ┆ error    ┆ TS     ┆ Required TS parameter 'SSTDTC' is missing      │
│         ┆          ┆        ┆ (FDA rejection criterion 1734)                 │
└─────────┴──────────┴────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 4. Fill TS from ClinicalTrials.gov
docs.text:
The registry already knows most of the FDA-required TS parameters — seed them straight from the study's NCT registration:

uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705 --write   # merge into trial_design.yaml

28 parameter(s) from NCT04280705 merged into metadata/sdtm/trial_design.yaml (2 already present).

docs.title: 5. Build (and re-audit) from the CLI
docs.text:
Persist the design as YAML next to your study metadata, then let the CLI do the rest — inside a study workspace, spec and output paths resolve from study_config.yaml:

design.to_yaml("metadata/sdtm/trial_design.yaml")

uv run fleet tdd audit                # conformance pre-check, exit 1 on errors
uv run fleet tdd build --format xpt   # audit + write te/ta/tv/ts/... to <sdtm_data>

docs.title: Bonus: the design is a diagram
docs.text:
to_mermaid() renders the arm/element/epoch structure for protocol review decks — and StudyDesign.from_mermaid() parses it back, so the diagram and the datasets can never drift:

print(design.to_mermaid())

flowchart TD
    subgraph EP0[SCREENING]
        SCRN["Screening<br/>P14D"]
    end
    subgraph EP1[TREATMENT]
        TRTA["Drug A Treatment<br/>P84D"]
        TRTB["Drug B Treatment<br/>P84D"]
    end
    subgraph EP2[FOLLOW-UP]
        FU["Follow-up<br/>P28D"]
    end
    SCRN -->|DRGA| TRTA
    TRTA --> FU
    SCRN -->|DRGB| TRTB
    TRTB --> FU

USDM imports (StudyDesign.from_usdm()), the subject-level SV/SE verbs, and the full rule table are covered in the Trial Design concepts page.

docs.title: TLG from a Spec
docs.text: One YAML file defines a clinical table; the same file drives the batch render, the interactive explorer, and the QC trail. This walkthrough takes the shipped aet01 (Overview of Adverse Events) spec from definition to rendered outputs.

docs.title: 1. The spec is the table
docs.text:
examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml, abbreviated — every knob is a plain spec field:

template: aet01                # resolves spec class + df.tlg.ae method
schema_version: 1

adsl_filter: 'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"'   # safety population (N and n)

header_rows:
  - label: Subjects with at least one adverse event
  - label: Subjects with at least one serious adverse event
    filter: 'pl.col("AESER") == "Y"'
  - label: Subjects with at least one adverse event leading to discontinuation
    filter: 'pl.col("AEACN") == "DRUG WITHDRAWN"'

statistics: [n_subjects, n_pct]

Discover the available templates and their spec schemas from the registry:

uv run fleet tlg list                 # every registered template
uv run fleet tlg schema aet01         # the spec's JSON Schema (editor validation)

docs.title: 2. Batch render
docs.text:
Inside a study workspace the datasets and output directory resolve from study_config.yaml — ADAE and ADSL are found by name in the configured adam_data directory and the table lands in the outputs directory:

uv run fleet tlg run examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml --format html

aet01.yaml → outputs/aet01.html  (aet01, table, 9 rows)

Outside a study (or to override), pass paths explicitly:

uv run fleet tlg run examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml \
  --data ADAE=adae.parquet --adsl adsl.parquet \
  -o out/ --format rtf --rows-per-page 40

--format selects the display format — html, rtf, pdf, or pptx (PDF/PPTX need the tlg-pdf / tlg-pptx extras).

docs.title: 3. The same spec, interactive
docs.text:
Declare degrees of freedom in an interactive: block (population presets, dataset filters, statistics variants) and render one self-contained HTML explorer — no server, every variant pre-computed by the same engine:

uv run fleet tlg explore examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml

The batch output is byte-identical to the explorer's default variant, so there is no second implementation to drift — see Interactive Explorer.

docs.title: 4. The same spec, from Python
docs.text:
import polars as pl
import fleet.tlg as tlg

adae = pl.read_parquet("data/adam/adae.parquet")
adsl = pl.read_parquet("data/adam/adsl.parquet")

spec = tlg.load_spec("examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml")
ard = tlg.run_spec(spec, adae, adsl=adsl)  # Analysis Results Dataset

The ARD is a long-format Polars DataFrame holding every computed statistic — rendering (HTML/RTF/PDF/PPTX) is a separate, display-only step, so QC compares numbers, not formatting. For ad-hoc summaries without a spec file, fleet tlg export --domain ae --format pdf renders a domain's t_summary directly from the configured datasets.

docs.title: Where to go next

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
Fleet ships the fleet command-line tool for bootstrapping studies, executing derivation pipelines, validating datasets, generating Define-XML, managing CDISC Controlled Terminology, and rendering TLGs. Commands that query the CDISC Library require a valid CDISC_API_KEY — set it in a .env file at your project root or as an environment variable.

.env
CDISC_API_KEY=your-api-key-here

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Config discovery — every command that needs study_config.yaml finds it git-style: the current directory first, then each parent. Pass --config <path> to override.
  • Exit codes — 0 success, 1 on a Fleet error (a single clean message on stderr), 2 on a usage error (missing/unknown command or flag). fleet compare turns its verdict into the exit code: 0 equal, 1 different, 2 the comparison could not run.
  • Errors go to stderr; results go to stdout.
  • fleet --version prints the installed version.

Run fleet <command> --help for the authoritative, always-current usage.

docs.title: Command inventory
docs.text: Command What it does fleet init Bootstrapping pipeline: cfg → define → ct → rules. fleet run Execute define.yaml derivation pipelines and write datasets. fleet validate Validate datasets with the CDISC Rules Engine, one engine run per standard. Every finding blocks unless validation.accepted lists it (exit 0 nothing blocks, 1 a finding blocks, 2 a dataset could not run). fleet check CI gate: config parse + define.yaml schema + codelists.py + run setup + custom-rule YAMLs. fleet compare Compare a candidate dataset against a base on keys (exit 0 equal, 1 different, 2 could not run). fleet new Bootstrap a study: init cfg → define → ct → rules, one confirmation. fleet migrate Rewrite removed pre-alpha verb/kwarg spellings to canonical ones (libcst). fleet tdd Trial design workflow: build/audit TDD datasets from trial_design.yaml. fleet tlg TLG workflow: list templates, run/explore YAML specs, export summaries. fleet define-xml Generate Define-XML 2.1 from a define.yaml specification. fleet add-acrf Declare the annotated CRF document (study.documents block) in define.yaml. fleet add-ct Add domains to an existing codelists.py (preserves existing). fleet add-rule Scaffold a new custom validation rule YAML. fleet check-rule Validate a custom rule YAML (syntax, structure, schema). fleet install-engine Download the CDISC Rules Engine binary for validation. fleet uninstall-engine Remove the managed CDISC Rules Engine binary. fleet doctor Check Fleet setup: engine, API key, codelists.py, optional extras. fleet derivation Scaffold and manage study-specific derivations. fleet mcp Serve Fleet tools to MCP-capable assistants (requires the 'mcp' extra). fleet lsp Language server for define.yaml files (requires the 'lsp' extra).

docs.title: fleet check
docs.text:
CI gate: parse the study config, check each define.yaml against its schema, check codelists.py against ct.package, ct.adam_package and the define.yaml files, build the validation run setup for SDTM and ADaM with no datasets, and check each custom rule YAML. An unsupported sdtm.ig_version or adam.ig_version and a configured validation.custom_rules directory that does not exist fail the gate. A missing rules engine and an unset CDISC_API_KEY are warnings only, because CI installs no engine. Exit 1 on any failure, else 0.

Option Default Description --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style).

docs.title: fleet compare
docs.text:
PROC COMPARE analogue: pair the two datasets on --keys, match variables by name and print the comparison report. --pairs compares variables named differently on each side and --variables restricts the comparison to the ones that matter. Equality is exact unless --abs-tol, --rel-tol or --ignore-trailing-whitespace widens it. --by sections the report per group and --allow-duplicates pairs duplicate keys by position. Exit 0 when the datasets are equal, 1 when they differ, 2 when the comparison could not run (unreadable file, missing keys, duplicate keys without --allow-duplicates, a negative tolerance, a --variables list of keys only, --out or --report not writable).

Argument Description base The reference dataset (parquet / csv / xpt / sas7bdat; SAS formats need the io extra). candidate The dataset measured against the base (same formats). Option Default Description --keys (required) Comma-separated variables that identify one observation on each side, e.g. USUBJID,AESEQ. Required; keys are never looked up. --by (none) Comma-separated variables to section the report by, e.g. TRT01P. They are prepended to --keys automatically, so they need not be repeated there. The observation and values summaries are also reported per group, and a group present on one side only is flagged and listed; the verdict stays global. --pairs (none) Comma-separated variable pairs whose sides carry different names, e.g. WEIGHT=WT. Applied on top of the automatic name matching, so a renamed column is compared rather than reported missing; the report names it after the base. A pair whose candidate variable is absent reports the base one as missing from the candidate. --variables (none) Comma-separated variables to restrict the comparison to, in base names, so a work-in-progress candidate is checked on the columns that are finished. A variable outside the list is ignored on both sides: neither compared nor reported as missing. --abs-tol 0.0 Absolute tolerance on the numeric variables (default: 0, exact). A numeric pair differs when the absolute difference exceeds max(--abs-tol, --rel-tol x |base|). --rel-tol 0.0 Relative tolerance on the numeric variables, as a fraction of the base value (default: 0, exact). It anchors on the base because the base is the reference, as in SAS: 0.01 is one percent of the base. --ignore-trailing-whitespace (none) Strip trailing whitespace from both sides of a string before comparing, so a legacy SAS dataset's padded character values equal Fleet's stripped ones. Leading whitespace still differs. --blank-is-missing (none) Read an empty string as missing on both sides, keys included, as SAS does. Use it when one side comes from a tool that kept blanks as empty strings (an R data frame without convert_blanks_to_na). A SAS file always reads a blank as missing. --text (none) Comma-separated CSV columns to read as text, the equivalent of a SAS $ informat, e.g. LBORRES. A CSV file holds no types: a column is text when a value on either side has a leading zero or is not a number, a number otherwise, and the other side's type when that side is not a CSV file. --encoding (none) Text encoding of a CSV or SAS file, e.g. iso-8859-1 for a file from a WLATIN1 SAS session (default: UTF-8). --allow-duplicates (none) Pair duplicate keys by their position within each key group instead of refusing to run. The report then counts the duplicates per side, raises the duplicate_keys flag and warns at the top: order within a key group decides which observations pair. --all (none) Print every unequal value (default: 50 per variable, 500 overall). --format text Output format: the text report, or one JSON document (verdict, flags, summaries, listing within the print limits, settings, Fleet version) and nothing else on stdout (default: text). Choices: text, json. --out (none) Also write the complete value listing (never truncated) to PATH as parquet, e.g. differences.parquet. --report (none) Also write a self-contained HTML report to PATH for a reviewer without Python: structural findings as chips, then every mismatched observation with the base and candidate values side by side, one collapsible block per variable.

docs.title: IDE & AI Tooling
docs.text: Fleet ships three optional layers of editor/assistant integration. None of them change what a pipeline does: each one exposes the workflow Fleet already has — its verbs, arguments and validation — to the editor or to an assistant, so the intended path is more obvious and the wrong path fails sooner. Pipelines run identically with or without them.

docs.title: Typed entry — fleet.frame() (optional)
docs.text:
df.sdtm / df.adam / df.tlg are registered on Polars frames at runtime, which static type checkers cannot see (pola-rs/polars#27795). Pipelines work either way — the only difference is what your editor reports:

import fleet
import polars as pl

# Without frame(): runs fine, but Pyright/Pylance flag `.sdtm` as unknown.
dm = pl.read_csv("dm_raw.csv").sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM").to_frame()

# With frame(): fully typed, zero runtime cost (returns its input unchanged).
raw = fleet.frame(pl.read_csv("dm_raw.csv"))
dm = raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM").to_frame()  # -> fleet.DataFrame
dm.tlg.ae  # typed downstream too, since to_frame() returns fleet.DataFrame

fleet.DataFrame / fleet.LazyFrame are plain aliases of the Polars classes at runtime (isinstance behaves normally); the namespace properties exist only for type checkers. Wrap loads at IO boundaries and everything downstream stays typed.

docs.title: Language server — fleet lsp (define.yaml intelligence)
docs.text:
uv add "fleet-cdisc[lsp]"      # adds pygls
fleet lsp --stdio              # spoken by any LSP client

Capabilities on define.yaml files, all discovered live from the installed Fleet package (never hardcoded):

Capability Source of truth Diagnostics on open/change generated JSON schema (define_spec_schema.json) Unknown algorithm: did-you-mean spec-algorithm registry Completions: algorithm ids and per-algorithm parameter keys registry (required params first) Completions: codelist OIDs the file's own codelists: section Hover: algorithm docs, codelist name + terms verb docstrings / inline codelists

VS Code: the client ships from its own repository, RealSlimMahdi/fleet-vscode (installation, settings, and the development loop are documented there). It finds the server via the fleet.server.path setting, then the FLEET_LSP env var, then .venv/bin/fleet, then uv run fleet. Other editors: point any LSP client at fleet lsp --stdio for YAML files.

docs.title: AI assistants — fleet mcp (Model Context Protocol)
docs.text: The MCP server lets any MCP-capable assistant (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, ...) call Fleet's pipeline intelligence as tools instead of guessing from source code.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
uv add "fleet-cdisc[mcp]"
# Claude Code (run from the study root — see note below):
claude mcp add fleet -- uv run fleet mcp --stdio

Any other MCP client uses the same stdio command. For JSON-config clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, a project .mcp.json):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fleet": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": ["run", "fleet", "mcp", "--stdio"],
      "cwd": "/path/to/your/study"
    }
  }
}

Launch from the study root. The tools take dataset/spec paths as arguments; registering the server with the study workspace as its working directory (cwd above, or running claude mcp add inside the study) lets the assistant pass the same relative paths your study_config.yaml uses (data/sdtm/ae.parquet, metadata/sdtm/define.yaml, ...).

docs.title: Exposed tools
docs.text:
Each is a thin wrapper over a public Fleet API:

Tool Does fleet_execution_order(spec_paths) topological dataset build order from define.yaml fleet_impacted_by(spec_paths, node) what must re-run if a dataset changes fleet_lineage(dag_json_path, dataset) variable-level lineage from a pipeline DAG export fleet_validate(dataset_path, standard?, version?, custom_rules?) CDISC Rules Engine validation from the run setup fleet_ct_terms(codelist, ct_path?) valid terms for a codelist fleet_tlg_catalog() all registered TLG templates fleet_tlg_run(spec_path, data_path, adsl_path?, groupby?) run a TLG spec YAML, return rendered HTML fleet_dataset_check(data_path, define_yaml, dataset) conformance check against the spec fleet_code_to_spec(source) derivation blocks reverse-mapped from a program's verb calls, without running it fleet_spec_to_code(define_yaml, dataset) an inline program skeleton rendered from a dataset's spec

fleet_validate builds the same run setup as fleet validate. It looks for the study_config.yaml from the directory of the dataset, not from the working directory of the server. So a dataset inside a study uses the study's IG version, custom rules and engine. When standard is not given, the configured data directory that holds the file names it, else the file stem (adsl.parquet is ADaM). The result lists each input with its source:

{
  "outcome": "pass",
  "dataset": "ADSL",
  "standard": "adam",
  "is_valid": true,
  "setup": {
    "standard": {"value": "adam", "source": "data directory"},
    "ig_version": {"value": "1.3", "source": "study config"},
    "custom_rules": {"value": "/study/metadata/custom_rules", "source": "study config"},
    "engine": {"value": "/home/me/.fleet/cdisc-rules-engine/core/core", "source": "default"},
    "engine_version": "0.15.0",
    "study_config": "/study/study_config.yaml"
  },
  "issues": []
}

A refused run setup does not raise. The tool returns {"outcome": "could not run", "reason": ...}: for example a standard conflict (data/adam/dm.parquet), an unsupported IG version, a custom rules directory that does not exist, or no engine found.

docs.title: What to ask your assistant
docs.text:
Once connected, these workflows stop being copy-paste-the-error loops and become one question each:

  • "In what order do I need to build the datasets in metadata/adam/define.yaml?" → fleet_execution_order
  • "If I change DM, which downstream datasets must re-run?" → fleet_impacted_by
  • "Where does ADSL.TRTSDT come from?" → fleet_lineage
  • "Validate data/sdtm/ae.parquet and summarise the errors." → fleet_validate
  • "Is 'INTERVENTIONAL' a valid term for C99077? What are the others?" → fleet_ct_terms
  • "Which TLG template covers an AE overview table, and run it against my ADAE." → fleet_tlg_catalog + fleet_tlg_run
  • "Does data/sdtm/dm.parquet conform to its define.yaml spec?" → fleet_dataset_check
  • "Turn this inline AE pipeline into define.yaml derivations." → fleet_code_to_spec
  • "Write me the ADSL program that metadata/adam/define.yaml describes." → fleet_spec_to_code

Combined with llms.txt (the machine-readable API summary shipped at the repo root), an assistant can both write Fleet pipelines and verify their outputs without leaving the conversation.

fleet doctor reports whether the lsp and mcp extras are installed.

docs.text:

uv (recommended)pip

docs.title: 1. SDTM domain from raw data
docs.text:
import fleet
import polars as pl
from codelists import SEX  # generated by: fleet add-ct --domains DM --output codelists.py

raw = pl.from_repr("""
┌────────────┬─────────┬────────────┐
│ patient_id ┆ sex_raw ┆ birth_date │
│ ---        ┆ ---     ┆ ---        │
│ str        ┆ str     ┆ str        │
╞════════════╪═════════╪════════════╡
│ 001        ┆ M       ┆ 1970-04-15 │
│ 002        ┆ F       ┆ 1985-11-02 │
│ 003        ┆ M       ┆ 1960-07-30 │
└────────────┴─────────┴────────────┘
""")

dm = (
    raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")
    .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=SEX, ct_map={"M": "M", "F": "F"})
    .date("BRTHDTC", source="birth_date")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 2. ADaM BDS dataset
docs.text:
vs_sdtm = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬────────────┬────────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ VISITNUM ┆ VSTESTCD ┆ VSSTRESN ┆ VSDTC      ┆ TRTSDT     │
│ ---     ┆ ---      ┆ ---      ┆ ---      ┆ ---        ┆ ---        │
│ str     ┆ i64      ┆ str      ┆ f64      ┆ str        ┆ str        │
╞═════════╪══════════╪══════════╪══════════╪════════════╪════════════╡
│ 001-01  ┆ 1        ┆ SYSBP    ┆ 120.0    ┆ 2024-01-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
│ 001-01  ┆ 2        ┆ SYSBP    ┆ 115.0    ┆ 2024-02-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
│ 001-01  ┆ 3        ┆ SYSBP    ┆ 118.0    ┆ 2024-03-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
└─────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴────────────┴────────────┘
""")

advs = (
    vs_sdtm.adam.source("USUBJID")
    .assign("PARAMCD", source="VSTESTCD")
    .assign("AVAL", source="VSSTRESN")
    .date("ADT", source="VSDTC")
    .study_day("ADY", date_col="ADT", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria='pl.col("VISITNUM") == 1', by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .pchg("PCHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 3. ADSL (one row per subject)
docs.text:
# Exposure rule of the admiral template (ad_adsl.R): a placebo dose of 0 is exposure.
# The SAP decides. Change this if placebo is not coded EXDOSE = 0 with PLACEBO in EXTRT.
treated = (
    '(pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0) | '
    '((pl.col("EXDOSE") == 0) & pl.col("EXTRT").str.to_uppercase().str.contains("PLACEBO"))'
)

adsl = (
    dm_sdtm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID", "AGE", "SEX")
    .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXSTDTC", where=treated)
    .last_date("TRTEDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXENDTC", where=treated)
    .duration("TRTDURD", start="TRTSDT", end="TRTEDT")
    .flag("SAFFL", criteria='pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null()', false_value="N")
    .count_events("NUMAE", from_dataset=ae_sdtm)
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 4. define.yaml-driven pipeline
docs.text:
Fleet can read a define.yaml specification and execute the whole pipeline without hand-writing verbs:

import polars as pl
import fleet  # noqa: F401

dm = pl.read_parquet("outputs/sdtm/dm.parquet")
ex = pl.read_parquet("outputs/sdtm/ex.parquet")

adsl = (
    dm.adam.pin("EX", ex)
    .from_spec("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml", dataset="ADSL")
    .to_frame()
)

from_spec is the execution entry point: pin any datasets the spec references by name, then materialise with .to_frame(). See How define.yaml works for the full spec format.

docs.title: 5. Generate Define-XML
docs.text:
One CLI command — inside a study workspace both paths default from study_config.yaml (--spec, --output, and --standard sdtm|adam override):

uv run fleet define-xml --standard adam

The same generation from Python, for notebooks or custom scripts:

from fleet import DefineSpecGenerator

DefineSpecGenerator("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml").generate(
    "outputs/cdiscpilot01/define_adam.xml"
)

docs.title: Your first SDTM domain — zero setup
docs.text:
No API key, no config file, no network. Import fleet and chain verbs on any Polars DataFrame:

import fleet
import polars as pl

raw = pl.from_repr("""
┌────────────┬─────────┬────────────┐
│ patient_id ┆ sex_raw ┆ birth_date │
│ ---        ┆ ---     ┆ ---        │
│ str        ┆ str     ┆ str        │
╞════════════╪═════════╪════════════╡
│ 001        ┆ Male    ┆ 1970-04-15 │
│ 002        ┆ Female  ┆ 1985-11-02 │
│ 003        ┆ Male    ┆ 1960-07-30 │
└────────────┴─────────┴────────────┘
""")

dm = (
    raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")
    .date("BRTHDTC", source="birth_date")
    .to_frame()
)
print(dm)

┌────────────┬─────────┬────────────┬────────┬───────────┬─────────┬────────────┐
│ patient_id ┆ sex_raw ┆ birth_date ┆ DOMAIN ┆ STUDYID   ┆ USUBJID ┆ BRTHDTC    │
│ 001        ┆ Male    ┆ 1970-04-15 ┆ DM     ┆ MYSTUDY01 ┆ 001     ┆ 1970-04-15 │
│ …          ┆         ┆            ┆        ┆           ┆         ┆            │
└────────────┴─────────┴────────────┴────────┴───────────┴─────────┴────────────┘

assign is the one assignment verb: source= copies a column, value= hardcodes a literal. All derivations accumulate lazily and collapse into a single optimized Polars pass at .to_frame().

More zero-setup wins

The Trial Design domains work fully offline too — SDTMIG 3.4 structures ship with Fleet, so fleet tdd build and the whole Trial Design walkthrough run without an API key.

docs.title: Add controlled terminology
docs.text:
CT is where the CDISC Library comes in. Put an API key in a .env file at your project root:

.env
CDISC_API_KEY=your-key-here

Then bootstrap typed codelist constants for your study's domains:

fleet add-ct --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --output codelists.py

This queries the SDTM Implementation Guide to discover every codelist referenced by variables in those domains, downloads the term definitions from the CDISC Library, and generates a typed Python module with IDE auto-completion. Now the same pipeline validates and recodes against real CT:

from codelists import SEX  # generated above

dm = (
    raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")
    .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=SEX, ct_map={"Male": "M", "Female": "F"})
    .date("BRTHDTC", source="birth_date")
    .to_frame()
)

ct= (a generated codelist class or an NCI concept ID) turns on controlled-terminology validation — no need to look up concept IDs. ct_map recodes collected values to CT submission values (here "Male" → "M"); omit it when the raw data already matches the codelist — values are then passed through and validated as-is.

docs.title: Your first ADaM BDS dataset
docs.text:
vs_sdtm = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬──────────┬─────────┬───────┬────────────┬────────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ VISITNUM ┆ PARAMCD ┆ AVAL  ┆ ADT        ┆ TRTSDT     │
│ ---     ┆ ---      ┆ ---     ┆ ---   ┆ ---        ┆ ---        │
│ str     ┆ i64      ┆ str     ┆ f64   ┆ str        ┆ str        │
╞═════════╪══════════╪═════════╪═══════╪════════════╪════════════╡
│ 001-01  ┆ 1        ┆ SYSBP   ┆ 120.0 ┆ 2024-01-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
│ 001-01  ┆ 2        ┆ SYSBP   ┆ 115.0 ┆ 2024-02-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
│ 001-01  ┆ 3        ┆ SYSBP   ┆ 118.0 ┆ 2024-03-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
└─────────┴──────────┴─────────┴───────┴────────────┴────────────┘
""")

advs = (
    vs_sdtm.adam.source("USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVAL")
    .study_day("ADY", date_col="ADT", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria='pl.col("VISITNUM") == 1', by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .pchg("PCHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

The flag → baseline → chg chain runs in one pipeline — no intermediate .to_frame(). study_day uses the CDISC algorithm (+1 when on/after the reference date, no day 0).

docs.title: ADSL — one row per subject
docs.text:
# Exposure rule of the admiral template (ad_adsl.R): a placebo dose of 0 is exposure.
# The SAP decides. Change this if placebo is not coded EXDOSE = 0 with PLACEBO in EXTRT.
treated = (
    '(pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0) | '
    '((pl.col("EXDOSE") == 0) & pl.col("EXTRT").str.to_uppercase().str.contains("PLACEBO"))'
)

adsl = (
    dm_sdtm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID", "AGE", "SEX")
    .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXSTDTC", where=treated)
    .last_date("TRTEDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXENDTC", where=treated)
    .duration("TRTDURD", start="TRTSDT", end="TRTEDT")
    .flag("SAFFL", criteria='pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null()', false_value="N")
    .count_events("NUMAE", from_dataset=ae_sdtm)
    .to_frame()
)

A population flag is never blank (ADaMIG 1.3), so false_value="N" gives N to the subjects outside the safety population.

Fleet also provides Admiral-parity verbs for advanced BDS derivations — bsa(), map(), qtc(), derive_summary_records(), derive_locf_records(), and derive_param() — as well as ADSL helpers age_years() and derive_period(). See the Cheat Sheet for the full list.

docs.title: Initialising a new study workspace
docs.text:
The bootstrapping pipeline is the recommended way to set up a new study. It creates the folder tree, queries the CDISC Library IG to generate define.yaml specs, and downloads the referenced codelists:

# Step 1 — create study_config.yaml + directory structure
fleet init cfg --study-id MYSTUDY01 --company "Acme Pharma" \
  --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS --root ./studies/MYSTUDY01

# Step 2 — generate define.yaml from the CDISC Library IG
fleet init define

# Step 3 — generate codelists.py from define.yaml codelist references
fleet init ct

See the CLI Reference for full argument details and standalone commands like fleet add-ct.

The same first step can be done programmatically with StudyContext.init():

from fleet import StudyContext, SDTMConfig, ADAMConfig

ctx = StudyContext.init(
    "./studies/MYSTUDY01",
    study_id="MYSTUDY01",
    company="Acme Pharma",
    sdtm=SDTMConfig(ig_version="3-4", domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]),
    adam=ADAMConfig(ig_version="1-1", datasets=["ADSL", "ADVS"]),
)

This creates:

studies/MYSTUDY01/
  study_config.yaml        ← load later with load_study_context()
  data/
    raw/
    sdtm/
    adam/
  metadata/
    sdtm/                  ← define.yaml created by `fleet init define`
    adam/                   ← define.yaml created by `fleet init define`
  outputs/

If study_config.yaml already exists, StudyContext.init() raises a StudyConfigError without touching anything — protecting in-progress work.

To reload an existing workspace in subsequent sessions:

from pathlib import Path
from fleet import load_study_context

ctx = load_study_context(Path("./studies/MYSTUDY01/study_config.yaml"))

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: When building SDTM or ADaM pipelines in Fleet, you may encounter errors either from data mismatches or pipeline syntax. This guide will help you understand common errors and debug effectively.

docs.title: CTError: Invalid value for codelist...
docs.text:
What it means: A value in your source data does not match the expected Controlled Terminology mappings for a variable derived using .assign(ct=...).

How to fix it:

  1. Check the raw values using Polars: df.select("raw_column").unique().
  2. Compare those values to the mapping dictionary provided in .assign(ct_map={...}).
  3. Add the missing key -> value pair, or fix upstream data collection errors.

docs.title: ColumnNotFoundError from Polars
docs.text:
What it means: You are attempting to derive a variable that depends on a column not yet present in the pipeline (e.g. asking for AVAL before it has been sourced or derived).

How to fix it: Order matters in a Fleet pipeline! Make sure that a dependency variable is derived before subsequent verbs that rely on it. For example, .source("AVAL") must appear before .baseline(aval="AVAL", ...)

docs.title: ValueError: Unknown algorithm in define.yaml
docs.text:
What it means: In a spec-driven pipeline, your define.yaml uses an algorithm name under a derivation block that doesn't match any recognised namespace verbs.

How to fix it: Check your spelling against the supported lists of verbs in the Namespace Pipeline or the API Reference. The JSON Schema (define_spec_schema.json) enforces a strict enum of valid algorithm names, so an editor validating against it flags invalid algorithms and empty derivation: {} blocks before you even run the pipeline — see Validating define.yaml below.

docs.title: Debugging Lazy Evaluation
docs.text:
Because Fleet builds pipelines conceptually and executes them lazily via Polars, a python stack trace might sometimes point to .to_frame() rather than the specific verb that caused an issue.

To inspect what expressions have been queued up before running:

pipeline = dm.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM").assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")

# Inspect the underlying Polars Expressions
print(pipeline._exprs)

You can also comment out .to_frame() and print intermediate outputs to verify your structure step-by-step.

# To debug an intermediate state, truncate the pipeline:
debug_df = (
    dm.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    # .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=...)  <-- Commented out to isolate the bug
    .to_frame()
)
print(debug_df.head())

docs.title: Validating define.yaml
docs.text:
If you are using the spec-driven approach, validate your define.yaml file against the Fleet schema before running pipelines. This ensures you don't waste time tracing runtime errors that are actually typos in the specification.

The Fleet VS Code extension does this with no setup: fleet lsp loads the schema from the installed package, so it can never drift from the Fleet that runs your pipeline.

Without the extension, a generic YAML language server can read the same schema from a comment at the top of the file:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=<path to define_spec_schema.json>

fleet init define prints that line with the path already resolved against your install. Scaffolded specs no longer carry it by default, because running both validators reports every schema error twice.
